interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and submitting to Allah throughout one's life. It underscores the concept that Islam is a chosen and divinely guided path, and believers should remain steadfast and sincere in their submission to God until the end of their lives, embodying true faith even in the face of challenges.

translation: Or were you witnesses when Jacob was dying and he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, one God, and to Him we submit."
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and unity of monotheistic faith across generations, emphasizing the sincere submission to one God as taught by the patriarchs. It underscores that true worship is rooted in acknowledging and following the same singular divine reality recognized by the prophets and their descendants.

translation: That was a nation who has passed away. For them is that which they earned, and for you is that which you earn. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse teaches us the principle of individual accountability, emphasizing that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly. It also reminds us that previous nations had their own deeds and consequences distinct from ours, reinforcing that we should focus on our own conduct and not be held accountable for others' deeds.

translation: And they say, "Be Jews or Christians so that you may be guided." Say, "Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal and foundational nature of the faith of Prophet Abraham, which is a monotheistic and pure devotion to God, free from any form of idolatry or association partners with Him. It addresses the claims of others who insist on following specific religious labels, reminding that true guidance lies in the sincere submission to one God, as exemplified by Abraham, who was neither a Jew nor a Christian but a true monotheist.

translation: Say, "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and continuity of divine revelation across different prophets and scriptures. It teaches that true faith requires acceptance of all the prophets and their messages without discrimination, highlighting a comprehensive belief that transcends sectarian divisions. The declaration of being 'Muslim' here signifies submission to Allah alone, uniting believers under the acknowledgment that God's guidance has been consistently conveyed through various messengers.

translation: If they believe in like what you believe in, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then they are only in dissension. And Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance is reached through shared faith in the core truths of Islam. Those who accept these truths are on the path of guidance, while those who reject them remain in conflict and division. It reassures the believer that God's support and protection are sufficient against opposition, highlighting His all-hearing and all-knowing nature.

translation: The color (or dye) of Allah; and who is better than Allah in dyeing? And we are worshippers of Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true and ultimate transformation or identity comes from Allah alone. 'صبغة الله' (the color of Allah) symbolizes the imprint or mark of divine guidance and faith on the heart and character of the believer, which is superior and more lasting than any worldly affiliation or influence. The verse asserts that no one can provide a better imprint or identity than Allah, and accordingly, sincere worship and devotion are directed solely to Him as the source of all true guidance and transformation.

translation: Say, "Do you dispute with us concerning Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. And we are sincere to Him alone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the sovereignty of Allah as the Lord of all. It underscores that disputes over faith should be grounded in sincere devotion and personal accountability, highlighting that everyone is responsible for their own actions before Allah, and true sincerity to Him is paramount.

translation: Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants were Jews or Christians? Say, "Then who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good?" And the religion before Allah is submission (Islam). And they were not divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in [taking] account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance and sincerity in faith are not confined to specific religious labels or groups such as Jews or Christians; rather, it lies in sincere submission to God and righteousness. It criticizes those who claim exclusive knowledge of divine truth, reminding them that God, in His omniscience, is fully aware of what is concealed or professed. It serves as a warning against hypocrisy and the concealment of truth, underscoring that accountability before God encompasses all actions, visible or hidden.

translation: Those were a nation who have passed away. They will have that which they earned, and you will have that which you earn. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and accountability before God. It teaches that each community and every person is judged only for their own actions, not for the deeds of others who have come before them. It reassures believers that past peoples are responsible for their own outcomes, while individuals are accountable for their own conduct, thus underscoring personal moral responsibility.

translation: The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they used to face?" Say, "To Allah belongs the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance and direction come solely from Allah, regardless of physical orientation or external changes. The question posed by the ignorant reflects a superficial concern with outward forms, whereas Allah's sovereignty encompasses all directions, and He alone guides people rightly. Therefore, the change in the qiblah is a reminder that spiritual direction is determined by divine will, not by tradition or human preference.

translation: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused your faith to be lost. Indeed, Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of the Muslim community as a balanced and just nation, chosen to bear the responsibility of testifying to the truth in human affairs. The change of the qiblah (direction of prayer) serves as a divine means to clearly distinguish sincere followers of the Prophet from those who abandon the path, highlighting that true guidance is ultimately granted by Allah's will. The verse reassures believers that their faith is safeguarded by Allah's compassion, affirming that divine mercy supports and preserves the integrity of the faithful community.

translation: We have certainly seen the turn of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it. Indeed, those who have been given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine command to change the direction of prayer (qiblah) from Jerusalem to the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, symbolizing a significant shift in religious practice and identity for the Muslim community. It reflects Allah's control over guidance, turning the Prophet's face to what is best and pleasing to him, and serves as a reminder that believers, regardless of their location, are unified in worship by facing the same focal point. It also acknowledges that the People of the Book recognize the truth of this command as from Allah, and that Allah is aware of all actions, reinforcing His omniscience and the importance of obedience.

translation: And even if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qibla; and you are not a follower of their qibla. Nor are they all alike; some of them are not followers of the qibla of others. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, indeed, you would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility in attempting to please everyone by aligning religious practices, such as the direction of prayer, with the varied preferences of different groups. The true guidance comes from divine knowledge, not from following the differing desires or traditions of others. It underscores the importance of adhering to the revelation given, even if others reject it or have their own practices, to avoid injustice in matters of faith.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture know it just as they know their own sons. Yet a faction of them conceal the truth, even though they know it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the paradox of people who have been bestowed with divine knowledge, such as the Scriptures, understanding it as intimately as they know their own families, yet some choose to deliberately hide or distort the truth despite their awareness. It reflects on human tendencies of willful concealment or misrepresentation of guidance for various motives, reminding believers to be cautious of such hypocrisy and to seek truth sincerely.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so be not among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth of the message revealed to the Prophet comes directly from God, and it urges the listener to fully accept this truth without hesitation or doubt, highlighting the importance of faith and trust in divine revelation.

translation: And to every person is a direction to which he turns, so race to [all that is] good. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse teaches that every individual has a unique orientation or path in life, be it in faith or deeds. It encourages striving earnestly in doing good deeds. No matter how different our directions or where we are, Allah’s power encompasses all, and He will assemble everyone for accounting or reward. This reminds believers to prioritize goodness and unity under Allah's all-encompassing authority.

translation: And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and direction in worship for the Muslim community by instructing believers to face the Kaaba during prayer, signifying submission to Allah's guidance. It also affirms the Qur'an as a truthful revelation from God and reminds that Allah is fully aware of all actions, encouraging sincerity and mindfulness in worship and daily life.

translation: And from wherever you emerge, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, so that people will have no argument against you except those among them who are unjust. So fear them not, but fear Me. And [it is] so I complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to face the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque during prayer, signifying unity and devotion. It emphasizes obedience to divine guidance over human opinions, encouraging the faithful to fear God alone. The directive underscores God's mercy in completing His favor by guiding them toward righteousness and spiritual cohesion.

translation: Just as We sent among you a Messenger from yourselves who recites to you Our verses, purifies you, teaches you the Book and wisdom, and teaches you what you did not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive role of the Prophet as a divinely appointed guide who not only conveys the revelations but also facilitates spiritual purification and imparts wisdom and knowledge beyond previous understanding, emphasizing the transformative effect of prophetic guidance on both the individual and the community.

translation: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reciprocal relationship between God and His servants, emphasizing that by sincerely remembering and acknowledging God, believers will find themselves remembered and favored by Him. It calls for gratitude as a means to deepen this connection and warns against ingratitude and denial, which sever the bond and lead to spiritual loss.

translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse teaches that enduring difficulties with patience and turning to prayer are essential means of seeking support and strength. It emphasizes that Allah's closeness and assistance are assured for those who remain steadfast and patient in the face of trials.

translation: And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive it not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who sacrifice their lives in the path of Allah are not truly dead; their existence transcends the physical world. Their souls continue to live, experiencing a form of life that is meaningful and honored in the sight of Allah, even though we may not perceive this reality in our worldly understanding.

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient.
interpretation: This verse highlights that life's trials—including fear, scarcity, and loss—are a means by which God tests human faith and resilience. The message encourages patience and steadfastness during hardships, assuring that those who endure such tests with perseverance are granted glad tidings of reward and divine pleasure.

translation: Those who, when afflicted with a calamity, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing that all things, including hardships and losses, ultimately belong to Allah and that returning to Him is inevitable. It teaches believers to respond to trials with patience and faith, acknowledging God's sovereignty and maintaining hope in His wisdom and mercy during times of distress.

translation: For them are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is they who are the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights that those who follow God's guidance and maintain righteousness receive His blessings and mercy, signifying that true guidance is marked by the presence of divine favor and compassion in one's life.

translation: Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the rituals of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, Allah is Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights that certain acts within worship, even if they seem unusual or particular, are divinely ordained rituals that must be respected and followed. It emphasizes that performing these rituals is not just permissible but also a recognition of God's guidance. Furthermore, it encourages voluntary acts of goodness beyond obligatory rituals, assuring that God is ever grateful and fully aware of all deeds, thereby inspiring sincere devotion and deliberate righteousness.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear for the people in the Scripture—those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe sin of deliberately hiding divine guidance and clear signs that have been revealed to humanity. It emphasizes that such concealment is not merely a personal wrongdoing but attracts a collective curse from God and the community, reflecting the gravity of obstructing others from accessing the truth and the means to guidance.

translation: Except for those who repent, reform, and clearly explain their wrongdoing, for those I will accept their repentance; indeed, I am the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless mercy and willingness to forgive those who sincerely repent, amend their ways, and make their transgressions known or clear. It conveys that no matter the severity of one's past sins, genuine repentance coupled with corrective actions leads to Allah's forgiveness, underscoring the hopeful opportunity for redemption and spiritual renewal.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers—upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of all mankind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequence for those who reject faith and die persistently disbelieving; it highlights that such a state invokes not only divine wrath but also condemnation by angels and all mankind, underscoring the gravity of disbelief and its isolation from any form of support or mercy in the afterlife.

translation: They will abide therein forever; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence and inevitability of the punishment for those who have earned it by their deeds, highlighting that there will be no mitigation or respite. It serves as a stern warning about the consequences of one's actions and the justice of the Hereafter, underscoring the importance of adhering to righteousness to avoid such a fate.

translation: And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God, affirming that He alone is worthy of worship. By highlighting His attributes of mercy and compassion, it reminds believers that God's singular divinity is coupled with profound benevolence, inviting trust and devotion.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships that sail through the sea with what benefits people, and the water that Allah sends down from the sky, reviving the earth after its death and dispersing therein every kind of moving creature, and the directing of the winds and the clouds subjugated between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the natural phenomena as clear signs of Allah's power and wisdom. It encourages understanding that the order and harmony in the universe—the creation of the heavens and earth, the cycle of night and day, the facilitation of human benefit through the sea, the revival of earth by rain after apparent death, the diversity of life, and the regulation of winds and clouds—are evidence for those who think deeply and recognize divine design in all aspects of existence.

translation: And among the people are those who take others besides Allah as equals [to Him], loving them as they should love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah. If only those who do wrong could see when they will see the punishment, that all power belongs to Allah alone, and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who misdirect their love and devotion towards beings other than Allah, treating them as equals to God, and the true believers whose love for Allah is profound and overwhelming. It warns that the wrongdoers fail to recognize the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah and the consequences awaiting them. The verse serves as a reminder to direct one's love and loyalty solely to Allah, understanding His ultimate authority and justice.

translation: When those who followed disassociated themselves from those who had followed them and saw the punishment, and the ties between them were severed.
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment of regret and despair on the Day of Judgment, where those who blindly followed others in error attempt to deny their complicity, but when faced with divine punishment, the bonds of excuse and association crumble, emphasizing personal responsibility for one's own choices regardless of whom one followed.

translation: And those who followed [the wrong path] will say, "If only we had another chance, we would disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated themselves from us." Thus does Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them; and they will not emerge from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse reflects the reality that in the Hereafter, remorse will be of no benefit for those who followed falsehood. Although they will wish to sever ties with those who misled them, it will be too late to escape the consequences of their deeds. It serves as a warning that disavowal after the fact cannot change one's destined outcome and emphasizes the importance of making righteous choices before death.

translation: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth [that is] lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse instructs humanity to consume only what is pure and permitted, emphasizing the importance of following divine guidance in our daily choices. It also warns against imitating Satan's temptations, which lead us away from righteousness, reminding us that Satan is an evident adversary striving to mislead us.

translation: He only commands you to do evil and immoral acts and to say about Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against following those who advocate wrongful deeds and attribute false statements to Allah without knowledge. It highlights the danger of blindly accepting teachings or commands that lead to immorality and fabrications about God's nature or will, urging believers to seek knowledge and truth before accepting any claims about the Divine.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our forefathers." Even though their forefathers understood nothing nor were they guided?
interpretation: This verse highlights the irrationality of adhering to customs blindly, without critical examination or consideration of divine guidance. It critiques those who cling to ancestral traditions merely for the sake of inheritance, neglecting the wisdom and truth revealed by God. The verse urges individuals to prioritize conscious understanding and genuine guidance over unreflective imitation of past practices.

translation: And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who shouts at what neither hears nor responds—deaf, dumb, and blind—so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and hopelessness of calling upon or expecting benefit from those who reject faith; their hearts and minds are so closed that they are incapable of understanding or responding to guidance, much like shouting at something utterly unresponsive and blind to your voice.

translation: O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah if it is indeed Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes not only the importance of consuming lawful and wholesome provisions but also links recognition of God's blessings with sincere gratitude. It teaches that faith is reflected in appreciating and utilizing the sustenance provided by God while acknowledging Him through thankfulness, thereby establishing a direct connection between belief, ethical conduct in consumption, and gratitude.

translation: Indeed, forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced by necessity, neither desiring sin nor exceeding limits, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse delineates clear boundaries regarding what is prohibited to consume, emphasizing the sanctity and purity in dietary laws. However, it also embodies the principle of mercy and practicality by allowing exceptions in cases of absolute necessity, where preserving life takes precedence over strict adherence to prohibitions. Thus, it highlights Allah's balance between justice in command and compassion in circumstance.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book and buy (exchange) it for a small price - those are not eating except into their bellies fire. And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who deliberately hide or suppress the divine revelations for worldly gains or trivial benefits. It emphasizes the severe spiritual consequences of such actions, portraying it as feeding a fire within oneself—a metaphor for consuming one's soul with sin and punishment. The denial of Allah's conversation and purification on the Day of Judgment highlights the ultimate alienation and loss of mercy, underscoring the gravity of tampering with divine guidance.

translation: Those are the ones who have exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment. How patient they will be in the fire!
interpretation: This verse highlights the tragic choice of those who knowingly trade the eternal blessing of guidance and forgiveness for the fleeting allure of misguidance and punishment. Despite having the opportunity to embrace the truth, they persist in error, leading to their inevitable endurance of severe consequences in the Hereafter. It serves as a profound reminder of the gravity of such voluntary misguidance and the immense suffering it entails.

translation: That is because Allah has sent down the Book with the truth. And indeed, those who differ concerning the Book are in extreme dissension.
interpretation: This verse reflects the reality that the Qur'an is a divinely revealed scripture containing ultimate truth. However, the divisions and disputes among people regarding its interpretation or other revealed scriptures stem from their failure to recognize and adhere to this truth, leading them into deep discord and separation from the guidance intended by God.

translation: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces towards the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is in one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets, and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing slaves; and who establishes prayer and gives zakah; those who fulfill their promise when they promise; and those who are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous.
interpretation: True righteousness extends beyond mere outward rituals or directional acts of worship; it encompasses sincere faith in the fundamental tenets of Islam and manifests through concrete acts of generosity, steadfastness in worship, commitment to promises, and endurance through trials. This verse illustrates that authentic piety is both a matter of internal belief and external action, reflecting a comprehensive approach to ethical and spiritual conduct.

translation: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever overlooks from his brother anything, then there should be a follow-up with kindness and payment to him with good conduct. This is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy. But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of justice balanced with mercy in matters of life and death. It mandates equitable retribution to uphold justice but also encourages forgiveness and kindness as a means to alleviate suffering and promote reconciliation. The allowance for forgiveness underscores the value of mercy in the Shariah, suggesting that true justice encompasses both holding wrongdoers accountable and offering room for compassion and peace among individuals.

translation: And there is for you in legal retribution [saving of] life, O you [people] of understanding, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the institution of justice through lawful retribution serves as a means to preserve life and maintain societal order. It calls upon people of intellect to recognize that adhering to just consequences is not merely punitive but a divine guidance aimed at fostering righteousness and preventing chaos, thus promoting a balanced and conscientious community.

translation: It has been prescribed for you, when death comes to one of you, if he leaves wealth, that he makes a bequest for the parents and relatives in a rightful manner. This is a duty upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of preparing for the inevitable reality of death by making fair and just bequests to one's parents and close relatives. It highlights that such responsible and thoughtful actions are a mark of true piety and righteousness, reflecting an individual's consciousness of their duties not only towards God but also towards their family and society.

translation: So whoever alters it after he has heard it - then indeed, his sin is only upon those who alter it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the responsibility and sin of altering the message of the Qur'an does not rest upon the one who hears and believes it with sincerity, but rather upon those who intentionally change or distort it. It highlights Allah's encompassing knowledge and awareness, affirming that no wrongful alteration goes unnoticed or unaccounted for by Him.

translation: So whoever fears from a transgressor or an oppressor some breach or sin and reconciles between them, there is no blame upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of fearing injustice or wrongdoing in disputes and taking the initiative to reconcile between conflicting parties. It highlights that such efforts at peacemaking, even if they involve addressing past grievances or sins, are free from blame because they promote harmony and prevent further harm. The Divine attributes of forgiveness and mercy underscore that the path of reconciliation is favored and protected by God, encouraging believers to act as agents of peace within their communities.

translation: O you who have believed, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that fasting is not a novel practice but one established among previous communities, intended as a means to develop piety and self-discipline. The purpose of fasting is to help believers cultivate God-consciousness and self-restraint, leading to righteousness and moral refinement.

translation: A limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey—then an equal number of days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship]—a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person. But whoever volunteers good—it is better for him. And fasting is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the balance between religious obligations and human circumstances. It acknowledges that fasting during Ramadan is a commanded act of worship but allows for flexibility in cases of illness or travel by permitting compensatory fasting. For those unable to fast, it prescribes feeding the needy as an alternative, highlighting social responsibility. Furthermore, it encourages voluntary goodness beyond what is obligatory, indicating that voluntary acts carry greater spiritual benefit. The concluding affirmation that fasting is better underscores its intrinsic value when one understands its wisdom.

translation: The month of Ramadan [is that] in which the Quran was revealed, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Ramadan as a significant time marked by the revelation of the Quran, emphasizing its role as guidance and a clear distinction between right and wrong. The command to fast during Ramadan is presented with compassion, allowing those who are ill or traveling to make up the missed days later, underscoring Allah's desire to facilitate ease rather than hardship. The verse calls believers to complete their observance fully and to express gratitude and glorification to Allah for His guidance, fostering mindfulness, discipline, and thankfulness as integral aspects of spiritual growth.

translation: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the closeness and accessibility of God to His servants. It reassures that God is always near, attentive, and responsive to the prayers and supplications of those who sincerely turn to Him. The verse encourages believers to maintain a direct relationship with God through faith and sincere invocation, highlighting that such sincere engagement and belief are the pathways to true guidance and enlightenment.

translation: It is made lawful for you to have intimate relations with your wives on the night of fasting. They are garments for you, and you are garments for them. Allah knows that you used to deceive yourselves, so He has turned to you in mercy and pardoned you. So now, go to them and seek what Allah has decreed for you. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread, then complete the fast until night. Do not have intimate relations with them while you are secluded in the mosques. These are the limits set by Allah, so do not approach them. Thus, Allah makes His signs clear for people, so they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse clarifies the permissible times and manners of intimacy during fasting, emphasizing that the night is a time of mutual support and closeness between spouses, who are likened to garments for one another, symbolizing comfort, protection, and intimacy. It also warns against violating the sanctity of the fast by engaging in such relations during the day when fasting is prescribed. Furthermore, the verse underscores God's mercy in forgiving past mistakes and setting boundaries to guide believers toward righteousness and self-discipline. The overarching message is that obedience to divine limits nurtures piety and spiritual growth.

translation: And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or use it to bribe the authorities so that you may knowingly consume a portion of the wealth of others unlawfully.
interpretation: This verse warns against wrongful acquisition and misuse of wealth, emphasizing the prohibition of unjustly taking others' property and corrupting the justice system through bribery. It highlights the ethical imperative to maintain fairness and honesty in financial dealings and the grave sin in exploiting both wealth and authority for personal gain at the expense of others.

translation: They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back; but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses from their doors. And fear Allah that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that natural phenomena like the new moons serve as signs and tools for humans to organize their lives, such as determining the proper times for worship and pilgrimage. It also emphasizes that true righteousness and piety lie not in mere outward conformity or superficial acts but in the consciousness and fear of God. The instruction to enter houses through their proper doors symbolizes following divine guidance and propriety, reinforcing that ethical behavior requires adherence to correct and sincere paths rather than shortcuts or deceitful means.

translation: And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of just warfare in Islam: while believers are permitted to defend themselves and fight those who initiate aggression against them, they must strictly avoid exceeding limits by committing acts of injustice or harming civilians. It teaches that the legitimacy of fighting is bound by moral restraint and that transgression undermines the righteousness of their cause.

translation: And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation of defensive warfare against those who persecute and expel believers from their homes. It emphasizes that fighting is permitted when one faces aggression and injustice, particularly in sacred places like the Sacred Mosque, but only in response to aggression. The verse also highlights that trials and oppression (fitnah) are more severe than killing, underscoring the gravity of persecution. Ultimately, it reflects the principle that resistance is justified against tyranny and oppression to uphold justice and protect the community.

translation: But if they desist, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and readiness to forgive those who abandon wrongful actions. It reminds us that sincere repentance and turning away from sin open the door to divine forgiveness, highlighting the compassionate nature of Allah even towards those who have erred.

translation: Fight against them until there is no more fitnah and the religion, all of it, is for Allah. But if they cease, then there is to be no aggression except against the oppressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that resistance and struggle against injustice and oppression are obligatory until peace and freedom to practice the true faith are achieved. However, once the oppressors desist and peace is restored, further aggression is not permitted except to prevent any renewed oppression. The root principle is justice and the protection of faith, not unwarranted violence.

translation: The forbidden month is for the forbidden month, and for [all] violations is legal retribution. So whoever has assaulted you, then assault him in the same way that he has assaulted you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is with those who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and proportional retribution while underscoring the importance of observing sacred times and places. It teaches that retaliation should be measured and equivalent to the offense, not excessive or vindictive. Additionally, it commands believers to maintain consciousness of God (taqwa), reassuring them that divine support accompanies those who act with righteousness and restraint. Thus, it balances justice with mercy, advocating for fairness grounded in moral responsibility before God.

translation: And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands. And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse exhorts believers to be generous in their charity and efforts for the sake of Allah, while cautioning them against actions that lead to their own ruin. It emphasizes the balance between selflessness in supporting good causes and preserving one's well-being. The command to "do good" highlights the importance of kindness and excellence in all deeds, reassuring that such conduct is beloved by Allah.

translation: And complete the Hajj and 'umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary] must offer a ransom of fasting, charity, or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs 'umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and seven when you return [home], a total of ten complete days. This is for those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling religious rites sincerely for the sake of Allah alone, even when faced with obstacles. It highlights a balance between commitment and ease, offering alternatives when the ideal act is hindered, reflecting Allah's mercy and justice. The verse also underscores the obligation to fear Allah and be mindful of His strict accountability, encouraging believers to approach worship with both dedication and awareness of divine consequences.

translation: The pilgrimage months are well known. So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein, he must not have sexual relations, nor commit sin, nor dispute unjustly during the Hajj. And whatever good you do - Allah knows it. And take provision, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and specific regulations of the sacred months of pilgrimage, underlining the necessity for pilgrims to maintain purity in both actions and conduct during Hajj. It teaches that outward obedience and internal piety are both essential; good deeds are recognized by Allah regardless of human awareness, but the ultimate provision for any journey, especially the spiritual journey of Hajj, is taqwa (God-consciousness and righteousness). This calls believers to cultivate inner awareness and reverence for God as the true sustenance for success and protection.

translation: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord [during pilgrimage]. But when you leave Arafat, remember Allah at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram. And remember Him as He has guided you, and indeed you were before that among those astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that seeking blessings or benefits from Allah during the sacred rites of pilgrimage is permitted, highlighting the importance of sincere devotion. It also instructs believers to remember Allah continuously and sincerely, especially during significant moments in the pilgrimage, acknowledging the guidance they have received which has saved them from being lost or misguided before.

translation: Then disperse from the place whence all the people are dispersing and ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of following the collective guidance of the community in acts of worship and movement, while simultaneously emphasizing the necessity of continuously seeking Allah's forgiveness. It highlights Allah's mercy and readiness to forgive those who repent sincerely, encouraging believers to combine obedience with humility and repentance.

translation: So when you have completed your rites, remember Allah like your remembrance of your forefathers or with even greater remembrance. And among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," but he has no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse encourages sincere and profound remembrance of Allah after completing acts of worship, emphasizing that such remembrance should be as intense or even more than that with which people recall their ancestors. It also highlights a type of person who is solely concerned with worldly gains without considering their spiritual or eternal outcome, reminding believers to balance their pursuits and prioritize the Hereafter.

translation: And among them are those who say, 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse encapsulates a balanced supplication that seeks well-being and blessings in both the worldly life and the hereafter, acknowledging the importance of success and happiness in this life while also earnestly seeking the ultimate salvation and protection from the torment of Hellfire in the afterlife. It reflects a comprehensive mindset in worship and reliance on God, prioritizing both immediate and eternal welfare.

translation: Those will have a share of what they earned. And Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine justice of Allah, affirming that every individual will receive the consequences of their own deeds, and that Allah promptly holds everyone accountable, ensuring there is no delay in recompense for one's actions.

translation: And remember Allah during specified days. So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him - for those who fear Allah. And fear Allah and know that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the timing of certain religious observances is flexible within a specified period, emphasizing intention and God-consciousness over rigid adherence to exact dates. It highlights that what truly matters is one's piety and mindfulness of Allah, as ultimate accountability lies with Him.

translation: Among the people is he whose speech about the life of this world pleases you, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between outward appearances and inner realities. It warns that some people may speak beautifully and seem sincere about worldly matters, but their true intentions and feelings are hidden, and they may be deeply argumentative or hostile when challenged. This serves as a caution not to judge others solely by their words or outward demeanor, as their inner disposition might be quite different.

translation: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and offspring, but Allah does not like corruption.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of those who, out of rebellion or wicked intent, spread corruption on earth, harming both the environment and future generations. It serves as a warning against such behavior, emphasizing that God disapproves of any form of harm or destruction that disrupts the balance and harmony established in creation.

translation: And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride in sin takes hold of him. Hell is sufficient for him, and how evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of arrogance and stubbornness in the face of divine guidance. When a person is admonished to be conscious of God but instead their pride leads them to persist in sin, they distance themselves from mercy and guidance, thereby sealing their own destruction. It serves as a warning that self-exaltation through wrongdoing not only alienates one from righteousness but also results in a terrible fate, represented here by Hell, which is described as the worst place to rest.

translation: Among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of self-sacrifice for the sake of Allah's pleasure. It highlights that there are individuals who dedicate themselves wholly, even at great personal cost, to attain Allah's reward. Meanwhile, Allah's kindness reassures that such sincere devotion is recognized and rewarded, and His compassion encompasses all His servants.

translation: O you who have believed, enter into peace completely and do not follow the footsteps of Satan; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to fully embrace peace—both in their dealings with others and within themselves—without hesitation or reservation. It warns against following the deceptive influences of Satan, whose tactics aim to sow discord and lead people away from righteousness. The verse emphasizes that Satan is an evident enemy, reminding believers to remain vigilant and committed to harmony and obedience to God's guidance.

translation: So if you deviate after the clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness of turning away or erring after receiving clear and undeniable guidance. It highlights that such deviation is not taken lightly in the sight of Allah, who possesses both immense power and perfect wisdom, implying that accountability and consequences follow deliberate rejection of truth.

translation: Do they wait except that Allah should come to them in covers of clouds and the angels, and the matter is decided? And to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the impatience and skepticism of some people who doubt the final judgment. It emphasizes that the decisive moment will come when Allah arrives with His angels amidst clouds, signifying divine authority and the culmination of all affairs. It reminds us that ultimately, all matters revert to Allah's judgment, underscoring the inevitability and absolute nature of divine decree.

translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We have given them. And whoever changes the favor of Allah after it has come to him - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse warns against ingratitude and the alteration of God's blessings and guidance after they have been clearly bestowed. It emphasizes that divine favors, such as guidance and mercy, are not to be taken lightly or abandoned, and turning away from them leads to severe consequences. The verse reminds believers to hold firmly to the blessings and commandments granted by God, as altering or rejecting them invites strict retribution.

translation: The life of this world has been made appealing to those who disbelieve, and they ridicule those who believe. But those who are conscious of Allah shall be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah grants provision to whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the temporary allure of worldly life to disbelievers and the true, abiding success of the pious on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers mock the believers, focusing on the material world's pleasures, yet their ridicule is transient and superficial. Meanwhile, those who possess taqwa (God-consciousness) will have a superior status in the hereafter. Furthermore, Allah's provision is not limited or measured, signifying His boundless generosity to whomever He wills, indicating that reliance on divine provision surpasses worldly gains.

translation: The people were [once] one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between the people concerning that in which they differed. And none differed over it except those to whom it was given - after the clear proofs came to them - out of jealous animosity among themselves. And Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the original unity of mankind and the reason for the sending of prophets: to guide people with clear guidance and resolve their disagreements by means of divine revelation. The disagreements that arose among certain individuals occurred only after they received clear evidence, driven by envy and rivalry. Despite these differences, Allah grants guidance to those who sincerely believe, leading them back to the truth by His will. It emphasizes that ultimate guidance is a matter of divine will, and encourages trust in Allah's ability to lead believers to the right path.

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were struck by poverty and hardship and were shaken until [even] the messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.
interpretation: This verse teaches that entering Paradise is not guaranteed without enduring trials and hardships like those faced by the earlier believers. It emphasizes patience and steadfastness in faith during times of difficulty, as even the Prophet and his followers experienced severe tests before receiving divine support. The verse reassures believers that Allah's help and relief are imminent, encouraging trust in God's timing despite adversity.

translation: They ask you what they should spend. Say, "Whatever good you spend is for parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and the traveler. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it."
interpretation: This verse instructs that when considering charity or spending in the way of goodness, priority should be given to close family members and those in need within one’s community—parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and travelers. It emphasizes that spending in these causes is a form of good, and Allah is fully aware of every act of charity undertaken. The verse encourages responsible and thoughtful giving, assuring believers that no act of kindness, however small or intimate, escapes the knowledge of Allah.

translation: Fighting has been prescribed for you, and it is disliked by you. But perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse teaches that what may seem difficult or unpleasant to us, such as the obligation of fighting in certain circumstances, can be ultimately beneficial according to divine wisdom. Conversely, what we desire may not always be in our best interest. It calls for trust in Allah's knowledge and wisdom beyond human understanding, encouraging patience and faith in His decrees even when they conflict with our personal feelings or desires.

translation: They ask you about the sacred month—fighting therein. Say, "Fighting therein is a grave matter; and hindering from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, and expelling the people from the Sacred Mosque are even greater in the sight of Allah. And persecution is greater than killing." They will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever among you reverts from their religion and dies while they are disbelievers—those their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound severity of fighting during the sacred months, which were traditionally times of peace. It underscores not only the act of fighting as serious but elevates the banning from God's path, disbelief, and forcible expulsion from the sacred sanctuary as even graver violations. The verse also indicates that the persecution—efforts to divert believers from their faith—is worse than killing, emphasizing spiritual harm over physical. Moreover, it warns against apostasy, associating it with eternal loss. Thus, the verse teaches that faithfulness to one's religion amidst persecution is paramount, and that spiritual fidelity and preserving the sanctity of collective worship spaces hold profound significance in Islam.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights that faith, migration for the sake of Allah, and striving in His path are precious acts that draw a believer closer to Allah's mercy. It conveys that sincere commitment and sacrifice in the way of God foster hope for divine forgiveness and compassion, emphasizing Allah's nature as both forgiving of sins and merciful toward His servants.

translation: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, "In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they should spend. Say, "The excess [beyond needs]." Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses that you might give thought.
interpretation: This verse teaches that while certain actions or substances, like wine and gambling, might have some benefits or appeal, their harmful consequences outweigh these benefits significantly. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing ethical and spiritual well-being over temporary pleasure or gain, and encourages thoughtful consideration of what one consumes or engages in. Regarding spending, it directs believers to give from what is beyond their immediate necessities, promoting generosity and self-restraint.

translation: "In this world and the Hereafter. And they ask you about orphans: Say, 'Improving their condition is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer. And if Allah willed, He could have put you in difficulty. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'"
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of kindness and fairness towards orphans, emphasizing that improving their condition is the best approach. It reminds believers to treat orphans as their own brothers, fostering a sense of brotherhood and compassion. It also highlights that Allah is fully aware of those who intend harm and those who seek to do good, assuring that divine justice is ultimate. Lastly, it conveys that difficulties are within Allah's control and that He alone possesses both might and wisdom.

translation: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you. And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. And a believing slave man is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you. Those [polytheists] invite to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, and He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith as the foundation for marriage in Islam, highlighting that belief is superior to worldly attractiveness or social status. It warns against forming marital bonds with those who do not share the same faith, as such relationships may lead one away from the path of righteousness. The verse also contrasts the calls of polytheists, which lead to destruction, with Allah's invitation to Paradise and forgiveness, underscoring that adhering to divine guidance leads to true success and remembrance.

translation: They ask you about menstruation. Say, "It is harm, so keep away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them until they are purified. And when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where Allah has ordained for you. Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves."
interpretation: This verse addresses the natural occurrence of menstruation and provides guidance on the physical boundaries related to it in the context of intimacy. It emphasizes respect for the physical and spiritual state of women during menstruation and promotes purity by instructing believers to abstain during this time and to resume intimacy only after purification. Additionally, it highlights the importance of repentance and spiritual cleanliness, indicating that Allah values both the turning back to Him after mistakes and maintaining purity in actions and intentions.

translation: Your wives are a tillage for you, so go to your tillage when or how you will; and give [them] their due compensation in kindness. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intimate and reciprocal nature of the marital relationship, likening it to cultivation where both spouses derive benefit. It emphasizes approaching this relationship with care, respect, and responsibility, ensuring kindness and just treatment. The reminder of meeting Allah serves as an encouragement to uphold moral conduct and consciousness of divine accountability within the relationship.

translation: And do not make Allah an excuse for your oaths to do good, to fear Him, and to reconcile between people. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers not to misuse oaths as a means to avoid doing what is right, such as showing kindness, having consciousness of God, and fostering reconciliation among people. It highlights that Allah is fully aware of one's intentions and actions, emphasizing sincerity and integrity in fulfilling one's vows and responsibilities toward others.

translation: Allah does not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He imposes blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah distinguishes between mistakes made unintentionally and deliberate actions stemming from the heart's intentions. It reassures believers that unintentional slips are not held against them, emphasizing Allah's mercy and understanding, while reminding that true accountability lies in the conscious choices and intentions of the heart.

translation: For those who divorce their wives, they must wait for four months. Then if they return [to them], indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes a waiting period (iddah) of four months for husbands who have divorced their wives, serving as a time of reflection and potential reconciliation. It underscores Allah's attribute of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that returning to the marriage within this period is encouraged and that Allah is ready to forgive those who repent and seek to restore their relationship.

translation: And if they have decided upon divorce, then indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that when individuals resolve to end their marriage, Allah, being all-hearing and all-knowing, is fully aware of their intentions, feelings, and circumstances. It serves as a reminder that such a serious decision is not hidden from divine scrutiny, encouraging believers to act with consciousness of God's presence and justice in matters of separation.

translation: And those who are divorced shall wait for themselves for three menstrual cycles, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have the right of returning them during that time if they intend reconciliation. And the wives have rights similar to those against them in kindness, and men have a degree over them. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the waiting period ('iddah) for divorced women; it serves as a time to ascertain whether the woman is pregnant, reflecting the sanctity of lineage and the acknowledgment of Allah's creation. This period also provides an opportunity for reconciliation between spouses. The verse highlights a balanced relationship of rights and responsibilities between men and women, recognizing men's degree over women as a form of responsibility rather than superiority. Ultimately, it affirms that Allah's wisdom and might govern these laws, underscoring their divine origin and just nature.

translation: Divorce is permitted twice, then either retain [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with kindness. It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she redeems herself with. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and seriousness of the marital bond and prescribes the process for divorce with strict limits to prevent injustice. It underscores that divorce should not be taken lightly and that once a husband divorces his wife twice, reconciliation should either be firmly maintained or the marriage ended amicably. It also forbids the husband from reclaiming any gifts given to the wife unless there is a genuine concern that both parties cannot uphold Allah’s prescribed boundaries, reflecting justice and compassion in dealing with family matters.

translation: So if he divorces her, she is not lawful for him afterward until she marries another husband. Then if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other, provided they believe they can uphold the limits set by Allah. And those are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and seriousness of the marital bond established through divorce and remarriage. It sets a legal and moral boundary to prevent the casual breaking and remaking of marital ties, thereby aiming to uphold social stability and respect within family structures. The allowance for reconciliation after a second divorce, contingent upon the sincere intention to honor Allah's commands, underscores the importance of responsibility and moral accountability in relationships, reinforcing that divine boundaries are not arbitrary limits but protections designed for the benefit of individuals and society.

translation: And when you divorce women and their prescribed term (iddah) comes to an end, either retain them in kindness or release them in kindness. Do not hold them back to cause harm, that you may transgress. Whoever does that has wronged himself. Do not take Allah's verses as a jest, and remember the favor of Allah upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, admonishing you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to treat their wives with kindness and justice during and after divorce. It emphasizes that one should not use the waiting period as a means to cause harm or injustice, nor should divine guidance be taken lightly or mocked. The verse calls for mindfulness of Allah's blessings and commandments, encouraging respect, fairness, and consciousness of God's omniscience in all actions.

translation: And when you divorce women and their term [of waiting] has come to an end, do not prevent them from remarrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves in a fair manner. That is advised to whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day. That is purer for you and cleaner. And Allah knows while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse teaches that when a woman’s waiting period after divorce ends, it is not right to hinder her from remarrying her former husband if they both consent with fairness. This principle promotes mercy and mutual agreement in relationships, emphasizing respect for individual choice and preventing unnecessary hardship. The guidance is rooted in faith, purity, and the divine wisdom beyond human understanding, encouraging believers to act with kindness, fairness, and awareness of God's knowledge.

translation: Mothers shall nurse their children for two full years, for those who wish to complete the nursing period; and the father shall provide for their food and clothing in a just manner. No soul is burdened beyond its capacity. No mother shall be harmed because of her child, nor shall the child be harmed because of the mother. And similarly for the heirs. But if both desire weaning, by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by a substitute, there is no blame upon you, provided you pay what you offered in a fair manner. And fear Allah and know that He is aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the balanced rights and responsibilities in the process of child-rearing and nursing, emphasizing mutual consent, fairness, and compassion. It acknowledges the physical and financial capacities of individuals, ensuring no one is burdened beyond their means. It also establishes that the wellbeing of both mother and child must be protected without causing harm to either party. The permission to wean early or to use a wet nurse—with clear, just arrangements—reflects Islam's practical approach to family matters grounded in mutual agreement and respect. Ultimately, it calls for consciousness of Allah's oversight in all actions, encouraging ethical conduct and adherence to divine guidance in our responsibilities.

translation: And those among you who die and leave behind wives, they [the wives] shall wait for themselves four months and ten days. And when their term has expired, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves in a lawful manner. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs on the period of waiting (iddah) that widows must observe before they may remarry. The specified duration, four months and ten days, is decreed to ensure clarity concerning lineage and emotional readiness. It highlights a period marked by respect, reflection, and legal preservation of rights. The verse also emphasizes that within this period, women have the right to choose what is lawful for them to do with their own selves, free from societal restrictions, underscoring respect for their autonomy. Finally, it reminds that God is fully cognizant of all actions, reinforcing accountability.

translation: There is no blame upon you for that to which you consented concerning the proposal to women or for what you concealed within yourselves. Allah knows that you will remember them. But do not promise them secretly except the saying of what is right. And do not determine to marry them until the term prescribed by Allah has come to an end. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and transparency in the intentions and dealings regarding marriage proposals. It highlights that concealing one's feelings or intentions internally is understood by Allah, who knows what is in the hearts. However, secret promises must be honorable and truthful, and formalizing the marriage should not be hastened before the prescribed waiting period (iddah) expires. It teaches believers to be mindful of their inner thoughts and external actions, to avoid deception and to trust in Allah's knowledge and forgiveness, encouraging them to act with patience, integrity, and reverence toward God.

translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before touching them or assigning them an obligation. And give them their due compensation according to what is acceptable—the wealthy according to his capability and the poor according to his capability—a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse establishes principles of justice and kindness in the event of divorce, emphasizing that a husband should provide appropriate compensation to his wife even if the marriage was not consummated. It promotes equitable treatment by commanding that the amount given should be based on one's financial means, ensuring that obligations are fair and within one's capacity. The verse encourages moral responsibility and benevolence in upholding rights during the dissolution of marriage.

translation: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already assigned for them an obligation, then half of what you assigned is due, unless they forgive or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives. And forgiveness is closer to piety. And do not forget graciousness between you. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and mercy in the treatment of women in the context of divorce. It advocates for a fair financial settlement even if the marriage was not consummated, ensuring women's rights are protected. The encouragement towards forgiveness highlights the virtue of compassion and self-restraint, recommending it as an act closer to God-consciousness (taqwa). Furthermore, the admonition not to forget the kindness and favors that existed between spouses serves as a reminder to maintain respect and decency despite the separation.

translation: Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah, devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistently observing all the prescribed prayers, with special attention to the 'middle prayer,' which many scholars interpret as the most significant prayer in the day. It calls believers to perform their prayers with full devotion and humility, demonstrating submission and consciousness of Allah in their worship.

translation: So if you fear (disobedience or fallibility), then send an emancipated slave, or a fasting person, or give charity. But when you are secure, then remember Allah as He has taught you what you did not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following prescribed expiations faithfully and encourages the continuous remembrance of Allah, especially when one is in a state of security. It underlines that learning and spiritual growth are a continuous process, and that one should be mindful of obligations and duties learned through divine guidance, even after initial ignorance.

translation: And those of you who die and leave behind wives, bequeath to your wives a maintenance for a year without causing them to leave. But if they leave, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of reasonable things. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's wisdom and compassion in regulating the rights and duties between spouses after the death of a husband. It ensures that the widow is maintained for a full year as a fair period of mourning and adjustment, reflecting respect and care. At the same time, it allows flexibility by not forbidding her from leaving the marital home if she chooses, emphasizing that such decisions should be met without blame if they are reasonable and well-intended. This balance upholds justice, kindness, and dignity in sensitive personal circumstances.

translation: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility to provide for divorced women in a manner that is just and respectful. It underscores the principle that those who are conscious of God (the righteous) must honor their obligations towards divorced women, ensuring their well-being without injustice or hardship.

translation: Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah reveals His signs in a clear manner to guide human understanding, inviting them to reflect and comprehend the wisdom and truths presented, thereby nurturing their faith and awareness.

translation: Have you not considered those who left their homes in multitudes, fearing death? Allah said to them, "Die," then He gave them life. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most people do not give thanks.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's supreme power over life and death, demonstrating that despite grave fears and dangers, He alone can grant life after death. It serves as a reminder of His mercy and favors upon humanity, urging people to recognize and be grateful for His blessings rather than neglecting to give thanks.

translation: And fight in the way of Allah and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving and struggling sincerely for the cause of Allah, with the awareness that Allah hears all supplications and observes all actions. It serves as a reminder that one’s efforts are never unnoticed by the Divine, encouraging believers to remain steadfast and conscious that their deeds, both hidden and apparent, are known to Allah, thus promoting sincerity and perseverance in their endeavors.

translation: Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allah who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to offer their wealth and deeds in the way of Allah, assuring them that whatever they give sincerely and selflessly will be greatly multiplied in reward. It emphasizes Allah's ultimate control over all resources and the final accountability that all will return to Him.

translation: Have you not seen the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Set for us a king, so we may fight in the way of Allah"? He said, "Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting was prescribed for you?" They said, "And why should we not fight in the way of Allah when we have been driven out of our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
