translation: But those two among you who commit it, punish them. Yet, if they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice balanced with mercy. It instructs the community to hold offenders accountable, but also stresses the significance of sincere repentance and reform. When individuals genuinely turn away from their wrongful acts and strive to correct themselves, they should be forgiven and left in peace, highlighting Allah's compassionate and forgiving nature.

translation: Indeed, repentance is only for Allah for those who do evil in ignorance then repent soon after. Those – Allah will forgive them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true repentance is an act towards Allah alone, and it is accepted when one commits wrongdoing out of ignorance, not with deliberate malice, and then sincerely turns back to Him promptly. It highlights Allah's mercy and willingness to forgive those who recognize their mistakes and seek His pardon, underscoring His attributes of complete knowledge and wisdom in dealing with human shortcomings.

translation: But repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere and timely repentance. It warns that repentance is not accepted if it is made insincerely at the moment of imminent death, or by those who die in disbelief. Hence, genuine reform and turning back to God must occur before the final moments, demonstrating a true change of heart rather than a last-minute attempt to escape punishment.

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take back part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of respect and kindness towards women, forbidding the practice of inheriting or claiming women against their will and cautioning against harsh treatment in an attempt to reclaim dowries or gifts. It acknowledges that marital relationships can face difficulties, but encourages patience and kindness, reminding believers that what they may dislike could ultimately bring about unforeseen goodness through God's wisdom.

translation: And if you intend to replace one wife with another and have given one of them a great amount (a hundred measures), do not take anything from it. Would you take it in injustice and manifest sin?
interpretation: This verse addresses the principle of fairness and respect in marital relationships. It warns against unjustly reclaiming the dower (mahr) given to a wife when seeking to replace her with another, emphasizing that such an act is both wrongful and sinful. The directive underscores the importance of honoring commitments and treating spouses with integrity, thereby preserving justice within the sanctity of marriage.

translation: And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers against unlawfully taking wealth or property from one another, especially after they have come together and established a serious agreement or trust. It underscores the sanctity of promises and mutual obligations, emphasizing that violating such covenants is unjust and disregards the trust and honor inherent in human relationships.

translation: And do not marry women whom your fathers married, except what has already passed; indeed, it was an immorality and hateful, and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse prohibits the marrying of women who were wed to one's fathers, highlighting that such a practice was considered morally reprehensible and detestable. The prohibition serves to maintain clear familial boundaries, to uphold social ethics, and to prevent the perpetuation of practices that were unjust and disruptive to the integrity of family structures.

translation: Prohibited to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, the daughters of your brothers, and the daughters of your sisters, and your mothers who nursed you, and your sisters through nursing, and the mothers of your wives, and your stepdaughters under your guardianship from your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage; but if you have not consummated with them, there is no sin upon you. And [prohibition of] the wives of your sons who are from your loins, and [prohibited to you are] that you combine between two sisters except what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the clear boundaries of prohibited marriage relations in Islamic law, emphasizing the sanctity of family ties and social order. By detailing the specific individuals whom one is forbidden to marry or have sexual relations with, it preserves the dignity and structure of family relationships and prevents moral confusion. The verse also shows that while certain relationships are strictly forbidden, there is mercy and forgiveness in Allah's law concerning unintentional violations, reflecting a balance between divine guidance and human circumstances.

translation: And [forbidden to you are] married women except those your right hands possess. [This is] the decree of Allah upon you. And lawful to you are [all others] beyond these, [provided] that you seek them [in marriage] with your property, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse. So for that [reason], give them their due compensation as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree after the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the boundaries related to relationships and marriage, emphasizing the sanctity and exclusivity of marital ties. It permits lawful relations with free women whom one lawfully marries, distinguishing them from those who are married and thus prohibited, except for those lawfully possessed as captives under certain circumstances. It further enjoins fairness and respecting obligations by mandating that men provide due compensation to women, which signifies the seriousness and responsibility entailed in marriage. The provision for mutual agreement beyond the obligatory dowry underlines the importance of consent and mutual respect, while affirming that Allah's laws are crafted with profound wisdom and comprehensive knowledge of human affairs.

translation: And if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with the believing women, then marry those that your right hands possess of believing girls. And Allah is most knowing of your faith; you are one from another. So marry them with the permission of their families and give them their due compensation in a proper manner, chaste women, not adulters nor those who take lovers. And when they are in a state of chastity, if they commit immorality, then half the punishment shall be upon them as is upon free chaste women. This is for those who fear hardship from you, but it is better for you to be patient. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the social realities and human limitations regarding marriage and justice with spouses, guiding believers to marry from among freed and chaste believing women if they fear injustice to others. It underscores the importance of permission, fairness, chastity, and proper treatment in marriage. The text also emphasizes restraint and patience, indicating that confronting one's appetites with justice is ideal, but recognizing human frailty, allowances are made within ethical boundaries. The extent of consequences for transgressions is balanced, and divine forgiveness and mercy remain overarching principles guiding human behavior.

translation: Allah wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you, and to accept your repentance. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse reveals that Allah's intention behind revealing guidance is to clarify the truth and lead humanity along the correct path, as exemplified by the experiences of previous generations. It emphasizes that through understanding these lessons, people are encouraged to repent and reform, highlighting Allah's encompassing knowledge and wisdom in guiding creation towards spiritual growth and rectification.

translation: And Allah wants to accept your repentance, but those who follow their desires want you to deviate greatly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and readiness of Allah to forgive and accept repentance from those who turn back to Him sincerely. At the same time, it warns that there are forces driven by mere desires which aim to lead people away from the straight path, causing them to deviate extensively from righteousness. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their intentions and remain steadfast in seeking Allah's forgiveness rather than succumbing to destructive temptations.

translation: Allah wants to lighten your difficulties; for man was created weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and understanding of human limitations. It acknowledges the inherent weakness in human nature and emphasizes that divine laws and commands are designed not to burden but to ease and accommodate human frailty, guiding believers toward a balanced and compassionate way of life.

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only [in lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves [or one another]. Indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and mutual agreement in financial dealings, prohibiting the unjust or deceitful acquisition of others' wealth. It also forbids self-harm or suicide, underscoring the sanctity of human life. Overall, the verse highlights Allah's mercy, encouraging believers to act with justice and compassion towards themselves and others.

translation: And whoever does that in aggression and injustice – then We will drive him into a Fire. And that, for Allah, is [always] easy.
interpretation: This verse warns that committing acts out of wrongful aggression and injustice will lead to severe consequences in the hereafter, emphasizing that divine retribution is certain and within Allah's power to enact effortlessly.

translation: If you avoid the great sins which you are forbidden from, We will forgive your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance (Paradise).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that repentance and refraining from major sins can lead to the forgiveness of smaller lapses. It reflects the mercy of Allah, encouraging believers to steer clear of major wrongdoing as a key to spiritual purification and ultimate acceptance into a dignified and honored state in the Hereafter.

translation: And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches us to accept the differences and diversity in blessings and abilities that Allah has distributed among people. It warns against envy and urges reliance on individual efforts while recognizing that ultimate provision comes from Allah's grace. The verse encourages seeking Allah's generosity through supplication, affirming His complete knowledge and control over all matters.

translation: And for everyone We have appointed heirs to what the parents and close relatives leave behind. And those with whom your oaths have been made – give them their due share. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine ordinance for the distribution of inheritance, emphasizing that rightful heirs must receive their due portions. It underscores the importance of fairness and justice in sharing the wealth left by deceased family members, while also acknowledging commitments made through oaths that also need to be honored with their rightful shares. Ultimately, it reminds believers that Allah is fully aware and cognizant of all actions, ensuring accountability and fairness in all dealings related to inheritance.

translation: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has given the one more strength than the other, and because they support them from their means. Therefore, the righteous women are devoutly obedient, and guard in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard. As for those from whom you fear disobedience, admonish them, forsake them in bed, and strike them. But if they obey you, seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.
interpretation: This verse establishes the responsibility and role of men as protectors and providers for women, highlighting a natural order and social structure designed by Allah based on differences in strength and provision. It emphasizes mutual rights and duties: righteous women are to be devoted and loyal, safeguarding the relationship and family integrity. In cases of serious marital discord, it prescribes a graduated approach to discipline aimed at reconciliation, with the ultimate aim of restoration and harmony. The verse underscores that any action taken should be just and not transgress boundaries, reminding that Allah's authority and greatness govern all relationships and that respect and care are paramount.

translation: And if you fear dissension between the two, send an arbiter from his people and an arbiter from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause it between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mediation and reconciliation in resolving conflicts, particularly within familial relationships such as marriage. It recognizes human differences and disputes but encourages seeking help through impartial and wise representatives from each party's community to facilitate understanding and harmony. The verse highlights that genuine efforts toward reconciliation, guided by fairness and sincere intention, receive Allah's support, demonstrating His knowledge and involvement in human affairs.

translation: And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and show kindness to parents, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the distant neighbor, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are self-deluding and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive ethical framework in Islam that combines absolute monotheism with social justice and interpersonal kindness. It teaches that true worship involves not just devotion to God alone but also expressing that devotion through benevolence towards a broad community encompassing family, relatives, vulnerable groups, neighbors, companions, travelers, and even servants. The verse further warns against arrogance and pride, highlighting that such traits are displeasing to God. Thus, sincere faith is inseparable from humility and active compassion towards others.

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon others stinginess, and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral degeneration that arises from miserliness, especially when combined with the act of promoting such behavior in others. Concealing the blessings bestowed by Allah reflects ingratitude and dishonesty, which distances individuals from the path of righteousness. Furthermore, it serves as a warning that such attitudes are not only personally detrimental but also attract severe consequences in the hereafter, as Allah has prepared a humiliating punishment for those who persist in disbelief and such unjust behavior.

translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people and do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day. And whoever is an ally of Satan, then indeed, Satan is an evil companion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who perform acts of charity not out of genuine faith or sincerity, but merely to gain praise and recognition from others. Such actions lack true spiritual merit because they are not rooted in belief in God and the hereafter. Associating oneself with Satan in this way signifies being led astray by insincere motives, resulting in harmful companionship and ultimate failure.

translation: And what is wrong with them that they should believe in Allah and the Last Day and spend out of what Allah has provided for them? And Allah is Knowing of them.
interpretation: This verse challenges the hesitance or refusal of some to believe in Allah and the Last Day, as well as to give charity from their provisions. It implies that faith and generosity are natural and rightful acts, and questions the obstacles in their hearts preventing them from embracing these virtues. Moreover, it emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their inner dispositions and circumstances, whether they are sincere or insincere.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an atom, but if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse conveys the perfect justice and mercy of Allah, emphasizing that no deed, no matter how small, is overlooked or unjustly treated. Even the tiniest act, whether good or bad, is accounted for, and good deeds are rewarded manifold. It reassures believers that every sincere effort is valued and that Allah’s generosity exceeds human expectations in rewarding righteousness.

translation: So how [terrible] will be the Day when We will bring from every nation a witness and We will bring you as a witness against these people?
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the Day of Judgment when Allah will bring forth a witness from every nation who will testify to the deeds of their people, and Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will bear witness over his own community. It signifies the comprehensive nature of the final accountability, highlighting that no one will be exempt from testimony, and it emphasizes the responsibility that comes with leadership and guidance.

translation: On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish the earth were leveled with them, and they will not hide any statement from Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the intense regret and hopelessness that will overwhelm those who rejected faith and disobeyed the Messenger on the Day of Judgment. Their desire for the earth to be flat against them reflects their wish to escape the inevitable divine reckoning, highlighting the severity of their punishment and the impossibility of evading God's justice on that day.

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor in a state of major impurity, except while passing through, until you have washed; and if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from relieving himself or you have touched women and you do not find water, then perform tayammum with clean earth and wipe your faces and hands. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of approaching prayer in a state of full awareness and physical purity, highlighting that sincere and conscious worship requires both mental clarity and ritual cleanliness. It teaches patience and adaptability by allowing exceptions in cases of illness, travel, or lack of water, and permits symbolic purification (tayammum) to maintain the dignity of worship. Ultimately, it underscores that God's mercy and forgiveness complement strict observance, encouraging believers to balance discipline with compassion in their spiritual practices.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who buy error [to mislead] and wish that you would lose the way?
interpretation: This verse highlights the misuse of knowledge and scripture by certain individuals who, despite being granted guidance, deliberately choose to promote misguidance. It serves as a warning about the dangers of knowingly distorting truth to lead others astray and emphasizes the importance of sincerity and integrity in conveying divine teachings.

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies; and sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes reliance on Allah alone for protection and support against one's enemies. It reassures believers that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything about their adversaries, and that placing trust in Him is sufficient for victory and aid, highlighting His role as the ultimate protector and helper in all circumstances.

translation: Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, "We hear and disobey," and "Hear but be not heard," and "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said, "We hear and obey" and "Observe us," it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe only a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the manipulation and intentional distortion of divine texts and messages by certain individuals to serve their own interests, demonstrating a failure to sincerely submit to God's guidance. It warns against corrupting the intended meanings of revelation and shows that true faith requires openness, obedience, and humility rather than defiance and twisting of words.

translation: O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have revealed, confirming that which is with you, before We erase faces and turn them backward or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers. And the command of Allah is always executed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder to the People of the Scripture to accept and believe in the final revelation of the Qur'an, which confirms and completes their previous scriptures. It warns against stubbornness and rejection, for those who persist in disbelief risk severe consequences: their honor and status may be obliterated, symbolized by 'erasing faces' and turning them backward, or they may be cursed as the Sabbath-breakers were punished in the past. Ultimately, the divine decree is certain and unstoppable, emphasizing the importance of sincere faith and submission before it is too late.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him (shirk), but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah and declares that associating partners with Him (shirk) is the gravest sin which Allah does not forgive if one dies upon it. However, Allah's mercy extends to all other sins and He forgives whom He wills. It serves as a stern warning against idolatry and polytheism, underscoring the importance of monotheism in Islam.

translation: Have you not considered those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even as much as the thread of a date seed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true purity and righteousness come not from self-proclamation or arrogance, but solely by Allah's will and decree. It warns against self-righteousness and emphasizes that divine purification is a gracious act bestowed upon those whom Allah chooses, underscoring His supreme justice and wisdom.

translation: See how they invent lies against Allah. And sufficient is that as a clear sin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of falsely attributing lies to Allah, emphasizing that fabrications against the Divine are not mere errors but grave sins with clear consequences, serving as a warning against such deception and a reminder of the sanctity of truth in matters of faith.

translation: Do you not see those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in superstition and false deities and say to those who disbelieve, "These are more rightly guided than the believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the phenomenon where some people, despite having received the truth through revelation, adopt false beliefs like superstition (al-jibt) and idolatry (al-taghoot). They then arrogantly claim that disbelievers who reject divine guidance are more rightly guided than the true believers. This reflects a misguided arrogance and denial of the clear signs of guidance, cautioning against following conjecture and rejecting authentic faith.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses - you will not find for him any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of divine curse, indicating that those whom Allah has condemned are utterly forsaken and devoid of any protector or supporter. It underlines the absolute power of God's judgment and the futility of seeking aid against His decrees.

translation: Or do they have a share of dominion? Then if they were given dominion, they would not give the people even a little.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the nature of those who unjustly seek power. It highlights their unwillingness to share authority or resources fairly, illustrating that if given control, they would be miserly and oppressive, denying people their rightful due. It serves as a critique of those who grasp for dominance without consideration for justice or generosity.

translation: Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and granted them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse highlights that envy over divine blessings is misplaced, reminding that God's favors are determined by His wisdom. The mention of the family of Abraham illustrates that their elevated status, knowledge, and dominion were granted by God, emphasizing the importance of gratitude over envy and that true worth comes from God's grace.

translation: Among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who turn away from it. And Hellfire is sufficient as a blazing flame.
interpretation: This verse highlights the differing responses people have towards the message of the Qur'an; some embrace faith, while others reject it. It warns that for those who refuse to believe, Hellfire is an adequate and severe consequence, emphasizing the reality and seriousness of divine punishment for disbelief.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe consequences of rejecting God's signs and messages. The continual renewal of the skin symbolizes an unending, intense suffering as a result of persistent disobedience. It emphasizes that God's justice is precise and unyielding, and He administers punishment wisely, proportionate to one's disbelief and rejection.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to shade, ample and ever-present.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal reward for those who combine faith with righteous action. It assures believers that their perseverance in faith and good deeds leads to a perpetual, blissful existence in Paradise, where they enjoy pure companionship and divine protection. The imagery conveys not only physical comfort but spiritual fulfillment and the continuous pleasure of God's grace.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of trust and justice in human interactions. It commands believers to fulfill their responsibilities and obligations honestly and to ensure fairness and equity when making judgments. The reminder that Allah is Hearing and Seeing serves to reinforce accountability, encouraging individuals to act with integrity even when no one else is observing.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best [way] and best in result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and obedience within the community of believers. It instructs Muslims to submit to the commands of Allah, follow the guidance of the Prophet, and respect the leaders appointed among them. In case of disputes, the verse advises returning to the foundational sources of Islamic law and guidance—the Qur'an and the Sunnah—to resolve differences. This reflects the principle that ultimate authority rests with divine revelation, and adherence to it ensures the best outcomes for the community both in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you, and what was revealed before you, yet they wish to arbitrate by Taghut, though they were commanded to disbelieve in it? And Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse warns against the hypocrisy of those who profess faith in the divine revelations yet resort to false authorities or unjust systems ('Taghut') for judgment, thereby contradicting the command to reject such entities. It highlights how Satan exploits this contradiction to mislead them far from true guidance, emphasizing the importance of sincere adherence to God's law and avoiding reliance on corrupt or unholy systems.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of hypocrites who deliberately avoid following divine guidance and the Messenger's teachings, demonstrating their insincerity and resistance to the truth despite being addressed directly. Their turning away signifies a rejection rooted not in ignorance but in a calculated attempt to obstruct the path of guidance.

translation: So how [will it be] when a disaster strikes them because of what their own hands have sent ahead, and then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good and reconciliation."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to deny responsibility for the consequences of one's own actions, even when faced with hardship caused by those actions. It serves as a reminder that one's deeds, whether good or bad, lead to corresponding outcomes, and merely professing good intentions or seeking to reconcile without genuine repentance does not absolve one from accountability.

translation: Those are the ones of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them, admonish them, and say to them words of profound wisdom.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God's knowledge encompasses the innermost motives and feelings of people, and that human efforts to guide others should be tempered with understanding and compassion. When faced with those whose hearts conceal harmful intent or disbelief, one is advised to turn away from them without harshness, to offer gentle admonishment, and to communicate with wisdom and eloquence, thereby maintaining dignity and effectiveness in guidance.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of Repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine purpose behind sending messengers: to guide people towards obedience to God. It highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness when one errs and stresses that turning sincerely to God, through both personal repentance and the intercession of the Messenger, opens the door to divine mercy and acceptance, reassuring that God's forgiveness is ever available to those who humbly seek it.

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort about that which you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith includes absolute acceptance of divine judgment through the Prophet. It highlights the believer's commitment to submit wholeheartedly to Allah's decrees without hesitation or internal resistance, reflecting sincere trust and obedience to God's guidance as conveyed by His Messenger.

translation: And if We had ordained for them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done it except a few of them. But if they had done what they were admonished to do, it would have been better for them and a firmer position [for them in faith].
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the depth of human resistance to extreme commands even when they come from divine authority, highlighting that true commitment is not mere superficial compliance but sincere, heartfelt obedience. It teaches that genuine submission to God's guidance is difficult but ultimately beneficial, leading to stronger faith and better outcomes, whereas half-heartedness leads to failure and weakness.

translation: And when We give them from Us a great reward,
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's generosity in bestowing great rewards upon His servants. It emphasizes that the blessings and rewards come directly from Allah's bounty and are of immense significance, encouraging believers to recognize and appreciate God's kindness and generosity.

translation: And We guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine guidance bestowed upon individuals or communities, leading them away from misguidance and toward a clear, upright way of living that aligns with God's commands, ensuring spiritual and moral clarity in their journey of life.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor: the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true obedience to Allah and His Messenger elevates a person to the highest spiritual company—the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous—signifying that following divine guidance aligns one with the most honored and purer souls, thereby granting one an exemplary spiritual rank and companionship.

translation: That is the bounty of Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Knower.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings and favors ultimately come from Allah alone, and He is fully aware of everything. It serves as a reminder to recognize and be grateful for Allah's grace, acknowledging His complete knowledge and authority over all matters.

translation: O you who have believed, take your precaution and either go forth in groups or go forth all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of preparedness and unity among believers when facing challenges or engaging in collective action. It advises them to be cautious and strategic, either sending a contingent with steadfastness or mobilizing as a whole, highlighting the need for careful planning and solidarity to achieve strength and success.

translation: And indeed, among you are those who will delay, and when a disaster strikes you, they say, 'Indeed, Allah has favored me that I was not present with them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights a human tendency to dissociate from communal responsibility in times of hardship. It critiques those who, upon facing collective suffering, take solace in their absence rather than empathize or assist. It serves as a reminder to uphold solidarity and shared accountability among the community rather than seeking personal relief through isolation.

translation: And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, they say, "Did He not forbid us from associating with him?" But if evil afflicts you, they speak of the former as if they were strangers to the latter. Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward; this is not but a message for the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and hypocrisy of certain people who, when they see others receiving blessings from Allah, reject their relationship and deny affection between them and those favored. Yet, when adversity strikes, they wish to be among them to succeed greatly. This teaches us about human fickleness and warns against envy and disunity, emphasizing reliance on divine guidance rather than human approval or disapproval.

translation: So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And whoever fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory - We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of sincere sacrifice and struggle for the sake of Allah, emphasizing that true believers are those who prioritize their eternal success over fleeting worldly gains. It assures that anyone who engages in such a righteous struggle, whether they are martyred or victorious, will be generously rewarded by Allah, reinforcing the concept of divine justice and compassion towards those who strive with pure intentions.

translation: And why do you not fight in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper?"
interpretation: This verse calls on believers to actively support and defend those who are oppressed and wronged, emphasizing that faith requires not only spiritual devotion but also practical action to uphold justice. It highlights the importance of solidarity with the vulnerable and the moral responsibility to combat tyranny and oppression, trusting in God's help and guidance to overcome adversity.

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut (tyranny and false gods). So, fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and ideological battle that believers engage in, standing firm for truth and justice under Allah's guidance, while those who reject faith support falsehood and oppression. It encourages the faithful to oppose the allies of evil with determination, reassuring them that the schemes of Satan and his supporters are ultimately futile and weak.

translation: Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands [from fighting] and establish prayer and give zakah"? But then when fighting was prescribed for them, at once a party of them feared men as they fear Allah or even more. They said, "Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? Would You delay it for us for a short time?" Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears Allah; and you will not be wronged, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a spiritual truth: the real challenge in faith is not merely in performing acts of worship or giving charity, but in facing trials and obligations that test one's trust in God, such as combat when prescribed. Many may fear people and worldly consequences more than they fear God, leading to reluctance. However, the verse reminds believers that the fleeting nature of worldly life pales in comparison to the eternal goodness of the Hereafter, which awaits those who truly fear and trust Allah. Therefore, one should prioritize fear of God over fear of people, embracing divine decrees with patience and faith.

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction. And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah;" but if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All [things] are from Allah." So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and universality of death, underscoring that no matter how secure or protected one may think they are, mortality is unavoidable as it is decreed by Allah. It also highlights human tendencies to attribute blessings to divine will but blame others or circumstances for misfortunes, urging a recognition that all events, good or bad, ultimately come from Allah alone. This recognition calls for humility and understanding of divine wisdom beyond superficial judgments.

translation: Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you, [O Muhammad], to the people as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability; the blessings and successes one experiences are from Allah's grace, while the misfortunes or wrongdoings stem from one's own actions or choices. It also reinforces the Prophet's role as a messenger sent to guide humanity, with Allah as the ultimate witness to all matters, affirming His justice and oversight.

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but those who turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that obedience to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is inherently obedience to Allah, as the Prophet conveys Allah's guidance to mankind. Conversely, those who reject or turn away from the Prophet's message are responsible for their own choices, as the Prophet is not a guardian over them to enforce belief but a warner and messenger.

translation: And they say, “We obey,” but when they leave you, a group of them plot other than what you say. But Allah records what they plan by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity of some who verbally express obedience yet secretly conspire against the Prophet's directives. It teaches that Allah is fully aware of hidden plots and intentions, thus the Prophet is instructed to disengage from such deceitful individuals and place his trust entirely in Allah's wisdom and protection, affirming that reliance on God suffices against all adversities.

translation: Do they not then ponder on the Quran? Had it been from any other than Allah, they would surely have found therein much discrepancy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and perfect consistency of the Quran, urging people to reflect deeply on its content. The absence of contradictions serves as evidence of its authenticity and the truthfulness of its message, distinguishing it from human-made works prone to errors and inconsistencies.

translation: And when a matter of security or fear comes to them, they spread it around; but if they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, then those who can draw correct conclusions from them would have known about it. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of consulting divinely guided authority in times of uncertainty or crisis, rather than hastily spreading information that may cause confusion or harm. It implies that true understanding and wisdom come from careful deliberation under the guidance of the Prophet and responsible leaders, and without Allah's mercy, people are prone to following misguided and harmful influences.

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers. Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is the most severe in punishment and most severe in imposing retribution.
interpretation: This verse instructs those who are capable to engage in struggle or defense for the sake of Allah, emphasizing that each person is accountable only for their own actions, not for the actions of others. It also calls for motivating and encouraging the believers, fostering unity and resolve among them. The verse highlights that through collective effort and faith, Allah may lessen the power or harm inflicted by the disbelievers. It underscores that Allah's punishment is severe and just, reminding believers of accountability and the ultimate justice that prevails.

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a share of it. And Allah is, over all things, a Keeper.
interpretation: This verse teaches that individuals are responsible for their actions, including the consequences of their intercession for others. If one pleads or mediates on behalf of something good, they will share in its reward; if they support something harmful, they share in its blame. It highlights the principle of accountability in interpersonal relationships and ensures that one cannot absolve themselves from the outcomes of their influence. Moreover, it reminds us that Allah is the ultimate overseer and judge of all affairs, maintaining justice across all matters.

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet with one better than it or return it; indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle of reciprocation and kindness in social interactions. It encourages believers to respond to greetings with equal or better greetings, fostering goodwill and harmony within the community. The reminder that Allah is watchful over all actions underscores the importance of sincere and considerate behavior, as every deed is accounted for by Him.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah as the sole deity worthy of worship and the ultimate truth in all existence. It assures believers that resurrection and the gathering of all humankind for accountability on the Day of Judgment is certain and free from any doubt, underscoring Allah's unmatched truthfulness and reliability in His promises.

translation: So why are you two groups concerning the hypocrites? And Allah has made them fall back because of what they earned. Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has led astray? And he whom Allah leads astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance and misguidance are ultimately in the hands of Allah. It cautions against division or excessive concern over hypocrites, as their fate is a result of their own actions and Allah's decree. It also warns that attempting to guide those whom Allah has purposefully allowed to stray is futile, highlighting the limits of human influence when divine will is at play.

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and do not take from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hostility of disbelievers towards the believers, wishing they would abandon their faith to become equal in disbelief. It instructs believers to avoid forming close bonds with such adversaries unless they genuinely commit to the path of God by migrating for His cause. If these individuals persist in hostility, believers are commanded to treat them as enemies wherever encountered, emphasizing the severe consequences of persistent opposition to the faith. This reflects the seriousness of allegiance in the context of faith and the necessity to safeguard the community from forces that actively oppose it.

translation: Except for those who are bound by a treaty between you and them, or those whose hearts prevent them from fighting you or fighting their own people. And if Allah had willed, He could have made them overpower you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you any way against them.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the complexities of human relationships and loyalties, recognizing that not everyone who refrains from engaging in conflict with the believers does so out of weakness or fear; some have sincere reasons, such as existing treaties or inner conflicts of loyalty. It teaches that God's will encompasses all situations, and human actions occur within His knowledge and allowance. Hence, if some avoid conflict and seek peace, believers are instructed not to force aggression upon them but to accept peaceful coexistence, emphasizing justice, respect for agreements, and restraint in conflict.

translation: You will find others who want to secure you and their own people. Whenever they are returned to temptation, they fall into it. So if they do not withdraw from you or offer you peace, or restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And those are the ones We have given you clear authority over.
interpretation: This verse addresses the stance towards those who consistently engage in hostility and do not cease their aggression or offer peace. It grants believers clear authority to defend themselves proactively against persistent enemies who refuse peaceful resolution, emphasizing the importance of security and the rejection of ongoing conflict from hostile parties.

translation: It is not for a believer to kill another believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay compensation to the deceased's family unless they remit it. But if the victim belonged to an enemy nation while you are at war with them, then freeing a believing slave is obligatory. And if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty, then compensation must be paid to his family and a believing slave freed. But if one is unable, then fasting for two consecutive months as a repentance to Allah. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life, especially among the faithful, by prescribing strict measures and penance for those who kill unintentionally. The prescribed acts—freeing a believing slave, paying compensation, or fasting—serve as means to atone for the unintended loss of life and to restore social harmony. The differentiation based on the victim's relationship (friend, enemy, or treaty-bound) reflects a justice system sensitive to context and the maintenance of social contracts. Ultimately, it teaches believers the gravity of taking life, the importance of sincere repentance, and upholds the wisdom and knowledge of Allah in legislating just and merciful laws.

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah is angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of human life, especially that of a believer, in Islam. It conveys that deliberately taking the life of a believer is a grievous sin with severe consequences, not only in the worldly realm but also in the hereafter. The punishment described highlights the serious moral and spiritual breach, indicating that such an act incurs Allah's wrath, curse, and a lasting punishment in Hell, reflecting the gravity of violating the trust and sanctity that Islam places on life.

translation: O you who have believed, when you are struck in the cause of Allah, make sure to verify [the facts], and do not say to anyone who gives you [a greeting of] peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of worldly life; for with Allah are many gains. Thus, you were before; then Allah conferred His favor upon you, so be clear-minded. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to exercise patience and discernment during conflict, urging them not to hastily judge or reject those who claim faith simply because they seek peace or worldly benefits. It emphasizes that true faith and allegiance are known to Allah alone, and believers should avoid causing division or wrongful accusations motivated by material desires, recognizing that Allah is fully aware of all intentions and actions.

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]—except those who are disabled—and the mujahideen [striving] in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred the mujahideen through their wealth and their lives over those who remain at home by a great degree. And to all, Allah has promised the best [reward]. Yet Allah has preferred the mujahideen over those who remain at home with a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the believers who actively struggle in the path of Allah using their resources and lives, and those who remain behind, except for those who are genuinely unable to participate due to valid obstacles. The emphasis is on the superior rank and reward granted by Allah to those who sacrifice and strive actively for righteousness and defending the faith. However, Allah's mercy ensures that all believers are promised goodness, reflecting both justice and generosity in rewarding efforts according to one's capability.

translation: Degrees [of reward] from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness of Allah's mercy and generosity, assuring believers that He bestows varying levels of reward, along with forgiveness and mercy. It reminds us that no matter the shortcomings, Allah's compassion encompasses all, encouraging hope and reliance on His kindness.

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsibility of individuals to seek better circumstances when faced with oppression or hardship. It teaches that while injustice may afflict people, they are encouraged to take positive action, such as migrating to places of safety or opportunity. Ignoring this obligation and remaining passive despite available alternatives is a form of self-oppression, for which accountability before Allah is emphasized in the Hereafter.

translation: Except for the weak among men, women, and children who have no means or guidance.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's compassion and justice by exempting those who are genuinely vulnerable—such as the weak, women, and children—from accountability when they lack the capacity or means to act rightly or find guidance. It emphasizes that responsibility in faith is related to one's ability and understanding, recognizing human limitations and ensuring that judgment is equitable and merciful.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah may forgive, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless capacity to forgive even those who have erred, emphasizing that sincere repentance and Allah’s mercy can erase past mistakes. It reassures believers that no matter the seriousness of their faults, Allah’s forgiveness and compassion are always accessible to those who seek it sincerely.

translation: And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has surely fallen upon Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that committing themselves to sacrifice, including migration for the sake of Allah, leads to abundant opportunities and divine support. It emphasizes that even if one does not reach the intended destination or goal due to death, their sincere intention and effort secure them Allah's reward and forgiveness, highlighting Allah's encompassing mercy regardless of worldly outcomes.

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the difficulties faced by believers when traveling, especially the risk of harm from hostile disbelievers. It permits the shortening of prayers as a concession to ease the burden during such journeys, emphasizing God's mercy and understanding of human circumstances, while also reminding believers of the ongoing enmity from disbelievers and the need to be cautious and steadfast.

translation: And when you are among them and lead the prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you and take their arms; then when they prostrate, let them be behind you. And let another group come forward who have not yet prayed and pray with you, taking precaution and their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you neglect your arms and your baggage so they could come down upon you in one single assault. But there is no blame upon you if you are ill or on a journey and do not find arms. And take precaution; indeed, Allah has prepared a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse instructs on maintaining vigilance and readiness even during acts of worship such as prayer, especially in environments where threats from disbelievers exist. The arrangement of worshippers with arms during prayer emphasizes the importance of being prepared for defense without neglecting spiritual duties. It also acknowledges situations of hardship, such as illness or travel, allowing leniency regarding carrying arms, while still urging caution. The verse reflects the balanced approach Islam enjoins between devotion and prudence, assuring believers that Allah has prepared a severe punishment for those who harbor hostility and seek to harm the faithful.

translation: So when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on your sides. But when you become secure, establish prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuous remembrance of Allah beyond the formalities of prayer, encouraging believers to maintain consciousness of God in all states—standing, sitting, and lying down. It also highlights the importance of performing the prescribed prayers punctually, showing discipline and dedication as these prayers are a fixed obligation upon the believers that structure their spiritual life.

translation: And do not lose heart in seeking the cause of the people. If you suffer pain, then indeed they suffer pain as you suffer. And you hope from Allah what they do not hope for. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages perseverance and patience in the face of adversity during efforts to guide and help others. It reminds believers that trials and hardships are part of the process, shared by both themselves and those they seek to support or invite to faith. The hope placed upon Allah's mercy and aid, which others might not expect or believe in, serves as a source of strength. The verse reassures that Allah’s knowledge and wisdom encompass all affairs, guiding the believer to trust in divine justice and planning despite challenges.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be a disputant for the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an as a guide for just judgment. It instructs the Prophet, and by extension all judges and leaders, to rule with fairness and adherence to God's guidance, avoiding bias or alliance with those who betray trust. It underscores the importance of integrity and justice when making decisions that affect others.

translation: And seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches us the importance of turning to Allah in repentance and seeking His forgiveness, reassuring believers that no matter the magnitude of their sins, Allah's mercy and forgiveness are vast and always accessible to those who sincerely repent.

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.
interpretation: This verse advises against defending or supporting those who engage in self-destructive wrongdoing, emphasizing that such betrayal is detestable in the sight of Allah. It highlights that aligning oneself with injustice or deceitful actions harms both the individual and the community, and that sincere morality requires distancing oneself from enabling or excusing such behavior.

translation: They seek to deceive the people, but they cannot deceive Allah, for He is with them when they spend the night devising words that displease Him. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse warns that while people may try to hide their intentions and actions from others, they are ultimately unable to conceal anything from Allah, who is ever-aware and fully encompassing of their deeds; it emphasizes the futility of secret transgressions and the certainty of divine knowledge and judgment.

translation: Here you are, those who argued on their behalf in the worldly life; so who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection? Or who will be a guardian over them?
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the futility and ineffectiveness of defending falsehood or injustice in this worldly life, emphasizing that ultimate judgment and accountability rest with Allah alone on the Day of Judgment. No human argument or intercession can alter divine judgment, underscoring the importance of acting righteously and being mindful of one's actions before facing the ultimate accountability.

translation: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from Allah will find that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless mercy and readiness to forgive those who recognize their wrongdoings and sincerely turn back to Him in repentance, highlighting that no matter the severity of one's sins, the door to forgiveness remains open for those who seek it with humility.

translation: And whoever earns a sin, only earns it against himself; and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility for one's actions, indicating that any sin committed affects only the individual who commits it, not others. It also reassures that Allah, with His perfect knowledge and wisdom, is fully aware of all deeds and the circumstances surrounding them, ensuring ultimate justice.

translation: And whoever earns a sin or a fault and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a falsehood and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse warns against the grave injustice of blaming an innocent person for a sin one has committed. It highlights how wrongful accusation compounds the original sin, turning it into a clear and aggravated wrongdoing. The verse teaches the importance of honesty and fairness, emphasizing that taking responsibility for one's own actions is crucial, and falsely accusing others leads to greater harm and spiritual corruption.

translation: And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group among them would have intended to mislead you; but they cause no harm except to themselves, and they do not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy and grace of Allah upon the Prophet, which protects him from the plots and schemes of those who seek to misguide him. It reminds us that the harm intended by opponents ultimately rebounds upon themselves and cannot truly affect the Prophet ordained by Allah. Furthermore, the verse emphasizes that the knowledge and wisdom bestowed upon the Prophet are divine gifts, enabling guidance beyond human capacity. This assures believers that divine support shields the truth and those chosen to convey it, underscoring that any adversity is surmountable through Allah's favor.

translation: There is no good in much of their private conversation except for those who enjoin charity or that which is right or reconciliation among people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah - We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights that private discussions are generally not beneficial unless they are aimed at promoting good deeds such as encouraging charity, advocating righteousness, or mediating peace between people. The genuine intention behind such actions should be seeking Allah's approval, and those who do so sincerely will be greatly rewarded by Allah. This serves as guidance to align one's speech and gatherings with positive and constructive purposes rooted in sincere faith.

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows a path other than that of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the guidance brought by the Prophet Muhammad once it becomes clear. It warns against opposing his teachings and choosing a path contrary to that of the true believers, highlighting that such rejection leads to severe consequences both in this life and the Hereafter. The verse serves as a caution that deviation from the prophetic guidance after recognizing it is a grave matter, resulting in being deprived of divine mercy and condemned to a dire fate.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating others with Him (shirk), but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk, associating partners with Allah, as an unforgivable sin if one dies without repenting from it. It underscores the unique status of monotheism in Islam and the merciful nature of Allah who forgives all other sins for those He chooses. Therefore, turning away from shirk is paramount in maintaining the correct relationship with Allah and attaining His forgiveness.

translation: Indeed, they call upon besides Him only females, and they call upon none but a rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided nature of those who associate partners with God, specifically by calling upon female deities or idols, which underscores the futility and error in their worship. It warns that such acts are not only incorrect but also represent following a rebellious and misleading force, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and the rejection of false deities.

translation: May Allah curse him and say: I will surely take a share from among My servants for him.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the individual mentioned is cursed by Allah due to their actions or beliefs, and Allah declares that this person will inevitably have to bear a portion or share of consequence or punishment from among His servants. It underscores Divine justice and the inevitability of accountability.

translation: And We will surely mislead them, and We will surely delude them, and We will command them, so they will slit the ears of livestock, and We will command them, so they will change the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the enormity of defiance against God's natural order symbolized by changing the creation of Allah, such as altering livestock physically. It warns that following Satan's path leads to deviating from divine guidance, resulting in manifest loss and spiritual ruin. The act of 'slitting ears of livestock' represents futile and misguided rituals, emphasizing that such actions rooted in misguidance are harmful and lead away from true faith and obedience to God's commands.

translation: He promises them and gives them an illusion, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan's promises, which are merely illusions that lead people astray from the path of truth; it serves as a warning to be cautious of false hopes that divert attention from genuine guidance and righteousness.

translation: Their home will be Hell, and from it they will find no escape.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and permanency of the punishment for those who have unleashed wrongdoing and injustice. It signifies that once such individuals are condemned to Hell, they will face the results of their deeds with no possibility of evading or escaping the consequences.

translation: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. [It is] the true promise of Allah, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and truthfulness of Allah's promise of Paradise to those who believe and act righteously. It assures believers that their faith combined with good deeds leads to eternal reward and bliss, encouraging steadfastness and sincerity in their spiritual and moral conduct.

translation: It is not [by mere] your desires or the desires of the People of the Scripture; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it and will not find besides Allah a protector or a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that outcomes and divine justice are not determined by human wishes or the wishes of previous religious communities, but by one's actions. It underscores the principle of accountability, stating that every person who commits wrongdoing will inevitably face its consequences, and there is no refuge or intercessor besides Allah. This serves as a reminder of the importance of sincere and righteous conduct, and that reliance should be solely on Allah for guidance and support.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the reward for righteous deeds is not limited by gender; both men and women who believe and act righteously will enter Paradise without any injustice. It affirms the absolute fairness of God's judgment and the equal value of good deeds regardless of the doer's identity.

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face (self) to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of sincere submission to Allah combined with righteous deeds and following the pure monotheistic faith of Prophet Abraham. It highlights that true religion is not mere external ritual but a complete devotion characterized by faith, good conduct, and adherence to the path of Abraham, who is exemplified as a model of unwavering faith and closeness to Allah.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and Allah is, over all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and comprehensive knowledge of Allah. Everything that exists in the heavens and on earth is under His dominion and subject to His authority. His encompassing nature indicates that nothing is beyond His awareness or control, reminding believers of His omnipresence and the extent of His power.

translation: And they ask you about women. Say, "God gives you judgment concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphans whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, and concerning the women to whom you desire to marry, and the weak among children, and that you maintain orphans with justice." And whatever good you do, indeed, God is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance on the matters of women, orphans, and vulnerable individuals comes from divine revelation and commands justice and fairness in their treatment. It underscores the responsibility of society to safeguard the rights and well-being of those who are vulnerable, ensuring equitable treatment and care. The ultimate accountability for these actions rests with God, who is fully aware of all deeds, prompting believers to act with sincerity and justice.

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no blame upon them if they make reconciliation between them – and reconciliation is best – and the souls are inclined to greed. But if you do good and fear Allah, indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse instructs that when a wife fears ill-treatment or neglect from her husband, both parties should strive to reconcile their differences, as reconciliation is the most virtuous path. It acknowledges human tendencies towards selfishness but emphasizes that righteousness, fear of Allah, and sincere efforts to mend relationships earn Allah’s awareness and reward.

translation: And you will never be able to be equal [in feeling] between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the human reality that perfect equality in emotional affection among multiple spouses is unattainable. It advises fairness in treatment so that no one feels neglected or abandoned, emphasizing the importance of maintaining justice and equity in relationships. Ultimately, it underscores that sincere efforts to uphold justice and mindfulness of God’s presence lead to His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And if they separate, Allah will suffice each [party] against the other. And ever is Allah, of all things, encompassing and wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that even if people part ways or disputes arise, Allah alone is sufficient to provide for and protect each group according to His wisdom and knowledge. It underscores Allah's comprehensive power and wisdom in managing affairs beyond human control, offering assurance that ultimate reliance should be placed on Him rather than on interpersonal conflicts.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute dominion and ownership of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth. It warns the People of the Book and all believers to have consciousness and fear of Allah as a crucial moral and spiritual obligation. The verse also underscores that disbelief and rejection of faith cannot diminish Allah's sovereignty or His sufficiency. Allah is independent of creation, possessing no needs, yet He is deserving of all praise for His perfection and grace.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute dominion and ownership of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on the earth. It serves as a reminder that ultimate authority and control rest with Him alone, and that He is fully capable of managing and overseeing all matters without any need for assistance. This instills a sense of reliance and trust in God's wisdom and power in handling the affairs of the universe and our personal lives.

translation: If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others [in your place]. And ever is Allah competent to do that.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute power and control over humanity. It illustrates that human existence and continuation are contingent upon His will; He has the ability to replace one group of people with another. This signifies that no one holds any inherent right to superiority or permanence, emphasizing humility and reliance on God's mercy and justice.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate source of all rewards, both worldly and spiritual. It reminds believers that their efforts and intentions are fully known to Allah, who hears all prayers and sees all deeds. Therefore, seeking the rewards of this life should not be divorced from seeking the eternal rewards of the afterlife, as Allah encompasses all that is in both worlds and grants accordingly.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desire, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount importance of justice and truthfulness in the life of a believer. It teaches that one's commitment to fairness must transcend personal bias, even when it involves oneself or loved ones. It warns against letting desires or social status impede one’s ability to be just.
