translation: Say, "O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion beyond the truth and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and had misled many and deviated from the sound way."
interpretation: This verse admonishes the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) to practice their religion in its true and balanced form without exaggeration or distortion. It warns against following misguided predecessors who deviated from the straight path, leading themselves and others astray. The emphasis is on adhering to the authentic teachings of faith and avoiding extremes or innovations that lead away from righteousness.

translation: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the rejection and transgression of certain individuals among the Children of Israel led to their explicit condemnation by revered prophets like David and Jesus. It illustrates that persistent disobedience to God's commands results not only in divine displeasure but also in public denunciation by truthful leaders, highlighting the gravity of defiance against divine guidance.

translation: They used not to abstain from evil deeds which they committed. Evil indeed was that which they used to do.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who persist in wrongdoing without any restraint or remorse. It underscores the moral failure of individuals who continue engaging in evil acts without seeking to correct themselves or prevent the harm they cause, highlighting the gravity and ugliness of such behavior in the sight of God.

translation: You see many of them taking as allies those who have disbelieved. Evil is what their own souls have put forward for them, that Allah's wrath may be upon them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave consequence of aligning oneself with those who reject faith and oppose the path of righteousness. It serves as a warning that such alliances are born out of misguided desires or ignorance and lead to Allah's displeasure and everlasting punishment. The verse urges believers to be cautious about their associations and loyalties, ensuring that they stand firmly with truth and avoid what leads to spiritual ruin.

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as guardians, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true belief in Allah, His Prophet, and the revealed scripture would lead a believer to choose righteous and trustworthy leaders. The fact that many do not do so is a sign of their rebelliousness and disobedience, indicating that their failure to recognize rightful leadership stems from a lack of genuine faith.

translation: You will certainly find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will certainly find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the differing attitudes of various communities toward the followers of Islam. It underlines that enmity is not a mere coincidence but often stems from deep-seated social and religious dynamics. The hostility of some Jews and polytheists toward believers may be linked to resistance against the transformative message of Islam, whereas the Christians’ closer affection is attributed to the presence of humility and piety within their ranks, embodied by clergy and monks who foster compassion and openness. The verse ultimately teaches that attitudes are shaped by the internal spirit and values of communities, especially humility and sincerity, rather than mere labels or identities.

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound emotional and spiritual impact that the revelation of divine truth has on sincere believers. Their tears signify genuine recognition and acceptance of the truth, demonstrating that faith is not merely intellectual assent but a deeply heartfelt conviction that moves one to a sincere declaration of belief and a desire to be counted among those who bear witness to God's message.

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and in that which has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people?
interpretation: This verse reflects a sincere recognition of the importance of faith in Allah and acceptance of divine truth. It demonstrates a hopeful desire to be among the righteous and highlights the natural inclination of the soul to seek God's mercy and companionship with the virtuous. The verse encourages believers to affirm their faith sincerely, motivated by the aspiration to attain a blessed status alongside the righteous in the Hereafter.

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah blesses and rewards those who maintain truthfulness and righteousness, promising them eternal bliss in Paradise. It serves as encouragement to uphold integrity and goodness, affirming that sincere deeds and words in accordance with divine guidance lead to everlasting reward and happiness.

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequence awaiting those who deliberately reject and deny the clear signs and revelations from God. It serves as a warning that persistent disbelief and denial lead to spiritual ruin and eternal punishment, reflecting the seriousness of turning away from divine guidance.

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the boundaries set by Allah regarding what is lawful and unlawful. Believers are reminded not to ban what Allah has permitted, as doing so exceeds rightful limits and imposes unnecessary restrictions. Furthermore, it warns against overstepping limits (transgression) in general, highlighting that such behavior is disliked by Allah. The verse encourages moderation and respect for divine guidance, discouraging extremism and unwarranted prohibitions.

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good; and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming what is permissible and pure, reminding believers to maintain consciousness of God in their actions, as their faith is rooted in this awareness, guiding them to live rightly and ethically.

translation: Allah does not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He takes you to task for the oaths you have deliberately sworn. Its expiation is to feed ten needy people with the average of what you feed your own family, or to clothe them, or to free a slave. But whoever cannot find the means, then fasting for three days is the expiation for your oaths when you have sworn. So protect your oaths. Thus Allah makes clear His signs to you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness of intentionally swearing oaths and the importance of fulfilling them. It acknowledges that unintentional or accidental oaths are not held against a person, showing Allah's mercy and understanding of human weakness. However, deliberate oaths carry responsibility and require expiation, highlighting the ethical importance of truthfulness and accountability. The prescribed expiations serve both as a means of atonement and social welfare, encouraging believers to care for the needy. Ultimately, the verse calls on believers to respect their oaths and understand Allah's guidance, fostering gratitude and mindfulness in their commitments.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificial] stones, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the harmful nature of certain practices such as intoxicants, gambling, and superstitious rituals, associating them with the corrupting influence of Satan. The command to avoid them is not just about abstaining from specific actions but about protecting one's spiritual and social well-being, leading to true success in this life and the hereafter.

translation: Satan only wants to sow enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling and to hinder you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So, will you desist?
interpretation: This verse highlights how intoxicants and gambling serve as tools for Satan to create discord and hostility within society, disrupting harmony and social bonds. By leading people away from the remembrance of Allah and the obligation of prayer, these vices weaken spiritual consciousness and moral awareness. The verse serves as a warning to recognize these harmful influences, encouraging believers to abstain from such practices to protect their faith, unity, and moral integrity.

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware; but if you turn away - then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveying.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of believers to obey both Allah and His Messenger, highlighting that obedience to the Prophet is inherently an obedience to God. It also serves as a warning to remain vigilant and cautious in faith. However, it clarifies that the Messenger's duty is solely to deliver the message clearly; he is not accountable for people's acceptance or rejection of it. Thus, each individual is responsible for their own response to guidance.

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten as long as they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy of Allah towards the believers who strive sincerely in faith and good deeds, illustrating that unintentional consumption or minor lapses do not burden those who maintain conscious God-fearing (taqwa) and persist in righteousness. It assures believers that continuous effort in faith and goodness, coupled with mindfulness of Allah, invites His love and forgiveness, highlighting the importance of perseverance and sincere piety over mere formalities.

translation: O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of game caught by your hands and your spears to know who fears Him unseen. So whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that trials, even in the form of permissible spoils of war or hunting, serve as a means to distinguish those who truly fear Allah and observe His commands even when unseen. It emphasizes that fear of Allah transcends mere visibility or direct observation, and those who exceed the bounds set by Allah after witnessing His tests expose themselves to severe consequences, highlighting the importance of self-restraint and conscious obedience.

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram (consecration for pilgrimage). And whoever among you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equal amount of that which he killed, judged by two just men among you as a gift to the Kaaba or as expiation: feeding the needy or an equivalent fast, so that he may taste the consequences of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns to it - then Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Retributive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sacredness of the state of ihram during pilgrimage, prohibiting the killing of game to maintain respect and sanctity. It underscores accountability by prescribing a fair and restorative penalty for intentional violation, facilitating repentance and community welfare through expiation acts. The verse also highlights Allah's mercy in forgiving past mistakes while warning of severe consequences for deliberate, repeated disobedience, demonstrating the balance between divine mercy and justice.

translation: He has made lawful for you the catch of the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, and has forbidden you the catch of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse establishes a specific law regarding what is permissible to eat during the sacred state of ihram in pilgrimage. It permits eating seafood while prohibiting hunting land animals during ihram, highlighting the importance of obedience and self-restraint in sacred rituals. The concluding admonition to fear Allah serves as a reminder that these laws are not arbitrary but are commands from the One who will hold us accountable in the hereafter, encouraging mindfulness and reverence in fulfilling divine injunctions.

translation: Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a sanctuary for the people, and the forbidden month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands. That you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sacredness and central role of the Ka'bah as a place of spiritual focus and pilgrimage for humanity. It also underscores the sanctity of certain times and rituals, such as the forbidden months and sacrificial practices, which serve as reminders of Allah's encompassing knowledge and authority over all creation, encouraging believers to recognize His omniscience and maintain consciousness of Him in their worship and actions.

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that while Allah's justice is strict and can bring severe consequences for wrongdoing, His mercy and forgiveness are vast and always accessible to those who sincerely repent and turn toward Him. It encourages mindfulness of one's actions, balancing fear of punishment with hope in divine mercy.

translation: The Messenger's duty is only to convey the message clearly. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to deliver God's message faithfully and without alteration, highlighting that his obligation is limited to clear communication. It also underscores that Allah has complete knowledge of all internal thoughts and intentions, whether openly expressed or hidden, reminding believers that nothing escapes His awareness.

translation: Say, "The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the evil may please you. So, fear Allah, O you of understanding, that you may be successful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental difference between what is morally corrupt and what is morally pure, underscoring that no matter how prevalent or seemingly attractive evil may appear, it cannot be equated with goodness. It serves as a reminder to use wisdom and discernment, urging believers to maintain piety and conscious awareness of God in order to attain true success.

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned that which is past; and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to avoid probing into details or matters that might cause distress or lead to unnecessary hardship, especially beyond what the revelation clarifies. It encourages trust in Allah's wisdom and timing, highlighting His mercy by pardoning past matters, and emphasizes that some knowledge can be a source of trial rather than benefit.

translation: A people before you asked about it, then they became disbelievers in it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some who seek knowledge or clarification about divine matters, only to reject the truths revealed to them afterward. It serves as a caution against approaching the message with insincere intentions or skepticism that leads to denial rather than understanding and acceptance.

translation: Allah has not made [any such things as] bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or hami; but those who disbelieve invent falsehood about Allah, and most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that certain pre-Islamic practices involving the designation of specific animals as forbidden for sacrifice are not sanctioned by Allah. It emphasizes that attributing such restrictions to divine decree is a falsehood fabricated by disbelievers, highlighting the importance of following the true guidance prescribed by Allah rather than superstitious or fabricated traditions.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our forefathers." Even though their forefathers knew nothing and were not guided?
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of blindly following tradition without seeking knowledge or guidance from divine revelation. It warns against the refusal to accept new truth merely because one is attached to ancestral practices, stressing that such inherited ignorance is not a valid excuse to reject guidance from Allah and His Messenger.

translation: O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in faith and conduct, assuring believers that the misguidance of others cannot harm them if they remain on the path of guidance. It also reminds that everyone's ultimate return is to Allah, who is fully aware of all their actions and will judge them accordingly.

translation: O you who have believed, when death approaches one of you while he is witnessing, two just men from among you or two others from outside should testify. If you doubt, they should swear by Allah that indeed, Allah will not allow us to accept any price, even if it is a near relative, and we will not conceal Allah's testimony. Indeed, we would then be among the sinful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of truthful and just testimony, especially concerning matters witnessed at the time of death, such as wills or final declarations. It underlines that witnesses must be impartial and honest, swearing by Allah to ensure their testimony is free from bias or corruption, even if it means testifying against close relatives. Concealing such testimony is considered a grave sin, highlighting the high value Islam places on justice, truthfulness, and moral integrity in dealings among believers.

translation: If the two who testify are found guilty of sin, then two others shall stand in their place from those who deserve the burden, and they shall swear by Allah that our testimony is truer than theirs; and we have not transgressed. Surely, we would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of bearing false testimony and the seriousness with which justice is maintained. It reveals a mechanism within the legal process to ensure truthfulness, where if initial witnesses are proven dishonest, substitutes must affirm the truth under oath. The emphasis is on the integrity of testimony and the condemnation of injustice, highlighting that wrongful accusations not only harm individuals but also constitute a grave sin against divine and moral law.

translation: That is more likely so that they bring the testimony in full or they fear that oaths will be repudiated after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen; and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and fear of God in bearing witness and taking oaths. It suggests that those involved in giving testimony should do so honestly and fully, fearing the consequences of falsely swearing or breaking oaths. It also serves as a warning that guidance from Allah is not granted to those who persist in rebellious and immoral behavior without regard to divine accountability.

translation: The Day Allah will gather the Messengers and ask, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is the Knower of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse highlights that even the Messengers, with all their dedication and efforts in delivering the message, do not possess knowledge of the unseen or of what ultimately happens to their people; such knowledge belongs solely to Allah. It emphasizes the absolute and unique knowledge of Allah over all things hidden from human perception.

translation: When Allah said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother: how I supported you with the Spirit of Holiness, so that you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and how I taught you the Scripture, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel; and how you shaped from clay the form of a bird by My permission, and breathed into it, and it became a bird by My permission; and how you healed the blind and the lepers by My permission; and how you brought forth the dead by My permission; and how I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs, but those who disbelieved among them said, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'"
interpretation: This verse highlights God's favors upon Jesus, emphasizing that all his miracles and teachings were granted by God's permission, which underscores the concept of divine authority and dependence. It serves to clarify that Jesus, though granted extraordinary abilities, was a servant and messenger of God, not divine in himself, and that rejection of his message by some was due to their disbelief and attribution of his miracles to magic rather than recognizing the divine origin.

translation: And when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and My messenger, they said, "We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsiveness and acceptance of the disciples to the divine message conveyed through the Prophet. Their immediate declaration of faith and submission signifies the importance of trust and conviction in the messenger's truth, emphasizing that genuine belief stems from both inner conviction and outward testimony.

translation: When the disciples said, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, can your Lord send down upon us a table spread with food from the heaven?" He said, "Fear Allah, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and God-consciousness when seeking divine miracles. Jesus reminds his followers that true belief entails trust in God's wisdom and power, and that requests for wondrous signs must be accompanied by piety and sincerity in faith.

translation: They said, "We want to eat from it and that our hearts may be assured, and we want to know that you have told us the truth, so that we may be among its witnesses."
interpretation: This verse reflects the human desire for reassurance and certainty when confronted with extraordinary claims. The people are asking for tangible proof—eating from the miraculous tree and experiencing its effects firsthand—to confirm the truth of the message they have been given, highlighting the need for direct evidence in matters of faith and the importance of authentic witnessing.

translation: Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven to be for us a feast for the first and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers."
interpretation: This supplication of Jesus highlights the profound human desire for divine support and blessing. It signifies the request for tangible evidence of God's mercy and sustenance, not merely for personal benefit but as a communal celebration that strengthens faith across generations. Furthermore, it acknowledges God's unparalleled ability to provide, emphasizing reliance on divine generosity rather than worldly means.

translation: Indeed, I have revealed it to you, so whoever disbelieves afterward among you - then indeed, I will punish him with a punishment the likes of which I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of rejecting the divine revelation after it has been clearly brought forth. It highlights that disbelief following the acknowledgment of God's message is a grave offense, warranting a unique and unparalleled punishment. The verse serves as a stern warning against obstinate denial and stresses the importance of sincere faith and acceptance of God's guidance.

translation: And when Allah said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'" He said, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would surely have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the innocence and purity of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him), clarifying that he never claimed divinity for himself or his mother. It emphasizes that any false attribution of divinity to them is unfounded, and that only Allah possesses full knowledge of all matters hidden or apparent. The verse serves as a reassurance that prophets are truthful servants of God, bearing witness to His oneness and rejecting any form of polytheism.

translation: I did not say to them except what You commanded me: to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the responsibility of the Prophet to convey the message of worshiping Allah alone, as commanded, and to serve as a witness over his people during his lifetime. It also emphasizes that after the Prophet's passing, Allah remains the ultimate Watcher and Guardian over all people, highlighting divine oversight and accountability beyond human stewardship.

translation: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of Allah's relationship with His creation: humanity is inherently His servant, deserving of discipline, yet He has the power and wisdom to forgive. It emphasizes the balance between divine justice and mercy, reminding us that forgiveness is a manifestation of Allah's supreme wisdom and strength, inviting believers to rely on His grace while recognizing their position as His obedient servants.

translation: This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward and success for those who are sincere and truthful in their faith and actions. It highlights that on the Day of Judgment, their honesty and integrity will lead them to eternal bliss in Paradise, signifying that divine pleasure and eternal happiness are the greatest triumphs one can achieve.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah over all creation. It serves to remind believers that everything in existence is under His control and authority. Nothing occurs without His will, and His power encompasses all matters, reinforcing the concept of Tawheed, the oneness of God, as the ultimate sustainer and ruler of the universe.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light. Yet those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unmatched power and sovereignty of Allah as the Creator of all things, highlighting the natural phenomena of darkness and light as manifestations of His will. The statement underscores the contradiction and injustice in the stance of disbelievers who equate or associate partners with Allah despite His clear signs and authority.

translation: He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a term predetermined with Him; yet you doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and divine wisdom behind human creation and the predetermined lifespan assigned by God. Despite the clear decree about the time of death ordained by God, humans still harbor doubts or question the reality of mortality and divine timing, highlighting human hesitation in fully accepting the inevitability and divine control over life and death.

translation: And He is Allah, in the heavens and on the earth; He knows your secret and your overt actions, and He knows what you earn (do).
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive knowledge and presence of Allah, emphasizing that nothing remains hidden from Him, whether concealed in the heart or openly done, underscoring His omnipresence and omniscience over all of creation and human deeds.

translation: And whenever there comes to them a sign from the signs of their Lord, they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring behavior of certain people who, despite witnessing clear signs from Allah, deliberately choose to ignore or reject them, reflecting a state of denial and obstinacy that prevents them from accepting the truth.

translation: Indeed, they denied the truth when it came to them; therefore, there will come to them news of what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that rejecting divine guidance and mocking the truth will not go unnoticed. The 'news' mentioned symbolizes the inevitable consequences or a revealing of realities that will sternly confront those who scorned the message, serving as a caution against arrogance and disbelief.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established upon the earth as We have not established you, and sent down rain from the sky in abundance, and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them another generation.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that past communities were granted great blessings and stability, yet they fell due to their transgressions. It teaches that divine favor is contingent upon righteousness and obedience, and that forgetting this leads to destruction regardless of temporal power or comfort. It also signals God's power to replace one generation with another, emphasizing the impermanence of worldly status.

translation: And if We had sent down to you a written scripture on paper, so that they could touch it with their own hands, the disbelievers would say, "This is nothing but clear magic."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stubbornness and denial of those who reject faith. Even if a tangible, undeniable proof were presented to them, they would still disbelieve and attribute it to magic, highlighting that their rejection is not due to lack of evidence but rather due to their hardened hearts and unwillingness to accept the truth.

translation: And they say, "Why was a messenger not sent down to him? If We had sent down a messenger, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be given respite."
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of some people who demand a visible, extraordinary sign such as an angelic messenger to believe in the message. Their demand, however, is not sincere; even if such a sign were given, they would not accept the truth wholeheartedly but would instead continue in their obstinacy. It highlights human stubbornness and skepticism that persist despite clear evidence, emphasizing that guidance ultimately depends on the willingness to accept the message rather than extraordinary signs.

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them in what they already confuse themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that even if the messenger were made an angel, appearing as a human is necessary for effective communication and understanding among people. Moreover, it highlights how people often confuse matters themselves, and making the messenger an angel would not alleviate their confusion—it suggests that misunderstandings arise from human misconceptions rather than the form of the messenger.

translation: Indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but those who mocked them were overtaken by that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that mocking or ridiculing the messengers of God is not only disrespectful but ultimately leads to consequences. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice where those who scorn the prophets will face the repercussions of their mockery, underscoring the seriousness of rejecting the message delivered by God's messengers.

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the deniers."
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the consequences faced by those who rejected divine guidance in the past. It serves as a reminder that denying the truth does not lead to success or happiness, but rather to destruction and regret, urging people to learn from history and recognize the reality of God's message.

translation: Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth?" Say, "To Allah." He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who have lost themselves [in disbelief] - they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, affirming that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone. It underscores Allah's self-imposed attribute of mercy, highlighting His compassionate nature despite His immense power. Furthermore, it assures the certainty of resurrection and accountability on the Day of Judgment, a pivotal point for human responsibility. Those who have harmed their own souls by rejecting faith are portrayed as irrevocably lost, unable to accept belief because their actions have severed them from guidance and truth.

translation: And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and ownership over all creation, regardless of time or place. It highlights that nothing escapes His knowledge or perception; He hears all sounds and is fully aware of all matters, reinforcing the concept of divine omnipresence and omniscience.

translation: Say, "Should I take as a guardian other than Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds but is not fed?" Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first to submit [to Allah] and not be among the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes exclusive reliance on Allah as the sole guardian and sustainer, highlighting His unique role as the Creator who provides for all creation without needing anything Himself. It instructs to submit wholly to Allah alone, rejecting any form of associating partners with Him, reflecting the fundamental monotheistic principle of Islam.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's deep consciousness of accountability before God. It highlights the seriousness of obedience to God's commands and the fear of the severe consequences in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to submit humbly to divine guidance to avoid the great calamity of the Day of Judgment.

translation: Whoever is averted from it (the punishment) that Day, it is because Allah has shown him mercy. That is the clear attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense value of Allah's mercy, indicating that being saved from punishment on the Day of Judgment is a profound blessing and signifies success. It reminds believers that ultimate salvation and triumph come from Allah's compassion, emphasizing reliance on His mercy rather than solely on one's deeds.

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, then there is no one who can repel His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all matters affecting human lives. It reminds us that only Allah has control over the trials and blessings we experience; no one else can alleviate harm or bestow good unless He wills it. This knowledge encourages reliance on Allah in times of hardship and gratitude when receiving His blessings, recognizing that all affairs are ultimately under His wise and merciful management.

translation: And He is the Subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted (with all).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute authority and control over all His creation, highlighting that His dominion is unquestionable and supreme. Additionally, it attributes to Him perfect wisdom and intimate knowledge of all matters, ensuring that His decrees and actions are based on profound understanding and justice.

translation: Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Quran has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Is it that you will testify that with Allah there are other deities?" Say, "I do not testify. Say, "Indeed, He is only one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate with Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah and rejects any form of polytheism. It highlights Allah as the ultimate witness and authority over all matters, including the relationship between the Prophet and the people. The Prophet is instructed to clearly deny witnessing the existence of any other gods besides Allah, affirming monotheism and distancing himself from any associations of partners with God.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it just as they recognize their own sons. Indeed, those who have lost themselves will not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound connection and familiarity that true recipients of divine revelation have with the Scripture, likening their understanding to the intimate knowledge one has of their own children. It implies that genuine believers deeply comprehend, accept, and live by the guidance of the Scripture. Conversely, those who have 'lost themselves'—meaning those who are heedless, misguided, or spiritually estranged—fail to recognize the truth of the message and therefore do not believe. This underscores that faith is intricately tied to recognizing and internalizing the divine guidance given.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who forges a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse warns against the grave injustice of falsely attributing lies to God or rejecting His revelations. Such acts not only distort the truth but also signify a deep transgression against the divine guidance, leading to inevitable failure in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Where are your 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reality of the Day of Judgment when all people will be resurrected and gathered. It confronts those who committed shirk (associating partners with Allah), exposing the falsehood of their claims by questioning the existence and power of their so-called partners. It underscores the futility of associating others with Allah and the ultimate accountability that everyone will face.

translation: Then their trial was nothing but that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment where people try to defend themselves by swearing an oath on Allah's oneness yet denying the reality of their polytheism. The interpretation is that mere words and oaths without true belief and sincere actions are meaningless; true faith is reflected in inner conviction and consistent worship, not in last-minute declarations.

translation: See how they lie against themselves, and what they were fabricating has led them astray.
interpretation: This verse teaches that when people invent falsehoods against divine truth or themselves, these lies ultimately lead them away from guidance, resulting in spiritual misguidance and self-deception.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed coverings over their hearts so they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. Even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. Until, when they come to you to argue, the disbelievers say, "This is nothing but ancient legends."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual blindness and obstinacy of certain disbelievers whose hearts are sealed and ears closed by divine decree, preventing them from truly comprehending the truth despite witnessing clear signs. Their rejection stems not from lack of evidence, but from an inner resistance rooted in prior denial and arrogance, leading them to dismiss prophetic messages as mere myths of the past.

translation: And they prevent [others] from it and turn away from it. And if they perish, they only perish for themselves, but they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and obstinacy of those who reject guidance and prevent others from following the truth. Their actions not only harm themselves through their misguided rejection, but they remain unaware of the consequences, demonstrating a lack of insight into the spiritual damage they incur.

translation: And if you could see when they stand before the Fire and say, 'Oh, would that we were returned [to life] and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound regret of those who rejected God's revelations during their lives. It emphasizes that denial of divine truths leads to severe consequences, and that the opportunity to believe and accept guidance must be seized in this world, as remorse after death comes too late.

translation: But what they hid before has now appeared to them. And if they were returned, they would return to that which they were forbidden. And indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitability of truth unveiling what was previously concealed by people, emphasizing that even if given another chance, many would revert to their past wrongful behaviors. It highlights human nature's tendency to resist righteous guidance and persist in falsehood despite clear warnings.

translation: And they say, "There is nothing but our worldly life; we are not to be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of those who deny the afterlife, focusing solely on the material and transient nature of this world. The interpretation highlights their disbelief in resurrection and life after death, emphasizing the Qur'an's challenge to this notion by asserting that human existence extends beyond the temporary worldly life.

translation: And if you could see when they stand before their Lord! He will say, "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will say, "So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of accountability before God, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, the deniers of truth will be confronted with undeniable evidence of the reality they've rejected. Their acknowledgment of the truth at that moment is too late to save them, and the consequent punishment is a direct result of their persistent disbelief and rejection of divine guidance during their lives.

translation: Indeed, those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost; when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, 'Oh, regret for us over what we neglected concerning it!' And they bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they carry.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable loss faced by those who reject the reality of the meeting with Allah and the accountability in the Hereafter. Their denial causes them to neglect preparation for the Day of Judgment, and when it arrives unexpectedly, they are overwhelmed with regret and burdened by the consequences of their deeds. It underscores the importance of belief and mindful action, as one cannot escape the weight of their choices and the poor outcome of neglecting faith.

translation: And the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement. Indeed, the home of the Hereafter is best for those who are conscious of Allah. Will you not then use reason?
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the worldly life, with all its pleasures and distractions, is temporary and insignificant compared to the eternal life of the Hereafter. It calls on the believers to prioritize their actions and mindset towards what holds true value—seeking the pleasure of Allah and the eternal rewards He has promised. The rhetorical question at the end encourages reflection and understanding, urging people to recognize the futility of being engrossed in fleeting worldly matters over everlasting spiritual success.

translation: Indeed, We know that what they say grieves you, but they do not reject you; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Prophet (peace be upon him) is not being lied about or wronged by the accusations made against him; instead, it is the wrongdoers who stubbornly deny the clear signs and messages of Allah, and this denial causes distress to the Prophet, reflecting the pain of witnessing injustice despite the truth he conveys.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were denied, but they persevered patiently in what they were denied and were harmed until Our help came to them. And there is no changing the words of Allah. And indeed, there has come to you news of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness in the face of rejection and adversity, as exemplified by previous messengers. It reassures that divine support will eventually prevail and that God's promises and commandments are unchangeable and true.

translation: And if it is hard for you to turn away from them, then if you are able, seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder in the sky to bring them a sign. And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance. So do not be among the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human limitation in guiding others; despite the Prophet’s desire to lead people to faith through manifest signs or miracles, true guidance is ultimately in Allah’s hands. It teaches patience and reliance on God’s wisdom, emphasizing that one should not be burdened by others’ rejection, nor act ignorantly by trying to force guidance beyond one’s means.

translation: Only those who listen respond. And Allah will resurrect the dead; then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of attentive listening and sincere acceptance of the message; those who truly hear and internalize it respond positively. It also reminds that life and death are under Allah's authority, and after resurrection everyone will ultimately return to Him for judgment and recompense.

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."
interpretation: This verse highlights that God has the power to send clear signs or miracles to substantiate the message of the Prophet. However, the real obstacle is not God's inability but the people's lack of understanding and unwillingness to accept the truth. The emphasis is on human ignorance and rejection rather than divine incapacity.

translation: And there is no creature on earth nor a bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of God's creation, indicating that every living being, whether animal or bird, exists in a community with its own manner of life and order, akin to human societies. It conveys the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge and decree, as nothing escapes His record or concern. Ultimately, all creatures will return to their Creator, highlighting the accountability and final gathering before God.

translation: But those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb in darkness. Whomever Allah wills, He leads astray; and whomever He wills, He puts on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual state of those who reject divine guidance: their hearts become closed, rendering them unable to perceive the truth, akin to being deaf and dumb in utter darkness. It also highlights Allah's ultimate authority in guiding or misguiding individuals based on His wisdom, reminding believers to seek His guidance earnestly and acknowledge that true guidance comes solely from Him.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon anyone other than Allah if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the reality and sincerity of turning to beings other than Allah in times of need or calamity, emphasizing the oneness and ultimate authority of Allah alone to grant relief or forgiveness, thereby urging the recognition of His exclusive divinity and sovereignty.

translation: But it is Him alone you call upon, and He reveals what you call upon Him for, if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of invoking other deities alongside Allah. It highlights that ultimately, only Allah responds to prayers and grants what is asked, while those who commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) forget the very beings they wrongly believe have power, underscoring the importance of monotheism and reliance solely on Allah.

translation: And indeed, We sent to nations before you, and We seized them with poverty and hardship so that they might humble themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that God’s trials, such as hardship and adversity, are meant as a means to bring people to humility and sincere supplication. The difficulties are not mere punishment but are opportunities for reflection, repentance, and turning back to God with heartfelt devotion.

translation: So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made their deeds pleasing to them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the condition of people who, despite facing severe consequences or divine retribution, fail to turn back in repentance or humility because their hearts have become hardened. The hardness of the heart here symbolizes a spiritual barrier that prevents them from perceiving the truth and recognizing their errors. Moreover, Satan's role in beautifying their actions implies that they are deceived into believing their wrongdoings are acceptable, thus perpetuating their misguided behavior.

translation: But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every (kind of) good thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder about the consequences of heedlessness. It illustrates that when people become negligent of divine guidance and warnings, worldly blessings alone do not guarantee lasting success or happiness. The passage warns that indulgence in such blessings without gratitude or mindfulness can lead to sudden downfall, emphasizing the importance of remembrance and humility before enjoying the fruits of provision.

translation: So the end of the wrongdoers was cut off. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine justice where those who commit injustice and wrongdoing ultimately face a decisive end, signifying that evil does not prevail. The praise to Allah affirms that all dominion and authority belong to Him, and He alone orchestrates the fate of nations and individuals, ensuring that justice is served.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, then who is an god besides Allah who could bring them back to you?" See how We diversify the verses; then they [i.e., the people] turn away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and control of Allah over human faculties and life itself. It serves as a reminder that all senses and hearts are gifts from Allah and that He alone can grant or withhold them. The rhetorical question emphasizes the futility of idol worship and reliance on anything other than Allah. The verse also indicates that despite clear signs and reminders, some people choose to turn away and reject guidance.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes to you suddenly or openly, will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoers?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice, highlighting that God's punishment, whether it strikes suddenly or in a manifest way, affects only those who commit injustice and wrongdoing, reinforcing the principle that evil deeds lead to consequences while the righteous are spared.

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. So whoever believes and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the primary role of the messengers is to guide humanity by delivering glad tidings and warnings. It underscores the direct connection between faith, righteous action, and the resulting peace of mind. Those who believe sincerely and amend their conduct can trust in God's protection from fear and sorrow, highlighting the transformative power of faith combined with ethical living.

translation: And those who deny Our verses will be afflicted by punishment for their transgressions.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who reject and deny the signs and revelations of God do so by engaging in sinful and disobedient behavior, and as a consequence, they will face divine punishment for their persistent wrongdoing and defiance.

translation: Say, "I do not say to you that I have the depositories of Allah or that I know the unseen, nor do I say to you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me." Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the humility and honesty of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in conveying the message of Islam. It highlights that he does not possess any divine treasures or hidden knowledge by himself, nor does he claim to be an angel or a supernatural being. Instead, he strictly follows the revelation given to him by God. The rhetorical question at the end serves to encourage people to use their intellect and discernment to distinguish between those who are spiritually 'blind' and those who have clear insight. It invites reflection on the truth of the message and the legitimacy of the Prophet's mission.

translation: And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord; for them there is no protector nor intercessor besides Him, so that they may become mindful (of Him).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and being conscious of standing accountable before Allah on the Day of Judgment, highlighting that no one can serve as a protector or intercessor except Allah Himself, thereby urging one to develop true piety and consciousness of Allah's authority and justice.

translation: And do not turn away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face. You are not responsible for their accounts, nor are they responsible for yours. If you were to turn them away, indeed, you would be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse instructs to show kindness and tolerance towards those who sincerely worship God with devotion at all times. It highlights that one is not accountable for others' spiritual state, and they too bear their own responsibility independently. The act of rejecting such devoted believers unjustly would make one a wrongdoer, emphasizing the importance of accepting diverse sincere acts of worship without prejudice.

translation: And thus We tested some of them by others that they might say, "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in allowing trials and tests among people, particularly when some are favored or blessed differently by Allah. Such situations serve to reveal true gratitude and sincerity; while some may envy or question God's choices, only Allah truly knows who is truly thankful and deserving. It reminds believers that human perceptions are limited and that gratitude and recognition belong ultimately to God alone.

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you." Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that whoever among you does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and reforms, indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless mercy towards His believers, assuring that despite human errors committed out of ignorance, sincere repentance and reformation will always lead to forgiveness. It highlights the importance of hope, encouraging believers not to despair over their past mistakes but to return to the path of righteousness with certainty in Allah's compassion.

translation: And thus We distinctly set forth the verses so that the way of the criminals may become clear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelations are made clear and detailed to distinguish right from wrong, making the path of those who transgress or reject guidance evident. It serves as a warning by demonstrating that the consequences and behaviors of wrongdoers are clearly exposed through divine signs, leaving no excuse for ignorance.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah." Say, "I will not follow your desires; indeed, I would then have gone astray, and I would not be among the guided."
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of exclusive devotion to Allah alone, rejecting the worship of any other entities or idols. It highlights the message that following one's own desires or the misguided practices of others leads to spiritual error and deviation from the true path. The speaker asserts due guidance is only found in adhering strictly to the commands of Allah, not in yielding to personal whims or societal pressures.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I am upon clear proof from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not possess for you [the power to hasten] that which you hasten." Indeed, the decision belongs only to Allah; He relates the truth, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophet's firm reliance on clear evidence from God in his mission, rejecting the premature demands of disbelievers for immediate signs or punishment. It teaches that ultimate judgment and the unfolding of truth rest solely with Allah, who alone is the perfect arbitrator. The verse encourages patience, trust in divine wisdom, and recognition that human impatience cannot alter the ordained timing of God's decree.

translation: Say, "If I had what you are in haste for, the matter would have been decided between me and you; and Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's honesty and the divine wisdom in the timing of events. It emphasizes that the outcomes and judgments are ultimately determined by Allah, not by human haste, and warns that rushing may overlook divine justice, especially concerning those who commit injustice.

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but that it is in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute and all-encompassing knowledge over every detail of existence, both seen and unseen. It reflects that nothing escapes His awareness—not even the smallest leaf falling or the tiniest seed hidden in darkness. This serves as a reminder of God's sovereignty and omniscience, affirming that all events and matters are under His precise control and recorded in a clear, preserved book.

translation: And He it is Who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day; then He raises you up therein so that the term appointed is fulfilled; then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty over life and death, highlighting that He is fully aware of all human actions, both hidden and apparent. It illustrates the cycle of life controlled by God: He causes death during sleep, brings people back to life, and ultimately, everyone will return to Him to be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: And He is the Irresistible, above His servants; and He sends guardians over you. Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect [their duty].
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over all creation. It highlights that Allah appoints angels as guardians over us, watching over our lives continuously. When the time of death arrives, these angels faithfully fulfill their task without delay or negligence, ensuring the soul is taken precisely as decreed by Allah. This serves as a reminder of the certainty of death and the precision of divine decree, urging consciousness of one's actions and accountability.

translation: Then they returned to Allah, their true Master. Surely, to Him belongs the judgment, and He is the swiftest in accounting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of returning to Allah, who is the ultimate authority and the rightful judge of all actions. It serves as a reminder that no matter how power or judgment may seem delayed, Allah's judgment is both just and swift, encompassing all deeds and holding everyone accountable without delay.

translation: Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea? You call upon Him humbly and secretly, 'If He saves us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn sincerely to God during times of distress, recognizing Him as the sole source of salvation from overwhelming dangers and uncertainties. It underscores that true gratitude is expressed through faith and acknowledgment of God's mercy, especially when one is delivered from hardship.

translation: Say, "Allah delivers you from it and from every distress; then you associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse highlights the contradiction in human behavior where people acknowledge that only Allah can save them from calamities and hardships, yet they persist in associating partners with Him. It serves as a reminder to recognize Allah's exclusive power and to worship Him alone without assigning partners or intermediaries, emphasizing the importance of sincere monotheism for true deliverance.

translation: Say, "He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you [so you become] sects and make some of you taste the harm of others." See how We diversify the verses that perhaps they will understand.
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's absolute power to administer different kinds of trials and punishments to humanity, whether from the skies, the earth, or through creating divisions among people themselves. The purpose behind these varying signs and tests is to awaken understanding and reflection in people, encouraging them to recognize divine authority and to learn from the consequences of their actions.

translation: And your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say, "I am not over you a guardian."
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Muhammad's position when faced with rejection from his own people; despite their denial of the divine message, he emphasizes that his role is to convey the truth, not to compel belief or act as their overseer, highlighting the principle of personal responsibility and freedom in accepting faith.

translation: For every news (matter) there is a fixed place of settling; and you will come to know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every event or piece of information has its appointed time and place of realization or resolution, reminding us that the unfolding of matters occurs according to divine wisdom, and in due course, the truth will become evident to us all.

translation: And when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a different topic. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse advises the believer to avoid participating or engaging with those who mock or trivialize the signs of God, to maintain one’s faith and peace. It acknowledges human fallibility—if one is momentarily led astray by Satan and forgets the reminder, one should not continue to associate with those who persist in injustice, in order to protect oneself from negative influence and remain steadfast on the path of righteousness.

translation: And those who are conscious of Allah - there will be no burden upon them concerning their accounting; but only a reminder that perhaps they will be mindful.
interpretation: This verse highlights that for the righteous who possess God-consciousness (taqwa), the accountability of their deeds will not be a source of distress or hardship. Instead, the command to be mindful and to seek righteousness serves as a reminder to maintain their consciousness of Allah, encouraging them to remain steadfast in their faith and actions. The emphasis is on inner mindfulness and the gentle nature of divine guidance for those who strive to live righteously.

translation: And leave those who take their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life has deluded. And remind by the Qur'an that the soul is restrained from wrongdoing which it has earned. It will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah, even though it offers every compensation. Those are the ones who are seized by what they earned; for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns against treating faith lightly, as mere play or distraction, especially when one is deceived by the allurements of worldly life. It reminds us that each soul is accountable for its deeds and cannot escape the consequences by seeking intercession or compensation apart from Allah's will. The ultimate punishment for such heedlessness and disbelief is severe, emphasizing the seriousness of true faith and responsibility in one's actions.

translation: Say, "Shall we invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us?" Like one whom the devils enticed into confusion on the earth, he has companions who invite him to guidance, saying, "Come to us." Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance; and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshiping or turning to anyone other than Allah, as they neither benefit nor harm. It highlights the contrast between true guidance from Allah and misleading paths inspired by devils, symbolizing confusion and deviation. The verse encourages steadfastness in following divine guidance and submission to Allah alone, affirming that genuine guidance comes solely from Him despite the presence of those who might call us away from the right path.

translation: And establish prayer and fear Him. And it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining regular prayers as a means to develop God-consciousness (taqwa). It serves as a reminder that all people will ultimately be gathered before Allah for judgment, encouraging believers to uphold their duties and be conscious of their accountability.

translation: And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the Day He says, "Be," and it is. His word is the truth. To Him belongs the dominion on the Day the Horn is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah as the Creator of all existence. His command brings about creation and the events of the hereafter without any delay or failure. The affirmation that His word is the truth affirms the certainty of resurrection and judgment. Allah's knowledge encompasses all that is hidden and apparent, underscoring His perfect wisdom and intimate awareness of all realities.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Prophet Abraham's profound awareness and courage in recognizing the futility of idol worship. Despite being in a society deeply rooted in polytheism, he openly confronts his father, emphasizing the clear misguidance in venerating lifeless idols. It reflects the unwavering commitment to monotheism and the responsibility to call others, even close kin, towards truth and righteousness.

translation: And thus did We show Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth that he would be among the certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine method of strengthening Abraham's faith by granting him a profound vision of the vastness and order of the universe. It signifies that true certainty in faith arises from witnessing or contemplating the signs of God's creation, reinforcing the belief in His sovereignty and power.

translation: When night covered him, he saw a star and said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said, "I do not love those that disappear."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the journey of a seeker grappling with the concept of divinity, initially attributing godhood to observable celestial phenomena. It signifies the human tendency to identify the divine with powerful and evident signs, yet also a discerning mind that recognizes their impermanence and thus rejects them as ultimate beings.

translation: When he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people gone astray."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to seek tangible signs as evidence of divine guidance, reflecting the struggle to find and accept spiritual truth. It underscores the acknowledgment that guidance from God is essential and cannot be based solely on observable phenomena, emphasizing the need for sincere faith and divine assistance to avoid misguidance.

translation: So when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my Lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the process of Abraham’s rejection of idolatry; by observing nature, he recognizes the limitations of worshipping the sun or other celestial bodies, affirming his belief in the One true God who transcends such created things. His declaration signifies a clear disassociation from the polytheistic practices of his people, emphasizing monotheism and the rejection of false deities.

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face sincerely towards He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to truth, and I am not among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse expresses the pure monotheistic devotion of the Prophet, emphasizing his sincere and unwavering commitment to worshiping the one true Creator alone, rejecting any form of idolatry or associating partners with God.

translation: And he argued with his people, saying, "Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then remember?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the firmness and confidence of a believer who, despite opposition, trusts the guidance of Allah and does not fear any false deities or forms of shirk posed by others. It highlights the importance of relying on divine guidance and knowledge over human argument, recognizing that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing and that ultimately, only what He wills will occur.

translation: And how should I fear what you associate with Allah while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down any authority? So which of the two parties is more deserving of security, if you should know?
interpretation: This verse challenges the logic of fearing false deities or partners besides Allah, while failing to fear the grave sin of associating partners with Allah itself. It emphasizes that true security and peace come from recognizing and submitting to the authority of Allah alone, as He alone possesses ultimate power and control. By associating others with Allah without any divine sanction, one invites insecurity and loss of true guidance.

translation: Those who have believed and whose faith has not been mixed with injustice — for them is security, and they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purity of faith, indicating that true belief must remain untainted by injustice or wrongdoing. It conveys that when believers uphold justice and avoid oppressive deeds, they attain inner peace and guidance. Hence, the security mentioned is both spiritual tranquility and protection in this life and the hereafter, signifying that ethical conduct is inseparable from genuine faith.

translation: And this was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people; We raise in degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that God provided Prophet Abraham with clear evidence and guidance to call his people to the truth, demonstrating that divine wisdom and knowledge govern whom God elevates in status and rank. It teaches that God's judgments are based on profound wisdom and knowledge, and individuals are raised or honored according to God's will and wisdom, particularly those who are steadfast in faith and righteousness.

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob; each We guided. And Noah We guided before; and among his descendants, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of divine guidance bestowed upon righteous individuals across generations. It serves to affirm that God's favor and guidance are a result of sincere faith and good deeds, and that He rewards those who consistently strive for righteousness, regardless of their lineage or time period.

translation: And Zakariya and Yahya and Isa and Ilyas - all were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary piety and righteousness of these prophets, emphasizing that their devotion and moral integrity serve as a model for believers to emulate in their own spiritual and ethical conduct.

translation: And [mention] Isma'il, and Al-Yasa', and Yunus, and Lut; and each one We favored over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and blessings granted to these prophets by God, emphasizing that each was chosen above others by virtue of their extraordinary faith, perseverance, and ability to guide their people. It underscores the concept that God's favor is bestowed upon select individuals to serve as exemplary guides and reminders for humanity.

translation: And from their fathers and their descendants and their brothers - and We chose them and guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special selection and guidance granted by God to a chosen group, signifying that divine guidance transcends mere familial ties and is instead a matter of divine will and favor, leading those chosen towards a righteous and straight path in life.

translation: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills among His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, then the deeds they were doing would have been rendered void.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that true guidance is a gift from Allah, granted to those He chooses according to His wisdom. It emphasizes that associating partners with Allah (shirk) not only corrupts the foundation of one's faith but also nullifies the value of all their good deeds, highlighting the fundamental importance of pure monotheism in Islam.

translation: Those are the ones to whom We have given the Scripture, the judgment, and the prophethood; but if they disbelieve therein, We will entrust it to a people who will not be disbelievers therein.
