interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine trust and responsibility given to those who receive revelation and guidance through scripture, wisdom, and prophethood. If a group rejects or fails to uphold this trust through disbelief or neglect, God will appoint another group who sincerely adhere to and preserve the truth. It highlights the principle that truth and guidance are not confined to a fixed group but are maintained through sincere commitment to faith and righteousness.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided; so follow their guidance. Say, "I ask you no reward for it; it is only a reminder for the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following those whom Allah has guided because their example leads to the right path. It also highlights the Prophet's sincerity in delivering the message, as he seeks no worldly compensation, underscoring that the guidance provided is a universal reminder meant for all humankind.

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal when they said, "Allah did not reveal anything to a human being." Say, "Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as light and guidance to the people? You make it into papers you display but conceal much, and you were taught that which you knew not, neither you nor your forefathers." Say, "Allah," then leave them in their discourse, amusing themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of underestimating the reality and magnitude of God's revelation. It highlights how some people deny that God has revealed anything to humans, thereby failing to recognize divine wisdom and authority. The verse urges recognition of God's role as the ultimate source of revealed guidance, exemplified by the Torah given to Moses, which served as a beacon for humanity. Furthermore, it criticizes those who selectively present or conceal parts of divine scripture for their purposes, thus distorting the original message. Ultimately, the verse calls for trusting in God's revelation and dismissing the frivolous disputes of deniers, implying that true understanding comes from acknowledging God's reality and accepting His guidance fully.

translation: And this is a blessed Book We have revealed, confirming what was before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they maintain their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a continuation and confirmation of previous divine scriptures, and it serves as a warning and guidance primarily to Mecca ('the Mother of Cities') and its surroundings. Believers who have faith in the Hereafter accept the truth of this revelation wholeheartedly and demonstrate that belief through their consistent observance of prayer, showing that faith and practice are intertwined.

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah or says, "It has been inspired to me," while nothing has been inspired to him, or who says, "I will reveal like what Allah has revealed?" But you will see the wrongdoers when they are in the overwhelming pangs of death while the angels are extending their hands, [saying], "Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth and [for] your being, toward His verses, arrogant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of falsely attributing words to Allah or claiming divine revelation without truth. It underscores the severe consequences for such arrogance and deceit, emphasizing that in the moment of death, wrongdoers will face the reality of their falsehoods and the just punishment decreed by Allah for their injustice and pride in rejecting His signs.

translation: And indeed, you have come to Us individually, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We granted you as a trust on your backs. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed to be partners with Allah. Indeed, the ties between you have been severed, and what you used to claim has forsaken you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reality of standing alone before God on the Day of Judgment, returning to the original state of creation without any worldly benefits or worldly intercessors to assist. It highlights that the supposed partners or intercessors relied upon in life will be absent, showing the futility of assigning partners with God or relying on anything besides Him. It serves as a reminder that all claims of association or support that contradict monotheism will be invalidated, and individuals will be fully responsible for their deeds.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Splitter of the grain and the date stone. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah; so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power to create life and bring forth growth from lifeless seeds, symbolizing His ability to resurrect the dead and control the cycle of life and death. It serves as a reminder that the same divine force responsible for the natural processes in the world is also capable of resurrection, challenging those who deny His power and encouraging reflection on His omnipotence.

translation: He splits the dawn and made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for calculation. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's precise control and order over the natural phenomena, reflecting His immense power and wisdom. The alternation of day and night, the calculated movements of the sun and moon, all serve as signs of His deliberate planning and mastery over the universe, guiding human understanding of time and encouraging reflection on His greatness.

translation: And He it is Who made for you the stars that you may be guided by them through the darknesses of the land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in creating the stars as a means of guidance, symbolizing that signs from God provide direction in life’s uncertainties. It encourages the recognition of natural phenomena as manifestations of God's guidance, meant for thoughtful reflection and understanding by those who seek knowledge and clarity in their faith and conduct.

translation: And He it is Who created you from a single soul, and made its mate from it, that he might dwell with her in tranquility. And when he covers her, she carries a light burden and continues therein. And when it grows heavy, they both invoke Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a good [child], we will surely be among the grateful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and common origin of all human beings, highlighting that all people come from a single soul created by God. It signifies the fundamental connectedness of humanity and the divine design of human relationships. The verse also serves as a reminder for people to ponder these signs deeply and derive understanding about their existence and dependence on God.

translation: And He it is Who sends down water from the sky, and with it We bring forth vegetation of every kind; from it We produce green plants from which We bring forth grain piled up, and from the palm trees, of its spathes come clusters of dates hanging low; and gardens of grapes, olives, and pomegranates, all similar and yet different. Look at their fruit when they bear fruit and their ripeness. Surely in this are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power and wisdom in the natural processes by which Allah nurtures life through rain, leading to the growth of diverse vegetation and fruits. It teaches believers to observe and reflect on the variety, order, and beauty in creation as clear signs of Allah's existence, mercy, and sustenance, thereby strengthening faith through contemplation of the natural world.

translation: And they have made the jinn, their creation, as partners with Allah, and they have attributed to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wrongful attribution of partners and offspring to Allah without any basis or knowledge. It emphasizes the purity and uniqueness of Allah's divinity, rejecting any associating of His creation with Him. The verse calls attention to the misguided beliefs of those who engage in such practices and elevates Allah above their false descriptions, underscoring His transcendence and sole sovereignty.

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a consort? He created everything, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and oneness of God, highlighting that He is the sole Creator of all existence. It refutes any notion of Him having offspring or partners, underscoring His transcendence beyond human attributes and relationships.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of everything that exists. It commands sincere worship directed only to Him, highlighting His exclusive right to be worshipped and His complete control over all affairs. It reminds believers to recognize His authority and trust in His wisdom and power in managing the universe and their lives.

translation: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transcendence and omnipotence of God. It teaches that human senses and perceptions are limited and cannot fully comprehend God's essence, yet God perceives all things completely, encompassing everything with His knowledge. It emphasizes that God's awareness and subtlety are beyond human reach, reminding us of the vast gap between Creator and creation.

translation: Indeed, there have come to you clear proofs from your Lord. So whoever sees (understands) will benefit for himself, and whoever is blind (to it) will be against himself. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in accepting and understanding divine guidance. The 'clear proofs' refer to the undeniable signs and revelations from God, which, if perceived and internalized, bring benefit to the individual alone. Conversely, rejection or blindness to these signs harms only oneself, underscoring that the Prophet's role is to convey the message, not to enforce belief or protect individuals from the consequences of their choices.

translation: And thus We alternate the verses so that they may say, "You have studied," and We make it clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in the arrangement of the Quranic verses, highlighting that their variation and alternation serve multiple purposes: some may criticize it as if the Prophet merely studied before reciting, but the clarity and presentation are designed for those who possess knowledge and understanding, enabling them to grasp the deeper meanings and benefits.

translation: Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord; there is no deity except Him. And turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastly adhering to the divine guidance revealed to the Prophet, affirming the oneness of God as the fundamental belief, while also instructing to distance oneself from polytheistic practices and ideologies that contradict the monotheistic message.

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated [others with Him]; and We have not appointed you over them as a guardian, nor are you responsible for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the persistence of shirk (associating partners with Allah) is ultimately within Allah's wisdom and decree. The Prophet Muhammad is reminded that his role is to convey the message, not to control the choices of people or to enforce guidance upon them. Responsibility for their actions lies with themselves, and the Prophet is not an overseer upon them.

translation: And do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah out of ignorance. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of maintaining respect even towards those holding differing beliefs, warning against provocation that may lead to greater disrespect towards the Divine. It implies that every community finds value and satisfaction in their own practices, and ultimately, all will be accountable to God, who has full knowledge of their actions. Therefore, one must exercise patience and avoid escalating conflict, understanding that judgment rests solely with God.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, "The signs are only with Allah," and what makes you perceive that when the signs do come, they will believe?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness of those who refuse to believe despite their claims that they would believe if they saw a sign. It reveals that their oaths are empty because true guidance and belief come from Allah alone; signs themselves are in His control, and even clear signs may not compel them to faith if Allah wills otherwise. This serves as a reminder that belief is ultimately a matter of divine will and sincere acceptance, not just witnessing miracles.

translation: And We turn their hearts and their eyes away; they do not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights how, due to persistent rejection and stubbornness in disbelief, the hearts and eyes of such individuals are turned away by divine decree, causing them to remain oblivious and misguided in their arrogance, unable to perceive the truth as they once did. It illustrates the spiritual consequence of persistent denial and the resulting estrangement from guidance.

translation: And if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We gathered together every kind of thing before them, they would not believe unless Allah wills. But most of them, [of that], are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith is ultimately dependent on God's will, not merely on witnessing extraordinary signs or miraculous events. Even if the most convincing evidence were presented—angels descending, the dead speaking, or all things being gathered—people would not believe unless God allows it. This teaches us that spiritual insight and acceptance of truth are granted by divine grace, and human understanding alone is insufficient to compel genuine faith.

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy — devils among mankind and jinn — who inspire one another with adorned speech to deceive. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it; so leave them and what they invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights that opposition to divine truth is not random but coordinated by forces that incite falsehood and deception. It suggests that the challenges prophets face are part of a greater plan, where misguidance is allowed to test faith and perseverance. God's will ultimately controls these events, emphasizing that humans should remain patient and not be swayed by the fabrications of these adversaries.

translation: And so that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline towards it, and that they may be pleased with it and commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse reveals how some false teachings or worldly desires are presented in a way to captivate the hearts of disbelievers, causing them to favor and accept such ideas. It indicates a divine wisdom that allows the hearts of those who reject the Hereafter to be inclined towards their wrongful actions and misconceptions, leading them to persist in their misdeeds. This serves as both a test and a manifest consequence of their rejection, highlighting the contrast between belief and disbelief.

translation: Should I seek a judge other than Allah, while He is the one who has sent down to you the Book fully detailed? And those to whom We gave the Scripture know that it is revealed from your Lord in truth, so be not among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate judgment and authority belong to Allah alone, who has revealed the detailed, clear guidance through the Qur'an. It cautions against doubting the divine origin of the scripture, affirming that those endowed with prior scriptures recognize its truth, thus urging believers to trust in Allah's guidance and reject skepticism about His judgment.

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty and unchangeability of God's decree. It assures believers that God's promises and commands are fulfilled with perfect truth and justice, and that His words are steadfast and cannot be altered by anyone. This underlines the reliability of divine guidance and the ultimate justice embedded in God's statutes.

translation: And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but misjudging.
interpretation: This verse warns against blindly following the majority, especially when their guidance leads away from divine truth. It emphasizes that many people act on conjecture and speculation rather than knowledge, resulting in erroneous paths. Therefore, one must adhere to the clear guidance from Allah rather than be swayed by popular opinion.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the most knowing of who goes astray from His way, and He is the most knowing of the guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect and comprehensive knowledge of human guidance and misguidance. It signifies that Allah alone knows the true state of every individual's heart and the reasons behind their choices, reminding us that ultimate guidance is in His hands and that He withholds or grants it according to His wisdom and justice.

translation: So eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming only those foods that have been sanctified by invoking the name of Allah, reflecting an obedience to divine guidance and an acknowledgment of Allah’s authority. It suggests that true faith is not only in belief but also demonstrated through adherence to the prescribed commands, including dietary laws, thereby linking spiritual belief directly with practical actions.

translation: And why do you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has explained to you what He has forbidden you, except in cases of necessity? Indeed, many mislead [others] by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord - He is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse teaches that consuming food needs to be accompanied by the acknowledgment of Allah through His name, signifying sanctification and gratitude. It also highlights the divine guidance provided on what is prohibited and permits exceptions only in situations of dire necessity, underscoring Allah's mercy. The verse warns against following desires without knowledge, which leads to misguidance, and reaffirms that Allah is fully aware of those who transgress His limits.

translation: And leave aside the apparent sin and its hidden aspect; indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit.
interpretation: This verse urges believers to avoid not only the obvious sins but also those concealed or subtle wrongdoings, emphasizing that all forms of sin—whether outwardly visible or inwardly concealed—are accountable before God, and individuals will receive just recompense for all their actions.

translation: And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is sinful. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed, you would be associators (polytheists).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging Allah's name when consuming food, highlighting that neglecting this act is considered a sin. It also warns against following the deceptive whispers of devils who incite disputes about such matters to confuse believers. Obeying such misleading instructions equates to associating others with Allah, which undermines the core principle of monotheism in Islam. Thus, believers are reminded to seek certainty and purity in their actions by adhering strictly to divine guidance.

translation: Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people the same as one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound contrast between those who have received guidance from Allah—akin to being brought from death to life and given light to navigate the world—and those who remain in spiritual darkness, unable to find their way. It emphasizes that true enlightenment transforms a person's existence, enabling righteous conduct and understanding, while the disbelievers prefer to stay in denial, finding their misguided deeds deceptive and pleasing because they have not accepted divine guidance.

translation: And thus We have made in every city the prominent criminals of it plot within it, but they do not plot except against themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that those who commit serious wrongdoings and schemes in their communities ultimately bring harm upon themselves. Their plans and machinations, no matter how cunning, eventually lead to their own downfall, even if they are initially unaware of this consequence.

translation: And when a sign (verse) comes to them, they say, "We will not believe until we are given like what was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah knows best where to place His message. The criminals will suffer humiliation in the sight of Allah and severe punishment for their plotting.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who demand extraordinary miracles as a condition for belief, disregarding the clear signs already provided. It emphasizes that divine wisdom determines how revelation is delivered, not human demand, and warns that the arrogance and scheming of such disbelievers leads to their disgrace and severe punishment from Allah.

translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide, He expands his chest to Islam; and whoever He wants to send astray, He makes his chest tight and constricted as though he is climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that guidance and misguidance are ultimately determined by Allah's will. When Allah intends to guide a person, He grants them openness, acceptance, and ease in embracing Islam—symbolized by the expansion of the chest. Conversely, when He intends to lead someone astray, their heart becomes constricted and burdened, making faith feel difficult and suffocating, akin to the hardship of climbing into the sky. Therefore, true belief and acceptance stem from divine facilitation, while rejection is a result of spiritual obstruction placed by Allah upon those who persist in disbelief.

translation: And this is the path of your Lord, straight; We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the guidance provided by Allah is clear and direct, serving as a straight path for believers. The detailed verses are meant to enlighten and remind those who are willing to reflect and remember, signifying that faith requires conscious attention and receptiveness to divine guidance.

translation: They will have the Home of Peace with their Lord; and He is their Protector because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward awaiting the righteous: a peaceful abode in the presence of God. It highlights that their actions in this life have earned them divine protection and the ultimate tranquility that comes from being close to their Lord.

translation: And [warn of] the Day when He will gather them all together and say to the jinn, "O company of jinn, you have [misled] much of mankind." And their allies among mankind will say, "Our Lord, we benefited from each other, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your residence, abiding eternally therein, except for what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the comprehensive accountability on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that the jinn and humans, despite their differences, influenced each other's misguidance leading to collective responsibility. It highlights that every soul is bound by the decreed lifespan and ultimate fate determined by God, who is all-wise and all-knowing. It warns that the Fire is the eternal abode for those who deviated, except by God's mercy and will, underscoring divine justice balanced with wisdom and knowledge.

translation: And thus do We give some of the wrongdoers power over others because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a divine consequence where the wrongdoing or injustices committed by some lead to their being granted dominance over others as a form of retribution or trial. It reflects the principle that the misuse of power and injustice have repercussions not only upon the individual but also upon their societal relations, as Allah allows certain oppressors to gain control over others in accordance with their deeds, highlighting both the reality of worldly balance and the ultimate accountability before God.

translation: O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They said, "We bear witness against ourselves." And the worldly life deluded them, and they bore witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal responsibility of all humanity and jinn to heed the messengers sent to them, warning of the inevitable meeting with their Lord on the Day of Judgment. It illustrates how some individuals, despite bearing witness to the truth through the messengers, become deceived by the allurements and distractions of worldly life. This deception leads them to deny the truth of their own testimony, resulting in their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning that neglecting the message due to the temptations of earthly life results in self-inflicted loss and spiritual ruin.

translation: That is because never would your Lord destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice: God does not punish entire communities without due cause and without giving them the opportunity to be mindful and repent. It underscores that destruction or punishment is not arbitrary but is a response to wrongdoing, and that neglect or heedlessness among the people does not exempt them from accountability.

translation: And for each [person] is a reward according to what they have done. And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice, affirming that every individual will receive recompense precisely corresponding to their deeds. It reassures believers that no action, good or bad, escapes God's knowledge, underscoring His complete awareness and fairness in judgment.

translation: And your Lord is the Free of need, the Merciful. If He wills, He can remove you and will bring forth after you another people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and mercy of God. It reminds us that while God is ever-merciful and generous, He is also the ultimate authority who can replace entire communities if they are ungrateful or disobedient. Our existence and continuation are dependent on His will, highlighting the importance of humility, obedience, and constant remembrance of His mercy and power.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is to come, and you will not be able to prevent it.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty of the divine promise and judgment; no one can escape or delay what Allah has decreed, underscoring the inevitability of the Day of Reckoning and the ultimate accountability before God.

translation: Say, "O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. And you will know who will have the best outcome in the Hereafter. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of divine justice and the ultimate failure of those who act unjustly. It encourages steadfastness in righteousness amidst opposition, assuring that sincere efforts in obedience to God are not in vain and that the true success belongs to those who uphold justice and truth.

translation: And they assign to Allah from what He has produced of crops and livestock a share, saying, "This is for Allah," according to their claim, and "This is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah — this reaches their partners. Evil is that which they judge.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the unjust practice of attributing portions of what belongs to Allah to false partners or idols, thereby corrupting the purity of worship and rightful ownership. It highlights the futility and wrongfulness of associating others with Allah in matters of divine right, as such fabrications neither benefit Allah nor adhere to true faith. The verse warns against misjudgments and invalid divisions that lead people away from sincere monotheism.

translation: And thus it was made pleasing to many of the polytheists to kill their children, to bring about their own destruction and to cover up their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and what they invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights how misguided beliefs can lead people to commit grievous acts, such as killing their children, driven by distorted notions of preserving their faith. It emphasizes that such actions are contrary to divine will and wisdom, and it instructs to leave those who fabricate such falsehoods to their own devices without engaging in dispute, as their actions stem from delusion rather than truth.

translation: And they say, "These (cattle) are livestock and crops of stone, and none will eat them except those we will," claiming by their assumption. And (some) cattle whose backs are forbidden (for riding), and cattle upon which they do not mention the name of Allah - falsely attributing lies to Him. He will surely recompense them for what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse addresses the distorted beliefs and customs that some people invent concerning lawful and unlawful animals and practices, attributing false rulings and prohibitions to God without knowledge. It warns that such fabrications—be they regarding the status of animals, dietary laws, or neglecting to mention God's name—are baseless and offensive to divine wisdom, and that those who engage in these falsehoods will face recompense for their misguidance and disrespect towards the divine ordinances.

translation: And they say, "There is nothing in the bellies of these cattle for our males, and it is forbidden for our wives," while indeed, for those thereof are shares and for the others, the harvest is a due. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the unjust reasoning of those who prohibit themselves and their families from consuming what Allah has permitted, based on false beliefs and customs. It teaches that Allah has wisely allocated portions of livestock's produce and benefits to different members of the community, and denying this equitable sharing is a misguidance. Ultimately, Allah's knowledge and wisdom encompass all matters, and He will justly recompense those who reject His laws and blame Him unjustly.

translation: Indeed, those who kill their children foolishly without knowledge and forbid what Allah has provided for them, inventing a lie against Allah, they have gone astray and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns the heinous act of killing one's children out of ignorance and foolishness, illustrating it as a grave sin rooted in false beliefs and a wrongful attempt to challenge divine provisions. It emphasizes that such actions stem from misguidance and a lack of true guidance, warning against fabricating justifications that oppose Allah's wisdom and blessings.

translation: And He it is Who produces gardens trellised and untrellised, and date palms, and crops of different shape and taste (its fruits and its seeds) and olives, and pomegranates, similar (in kind) and different (in taste). Eat of their fruit when they ripen, but pay the due thereof (its Zakat, according to Allah's Orders, 1/10th or 1/20th) on the day of its harvest, and waste not by extravagance. Verily, He likes not Al-Musrifun (those who waste by extravagance).
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine wisdom and benevolence in creating diverse forms of sustenance for humanity, emphasizing the balance between enjoying Allah's provisions and fulfilling one's responsibilities such as giving the due charity at harvest. Furthermore, it warns against excess and wastefulness, highlighting that God disapproves of those who squander resources, encouraging moderation and gratitude.

translation: And among the livestock are those for burden and those for food. Eat from what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse guides believers to recognize the blessings of Allah in providing different types of livestock for both carrying loads and as a source of nourishment. It emphasizes the importance of consuming what is lawful and provided by Allah while warning against following the temptations of Satan, which can lead them away from righteousness and obedience, thus reinforcing the need for vigilance and adherence to divine guidance.

translation: Eight pairs; of the sheep two and of the goats two. Say, "Is it the males that He has forbidden or the females? Or is it that He has taken upon Himself a covenant with you, so you are through the male livestock unable to have?" Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges the beliefs of those who impose arbitrary prohibitions on certain animals, questioning whether the restriction is on the males or females, or based on some covenant. It emphasizes the importance of basing religious rulings on clear evidence rather than conjecture or imitation, urging believers to seek knowledge and truth rather than follow unfounded prohibitions.

translation: Among the camels, two and among the cattle, two. Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden, or the two females? Or was it that the wombs of the females that He aims at? Or were you witnesses when Allah charged you with this?" Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse challenges false attributions made to divine law, emphasizing that prohibitions must be understood with precise knowledge rather than assumptions or fabricated claims. It highlights the injustice of fabricating religious rulings to misguide others, urging sincere adherence to God's guidance and condemning deceit that leads people astray.

translation: Say, "I do not find within that which was revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal, or blood spilled out, or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse sets clear boundaries regarding lawful and unlawful foods, emphasizing that what is prohibited is inherently harmful or impure, such as carrion, blood, and pork, or food dedicated to others besides Allah. However, it highlights the principle of necessity and mercy in Islamic law: if someone is compelled by dire need to consume forbidden items without intention or excess, Allah's forgiveness and compassion accommodate such circumstances. This demonstrates Islam's balance between strict adherence to divine commands and compassionate consideration for human hardship.

translation: And for those who follow Judaism, We forbade every animal with claw. And of the cattle and the sheep, We forbade to them their fat, except what is on their backs or that which is joined to the bone, or what is mixed with a bone. That was recompense for their injustice. And indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the specific dietary restrictions ordained for the Jewish people as a consequence of their disobedience and transgression. It serves as a reminder that God's laws and prohibitions are tailored to the behavior and circumstances of different communities. The restrictions on certain fats symbolize boundaries set due to their past misdeeds, emphasizing that divine commandments are both a form of guidance and a measure of justice, reflecting consequences for injustice while maintaining the truth and wisdom behind God's decrees.

translation: So if they deny you, say, 'Your Lord is the Possessor of vast mercy, but His punishment cannot be averted from the sinful people.'
interpretation: This verse teaches that God's mercy is immense and encompasses all, offering hope and forgiveness; however, it also establishes that His justice is certain and inescapable, especially for those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the truth, emphasizing the balance between divine compassion and accountability.

translation: Those who associate partners with Allah will say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated partners, nor would our ancestors, nor would we have forbidden anything." Thus did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but assumption, and you are only guessing."
interpretation: This verse addresses the futile excuse of polytheists who claim that associating partners with Allah was not their choice but fate, dismissing personal responsibility. It highlights a recurring pattern where previous peoples made similar false claims and faced consequences. The verse challenges them to produce any evidence or knowledge supporting their claims, exposing that their belief is based on conjecture and unfounded assumptions rather than knowledge. This serves as a reminder that true guidance comes from knowledge and revelation, not mere speculation.

translation: Say, "For Allah is the clear proof." If He had willed, He would have guided you all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate guidance and truth belong solely to Allah. No matter the efforts of any person or group, it is only by Allah's will that guidance is granted. The phrase highlights both Allah's sovereignty and the necessity for humans to acknowledge their dependence on Him for true understanding and guidance.

translation: Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you: [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them; and do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed; and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right; and do not commit oppression among yourselves."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the prohibitions set by Allah, highlighting that one should not follow the desires of those who reject faith or deny the Hereafter. It underlines that obedience to divine commandments is essential to maintain moral integrity and avoid injustice, especially when confronted with false testimonies or practices that contradict divine law.

translation: Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you: [He commands] that you do not associate anything with Him, and to parents, do good, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them. And do not approach immoralities — what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right. This is what He has instructed you that you may use reason."
interpretation: This verse guides humanity to adhere strictly to the prohibitions ordained by God, emphasizing monotheism as paramount. It highlights social ethics such as respect and kindness towards parents and forbids killing children out of fear of poverty, affirming God's provision. It calls for avoidance of all forms of immorality, both overt and hidden, and prohibits unjust killing, underscoring the sanctity of life. The closing statement encourages reflection and rational understanding, implying that these divine commands are meant to cultivate a just, compassionate, and conscientious society.

translation: And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. This is what He instructs you that you may take heed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice, responsibility, and integrity in dealings with others, especially in protecting the vulnerable such as orphans. It advocates for treating an orphan’s property with utmost care until they are mature enough to manage it, ensuring honesty in trade and measurement, and maintaining fairness even when dealing with close relatives. It also reminds believers not to overburden themselves beyond their capacity and to uphold their promises to Allah, highlighting the ethical and moral conduct expected from them as a means to become mindful and conscious servants.

translation: And indeed, this is My straight path, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the prescribed path of guidance revealed by God, warning against deviating onto other paths that lead to division and alienation from divine truth. It highlights that steadfastness on the straight path is crucial for attaining piety and righteousness.

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture complete for him who does right, and an explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the revelation given to Moses was thorough and precise, serving as clear guidance and a source of mercy. Its purpose is to encourage belief in the ultimate meeting with God, emphasizing that the divine message is both comprehensive and meant for people who strive to do good.

translation: And this is a blessed Book which We have revealed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and blessing of the Qur'an, urging believers to adhere to its guidance and maintain consciousness of God (taqwa) so that they may be granted mercy and favor in this life and the hereafter.

translation: That you say, "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us, and indeed we were unaware of their study."
interpretation: This verse addresses the claim that the revelation was limited to previous groups and that they were unaware of others' scriptures. It emphasizes the continuity and universality of divine revelation, countering the notion that God's guidance is confined to certain people or times.

translation: Or do they say, "If only a scripture had been sent down to us, we would be better guided than they"? But there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord and a guidance and mercy. So who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our verses with the worst punishment for their turning away.
interpretation: This verse addresses the attitude of those who demand a specific scripture or miracle to believe, claiming they would be better guided if it were sent to them. It highlights that clear evidence, guidance, and mercy have already been provided by Allah, yet some still reject and deny these divine signs. Their denial and turning away represent profound injustice and lead to severe consequences. Thus, the verse serves as a reminder that rejecting clear divine guidance is a grave act deserving of strong recompense.

translation: Do they wait except that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? On the Day that some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned goodness through its faith. Say, "Wait; indeed, we are waiting."
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the futility of delaying belief until that moment. It emphasizes that faith must be firmly established before the signs and the coming of the Lord; otherwise, on the Day of Judgment, no newfound belief will avail a person. The verse also portrays the inevitability and seriousness of the Day, urging patience and readiness while affirming the certainty of divine justice.

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you, [O Muhammad], are not [associated] with them in anything. Their affair is only to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that division within the religion is not sanctioned or approved. The Prophet is instructed not to align himself with these sects, indicating that unity in faith is essential. Ultimately, judgment and accountability for such divisions belong solely to Allah, reaffirming that human beings must be cautious about causing schisms, as Allah will make known the true nature of everyone's deeds on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Whoever brings a good deed will receive ten times as much, but whoever brings an evil deed will be recompensed only with its like; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and generosity of Allah by promising a manifold reward for good deeds, while ensuring justice by holding individuals accountable for their bad deeds without excess punishment. It underscores the principle that divine recompense is both equitable and magnanimous, encouraging believers to pursue righteousness with the assurance of abundant reward, and cautioning them against wrongdoing knowing that they will be fairly held to account.

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion - the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not among the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the returning to pure monotheism and upright faith exemplified by the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), affirming that true guidance comes from God alone. It stresses the importance of following a clear, uncorrupted path of worship and belief, distancing oneself from polytheism and deviations.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of complete devotion and sincerity in all aspects of life and worship, affirming that every action—from prayer and ritual sacrifice to one's entire existence and even death—should be solely for Allah, highlighting the importance of monotheism and dedicating oneself wholly to the Creator alone.

translation: He has no partner. That is how I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God, affirming that He has no partners or equals. It also highlights the Prophet Muhammad's commitment to this truth as a fundamental principle of faith, underscoring his role as the foremost believer who submits entirely to God's command.

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the sole Lord and Creator of everything. It teaches personal responsibility, indicating that each individual is accountable for their own actions and sins, with no one bearing the burden of another's wrongdoings. Ultimately, all people will return to Allah, who will judge and clarify the matters about which they disagreed, highlighting the importance of recognizing Allah's authority and seeking His guidance.

translation: And He it is Who has made you successors on the earth and has raised some of you above others in ranks, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind the diversity and differences among humans, emphasizing that the varying statuses and provisions are a divine test. It reminds us that worldly ranks are temporary and serve as means to assess our gratitude, responsibility, and humility before God, who balances justice with mercy.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These opening phrases invoke Allah's name and emphasize His mercy and compassion. The letters "Alif, Lam, Meem" are among the mysterious letters (Muqattaʿat) whose exact meaning is known only to Allah, serving as a divine sign that invites contemplation and reflection upon the Quran's miraculous nature.

translation: A book revealed to you so that there is no distress in your heart because of it, to warn thereby and as a reminder to the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the revealed scripture: to provide guidance and reassurance to the Prophet and believers. It highlights that the revelation is meant to remove any burden or doubt from the Prophet's heart, serving both as a warning to those who reject the message and as a reminder to strengthen the faith of the believers.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord and do not follow any guardians besides Him. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the guidance provided by Allah through revelation and warns against following other protectors or leaders who might divert one from His path. It underscores that true success lies in obedience to divine instruction and that neglecting this remembrance and adherence leads to spiritual failure.

translation: And how many a city did We destroy, and Our punishment came to it by night or while they were unaware.
interpretation: This verse underscores the suddenness and inevitability of divine retribution upon communities that persist in wrongdoing and deny the signs of Allah. It emphasizes that destruction can come unexpectedly, either during the night or when people are not expecting it, highlighting the importance of constant vigilance and adherence to righteousness.

translation: So their only response when Our punishment came to them was to say, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates human nature's tendency to recognize faults and injustices only after facing consequences or calamities. It serves as a reminder to preemptively acknowledge and rectify our wrongs rather than admitting them too late when punishment has already arrived.

translation: So let us ask those who were sent before us and let us ask the messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding from previous messengers and those who were sent with guidance before us. It highlights the continuity of divine revelation and encourages reflection on earlier teachings to gain insight and wisdom.

translation: So We relate to them with knowledge, while We were not absent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the recounting of past events or stories to people is done with certainty and knowledge from Allah, affirming that He was always present and fully aware, even if humans were oblivious to those events. It reassures believers that the divine narratives are truthful and that God’s knowledge encompasses all things, past and present.

translation: And the weighing on that Day will be the truth. So whoever's scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment where the deeds of individuals will be weighed with absolute truth, highlighting that genuine righteousness and good actions carry real weight. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad are assured success, illustrating the importance of sincere and consistent moral conduct in achieving true success in the Hereafter.

translation: And those whose scales are light, it is they who have lost themselves, because they used to wrong Our verses.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the metaphorical scales represent the weight of a person's good deeds. Those whose good deeds are insufficient or 'light' have essentially harmed themselves by neglecting or denying God's signs. It highlights the consequence of injustice towards divine guidance leading to self-loss and failure in the hereafter.

translation: And indeed, We have established you upon the earth and made for you therein livelihoods. Little is the thanks you give.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the blessings and provisions we enjoy are granted by God through His mercy and wisdom. Despite being firmly established on earth with means to sustain ourselves, humans rarely show true gratitude. The verse calls for mindfulness and appreciation of the favors we receive, underlining that thankfulness is a fundamental attitude expected from believers towards their Creator.

translation: And indeed, We created you, then fashioned you; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblees; he was not of those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of human beings as intentional creations of God, fashioned with care and bestowed with honor above angels, as evidenced by the command to prostrate to Adam. It also emphasizes the deliberate choice of Iblees to reject God's command, signifying arrogance and disobedience that separates him from the obedient beings, setting the stage for the ongoing struggle between submission to God and rebellion.

translation: He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" He said, "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and pride of Iblis (Satan) in defying Allah's command to prostrate before Adam. His claim of superiority based on the nature of his creation—fire versus clay—indicates how his pride led to his downfall, emphasizing the lesson that arrogance and self-exaltation lead to disobedience to God and ultimately to one's ruin.

translation: He said, "Descend from it, for you are to me no longer worthy of arrogance therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the humiliated."
interpretation: This verse conveys the consequence of arrogance and disobedience to God. It teaches that pride leads to humiliation and removal from a favored state; one must recognize their limitations and adopt humility to remain in a good standing with God.

translation: He said, 'Look at me to the Day they will be resurrected.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Abraham's challenge to his people, urging them to consider the reality of the Resurrection. It emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, where all will be brought back to life and held accountable for their deeds, urging reflection on the afterlife and the consequences of disbelief.

translation: He said, "Indeed, you are among the messengers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition and affirmation of a person's role as a messenger or prophet. It signifies a divine acknowledgment of their responsibility to convey God's message and the trust placed in them to guide people towards righteousness.

translation: He said, "Because You have misled me, I will ambush them on Your straight path."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Satan admits his intent to mislead humanity by lying in wait along the straight path ordained by God, symbolizing the deliberate effort to divert people from guidance and righteousness.

translation: Then We will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the comprehensive manner in which divine punishment or trials may befall those who persist in ingratitude and rebellion against God, coming from all directions—front, back, right, and left—signifying that no escape is possible. It highlights human ingratitude even in the face of clear evidences and favors from God, emphasizing the consequences of such persistent ungratefulness.

translation: He said, "Get out of it, disgraced and expelled. Whoever follows you among them - I will surely fill Hell with all of you."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of defying divine commands and aligning oneself with evil. It emphasizes the inevitability of punishment for those who persist in wrongful paths, highlighting that not only the initial transgressor but also those who follow will face accountability. The imagery of being expelled in disgrace and the threat of filling Hell signifies total rejection and severe retribution for persistent disobedience.

translation: And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the command and the boundary set by God for Adam and his wife, emphasizing the importance of obedience and restraint. It reflects on the concept that while humans are granted freedom and blessings, they must recognize limits established by divine wisdom. Crossing these limits leads to injustice and wrongdoing, showing that true harmony and righteousness come from adhering to God's guidance.

translation: Then Satan whispered to them to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts. He said, "Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Satan exploits human curiosity and desire to mislead them. He tempts Adam and Eve by suggesting that God's prohibition is out of jealousy or to deny them elevated status or immortality, thereby sowing doubt about God's wisdom and commands. It warns us about the subtlety of Satan's whispers that seek to distort truth and encourage disobedience by appealing to false desires and misconceptions.

translation: And I swear by the two _Ṭūrs_ (mountains), Indeed I am to you from among the sincere advisors.
interpretation: This verse reflects a solemn oath taken by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to assert the truthfulness and sincerity of his message. By swearing upon the two sacred mountains, often interpreted as Mount Sinai and Mount Tur, it emphasizes his role as a faithful and honest warner and adviser to his people.

translation: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and made them fall, and thus their private parts became apparent to them. They began to cover themselves with the leaves of Paradise. Their Lord called out to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is your clear enemy?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when Adam and Eve disobeyed God's command by succumbing to Satan's temptation, resulting in a loss of their original state of innocence. The revelation of their nakedness symbolizes the awakening of human consciousness and awareness of their own imperfections. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of yielding to temptation and the ever-present nature of Satan as an adversary to humanity.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound humility and recognition of human fallibility before God. It teaches that acknowledging one's mistakes and turning to God with sincere repentance and hope for His mercy is essential. Without God's forgiveness and mercy, efforts and deeds ultimately result in loss, emphasizing God's central role in salvation and success.

translation: He said, "Descend, being to one another enemies, and for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time."
interpretation: This verse reflects God's command to humanity after their initial encounter in the higher realms, indicating that humans and jinn are destined to live on Earth in mutual enmity. The phrase underscores the inherent challenges and conflicts in human relationships and existence, but also acknowledges the Earth as a temporary abode where people have the opportunity to live, work, and find sustenance until their appointed time in the hereafter.

translation: In it you live, and in it you die, and from it you will be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental role of the earth as the origin and end of human life. It signifies that human existence is deeply connected to the earth—our life begins on it, our physical life ends within it through death, and ultimately, on the Day of Resurrection, all will be resurrected from it. This highlights the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of resurrection, reminding believers of the cycle of life decreed by Allah.

translation: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to cover your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness—that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights that while physical clothing serves to cover our bodies and beautify us, the garment of righteousness, meaning piety and God-consciousness, is far superior because it guards our morality and dignity. True honor arises not from outward appearances but from inner virtue, and recognizing this divine guidance leads us to mindfulness of God.

translation: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to expose their shame. Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse warns humanity of Satan's cunning tactics to lead them astray, just as he deceived Adam and Eve into disobedience. The mention of Satan revealing their shame symbolizes not only physical exposure but also spiritual vulnerability caused by sin. The verse emphasizes that Satan and his followers have unseen influence over humans, silently working to misguide those who reject faith. It conveys that disbelief makes one susceptible to becoming an ally or follower of such evil forces, highlighting the importance of vigilance and firm faith to resist temptation.

translation: And when they commit an immoral act, they say, "We found our fathers doing it," and Allah has commanded us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command immorality. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse criticizes the justification of sinful actions by appealing to ancestral traditions, emphasizing that such reasoning is invalid because Allah never commands wrongdoing. It teaches that divine guidance is inherently just and moral, and one should not attribute unjust practices to God based on inherited customs without knowledge or evidence.

translation: Say, "My Lord has commanded justice and that you maintain yourselves [in worship] at every place of prayer, and invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion." Just as He originated you, you will return [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing justice in all aspects of life and maintaining sincerity and dedication in worship. It calls for turning towards God with pure devotion at every place of prayer, underscoring a consistent, heartfelt connection regardless of location. It also reminds believers of their origin and eventual return to God, highlighting accountability and the continuous cycle of life and divine worship.

translation: They are of two groups: one guided, and the other upon error. Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think that they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the division between those who follow the guidance of Allah and those who have fallen into misguidance. The ones who stray have chosen false guides—represented here as devils—instead of turning to the true guidance from Allah. Their illusion of being rightly guided is a delusion, masking their deviation and refusal to accept divine truth.

translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and restraint in both appearance and consumption. It encourages believers to present themselves properly and respectfully when coming to places of worship, highlighting the significance of dignity in communal spirituality. Simultaneously, it warns against extravagance and wastefulness, reminding that balance and moderation in eating and drinking are pleasing to God. Overall, it instills a balanced approach to life that combines reverence, self-discipline, and mindfulness of God’s displeasure towards excessiveness.

translation: Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?" Say, "They are for those who believe during the life of this world, exclusively on the Day of Resurrection." Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and adornments provided by Allah are lawful and intended for the enjoyment of the believers in this worldly life. It rejects the idea that such worldly pleasures are inherently forbidden, affirming that the lawful enjoyment of good provisions is a part of a believer's rightful share. Moreover, it indicates that on the Day of Resurrection, these blessings will be reserved solely for the faithful, highlighting the contrast between the worldly life and the hereafter. This serves to remind believers that worldly enjoyment is permissible within divine limits and that true and ultimate reward and ownership belong to them in the afterlife.

translation: Say: "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, whether apparent or concealed, and sin, and aggression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down any authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of prohibitions ordained by Allah, encompassing both obvious and hidden immoral acts, unjust aggression, false associations with Allah, and speaking without knowledge about Him. It serves as a reminder to adhere strictly to what Allah has revealed, avoiding presumptions that extend beyond divine guidance, thus preserving the purity of faith and moral conduct.

translation: And for every nation is a term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it by a single hour, nor can they advance it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and exactness of the appointed time for every community or individual, especially concerning life and the Day of Judgment. It teaches that divine decree is absolute, and no one can alter the set time of their destiny, highlighting the importance of being mindful of one's actions before that inevitable moment arrives.

translation: O children of Adam, indeed messengers have come to you from among yourselves relating to you My verses. So whoever fears Allah and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the compassionate approach of divine guidance, highlighting that messengers arise from among humanity itself to remind and instruct people about God's signs. Those who heed this guidance with consciousness of God (taqwa) and strive to amend their behavior will find security and peace, free from fear of punishment and sorrow in this world and the hereafter.

translation: And those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them – those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that rejecting God's revelations with arrogance is not merely a denial of faith but an act of defiance that seals one's destiny in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning that such prideful rejection leads to eternal punishment, emphasizing the importance of humility and submission to divine guidance.

translation: So who is more unjust than one who invents falsehood against Allah or denies His verses? Those will have their share of the decree until Our messengers come to them and take them in death, and they will say, "Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have departed from us," and will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave injustice committed by those who fabricate lies against Allah or reject His signs. It emphasizes that such individuals inevitably face the consequences of their actions during their lives and at the moment of death. When death comes, and the messengers retrieve their souls, they witness the absence of the false deities they used to invoke, confirming their misguided disbelief and making them bear the burden of their own denial.

translation: He said, "Enter among nations of jinn and mankind who passed away before you, into the Fire." Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister until, when they all have assembled therein, the last of them says to the first, "Our Lord, these caused us to be lost; so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a profound reality about intergenerational accountability and the cumulative consequences of persistent wrongdoing. It shows that every community that sinned in the past is punished, and when they meet in the Hereafter, each blames the other for leading them astray. The request for giving a double punishment to those who misled others highlights the intensified consequences for those who cause others to deviate from guidance. The final response indicates that all receive just recompense according to their deeds, even beyond their understanding, emphasizing God's perfect justice and the gravity of misleading others.

translation: And the last will say to the first, "So taste the punishment for what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of one's actions and serves as a warning that those who have committed wrong will face the results of their deeds, emphasizing divine justice is impartial and based on the choices and actions one has taken.

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of a needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores the impossibility of the arrogant disbelievers receiving divine mercy or entering Paradise. Their denial and pride create an insurmountable barrier between them and salvation, emphasizing that humility and belief are prerequisites for God's grace. The metaphor of a camel passing through the eye of a needle illustrates how utterly impossible it is for those who reject God's signs with arrogance to attain the ultimate reward.

translation: For them is a couch of Hellfire, and above them a canopy, and thus do We reward the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences that await those who perpetrate injustice and wrongdoing. The imagery of a couch in Hellfire with an overlying canopy emphasizes the inescapable and encompassing nature of their punishment, signifying that their evil deeds will lead to both physical torment and an all-encompassing state of loss and regret in the hereafter.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We do not charge any soul except [within] its capacity. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the justice and mercy of Allah in judging His servants, emphasizing that He does not burden any soul beyond its ability to bear. It assures believers that sincere faith combined with righteous actions leads to eternal reward in Paradise, affirming the principle that divine accountability is always fair and within human capacity.

translation: And We removed from their breasts any resentment, flowing beneath them rivers, and they said, "Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this; and we would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Indeed, the messengers of our Lord have come with the truth." And they were called, "This is Paradise which you have inherited for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformative power of divine guidance in purifying the hearts from bitterness and enmity. It emphasizes gratitude towards Allah as the ultimate source of guidance and acknowledges that true guidance cannot be attained without divine help. The verse also affirms the justice and truthfulness of the messengers' message and reassures believers of their rightful inheritance of Paradise as a reward for their righteous deeds.

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They will say, "Yes." Then a caller will proclaim between them, "The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate realization of divine justice on the Day of Judgment, where the believers acknowledge the fulfillment of God's promise of Paradise, and the wrongdoers admit the reality of their punishment. It emphasizes that God's promises, both of reward and punishment, are true and certain, reaffirming that those who perpetrate injustice will rightfully receive the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Those who hinder [others] from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked while they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave sin of obstructing the path of Allah, which means preventing others from understanding or following the truth. It emphasizes that such people not only distort the true path but also reject belief in the Hereafter, indicating a profound spiritual loss and a deliberate rebellion against divine guidance.

translation: And between them is a partition, and on the heights are men who recognize all by their marks. And they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you!" They have not yet entered it, but they long to.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the precise and just nature of the afterlife, where there is a clear separation between the dwellers of Paradise and Hell. The existence of men on the heights who recognize each soul by its distinctive marks signifies divine knowledge and the permanence of one's deeds. The greeting of peace to the inhabitants of Paradise reflects the mercy and hope even for those not yet admitted, emphasizing that ultimate entry depends on God's judgment but that yearning for Paradise is a sign of faith and aspiration toward righteousness.

translation: And when their eyes are turned towards the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sincere plea of the believers who, upon witnessing the fate of the wrongdoers in Hellfire, earnestly supplicate to Allah to be spared from such torment. It emphasizes the human desire for mercy and the recognition of injustice as a path leading to punishment. The verse serves as a warning to avoid oppressive actions and a hopeful invocation for mercy and protection from wrongdoing.

translation: And the companions of the Elevations called out to men they recognized by their marks, saying, "What has availed you your gathering and that you were arrogant?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of arrogance and worldly alliances on the Day of Judgment. Despite the connections and social status one might have had in the world, they will be powerless and their pride meaningless in the Hereafter.

translation: Are these the ones upon whom you swore that Allah would never bestow His mercy? Enter Paradise; there is no fear concerning you, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers who might have doubted their own salvation due to past sins or difficulties. It emphasizes that Allah's mercy is vast and surpasses human judgement or oaths sworn against receiving mercy. Those whom Allah admits into Paradise need not fear or grieve, as they have secured a place of eternal peace and happiness.

translation: And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or from whatever Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark separation between the inhabitants of Paradise and Hellfire, emphasizing the eternal consequences of disbelief.
