interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when the angels, disguised as men, show protection and reassurance to Prophet Lot against the threatening intentions of his people. It underscores the divine protection granted to the prophets and serves as a reminder that even in moments of danger, believers should trust in God's support and the mission of His messengers.

translation: And his wife stood, and she laughed; so We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine power of God to bring joy and hope in the face of doubt or surprise. The wife’s laughter signifies human amazement at God's ability to grant offspring despite apparent impossibility, showing that God's mercy and will transcend human limitations and expectations.

translation: She said, "Woe to me! Am I to give birth while I am an old woman, and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is a strange thing."
interpretation: This verse reflects the natural human astonishment and doubt faced when witnessing what seems impossible by worldly standards. It teaches that God's power transcends human limitations, reminding believers that with divine will, even what appears absurd can come to pass, thus encouraging faith in the miraculous and the unseen.

translation: They said, "Do you marvel at the command of Allah? May the mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O family of the House. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind Allah's decisions, encouraging believers not to be surprised by His decrees. It also conveys a special invocation of mercy and blessings upon the family of the Prophet, emphasizing their honored status. The attributes 'Praiseworthy' and 'Glorious' affirm Allah's perfect nature and the righteousness of His judgment, inspiring trust and submission among the faithful.

translation: When the fear had left Abraham and the good news had come to him, he began to plead with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the compassionate nature of Prophet Abraham, who, upon receiving reassurance and glad tidings, actively interceded on behalf of the people of Lot despite their wrongdoing, highlighting the qualities of mercy and hope for guidance even for those who have strayed.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, most tender-hearted, and penitent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Abraham, portraying him as a model of patience, compassion, and sincere return to God in repentance. It teaches believers the importance of embodying these virtues in their own lives, emphasizing that true faith involves both enduring hardships with patience and turning to God humbly.

translation: O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will come to them a punishment that cannot be repelled.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the divine decree is inevitable and must be accepted without resistance. It serves as a reminder that despite human opposition or disbelief, God's judgment is certain and unstoppable, emphasizing the importance of submission to God's will and the consequences of rejecting His guidance.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt themselves to be encumbered, and said, "This is a difficult day."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the emotional turmoil and deep concern Prophet Lot experienced upon the arrival of the angels as messengers, knowing the severe consequences that would befall his people for their misconduct. It reflects the weight of prophetic responsibility and the sorrow felt when witnessing impending divine punishment upon one's own community.

translation: And his people came rushing to him, while they had been doing evil deeds before. He said: "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a single right-minded man?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's commitment to moral principles and the protection of guest rights despite the misconduct of his people. It underscores the importance of righteousness and respect even when facing opposition or ingrained wrongdoing, calling for wisdom and restraint in protecting what is just and honorable.

translation: They said, "You certainly know that we have no right over your daughters, and indeed, you know what we want."
interpretation: This verse reflects a dialogue where a party acknowledges that they have no entitlement or claim over the daughters mentioned, but also that the addressee understands their true intentions or desires. It underscores the principle of respect for boundaries and honest communication about underlying motives in human interactions.

translation: He said, "If only I had strength over you or could take refuge in a strong support."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of frustration and acknowledgment of human limitation in the face of adversity; it highlights the speaker's desire for power or refuge to overcome difficulties, emphasizing the vulnerability that even the strong can experience without divine assistance or a firm support.

translation: They said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers from your Lord; they will not reach you. So travel with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back except your wife. Indeed, she will be afflicted by that which afflicts them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning; is not the morning near?
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the mercy and protection granted by Allah through His messengers. Despite the impending punishment facing the people for their wrongdoing, the messengers provide Lot and his family with a specific guidance to escape safely. The instruction to not look back, except for Lot's wife, symbolizes the need to leave behind disbelief and sinful ways completely, without hesitation or regret. The inevitability of the punishment at dawn signifies the certainty of divine justice, while also highlighting that deliverance is possible through obedience and trust in Allah's guidance.

translation: So when Our command came, We made the highest part (of the city) its lowest and rained upon it stones of layered hard clay.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute power of Divine judgment, demonstrating that no earthly height or status can protect against the consequences decreed by God. It serves as a reminder that human pride and worldly status are transient and can be overturned by Divine will at any moment.

translation: They are recorded with your Lord, and it is not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the deeds of all individuals are meticulously recorded by Allah, and those who commit injustice cannot escape His knowledge and judgment. It assures that divine justice is inevitable, and wrongful acts will not go unaccounted for.

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not reduce the measure and the balance. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day."
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic mission of Shu'ayb to his people, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and honesty in trade. It teaches that true prosperity is not just material wealth but ethical integrity, warning that ignoring moral responsibilities, like cheating in measures, leads to divine punishment despite apparent success.

translation: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse instructs the community to maintain fairness and integrity in trade and dealings, emphasizing that upholding justice is not only about avoiding harm to others but also about fostering societal harmony; corruption and injustice disrupt the moral fabric of society, and believers are called to prevent such damage by being equitable and honest.

translation: Allah's remainder (grant) is better for you if you are believers, and I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on God's guidance and ultimate support rather than solely on human authorities or leadership. It encourages believers to recognize that God's favor is the most beneficial and secure provision, and that prophets or leaders are not ultimate protectors or guarantors over others; instead, individuals must maintain their own faith and responsibility.

translation: They said, "O Shu'ayb, do your prayers command that we leave what our forefathers used to worship, or that we do with our wealth whatever we please? Indeed, you are surely the forbearing, the insightful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance of people to abandoning their traditional beliefs and practices, especially concerning their worship and use of wealth. It reflects the tension between divine guidance and human customs, emphasizing the challenge faced by prophets in persuading their communities to adopt justice and monotheism. The description of Shu'ayb as 'forbearing' and 'insightful' underscores the patience and wisdom required to guide people towards righteousness despite their stubbornness.

translation: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him? And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I forbid you; indeed, I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's patient and sincere approach when addressing his people, emphasizing that his guidance is based on clear divine evidence and sincere concern for their well-being rather than opposition or rebellion. It teaches us to communicate truth with wisdom and humility, striving always for reform and relying solely on Allah for success and guidance.

translation: And O my people, let not my detractors make you fall into the same fate as the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih; and the people of Lot are not far from you.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against allowing personal hostility or division to blind us to justice and truth. It reminds the community that failing to heed divine guidance like previous peoples who were destroyed due to their denial and disobedience can lead to similar disastrous consequences. The mention of these past peoples highlights the recurring pattern of ignoring prophetic warnings and suffering the ensuing punishment, urging people to unify and sincerely follow righteousness to avoid such a fate.

translation: And seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah. It assures that no matter the shortcomings or sins, turning back with a heart full of remorse will be met with Allah's boundless mercy and love, highlighting the compassionate nature of the Divine towards His servants.

translation: They said, "O Shu'aib, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we see you among us as weak. And if it were not for your clan, we would have stoned you; and you are not able to protect us from harm."
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge faced by Prophet Shu'aib from his people who rejected his message due to misunderstanding and arrogance. It highlights how people often resist divine guidance when it confronts their entrenched interests or beliefs, relying instead on social power and threats to silence those who admonish them. The verse teaches that strength in faith and righteousness may appear weak in the eyes of worldly power, yet true support lies in God's protection beyond human alliances.

translation: He said, "O my people, is my family more honored to you than Allah? And have you taken Him in neglect behind your backs? Indeed, my Lord encompasses what you do."
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of valuing worldly ties or family over the acknowledgment and fear of God. It warns against turning away from God's guidance and protection, implying that such neglect leads to spiritual ruin, as God is fully aware of all actions and intentions.

translation: O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You will soon know who it is that will bring upon himself a humiliating punishment and who is lying. And wait, indeed, I am with you, observing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of individual responsibility and accountability. The speaker asserts their own commitment to action while warning others that the consequences of their deeds will become clear in due time. It highlights that truth and falsehood, as well as rightful and wrongful actions, cannot remain hidden indefinitely; divine justice will manifest, exposing the true nature of people's deeds and intentions.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the ones who wronged were seized by the blast, and they became motionless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the decisive intervention of divine justice when the time set by God arrives. It highlights that those who uphold faith and righteousness are protected by God's mercy, while those who persist in wrongdoing and injustice inevitably face the consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder that divine judgment is certain and just, ensuring the triumph of truth and the downfall of oppression.

translation: As if they had never prospered there; except for the fact that there came after them the people of Thamud.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly success and civilizations; it serves as a warning that despite apparent prosperity, communities can perish due to their corruption and rejection of divine guidance, reminding us that true success is tied to righteousness, not just material wealth or power.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Prophet Moses was sent by God endowed with unmistakable miracles and a decisive mandate, signifying divine support in conveying the message and establishing justice, thereby affirming the truth of his prophethood and the legitimacy of his mission.

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs; they followed the command of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh's command was not rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Pharaoh and his leaders pursued their own misguided and oppressive commands without heed to justice or truth, serving as a warning against blindly following unjust authority.

translation: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and will thrust them into the Fire; what an evil resting place!
interpretation: This verse warns of the consequences of one's deeds and leadership on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that a leader who misguides or wrongs his people will not only bear the burden of his own sins but also be responsible for the punishment of those he led astray, resulting in a dreadful end in the Hellfire.

translation: And they will follow [instead] a curse and [the consequence on] the Day of Resurrection. Evil is the support that is supported.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who choose misguided paths or reject the truth will bear the burden of divine curses both in this world and on the Day of Judgment. The 'support that is supported' refers to false beliefs or alliances that seem strong but ultimately bring ruin and no real benefit.

translation: That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you. Some of them are standing, and some are [reduced] to ruins.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transitory nature of worldly civilizations and the lessons that can be drawn from their rise and fall. It serves as a reminder that despite the grandeur of past communities, their ultimate fate is submission to God's will and the consequences of their deeds, prompting us to reflect on our own actions and the impermanence of worldly life.

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. And their gods whom they invoked besides Allah did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came; and they increased them not in loss.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of personal accountability; it conveys that the wrong and suffering a people experience are ultimately consequences of their own misdeeds and choices rather than injustices inflicted by Allah. It also emphasizes the futility of seeking help from false gods or idols, as they have no power to change fate or avert divine decree. The arrival of Allah's command—such as punishment or decree—renders the intercession of idols ineffective, and those false deities only increase the wrongdoers in confusion and loss.

translation: And thus did your Lord take [enforcement] when He took the towns while they were committing wrong. Indeed, His taking is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severity and certainty of divine justice when communities persist in wrongdoing. It serves as a warning that Allah's punishment is both painful and severe, emphasizing that no wrongdoing goes unnoticed and that ultimate accountability cannot be escaped.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is the Day when the people will be gathered together; that is a Day witnessed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being mindful of the consequences in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that the events of the Day of Judgment, when all humanity will be gathered and held accountable, are true and certain. The awareness of this reality encourages believers to lead lives conscious of Allah's commands and the ultimate accountability, motivating them to avoid actions that would incur punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: And We delay it only for a limited term.
interpretation: This verse indicates that any postponement in the punishment or decree of Allah is purposeful and limited; it serves a specific wisdom within Divine wisdom, such as allowing time for repentance, for the fulfillment of a predetermined plan, or for the manifestation of justice in due course. The delay is not arbitrary or infinite but consciously measured according to Allah's knowledge and wisdom.

translation: The Day will come when no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them, some will be wretched, and some will be happy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where no one can utter a word without His approval. It signifies that speech and expression will be perfectly controlled and purposeful, reflecting one's ultimate state—either happiness for the righteous or misery for the wicked—highlighting the decisive nature of that day.

translation: As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, wherein they will have loud exhalations and inhales.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the torment of those who have chosen the path of evil and disbelief. The descriptions of "zafīr" (loud exhalation) and "shahīq" (intense inhalation) evoke the image of severe suffering and distress in the Fire, emphasizing that their punishment is both continuous and overwhelming, reflecting the consequence of their rejection of guidance and persistence in wrongdoing.

translation: They will abide therein forever as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is ever doing what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence of the state of the inhabitants of Paradise or Hell, underscoring that their eternal abode is ultimately subject to the will of Allah. It conveys that while the duration is infinite from a human perspective, the absolute authority and power to alter or end existence belong solely to God, highlighting His supreme control over all creation and destiny.

translation: As for those who are fortunate, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. An unending gift.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal reward prepared for the righteous, emphasizing the permanence and generosity of God's blessings in Paradise. It teaches that the ultimate success and happiness lie in abiding eternally in God's favor, a state that surpasses all worldly pleasures and is sustained by God's will and mercy.

translation: So do not be in doubt about what these [polytheists] worship. They worship not except as their forefathers did before [them]. And indeed, We will give them their share [of punishment] fully and not [allow to] diminish.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet not to be uncertain or distressed about the worship practices of the polytheists, emphasizing that their forms of worship are inherited traditions rather than guided by truth. It assures that divine justice will be fully meted out to them for their deviations, indicating that their inherited practices do not absolve them from accountability in the sight of God.

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture, and after that they differed concerning it. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, their matter would have been concluded between them, but indeed they are in deep doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to dispute divine guidance despite clear revelations. The "word" from God refers to His divine decree allowing the continuation of such differences temporarily, emphasizing God's wisdom and mercy in giving people opportunities to seek truth. The verse warns that persistent doubt and dispute over what is clearly revealed stem from either misunderstanding or intentional disregard, urging believers to seek clarity and sincerity in their faith.

translation: Indeed, upon the fulfillment of their deeds, your Lord will surely recompense them. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute knowledge and justice in rewarding every individual's actions. It conveys that no deed, large or small, goes unnoticed by God, and He will recompense each person fairly according to their deeds, underscoring His intimate awareness and perfect justice regarding human conduct.

translation: So remain steadfast as you have been commanded, along with those who have turned to Allah with you; and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance in following the commands of Allah, while also highlighting the need to maintain humility and avoid exceeding limits. It teaches that sincere repentance and unity with fellow believers strengthen one’s faith, and that God is fully aware of all actions, reinforcing accountability and mindfulness in conduct.

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you, and you will have no protectors besides Allah, nor will you be helped.
interpretation: This verse warns against forming close alliances or sympathizing with wrongdoers and oppressors, as doing so can lead one away from divine guidance and make one vulnerable to punishment. It emphasizes that true protection and support come only from Allah, and reliance on unjust people offers no real safeguard or assistance.

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds erase bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining regular prayers at specific times as a means to cultivate spiritual discipline and mindfulness. It teaches that consistent good actions, such as prayer, serve to cleanse the soul by erasing sins, thus encouraging believers to persist in righteous deeds and constant remembrance of God to attain purification and improvement in character.

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to maintain patience in times of hardship and perseverance in righteous deeds, assuring them that Allah values their efforts and will not let their sincere actions and good conduct go unrewarded, even if the results are not immediately visible.

translation: If there had not been a kind of people among previous generations who forbade corruption on earth, it would have been ruined; but only a few of them, whom We saved, did so. Yet those who did wrong pursued what luxury they had and were criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores the necessity of righteous individuals who actively prevent corruption and wrongdoing in society. The scarcity of such people in previous eras led to the persistence of evil and decline. It serves as a reminder of the critical role that moral leadership and accountability play in maintaining social order and justice, and highlights the consequences when society indulges in excess without restraint.

translation: And never would your Lord destroy the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice and mercy of God, indicating that divine punishment is not meted out indiscriminately or unjustly. It assures that destruction befalls a community only if the inhabitants are corrupt and rebellious, and that if a people strive to reform and do good, God's justice will protect them from such ruin.

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine wisdom in human diversity, illustrating that differences in beliefs, cultures, and opinions among people are part of God's plan. Such diversity serves as a test and an opportunity for humans to engage with one another, seek truth, and demonstrate patience and understanding. It highlights that uniformity is not the intended state; rather, the existence of varying perspectives is a means through which individuals can grow spiritually and socially.

translation: Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the command of your Lord is completed that, "Indeed, I will fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and decree behind creation and judgment. It emphasizes that God's mercy is the ultimate determinant of salvation, and except for those whom He chooses to show mercy, all others face the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse also reflects the certainty of God's plan and justice in filling Hell with those who reject faith, underscoring the gravity of human and jinn accountability before God.

translation: And We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the news of the messengers in order to strengthen your heart thereby. And We have brought you the truth and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that recounting the stories of previous messengers serves to fortify the Prophet's resolve and provides lessons and reassurance for believers, emphasizing that knowledge of prophetic histories strengthens faith and guides conduct.

translation: And say to those who do not believe, "Work according to your position; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse serves as a response to the disbelievers, indicating that they should continue in their ways according to their stance and choices, while the believers remain steadfast in their own righteous efforts. It emphasizes that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable for their deeds, and God's support is with those who persist in faith and good actions.

translation: And wait, indeed, We are waiting.
interpretation: This verse expresses a confident and resolute stance of patience and vigilance. It signifies that Allah is fully aware of the unfolding events and the outcome, emphasizing that He is present and prepared, awaiting the consequences of human actions. It reassures believers to remain steadfast and patient, trusting in Allah's timing and ultimate justice.

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And to Him returns all matters. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's exclusive knowledge of the unseen and the ultimate control He has over all affairs. It teaches us to place our trust and devotion solely in Him, recognizing that despite human limitations, Allah is fully aware of all actions and events. Therefore, sincere worship coupled with complete reliance on Him is the appropriate response to His encompassing authority and awareness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and clarity of the Qur'an as a revealed scripture from Allah. The letters Alif, Lam, Ra serve as signs of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which despite being composed of common letters, conveys profound, unalterable guidance. It establishes the Qur'an as a clear and decisive source of knowledge, meant to guide humanity unmistakably.

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an so that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language intentionally, as it is the native tongue of its initial audience, to ensure clarity and facilitate deep comprehension, reflection, and guidance in their lives.

translation: We relate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an, although before it you were among the unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains the most excellent and perfect narratives, revealed by God to the Prophet Muhammad, to guide and awaken him from any ignorance. It highlights the divine wisdom in these stories, intended not merely as historical recounting but as profound lessons to instill awareness and faith.

translation: When Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Joseph's dream, which symbolizes his future rise to a position of authority and respect. The eleven stars represent his brothers, while the sun and the moon symbolize his parents. Their prostration signifies his family's eventual recognition of his elevated status and God's plan unfolding despite present hardships.

translation: He said, "O my sons, do not relate your vision to your brothers lest they contrive against you a plan. Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy."
interpretation: This verse warns about the dangers of sharing one's dreams or visions with those who may harbor jealousy or ill intent. It highlights the reality of human susceptibility to envy and deception, reminding believers to exercise caution and awareness of the harmful schemes that can arise from others' malice, all while being mindful of Satan's role as an explicit adversary seeking to mislead humanity.

translation: And thus your Lord will choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that divine election is accompanied by the endowment of profound knowledge and understanding, specifically of hidden or complex truths. It highlights the continuity of God's benevolence and wisdom through generations, emphasizing that true guidance and insight come as a completion of God's grace, rooted in His infinite knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, in [the story of] Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights the narrative of Prophet Joseph and his brothers as a source of profound insights and lessons about human nature, patience, forgiveness, and divine wisdom, serving as a guidance for those who earnestly seek understanding.

translation: When they said to Yusuf and his brother, "Indeed, our father loves you more than us, although we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse reveals the feelings of jealousy and suspicion among Yusuf's brothers, highlighting how human emotions such as envy can lead to misunderstanding and discord within families, even when there is clear affection from the father. It serves as a reminder to guard against jealousy and to foster trust and communication to maintain harmony.

translation: Kill Yusuf or cast him out to some remote land; perhaps your father will forget him, and you will be after that a righteous people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of jealousy and plotting by Yusuf's brothers, highlighting human tendencies toward envy and fear of favoritism within the family. It reflects how such negative emotions can lead to harmful plans against loved ones. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of envy and the importance of trust and righteousness in familial relationships.

translation: One of them said, "Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the bottom of the well, so some caravan may pick him up if you would do [something]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the mercy and wisdom of the speaker among Joseph's brothers, who intervened to prevent the killing of Joseph. It teaches the importance of compassion and seeking alternatives to harm, emphasizing that even in moments of jealousy or conflict, one should strive for a solution that preserves life and leaves the outcome to God's plan.

translation: They said, "O our father, why do you not entrust Yusuf to us, while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers’ attempt to persuade their father to let them take care of Yusuf, presenting themselves as trustworthy and well-intentioned, though their underlying motives may not be pure. It highlights human tendencies to conceal true intentions under the guise of concern and advice.

translation: We will send him with Us tomorrow so that he may wander and play, and indeed, We are his Guardian.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's care and protection even when allowing freedom and enjoyment. Though the individual is sent to engage in natural human pleasures and exploration, the Divine Watchfulness ensures safety and guided care, reassuring that freedom does not mean abandonment but is encompassed by mercy and guardianship.

translation: He said, "Indeed, it saddens me that you should carry it away, and I fear that the wolf will eat it while you are heedless of it."
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep sense of responsibility and concern for the safety of a vulnerable being. The speaker expresses sorrow at the thought of the one being taken away and fears harm coming to it due to negligence. It highlights the importance of vigilance and care, especially when entrusted with the welfare of something or someone vulnerable.

translation: They said, "If the wolf should eat him while we are a strong, united group, indeed, we would then be the losers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the folly of claiming strength in numbers yet failing to protect one among them, highlighting that true power lies not merely in unity but in the effectiveness of that unity. It warns against complacency in collective strength without taking responsible action, as failure to safeguard the vulnerable leads to true loss and disgrace.

translation: So when they took him and agreed to cast him into the bottom of the well, and We inspired to him, saying, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive."
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine wisdom and protection in moments of apparent abandonment or betrayal. Despite the conspiracies against the individual, God's revelation assures that the truth will eventually be made known, emphasizing that God's plans transcend human schemes and that ultimate justice and awareness will prevail even when others are unaware.

translation: And they came to their father at nightfall, weeping.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound sorrow and remorse felt by the brothers as they return to their father, signifying the pain and consequences of their actions or events that have transpired, highlighting themes of repentance and the emotional weight of familial bonds.

translation: They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and the wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."
interpretation: This verse reflects human tendencies towards deception and evasion of responsibility when confronted with difficult circumstances. It illustrates how fear and guilt can lead individuals to fabricate falsehoods instead of facing the truth. Moreover, it highlights the struggles in maintaining trust within relationships, as the father's disbelief underscores the consequences of dishonesty and broken trust among family members.

translation: And they came upon his shirt with false blood; he said, "Rather, your own selves have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help concerning what you describe."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of patience and reliance on Allah in the face of false accusations and deceit. The mention of 'false blood' symbolizes fabricated evidence, yet the response emphasizes self-restraint and trust in Allah's justice rather than retaliation or despair. It teaches that when confronted with slander and wrongdoing, one should respond with patience and seek Allah's aid, recognizing that ultimate vindication and justice come from Him alone.

translation: And a caravan came, and they sent their water drawer; so he lowered his bucket. He said, "Good news! This is a boy." And they concealed him as merchandise, but Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the covert and deceitful actions undertaken by the women who found the boy, seeking to protect him by treating him as a secret commodity. It illustrates the tension between human plans and divine knowledge, emphasizing that while people may attempt to hide their deeds and intentions, Allah is fully aware of all actions and circumstances, ensuring that nothing escapes His knowledge or judgment.

translation: And they sold them for a small price, a few dirhams, and they were, concerning it, disinterested.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sincere detachment and humility of those who did not value wealth or material gain over their principles and convictions. Their readiness to part with something valuable for a trivial amount signifies their profound spiritual commitment and prioritization of ethical integrity above worldly possessions.

translation: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Make his stay comfortable; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." Thus We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how divine wisdom operates through human actions and circumstances. Despite the apparent hardships Joseph faced, Allah's plan was unfolding to place him in a position where he could serve a greater purpose: understanding and interpreting significant events. It affirms that Allah's control and planning transcend human awareness, guiding situations beyond immediate perception toward a destined outcome.

translation: And when he reached maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon those who mature and develop in righteousness, granting them wisdom and knowledge as a reward. It emphasizes that true goodness is recognized and honored by God through bestowing understanding and insight, encouraging believers to strive for excellence in their character and deeds.

translation: And she who was in his house sought to seduce him, and she closed the doors and said, "Come, you!" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, my Lord is the best disposer of affairs. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse highlights Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph's) steadfastness and moral integrity in the face of temptation. Despite the closeness of the situation and the pressure exerted, he immediately turns to Allah for protection, affirming that ultimate trust in God and adherence to righteousness are the true paths to success, whereas wrongdoing leads to failure.

translation: And indeed he was inclined to her, and she was inclined to him, had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus We avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the strength of faith and divine guidance in restraining a believer from committing wrongful acts despite strong personal inclinations. It emphasizes that the awareness of God's presence and signs acts as a protective barrier, enabling a person to overcome base desires and remain righteous. This reflects the principle that sincere faith instills self-control and moral integrity, guiding one away from sin and towards purity.

translation: And she raced to the door and tore his shirt from the back, and they found her lord at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended ill for your family except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the courage and quick thinking of the woman, who actively defends her chastity and honor by exposing the wrongful intention of the man. It emphasizes that those who seek to harm the innocent must face just consequences, highlighting the importance of protecting virtue and ensuring justice against transgressors.

translation: She said, "He attempted to seduce me against my will." And a witness from her own people testified, "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she is telling the truth," and he is one of the liars.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a scenario where conflicting testimonies arise regarding an accusation. It emphasizes the importance of corroborating evidence and honest witnesses in discerning truth from falsehood, highlighting that mere claims are insufficient without credible proof, and that even apparent evidence can be deceptive if the witness is dishonest.

translation: And if his shirt is torn from the back, then indeed, he has told a lie, and he is surely one of the liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the evidence of the Prophet Joseph's innocence by noting the detail of his shirt being torn from behind, which contradicts his accuser's claim. The tearing from behind indicates that he was fleeing from the assault, not pursuing it, thus affirming his truthfulness and the falsehood of the accusation against him.

translation: When he saw his shirt torn at the back, he said, "Indeed, it is from your cunning. Indeed, your cunning is great."
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition of a woman’s cleverness in an attempt to protect her own honor. It reflects the complexity of human interactions where appearances can be deceptive, and schemes or misunderstandings may arise from situations. The acknowledgment of 'great cunning' serves as an admission of the intricate and sometimes subtle ways in which events unfold, emphasizing the importance of discerning truth beyond surface evidence.

translation: Yusuf, turn away from this and ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you have been among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) advises his son Yusuf (Joseph) to leave an inappropriate or harmful situation and seek forgiveness from Allah, acknowledging that humans are prone to mistakes. It teaches humility and the importance of recognizing one's faults, turning back to God in repentance to attain spiritual purification and guidance.

translation: And the women in the city said, "The wife of al-'Aziz is seeking to seduce her servant; indeed, she is infatuated with him in love. We surely see her in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal judgment and gossip that can arise from misunderstanding or suspicion, demonstrating how public opinion often leaps to conclusions about someone's character or actions without full knowledge, reflecting human tendencies toward suspicion and suspicion's consequences on personal reputations.

translation: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent to them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said, "Come out before them." But when they saw him, they were awestruck and cut their hands and said, "Exalted is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when the women, who plotted deceitfully, were confronted by the truth embodied in the presence of a noble messenger. Their reaction—shock and the involuntary injury to themselves—reflects the overwhelming power of divine truth and realization. It signifies that when confronted with undeniable truth, falsehood and deception are exposed, leading to recognition of the purity and majesty of God's messengers, who are not mere humans but honored angels.

translation: She said, "That is the one in whose presence you blamed me. And indeed, I sought to seduce him from himself, but he firmly refused. And if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be among those humiliated."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the steadfastness and moral integrity of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) in the face of a severe temptation and trial. Despite intense provocation by the woman, who tries to seduce him, he resists firmly, adhering to his righteousness and obedience to God. This demonstrates the principle that true faith and discipline in ethical conduct provide a shield against sin, even when pressure or consequences are severe. It also highlights the consequences of rejecting immoral commands—here, the threat of imprisonment and humiliation—which contrast with the spiritual and personal dignity maintained through steadfast virtue.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the speaker's earnest plea to God for protection from being led astray by the deceptive plans of others. It highlights the preference for suffering in isolation (prison) over succumbing to harmful temptations, emphasizing the importance of divine guidance to maintain righteousness and avoid yielding to ignorance or wrongdoing.

translation: So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plot; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that when a believer calls upon Allah sincerely, Allah listens and intervenes to protect them from harm and deceit. It affirms Allah's attributes of being all-hearing and all-knowing, reassuring that no plea or situation escapes His awareness and that He responds to safeguard His servants from the schemes of others.

translation: Then, after they saw the signs, it appeared to them that he would surely be imprisoned for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to form judgments based on observed events, reflecting how people, upon witnessing clear signs or miracles, often conclude outcomes like imprisonment or punishment without understanding the divine wisdom behind those events.

translation: And there entered with him two young men into the prison. One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine." The other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head, and the birds are eating from it." Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a scenario where two prisoners share their distinct dreams with Prophet Joseph, recognizing his wisdom and goodness. It highlights the theme of divine revelation and interpretation, emphasizing that insights and guidance can come through those endowed with knowledge and righteousness, enabling the truth behind mysterious or symbolic experiences to be uncovered.

translation: He said, "No food will come to you but that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter."
interpretation: This verse reflects the speaker's divine wisdom and knowledge granted by Allah, which allows him to interpret the meaning behind certain events symbolized by food. It also underscores a conscious and deliberate distancing from a community that rejects belief in God and the afterlife, highlighting the importance of faith and acknowledgment of the unseen in fulfilling one's spiritual duties.

translation: And I have followed the religion of my forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most people do not give thanks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of pure monotheistic faith passed down through generations, highlighting the importance of maintaining the original teachings of prophets without introducing any form of idolatry or shirk. It reminds us that this steadfastness in faith is a blessing from God, and despite such grace, humanity often fails to recognize and be grateful for it.

translation: O my fellow prisoner, are various lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah over all other deities or authorities. It challenges the notion of multiple gods or rulers by highlighting that true power and dominion belong solely to Allah, who is singular and all-encompassing in His might.

translation: You do not worship besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your forefathers, for which Allah has not sent down any authority. The judgment is only for Allah. He commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the objects of worship besides Allah are merely names or concepts invented by humans without any divine sanction or power. True authority and judgment belong solely to Allah, and genuine religion requires worship exclusively directed to Him. It warns against false deities and calls people to recognize the uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah alone, highlighting that many remain unaware of this fundamental truth.

translation: O my fellow prisoner, as for one of us, he drinks wine for his Lord, but as for the other, he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate justice and decree of God, highlighting the contrasting fates of two prisoners who had hoped for mercy. It teaches that human affairs are under divine judgment and that one's ultimate destiny is determined by God's wisdom and will; thus, believers should trust in God's decree even in seemingly dire situations.

translation: And he said to the one whom he thought would be saved from them, "Mention me before your Lord." But Satan made him forget to mention his master, and he remained in prison for several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights how reliance on others’ promises without earnest personal effort and sincere supplication to God can lead to prolonged hardship. The man’s failure to remember Joseph before his Lord, due to Satan’s influence, underscores the importance of mindfulness and constant remembrance of God, especially in times of distress, to attain relief and fulfillment of prayers.

translation: And the king said, "Indeed, I see [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that are] lean, and seven green ears of grain and others dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the story of Prophet Joseph interpreting the dream of the king of Egypt. The king's dream symbolically foretells a coming period of prosperity followed by famine. The seven fat cows represent seven years of abundance, while the seven lean cows represent seven years of severe drought and hardship. Similarly, the seven green ears of grain followed by seven dry signify this cycle. The verse emphasizes the importance of insight and divine wisdom in understanding hidden meanings and future events.

translation: They said, "Confused dreams! And we are not the ones who interpret dreams."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a common human response to visions or revelations that are not immediately understood or are dismissed as mere fantasies. It highlights the tendency to deny or reject messages when their meaning is unclear, emphasizing the distinction between those who possess divine knowledge and interpretation and those who do not.

translation: And the one who was saved from the two said, "Do not forget me in my matter; I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me."
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding, especially in matters that are distressing or unclear. It highlights the human tendency to turn to those who possess insight and wisdom for guidance, emphasizing the role of communication and revelation in resolving doubts and ensuring clarity.

translation: Joseph, O truthful one, inform us about seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of corn and others dry, so that I may return to the people; perhaps they will know.
interpretation: This verse reflects the request made to Prophet Joseph to interpret a complex dream, which symbolizes a cycle of prosperity and hardship. The seven fat cows and green ears represent years of plenty, while the seven lean cows and dry ears symbolize years of famine. The interpretation emphasizes the divine wisdom in foreseeing and preparing for future challenges, highlighting the importance of patience and trust in God's plan during times of both abundance and scarcity.

translation: You will sow for seven consecutive years, but what you harvest leave it in its ear, except a little of what you eat.
interpretation: This verse conveys the concept of enduring hardship and patience during times of scarcity. It instructs that despite sowing and investing effort for seven continuous years, the actual benefit or yield should be preserved rather than consumed immediately, highlighting the importance of restraint and foresight to ensure survival and sustainability through difficult periods.

translation: Then after that, there will come seven harsh years that will devour what you have prepared for them, except a little of what you guard carefully.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about severe famine following seven years of plenty; it emphasizes the importance of prudent stewardship and cautious management of resources during times of abundance to prepare for inevitable times of difficulty and scarcity.

translation: Then comes after that a year in which the people are given abundant rain and they are made to endure hardship.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cyclical nature of human experiences under divine providence, emphasizing that periods of ease and hardship alternate by God's decree, teaching us patience during trials and gratitude during blessings.

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, he said, "Return to your Lord and ask Him what is the matter with the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is knowing of their plot."
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom of consulting God for deeper understanding, emphasizing that human judgments can be mistaken, and true knowledge comes from divine insight; it also illustrates God's awareness of hidden matters and warns against deceit and plotting among people.

translation: He said, "What is the matter with you that you sought to seduce Joseph to himself?" They said, "Allah forbid! We know no evil against him." The wife of Al-Aziz said, "Now the truth has come to light. Indeed, I solicited him to myself, and he is surely of the truthful ones."
interpretation: This verse highlights the innocence and integrity of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) in facing wrongful accusations. Despite intense temptation and false charges from the wife of Al-Aziz, Joseph remains steadfast and truthful. It teaches the principle of unwavering virtue and trust in God's justice, even when confronted by misleading situations and injustice.

translation: That He may know that I did not betray the secret, and that Allah does not guide the plan of the betrayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the integrity and sincerity of the speaker in maintaining trust and confidentiality. It also highlights that God's guidance and success are not granted to those who engage in treachery or deceit, illustrating a moral principle that betrayal leads to failure and divine disapproval.

translation: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the inherent weakness and inclination of the human self towards wrongdoing, emphasizing the necessity of divine mercy and forgiveness for guidance and reformation. It reflects the understanding that without God's mercy, the soul would be misled, underscoring reliance on God's compassion as essential for overcoming one's base tendencies.

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me that I may appoint him exclusively for myself." But when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted."
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition of wisdom and integrity in a person who was once a prisoner, showing that true character and divine support can elevate someone to a position of trust and authority. It emphasizes that trust and power are granted by divine will based on one's righteousness and capabilities.

translation: [He said:] "Appoint me over the treasures of the earth; indeed, I am a knowing guardian."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of trust and responsibility, where the speaker requests to be entrusted with the wealth of the earth, emphasizing their capability and wisdom to safeguard and manage it justly. It highlights themes of stewardship, accountability, and the importance of knowledge in overseeing resources.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land that he might settle wherever he willed. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We please, and We do not let the reward of the doers of good be lost.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that the position and success granted to Joseph were acts of divine will and mercy, signifying that real power and settlement are granted by God’s grace. It also emphasizes that God's reward for those who act with goodness and righteousness is never overlooked or wasted, reinforcing the principle that sincere efforts and virtuous deeds are ultimately recognized and compensated by God.

translation: But the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are mindful of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the superior value of the eternal reward in the Hereafter compared to worldly gains, emphasizing that true believers who live with consciousness of Allah's presence and commandments prioritize their faith and righteousness above fleeting worldly pleasures.

translation: And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the theme of divine wisdom and the unfolding of fate; despite the physical presence and recognition by Joseph, his brothers’ inability to recognize him reflects the complexities of relationships altered by time, trials, and God’s plan to test and ultimately reconcile them.

translation: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the emphasis on justice, generosity, and hospitality. The speaker reassures his guests by promising fair treatment and abundant provision, highlighting the value of treating others with kindness and integrity. It also reflects the importance of solidarity and family bonds, as the exchange and acceptance of a brother among them serves to strengthen trust and reconciliation.

translation: But if you do not bring it to me, then no measure is given to you by me, nor are you to approach me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of presenting clear evidence or proof when making claims before the Prophet or in judgment. It underscores that without such concrete proof, one's word will not be accepted, and one will not be granted consideration or closeness in such matters, highlighting the importance of truthfulness and accountability.

translation: They said, "We will surely try to seduce his father away from his religion, and indeed, we are well determined to do so."
interpretation: This verse highlights the determined intent of certain individuals to lead righteous people astray by targeting their closest relationships, understanding that influencing one's family can weaken their religious commitment. It reflects the tactics of evil to disrupt faith through personal and familial pressure.

translation: And he said to his young men, "Put their merchandise into their saddlebags so that they might recognize it when they return to their people, that perhaps they will return."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a wise and compassionate approach to dealing with others by subtly returning their goods to help them realize their loss or error. It reflects the principle of gentle guidance and encouragement towards positive change, showing that compassion coupled with thoughtful actions can lead people to reflect and possibly reconsider their ways.

translation: When they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, indeed, we were prevented from [buying] food, so send with us our brother that we may be conspire against him and indeed, we will be his protectors."
interpretation: This verse reveals the brothers' deceitful plan as they attempt to manipulate their father by pretending to be trustworthy, while hiding their true intention to harm their brother. It serves as a warning about the dangers of deceit and the importance of honesty within family relations.

translation: He said, "Did I take responsibility for you over him except as I took responsibility for you over his brother before? And Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that trust and responsibility should be given with sincerity and fairness, just as one would expect to be treated. It reminds us that ultimate protection and care come from Allah, who is the best guardian, emphasizing reliance on divine mercy and justice above human arrangements.

translation: And when they opened their goods, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what do we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us; we will feed our family, preserve our brother, and increase our camel's load. That is a small measure."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the mercy and providence granted by God, as the brothers find their merchandise restored after a trial. It signifies that reliance on God's wisdom can lead to the fulfillment of needs, preservation of family ties, and increase in provision even when expectations are modest, emphasizing trust in divine assistance and the hope that from small beginnings great sustenance can grow.

translation: He said, "I will not send him with you until you bring me a pledge from Allah confirming that you will bring him back to me, unless you are encompassed [i.e., taken captive by enemies]." When they had brought their pledge, he said, "Allah is (rightly) the Trustee over what we say."
interpretation: This verse highlights the necessity of trust and accountability in dealings, especially when it involves the welfare of others. The insistence on a pledge from Allah serves as a solemn guarantee that the responsibility entrusted will be honored, symbolizing deep commitment and reliance on divine witness. It teaches that in matters of significant trust, one must seek assurances that go beyond mere human promises, invoking God's oversight to ensure integrity and seriousness.

translation: And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates. And do not forget to seek help from Allah; nothing can protect you except Him. Indeed, the decision belongs to Allah alone; on Him I have relied, and upon Him let the reliant rely."
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of prudence and trust in Allah during times of difficulty or danger. It emphasizes that while using wise and varied strategies to overcome challenges is necessary, ultimate reliance must be placed on Allah alone, as He is the sovereign decision-maker and the true source of protection and success.

translation: And when they entered from where their father had commanded them, it did not avail them against Allah any harm or benefit, except a need that Jacob had to fulfill. Indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that regardless of human plans or efforts, ultimate outcomes are determined by divine wisdom and decree. The specific event with Jacob's sons emphasizes that while human intention and obedience matter, they do not override God's greater plan. Moreover, Jacob's knowledge—bestowed by God—allows him to understand subtleties beyond ordinary perception, highlighting that true knowledge comes from God and that many remain unaware of the deeper realities that govern human affairs.

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself and said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deep bond of brotherhood and compassion between Joseph and his brother. Despite the hardships and injustices they endured, Joseph reassures his brother not to be disheartened, emphasizing trust in God's plan and the importance of maintaining hope and patience in difficult times.

translation: So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he placed the water-skin upon his brother's camel; then a herald called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves!"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the unfolding of a test or a trial, where the act of placing the water-skin on the brother's camel sets the stage for a confrontation. The call accusing the caravan of theft symbolizes the unveiling of hidden truths and the challenge of justice, emphasizing that appearances can be deceptive and that divine scrutiny will ultimately reveal the reality of one's actions.

translation: They said, "What are you seeking?"
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of questioning or confrontation, highlighting the intent behind someone's actions or search. It invites reflection on the purpose and goals that drive human behavior, emphasizing the importance of understanding one's true objectives rather than acting aimlessly.

translation: They said, "We are missing the staff of the king; and for whoever brings it, there will be a camel burdened (with goods)." But I am its keeper.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the significance attributed to the staff as a symbol of authority and power. The people emphasize the importance of the staff by offering a substantial reward to anyone who returns it, reflecting the value of leadership and legitimacy in their society. It also highlights the speaker's role as the guardian of this symbol, underpinning the theme of rightful custodianship and the responsibility tied to authority.

translation: They said, "By Allah, indeed you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, nor were we thieves."
interpretation: This verse reflects the innocence of the speakers who emphasize their honorable intentions and deny any wrongdoing or misconduct. It teaches the importance of truthfulness and the rejection of baseless accusations, highlighting that one's actions and intentions are known by God and that false suspicions detract from justice and trustworthiness.

translation: They said, 'Then what is his recompense if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of the disbelievers who challenge the truthfulness and consequences of the Prophet's message, implying that if the warning is true, what punishment or reward awaits; it underscores their doubt and resistance to accepting divine guidance.

translation: They said, "His recompense is that he who finds it within his journey - let him have the recompense." Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the principle that consequences correspond to one's actions; those who commit wrongdoing will receive a fitting punishment commensurate with their deeds, emphasizing the divine justice that ensures wrongdoers do not go unpunished.

translation: So he began with the container of his brother before the container of his brother, then he extracted it from the container of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not take his brother under the king's law except that Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Divine wisdom and control in the unfolding of events. It emphasizes that all occurrences, especially those involving justice and leadership, happen only by Allah's will. It also teaches that true knowledge is layered, and no matter how knowledgeable someone is, there is always a higher level of understanding with Allah, who elevates and decrees the ranks of individuals according to His wisdom.

translation: They said, "If he stole, then a brother of his has stolen before." But Yusuf kept it within himself and did not disclose it to them. He said, "You are in a worse place," and Allah knows best what you describe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Yusuf's (Joseph's) patience and wisdom in facing false accusations and jealousy from his brothers. Despite their claims and attempts to discredit him by referencing past faults of his siblings, Yusuf chooses to withhold exposing them, showing his restraint and trusting Allah's ultimate knowledge and justice. It teaches the virtue of patience, avoiding escalation of conflict, and reliance on divine wisdom rather than responding with retaliation or defamation.

translation: They said, "O noble one, he has a very old father. Take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good."
interpretation: The brothers are expressing their desire to protect their youngest brother by offering themselves as substitutes, showing their recognition of the speaker's kindness and justice. This reflects themes of self-sacrifice and trust in the character of the noble one, highlighting the moral values of care for family and reliance on integrity.

translation: Mu'adh said: "May Allah forbid that we should take except from that with whom we find our belongings. Indeed, we would then be wrongdoers."
interpretation: This statement highlights the principle of honesty and integrity in dealings, emphasizing that one should only claim or take what rightfully belongs to them. It condemns wrongful appropriation and stresses the importance of justice in interpersonal transactions.

translation: So when they despaired of him, they withdrew, returning safely. Their eldest said, "Did you not know that your father has taken an oath from you in the name of Allah, and before you neglected Joseph? So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me, and He is the best of judges."
interpretation: This verse reflects the conflict between fulfilling familial obligations and abiding by ethical commitments. The eldest son's resolve to stay until he receives his father's permission or a divine ruling signifies the importance of maintaining trust and patience within family dynamics, and it highlights the reliance on God's ultimate justice when human guidance is insufficient.

translation: Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we only testify to what we know, and we were not witnesses to the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of honesty and integrity in testimony, emphasizing that one should only speak to what they have personally witnessed and not make allegations based on speculation or assumptions.

translation: And ask the village where we were, and the caravan in which we came; indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking truthful testimony and verification from witnesses to confirm the speaker's honesty, highlighting the value of accountability and integrity in communication.

translation: He said, "Nay, it is your own selves whispering to you a thing, so a beautiful patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal struggle and trials faced due to personal fears or doubts. It encourages one to exhibit beautiful patience, acknowledging that such restraint and trust in Allah's wisdom and knowledge may lead to a positive outcome. It teaches that challenges often stem from our own minds, and by enduring patiently and having faith in Allah's plan, we align ourselves with divine wisdom.

translation: And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow for Joseph!" and his eyes became white from grief, for he was overwhelmed with sorrow.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound depth of Jacob's (Ya'qub's) grief and sorrow for his son Joseph (Yusuf). His turning away and the whiteness of his eyes from anguish symbolizes the intense pain and helplessness he feels. It highlights the human experience of deep loss and the overwhelming emotional impact when separation from a beloved occurs. The verse teaches that even the noblest of prophets endure profound sorrow, showing the realism and emotional depth in the experiences of the righteous.

translation: They said, "By Allah, you will surely remember Joseph until you become exhausted or become among those who perish."
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense emotional impact that the story of Joseph (Yusuf) has on the listener, to the point of causing deep distress or fatigue. It reflects how profound and stirring the narratives of the Qur'an can be, touching the hearts so deeply that repeated contemplation may lead to emotional turmoil or spiritual trials.

translation: He said, "Indeed, I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress and hardship, recognizing that He possesses knowledge and wisdom beyond human understanding. It encourages believers to trust in Allah's plan, even when facing difficulties that others may not comprehend.

translation: O my sons, go and inquire about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining hope and trust in Allah's mercy and assistance, regardless of how dire the situation may seem. It teaches that losing hope in Allah is a sign of disbelief, encouraging believers to persist in their efforts and remain patient, trusting that Allah's help will come despite apparent hardships.

translation: So when they entered upon him, they said, "O Aziz, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with merchandise to sell. Give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how even in times of hardship, turning to kindness, honesty, and charity is valued. The appeal to generosity is not just a request for aid but also an acknowledgment of God's reward for those who are charitable, emphasizing that compassion and fairness in dealings are virtuous and spiritually beneficial.

translation: He said, "Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of reflection and rebuke, highlighting the recklessness and wrongdoing committed in ignorance. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of actions taken without understanding or awareness, urging individuals to seek knowledge and consciousness before acting, especially when dealing with matters of great importance or involving others.

translation: They said, "Are you truly Yusuf?" He said, "I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who is conscious of Allah and patient - then indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith (taqwa) and patience (sabr) during trials and hardships. It reassures believers that steadfastness and conscious fear of Allah ultimately lead to divine favor and reward. The verse encourages trust in Allah's justice and mercy, affirming that those who do good with sincerity will not have their efforts wasted.

translation: They said, "By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and indeed we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse reflects an acknowledgment of one's own mistakes in comparison to another's favored position by Allah. It emphasizes the human tendency to recognize divine preference and admit fault, underscoring themes of humility and accountability before God's will.

translation: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy and forgiveness, emphasizing that despite past mistakes, sincere repentance is met with compassion and pardon, reassuring believers of hope and redemption.

translation: Go, take this shirt of mine and throw it over the face of my father; he will regain his sight. Then come to me with all your family.
