interpretation: This verse highlights the power of divine intervention through a prophet's sincere supplication and action. It demonstrates that with God's will, a seemingly impossible miracle—restoring sight to the blind—can occur, motivating the people to reunite and reaffirm their faith and kinship under divine blessing.

translation: And when the caravan set out, their father said, "Indeed, I perceive the smell of Joseph, if you did not think me to be mistaken."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep intuition and hope of Prophet Jacob (Ya'qub) regarding the presence of his son Joseph (Yusuf) in the caravan. Despite the years of separation and the apparent loss, his strong emotional bond and faith lead him to sense Joseph's closeness, demonstrating the enduring nature of love and trust in divine reunion even amidst hardship.

translation: They said, "By Allah, indeed you are in your former error."
interpretation: This verse reflects the accusation directed at the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by disbelievers who insist that he remains in the same mistaken beliefs as before, rejecting the message he brings. It highlights their stubborn refusal to accept the truth and their commitment to persistent denial despite clear evidence, illustrating the challenge faced by the Prophet in conveying God's guidance.

translation: So when the bearer of good news came, he cast him down on his face, and he turned away seeing clearly. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the manifestation of divine knowledge granted to the Prophet, which surpasses human understanding. It signifies that true enlightenment and insight come from God alone, and those who possess this divine wisdom recognize realities beyond ordinary perception, underscoring the authority and truthfulness of the Prophet's knowledge.

translation: They said, "O our father, ask forgiveness for us of our sins; indeed, we have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and repentance of the sons towards their father, acknowledging their mistakes and seeking intercession and forgiveness. It illustrates the importance of recognizing one's faults, turning to God through supplication, and the role of righteous individuals in interceding or praying for others to attain forgiveness.

translation: He said, "I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound mercy and compassion of Prophet Muhammad, who continually intercedes on behalf of his people by seeking forgiveness for their sins from Allah. It emphasizes that no matter the shortcomings or mistakes committed, Allah's forgiveness and mercy are vast and encompass all who sincerely repent.

translation: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, God willing, safe and secure."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Joseph's compassion and sense of responsibility as he reunites with his parents and ensures their safety. It highlights the fulfillment of divine promises and the establishment of security and peace for his family under God's will.

translation: He raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. He said, "O my father, this is the realization of my vision of before; my Lord has made it true. He was indeed good to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you all from the desert after Satan had interposed between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is subtle in what He wills. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience, trust in God's wisdom, and the fulfillment of divine promises despite adversity. Joseph recognizes that God's subtle planning turns trials, such as imprisonment and familial discord, into blessings, demonstrating that God’s knowledge and wisdom govern all affairs and bring about justice and restoration at the right time.

translation: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound acknowledgment of divine favor and guidance, highlighting that all authority and knowledge, especially of the unseen like the interpretation of dreams, come from God. It emphasizes reliance on God as the ultimate protector and guide across both worldly life and the hereafter, expressing a desire for a life grounded in submission to God and for an honorable end joined with the righteous, which underscores the believer's aspiration for spiritual success and eternal peace.

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they put their plan together while they were devising schemes.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the knowledge conveyed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) comes from divine revelation concerning the unseen, which humans cannot access on their own. It also highlights the Prophet's innocence in the conspiracies of others, affirming that he is informed by God rather than by any human collusion or espionage.

translation: And most people, even if you strive [to be] of the believers, are not.
interpretation: This verse indicates the challenging reality that the majority of people do not embrace faith, despite sincere efforts and longing for them to do so. It underscores the importance of not being discouraged by widespread disbelief or heedlessness, reminding the believer that guidance ultimately rests with Allah and that one's duty is to strive earnestly in calling to faith without expecting universal acceptance.

translation: And you do not ask them for any reward for it. It is nothing but a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity and selflessness of the prophetic message, indicating that the Messenger does not seek worldly compensation for delivering God's guidance. The reminder is intended for all people across time and space, highlighting the universal and timeless nature of the Qur'anic message.

translation: And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by while they are turning away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of many people to overlook or ignore the clear signs of God's existence and power that are manifested throughout the creation of the heavens and the earth. Despite these evident signs, they choose to turn away, either out of heedlessness or denial, thereby missing the opportunity to recognize and understand the divine truth.

translation: And most of them believe not in Allah except that they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that many people profess belief in Allah yet simultaneously commit shirk, associating partners with Him. True faith demands exclusive devotion to Allah alone, without attributing divine qualities to others. The verse warns against superficial belief that is contradicted by actions, emphasizing that true iman (faith) is free from any form of polytheism.

translation: Do they feel secure that a sudden overwhelming punishment from Allah will not come upon them, or that the Hour will not come upon them unexpectedly while they do not perceive it?
interpretation: This verse cautions against complacency and false security regarding divine justice and the Day of Judgment. It reminds that God's punishment, or the Hour, can arrive suddenly and without warning, emphasizing the need for constant awareness, repentance, and preparation for accountability before God.

translation: Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and certainty of the prophetic mission. It highlights the necessity of calling to God with understanding and conviction, distinguishing the path of true monotheism from idolatry. It affirms the sincerity of the Prophet and his followers in their devotion to Allah alone, rejecting any form of association or polytheism.

translation: And We have not sent before you [O Muhammad] except men to whom We revealed [Our message] from among the people of the towns. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the hereafter is better for those who fear Allah; so will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all prophets before Muhammad were ordinary men chosen to receive divine revelation. It urges people to reflect on history and the consequences faced by previous communities who rejected guidance, highlighting that the ultimate success lies in the life to come for those who are conscious of God. It calls upon people to use reason and learn from the past to make choices that lead to eternal benefit.

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the sinful people.
interpretation: This verse teaches that even when messengers and their followers face extreme despair and feel abandoned, divine assistance arrives at the appointed time. It highlights God's absolute power and wisdom in delivering aid and justice, ensuring that no harm can be removed from wrongdoers without His will, and that ultimately, those chosen by God will be saved.

translation: Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding. It is not a fabricated tale, but a confirmation of what was before it, a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the narratives in the Qur'an are intended to provide thoughtful lessons and reflections for those who possess wisdom and understanding. It emphasizes the truthfulness of these stories, affirming that they are not inventions but confirm earlier revelations, offering comprehensive details and serving as guidance and mercy for believers. The verse encourages believers to seek the deeper meanings and lessons within these stories to strengthen their faith and moral conduct.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Book, and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth; but most people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran is a divine revelation containing true guidance from Allah. Despite the undeniable truth of these revelations, the majority of people reject faith, illustrating human tendencies toward disbelief and resistance to accepting divine truth.

translation: Allah is the One who raised the heavens without any pillars that you can see; then He established Himself above the Throne. He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its fixed course. He regulates the affair, explaining the signs so that you may be certain of meeting your Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in creating and sustaining the universe without visible supports, emphasizing that natural phenomena operate under His precise control and purpose. It invites reflection on the miraculous order of creation as a means to strengthen faith and certainty in the eventual meeting with the Creator.

translation: And He it is Who spread out the earth and placed firm mountains therein and rivers; and of all fruits He made pairs two mates; He covers the night with the day. Indeed in that are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deliberate design and balance in the natural world, highlighting the earth's expansiveness, the stability provided by mountains, the life-sustaining rivers, and the duality found in fruits, as well as the continual alternation of night and day. These elements serve as profound signs of Allah's wisdom and power, meant to inspire thoughtful contemplation and recognition of the Creator's meticulous order in the universe.

translation: And [He] has made in the earth [mountain] ranges standing and [made] gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees [growing] in clusters and [others] uncultivated, watered with one water; yet We make some of them exceed others in quality of fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's creation of diverse natural elements that coexist harmoniously and are sustained by a single source of water, symbolizing unity amidst diversity. The varying qualities of fruits arising from this shared sustenance serve as a sign to those who reflect, demonstrating Allah's wisdom and the purposeful design in creation, encouraging humans to contemplate His power and the interconnectedness of all creation.

translation: And if you are amazed, then [be] amazed at their saying, "When we have become dust, will we indeed be brought into a new creation?" Those are the ones who disbelieve in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the astonishment and skepticism of disbelievers regarding resurrection after death. Their disbelief is not merely an intellectual stance but a rejection that leads to spiritual bondage—symbolized by shackles—and eternal punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying God's power to resurrect and the reality of the hereafter.

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment before the good (comes), while there have already passed away before them examples (of punishment). And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the impatience of some people who demand immediate punishment for wrongdoing, neglecting the mercy and forgiveness that God extends to humanity. It reminds us that while God is generous and forgiving, His justice is real and severe, and that previous communities that rejected the message faced consequences as well. The verse teaches that God's mercy precedes His punishment, and that human impatience should be tempered with awareness of God's justice and forgiveness.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?" You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the common objection of disbelievers who demand miraculous evidence to believe. It emphasizes that the Prophet's role is primarily to deliver the warning and guidance, while guidance itself is granted according to God's wisdom to each community through their appointed guides or messengers; thus, faith requires trust in the message rather than dependence solely on miracles.

translation: Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs decrease or increase, and everything with Him is by measure.
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's comprehensive knowledge and control over the intricacies of creation, including the hidden processes of reproduction and growth. It emphasizes that all changes, whether gains or losses, occur within His precise and measured decree, highlighting His omniscience and perfect regulation of all matters.

translation: [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted.
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes God's comprehensive knowledge over all things hidden and apparent, affirming His supreme greatness and transcendence above all creation, highlighting that nothing escapes His awareness and His majesty is beyond comparison.

translation: Whether among you are those who conceal the word and those who manifest it, and those who are fearless by night, and who steal away by day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different ways in which people may express or conceal their thoughts and beliefs. It indicates that some individuals may hide their faith or convictions due to fear or caution, while others openly declare them regardless of circumstances. The mention of night and day symbolizes secrecy and openness, showing that true intention and sincerity are known to God alone, beyond outward appearances or actions.

translation: For him are angels in succession, before and behind him; they guard him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no repeller of it. And they have no protector besides Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of personal and collective responsibility in reform and change. While divine protection and blessing are assured by Allah’s command, true transformation occurs only when individuals or communities actively seek to improve their inner selves—beliefs, intentions, and actions. It teaches that without sincere effort and self-initiative, divine assistance alone will not alter one’s state. Additionally, it highlights the absolute authority of Allah’s will: once He decrees a consequence, it cannot be averted by others, underscoring His ultimate control and the futility of relying on other protectors besides Him.

translation: He it is who shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and who produces the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's control over the natural phenomena that evoke deep emotions within us. The lightning that instills both fear and hope symbolizes the dual aspects of divine power: awe of His might and the hope for His mercy. It exemplifies how Allah manages the forces of nature, reminding believers of His omnipotence and the delicate balance between fear and hope in our relationship with Him.

translation: And the thunder glorifies His praise, and the angels from fear of Him; and He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills. Yet they dispute about Allah, while He is severe in assault.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the supremacy and awe-inspiring power of Allah manifested through natural phenomena like thunder and lightning, emphasizing that even the angels glorify Him out of reverence. It serves as a reminder that humans, despite witnessing such signs, engage in disputes about the existence and nature of Allah, neglecting His undeniable might and authority.

translation: It is the call of Truth, but those whom they call besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except as if one stretches out his hands to water to reach his mouth, but it does not reach it. The calls of the disbelievers are but in error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of invoking false deities or partners alongside Allah. Their inability to respond or help, likened to the impossible act of water reaching the mouth by merely stretching out hands, signifies their absolute impotence and the misguided nature of such worship. It underscores that true assistance and response come only from Allah, and calling upon others leads one further into misguidance and error.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the afternoons.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that all creation, without exception, submits to the will and majesty of Allah, whether willingly out of recognition and love or unwillingly out of divine decree. The mention of prostration emphasizes ultimate humility and devotion, while the reference to shadows prostrating at different times signifies the continuous, unceasing nature of this submission, highlighting the comprehensive sovereignty of Allah over all existence across time and space.

translation: Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allah." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or are darkness and light equal? Or have they assigned partners to Allah who created as He created, so that the creation seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It challenges the notion of associating partners with Allah by highlighting their impotence and inability to benefit or harm themselves or others. The rhetorical questions illustrate the impossibility of equating Allah with false deities or idols, likening it to comparing blindness with sight or darkness with light. The passage underlines that no creation can be like Allah, who alone is powerful and overriding. It calls for a clear recognition of Allah's singular divinity and rejection of polytheism.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries foam, rising up. And from what they kindle on the fire seeking adornment or enjoyment, there arises foam like it. Thus Allah strikes the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, [being] scum; but what benefits the people remains on the earth. Thus Allah presents examples.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrast between what is temporary and worthless versus what is lasting and beneficial through the metaphor of foam carried by water or fire. The foam, which quickly disappears, represents falsehood or superficial things that leave no lasting impact, while the beneficial substance that remains symbolizes truth and actions that have enduring value for humanity. Allah uses such allegories to help us discern between what is transient and misleading and what is truly valuable and meaningful in life.

translation: For those who obey their Lord in truth (the best), but those who do not obey Him, even if they had all that is in the earth and twice as much with it, they would certainly seek to ransom themselves with it. Those have a dreadful account, and their abode is Hell—and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound value of sincerely responding to the call of God. It teaches that genuine obedience and submission to God are more precious than all the wealth of the world combined. Those who reject this obedience, despite any worldly riches, remain in a state of loss and face severe consequences in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that spiritual success and ultimate salvation depend not on material wealth but on sincere submission to God’s guidance.

translation: Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those endowed with understanding take heed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who recognize and accept the divine truth of revelation and those who remain heedless or blind to it. It implies that true insight and wisdom involve acknowledging the authenticity and significance of the message from Allah, and that only people of sound intellect who reflect deeply benefit from it.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of faithfulness and integrity in upholding the commitments made to Allah. It highlights that true believers are those who honor their agreements and remain steadfast in their obligations, reflecting sincerity and trustworthiness as foundational qualities in their relationship with God and with others.

translation: And those who join that which Allah has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of [their] account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of maintaining bonds—whether social, familial, or communal—that Allah has enjoined upon us, highlighting a spiritual commitment to uphold relationships and responsibilities. It underscores the importance of God-consciousness and fear of accountability in the Hereafter as motivating factors to preserve these ties, reflecting a profound moral consciousness guiding ethical behavior.

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the pleasure of their Lord, and establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, and prevent evil with good - those will have the good consequence of [this] home (paradise).
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of truly patient believers whose endurance is not passive but active and purposeful, aimed at pleasing God. Their commitment to regular prayer, generous giving both openly and discreetly, and their character in responding to wrongdoing with kindness, collectively cultivate a moral and spiritual excellence. This conduct leads to a lasting and blessed reward, signifying that steadfastness combined with righteous actions ensures success in the hereafter.

translation: Gardens of Eden, they will enter them, along with the righteous of their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants; and the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse signifies the comprehensive and inclusive nature of Allah's mercy and reward in Paradise, where not only the individual but also their righteous family members share in the blessings, highlighting the interconnectedness of faith and righteousness across generations and emphasizing the communal joy and honor bestowed upon the believers, as manifest by the angels entering from all gates to greet them.

translation: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home (Paradise).
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for patience amid trials and hardships, assuring believers that enduring difficulties with steadfastness leads to ultimate peace and a splendid eternal abode in the hereafter.

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on the earth — for them is the curse, and they will have the worst home.
interpretation: This verse warns against betraying the commitments made to Allah and disrupting the harmony and unity that He has commanded among people. It underscores that breaking such sacred covenants and causing disorder on earth violates divine trust and justice, leading to severe consequences both spiritually, through the curse, and in worldly life, by inhabiting a place fraught with hardship and misery.

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. They rejoice in the life of this world, while the life of this world compared to the Hereafter is but a fleeting enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that sustenance and provision come solely from Allah's will, highlighting His absolute control over the affairs of this world. It also warns against becoming overly attached to worldly pleasures, as they are temporary and insignificant compared to the eternal and true bliss of the Hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been revealed to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates that guidance and misguidance are ultimately under Allah's control. It teaches that miracles or signs are not given on demand by human will, but guidance is granted to those who sincerely return to Allah with repentance and humility. The verse emphasizes personal responsibility in seeking guidance and acknowledges Allah's wisdom in directing people according to His knowledge and justice.

translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Indeed, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is accompanied by inner peace and tranquility, which are achieved through the constant remembrance of Allah. It teaches that the heart finds true calmness not through worldly means, but by turning to God in consciousness, prayer, and reflection, highlighting the spiritual practice of dhikr as the source of reassurance and steadfastness in faith.

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, good tidings for them and an excellent final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is inseparable from righteous actions; the ultimate success and happiness belong to those who not only hold sincere belief but also manifest it through good deeds, leading to a rewarding and honorable outcome in the hereafter.

translation: Thus We have sent you as a messenger to a people before whom other peoples have passed away, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, 'He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. In Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn in repentance.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the continuity of prophethood, revealing that the Messenger is sent to a new community just as messengers were sent to past nations who also rejected the revelation. It highlights the prophet’s unwavering trust in God's sovereignty and mercy despite the disbelief he faces, serving as a model of steadfast faith and complete reliance on God alone.

translation: And if a Qur'an is sent down and it causes mountains to move, or the earth to be cleaved apart, or the dead to speak by it, then surely the command belongs entirely to Allah. Have those who believe despaired that if Allah wills, He would guide all people? And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck with calamities due to what they have done, or a punishment will come close to their homes, until the promise of Allah arrives. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the power and will of Allah transcend all miraculous phenomena; even extraordinary signs like moving mountains or raising the dead are under His control. It rebukes those believers who despair of Allah's ability to guide all humanity, reminding them that guidance is solely by Allah's will. Furthermore, it warns disbelievers that divine retribution is certain and will continue until the fulfillment of Allah's promise, highlighting the inevitability of justice. The verse ultimately teaches reliance on Allah's authority and patience in awaiting the realization of His decree.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them. So how [terrible] was My punishment?
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the rejection and mockery faced by messengers is not new; past nations also ridiculed their prophets yet were given time to repent. However, procrastinating repentance and persisting in disbelief leads inevitably to divine punishment. The passage warns against complacency and denial towards truth, emphasizing that God's mercy has limits, and ultimate justice will prevail.

translation: Is then one who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned—while they have assigned partners to Allah—better? Say, "Name those partners." Or do you inform Him of what He does not know in the earth, or is it a statement of disbelief? Rather, their deception is made alluring to those who disbelieve, and they are barred from the way. And whoever Allah sends astray - none can guide him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and injustice of assigning partners to Allah, highlighting His exclusive authority and knowledge over all souls and their deeds. It challenges the believers to name these supposed partners or to prove any knowledge they have beyond Allah's, underscoring human incapacity to rival divine wisdom. The verse also warns that such false beliefs deceive and mislead the disbelievers, causing them to stray from the true path, and affirms that guidance ultimately rests solely in Allah's hands.

translation: They will have a punishment in this worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. They will have no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and justice of divine retribution both in this life and the hereafter. It serves as a warning that wrongdoing and disbelief lead to consequences not only in this world but even more intensely in the eternal life, highlighting the certainty and inescapability of God's judgment.

translation: The example of Paradise, which the righteous are promised, is that beneath it rivers flow; its fruit is everlasting, and its shade. That is the consequence for those who have taqwa (piety). But the consequence for the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal reward awaiting those who cultivate God-consciousness and righteousness: a blissful paradise with flowing rivers, perpetual fruits, and comforting shade, symbolizing eternal peace and sustenance. It contrasts their fate with that of the disbelievers, emphasizing that moral and spiritual consciousness leads to lasting success and happiness, while heedlessness leads to destruction.

translation: And those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, and among the parties are those who reject some of it. Say, 'I am only commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I call and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who accept and rejoice in the revelation brought by the Prophet—acknowledging its continuity with previous scriptures—and those factions who reject parts of it out of division or prejudice. It emphasizes the Prophet's fundamental duty: pure monotheistic worship devoid of any partnership with Allah. The verse calls the believer to sincere devotion and ultimate reliance upon Allah, recognizing Him as the final destination and judge.

translation: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic judgment. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have against Allah no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and clarity of the Quranic revelation, affirming its role as a clear and just ruling. It warns against following personal desires or the whims of others when they contradict the knowledge brought by God, highlighting that true guidance and support come only through adherence to divine guidance, not through succumbing to misguided inclinations.

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you, and We made for them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human aspects of the prophets, emphasizing that they lived normal human lives with families, which underlines their relatability and humility. It also stresses that the miracles or signs they brought were not by their own power, but solely by Allah's permission, reminding believers that divine authority governs all events. Furthermore, the mention of a fixed term for every decree reflects the predetermined nature of destiny under God's wisdom and control.

translation: Allah erases what He wills and confirms; with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute authority of Allah over destiny and divine decree. It signifies that Allah has the power to remove or affirm anything in creation or in the course of events according to His wisdom. The reference to the "Mother of the Book" indicates the Preserved Tablet, the ultimate source and record of all knowledge and decrees, affirming that everything that happens is in accordance with Allah's eternal and unalterable knowledge.

translation: And if We show you some of what We promise them, or cause you to die before it, then upon you is only the duty to convey [the message], and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet’s responsibility in delivering the message with clarity, irrespective of the outcome. It highlights that the ultimate judgment and recompense lie with Allah, relieving the Prophet from the burden of influencing outcomes. The emphasis is on the trustworthiness of the message transmission, not the Prophet’s control over how people respond or when divine justice is enacted.

translation: Do they not see that We gradually reduce the land from its outskirts? And Allah decides; none can reverse His decision. He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute authority and control over the natural world, illustrating how He diminishes the land bit by bit as a sign of His power and judgment. It reminds us that His decrees are final and unchallengeable, and that He swiftly holds all accountable for their actions.

translation: And those who preceded them had plotted, but to Allah belongs all planning. He knows what every soul earns. And the disbelievers will soon know to whom will belong the final home.
interpretation: This verse highlights that while people may scheme and plan, ultimate control and outcome are determined by Allah alone, who is fully aware of every individual's deeds. It serves as a reminder that despite apparent success or failure, the final destiny lies with Allah's judgment, reassuring believers that truth and justice will prevail in the hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "You are not sent." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and [the one] upon whom knowledge of the Scripture rests."
interpretation: This verse addresses the denial faced by the Prophet Muhammad from the disbelievers who reject his prophethood. It emphasizes that the truth of the message does not rely on human acceptance but rests firmly on God's testimony and the knowledge established in the divine scripture. This serves as a reminder that ultimate judgment and validation come from Allah alone, and human rejection cannot nullify the truth of the prophetic mission.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine purpose of the Qur'an as a guidance granted by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad, serving as a means to elevate humanity from ignorance, confusion, and misguidance ('darknesses') into enlightenment, clarity, and spiritual awareness ('light'). It highlights that this transition occurs only through Allah's permission, underscoring His ultimate authority and the reliance on His guidance. The verse concludes by directing believers to the 'Path' characterized by strength and praiseworthiness, reflecting the ideal way of living under divine guidance.

translation: Allah is the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah, emphasizing that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, underscoring His supreme authority and ownership over all creation. It also serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith, indicating that disbelief leads to a grievous and severe consequence, thus urging reflection on belief and the reality of divine justice.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter, and who hinder others from the way of Allah, seeking to make it crooked, those are in far error.
interpretation: This verse warns against prioritizing worldly gains and pleasures over spiritual and eternal success. It highlights the dangers of such a preference, noting that those who not only choose the temporal life over the eternal one but also attempt to obstruct the path of divine guidance and bend it to their own desires are deeply misguided and far from the truth.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people to clearly convey the message to them. Allah causes whom He wills to stray and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine wisdom in sending messengers who communicate in the language and context familiar to their own communities, ensuring the message is understood deeply. It also highlights Allah's ultimate authority in guiding or allowing misguidance based on His wisdom, affirming that guidance is a divine gift given to those whom He wills, and His power and wisdom are absolute.

translation: And indeed We sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring out your people from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah." Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission of Prophet Moses as a guide to lead his people from ignorance, oppression, and misguidance (darkness) to knowledge, liberation, and faith (light). It emphasizes the importance of remembering and reflecting on God's favors and miraculous interventions ('the days of Allah') to strengthen faith. The signs mentioned are meant to encourage perseverance and gratitude, showing that true understanding and success come through patience and thankfulness to God.

translation: And remember when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive.' And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude towards God's blessings, especially in moments of deliverance from severe oppression and hardship. It emphasizes that trials and suffering, such as those faced under Pharaoh's tyranny, are tests from Allah designed to strengthen faith and reliance on Him. Remembering these blessings fosters resilience, thankfulness, and awareness of God's mercy amid adversity.

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle that gratitude to God not only earns His blessings but also leads to their increase, highlighting the positive cycle of thankfulness fostering growth in divine favor. Conversely, ingratitude or denial results in severe consequences, underscoring the importance of recognizing and appreciating God's bounties as a means to receive more, while warning against the spiritual and worldly detriments of ungratefulness.

translation: And Moses said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, Allah is Free from need, Praiseworthy."
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-sufficiency and independence of Allah from His creation. It teaches that disbelief or rejection by all of humanity does not diminish Allah's existence or worthiness. Allah’s attributes of being free from need and praiseworthy emphasize that His reality and value are intrinsic and not dependent on human recognition or acceptance.

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those before you—the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, and those after them? Only Allah knows them. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they rejected them by putting their hands over their mouths, saying, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us."
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the fate of past peoples who rejected divine guidance despite clear evidence, illustrating human tendencies towards denial and skepticism when confronted with inconvenient truths. It underscores the idea that such rejection leads to spiritual ruin and warns the current audience to avoid similar stubbornness, emphasizing the importance of humility and openness to truth as revealed by God.

translation: Their messengers said, "Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you that He may forgive you of your sins and delay you to a specified term." They said, "You are not but human beings like us, seeking to turn us away from what our forefathers used to worship. So bring us a clear authority."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the skepticism and rejection often faced by prophets when they bring the message of monotheism. It highlights the challenge of changing established beliefs and the human tendency to demand tangible proof before accepting truth. The verse reminds us that doubt about the Creator is unfounded and that God's invitation is one of mercy and forgiveness, urging people to look beyond inherited blind traditions and to embrace faith based on certainty and understanding.

translation: Their messengers said to them, "We are only human like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants. It was never for us to bring you a clear authority except by Allah's permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that messengers are human beings like us, but what distinguishes them is that they receive divine guidance and authority from Allah. It emphasizes that true power and authority come only through Allah's will, and believers should place their trust and reliance in Allah alone, recognizing that human efforts are dependent on His permission and support.

translation: Why should we not rely on Allah while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient over what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant rely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound strength and confidence that comes from placing trust in Allah. It emphasizes that true reliance on God is born of the guidance He provides, which illuminates the correct path. Patience in the face of adversity and harm is possible when such trust is rooted in divine support, demonstrating that reliance on Allah is both a source of endurance and a shield against hardship.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion." So their Lord inspired to them, "Indeed, We will destroy the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the steadfastness of the disbelievers in opposing the messengers and their message, threatening expulsion or forced return to disbelief. Despite their threats, God's promise to annihilate the wrongdoers underscores the ultimate failure of injustice and tyranny, affirming divine justice and protection for the righteous.

translation: And We will make you dwell in the land after them. That is for he who fears My standing and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who maintain a deep consciousness and reverence for God's presence and punishment will be granted the honor and stability of inhabiting the earth after previous generations. It highlights the virtue of piety and fear of God as the basis for divine favor and the continuity of a righteous legacy.

translation: And they sought victory, but every arrogant tyrant failed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable downfall of those who persist in arrogance and tyranny despite their efforts to gain triumph, emphasizing that true success does not belong to the proud oppressors.

translation: Behind them is Hell, and they will be given to drink scalding water.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning about the consequences of certain wrongful actions. It illustrates the severe punishment that awaits those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing that their ultimate fate is Hell, and that they will endure suffering symbolized by being forced to drink boiling, unpleasant water. This portrayal underscores the seriousness of moral accountability and the reality of divine recompense.

translation: He drinks it, but hardly can he swallow it, and death comes to him from everywhere, yet he is not to die. And behind him is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse depicts a state of intense agony and impending doom where the person is caught in a tormenting cycle of suffering and evasion of death, highlighting the inevitability of divine punishment and the futility of escaping God's decree. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability and the severe consequences that await those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing.

translation: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes stirred up by a violent wind on a stormy day; they cannot retain anything of what they have earned. That is the extreme error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and instability of the deeds of those who reject belief in their Lord. Their actions, lacking divine guidance and purpose, are compared to ashes scattered by a strong wind—meaning they have no lasting value or impact. Without faith, good deeds do not find firm grounding and thus cannot benefit the individual, symbolizing the profound misguidance and loss faced by disbelievers.

translation: Have you not considered that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over all existence, reminding us that the creation of the heavens and the earth is purposeful and real. It warns of the impermanence of humans and all creation, highlighting that if Allah wills, He can replace the current creation with entirely new beings, reinforcing our dependence on His will and encouraging humility and mindfulness of His authority.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and capability, affirming that no matter the task or decree, it poses no difficulty or impossibility for Him to accomplish it.

translation: And they will all appear before Allah; then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so will you avert from us the punishment of Allah at all?" They will say, "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show impatience or are patient; there is no refuge for us.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of blindly following arrogant leaders who rejected guidance. It highlights that one's proximity to misguided individuals cannot provide protection from Allah's punishment; responsibility is individual. It emphasizes the futility of excuses based on following others and the inevitability of accountability before Allah.

translation: And the devil will say when the matter has been concluded, "Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when Satan admits his deception, clarifying that his influence over humans is limited to his invitation, which they accepted of their own free will. It emphasizes personal responsibility for one's choices and rejects the idea of blaming external forces for one's wrongdoings. Ultimately, it affirms that those who commit injustice and associate partners with Allah will face severe consequences, highlighting the justice and accountability inherent in divine judgment.

translation: And admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein by permission of their Lord; and their greeting therein will be, "Peace."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who combine faith with righteous actions, emphasizing that their eternal abode is a place of ultimate peace and blessing, underscoring the mercy and justice of God in granting paradise to the faithful who live righteously.

translation: Have you not seen how Allah sets forth the example of a good word as a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches reach to the sky?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound impact and enduring nature of a righteous word or deed. Like a tree with a strong root and lofty branches, a good word grounds a person in faith and virtue, growing and spreading benefits far and wide, symbolizing stability, growth, and continuous positive influence in this life and beyond.

translation: It gives its fruit at all times by the permission of its Lord. And Allah sets forth parables for the people that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuous and perfect provision of sustenance by God's will, symbolized by the tree that bears fruit at all times. It signifies God's control over nature and life's blessings, and the parables serve to remind people to recognize and be grateful for these divine favors, encouraging mindfulness and reflection on God's signs in the world.

translation: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the destructive nature of corrupt or false speech by comparing it to a tree that is completely uprooted, symbolizing instability and lack of foundation. Just as such a tree cannot survive or bring benefit, evil words lack permanence and lead to ruin, emphasizing the importance of truthful and beneficial speech.

translation: Allah firmly establishes those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. And Allah leads astray the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah strengthens and supports the believers by grounding them in unshakable truth and guidance, both in this life and the hereafter. It highlights divine justice, where the oppressors are misled as a consequence of their actions, underscoring that ultimately, Allah's will prevails in guiding or leading astray according to His wisdom and decree.

translation: Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and have settled their people in the abode of ruin?
interpretation: This verse warns against the ingratitude of those who abandon faith despite the countless blessings bestowed upon them by Allah. It highlights the consequence of such disbelief—bringing ruin not only upon themselves but also upon their descendants, emphasizing the far-reaching impact of turning away from divine guidance.

translation: They will enter Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse serves as a grave warning about the consequences of persistent wrongdoing and rejection of truth. It highlights the inevitability of accountability and the severe punishment awaiting those who persist in evil, emphasizing the importance of adhering to righteousness and seeking forgiveness to avoid such a dreadful fate.

translation: And they have attributed to Allah equals to mislead [people] from His way. Say, "Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire."
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of associating partners with Allah, emphasizing that those who do so are deliberately diverting themselves and others from the true path. It serves as a stern reminder that worldly enjoyments and distractions are ultimately futile, as the final abode for such misguided actions is punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: Say to My servants who have believed, establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, before there comes a Day when there will be no exchange or friendship.
interpretation: This verse invites believers to actively practice devotion and generosity, emphasizing the urgency of performing righteous deeds now, as there will come a final Day of Judgment when worldly transactions and intercessions will cease to benefit anyone.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky, through which He brought forth fruits as provision for you. He has subjected the ships to serve you, so that they may sail through the sea by His command, and has subjected the rivers for you.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's sovereignty and mercy in providing for human needs. It reminds us that every blessing, from sustenance to means of transportation, is under His control and given to us out of His grace. Recognizing this should inspire gratitude and dependence upon Allah alone, acknowledging that all aspects of life are interconnected through His will and power.

translation: And He has subjected for you the sun and the moon, continuously pursuing their courses; and He has subjected for you the night and the day.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's control over the natural phenomena that are essential for human life, emphasizing that the orderly movement of the sun, moon, and the alternation of night and day are means provided by God to benefit humanity, facilitating timekeeping, growth, and rest.

translation: And He provided you with all that you asked for. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, man is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the boundless blessings and provisions bestowed upon humanity by Allah, highlighting that no matter how much we try, we cannot fully account for His favors. Yet, despite these countless blessings, human nature tends toward ingratitude and injustice, failing to recognize and appreciate Allah's generosity.

translation: And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols."
interpretation: This verse highlights Prophet Abraham's prayer for the safety and sanctity of Makkah and for himself and his descendants to remain steadfast in monotheism, rejecting idolatry. It reflects the importance of seeking divine protection for places of spiritual significance and upholding pure faith free from polytheism.

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led many astray. So whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me – indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of a prophet acknowledging that many people have been misguided by the actions of others, yet he affirms the importance of following the true prophetic guidance to be rightly connected to him. It emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness even towards those who disobey, reminding us that while guidance is crucial, God's compassion encompasses human shortcomings.

translation: Our Lord, indeed I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reflects a heartfelt supplication, emphasizing the importance of establishing a community devoted to spiritual practices, such as prayer, in a place close to the sacred. It teaches that divine guidance and provision are essential for the growth and gratitude of a people, underscoring the link between faith, sustenance, and communal harmony.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah in the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute knowledge of Allah over all matters, both hidden and apparent. It reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of their inner thoughts, intentions, and outward actions, emphasizing that there is no secret in the universe beyond His knowledge. This serves as a reminder to maintain sincerity and consciousness of God in all aspects of life, knowing that one’s true intentions are always known to Him.

translation: All praise is due to Allah, who has granted me, even in old age, Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of Allah's mercy and blessings, demonstrating that He answers sincere prayers regardless of one's age or circumstances. It emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah with faith and patience, trusting that He listens and responds to the heartfelt calls of His servants.

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This verse is a humble prayer to God, emphasizing the importance of consistency in worship and the desire for that devotion to be passed down through generations. It highlights the believer's recognition that establishing prayer is vital for spiritual growth and seeking God’s acceptance encourages sincerity and connection in worship.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established.
interpretation: This verse is a heartfelt supplication seeking divine mercy and forgiveness not only for oneself but also for one's parents and all believers on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the importance of collective supplication, acknowledging that the well-being of the individual is connected to the community of faith and that ultimate accountability lies with God on the Day when all deeds are judged.

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare intensely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of every injustice and wrongdoing committed by the oppressors. The apparent delay in punishment is not negligence but a divine wisdom, allowing for a final, just reckoning on the Day of Judgment when all hidden deeds will be exposed and accounted for.

translation: Hurried away, their heads covered; they do not turn their eyes back to them, and their hearts are void.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the state of those who reject the truth and rush away from it, covering their heads as a sign of shame or avoidance. Their refusal to look back symbolizes a denial or deliberate avoidance of guidance, and their hearts being described as 'void' signifies a lack of sincere faith or understanding, resulting in emptiness of spirit and disconnect from divine truth.

translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who have wronged will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will respond to Your call and follow the messengers." "Did you not swear before that there would be no cessation [to time]?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to procrastinate repentance and obedience until faced with imminent punishment. Even those who have wronged intend to reform when confronted with the reality of judgment, but their delayed admission underscores the gravity of their prior denial and broken promises, emphasizing the urgency of responding to guidance before it is too late.

translation: And you dwelled in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them; and We presented to you examples.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of historical lessons by reminding that the inhabitants lived in the homes of wrongdoers who brought ruin upon themselves. By observing their fate, believers are cautioned to avoid similar paths of injustice and heed divine guidance to prevent self-destruction.

translation: And they have planned their plan, but with Allah is their plan, even if their plan should be to move the mountains.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the futility of human scheming when it opposes God's will. No matter how powerful or determined the plans of people may be—even plans as ambitious as moving mountains—ultimately, God's authority and control surpass all, rendering such plots ineffective against His divine decree.

translation: So do not think that Allah will fail in His promise to His Messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and reliability of Allah’s promises made through His messengers, reassuring believers that divine justice and support will inevitably manifest. It highlights Allah's supreme power and ability to enforce His will, assuring that any apparent delay is not a breach of promise but part of divine wisdom.

translation: The Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well]; and they will emerge before Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse portrays the profound transformation that will occur on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that the reality as we know it will be completely altered. It underscores the absolute power and dominance of Allah, before whom all creatures will stand accountable. The emphasis on Allah as 'the One, the Prevailing' reflects His unmatched authority and the inevitability of His judgment over all affairs.

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in chains.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitable punishment and humiliation awaiting wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that their deeds have led them to a state of captivity and disgrace from which there is no escape.

translation: Their garments will be of pitch, and fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the severe punishment awaiting the wrongdoers in the hereafter; the garments of pitch denote oppressive, burning clothing that causes extreme pain, and the covering of fire over their faces signifies the overwhelming and inescapable nature of divine retribution for those who persist in evil deeds.

translation: That Allah may recompense every soul for that which it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice: every individual is accountable for their own actions, and Allah will reward or punish accordingly without delay or oversight. It serves as a reminder of personal responsibility and the certainty of judgment, encouraging believers to act rightly knowing that their deeds will be swiftly and fairly recompensed by Allah.

translation: This is a proclamation for the people, that they may be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Quran as a clear and universal message intended for all humanity, serving as a warning and a reminder. It underscores the fundamental belief in the oneness of God, encouraging thoughtful reflection and understanding among those who possess intellect and wisdom.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting its clarity and the distinct revelation it embodies. It serves as an affirmation that the scripture contains profound guidance and undeniable signs meant to lead humanity to truth and understanding.

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve wish that they were Muslims.
interpretation: This verse reflects the idea that those who reject faith may, in moments of reflection or distress, wish they had embraced Islam. It highlights the internal conflict and regret that can occur when one resists the truth, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and openness to guidance before it becomes too late.

translation: Let them eat and enjoy themselves and be distracted by [false] hope, for indeed, they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and false hopes held by those who reject the truth. It serves as a warning that despite their current enjoyment and distractions, they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions and come to realize the reality of the hereafter.

translation: And We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree (destiny).
interpretation: This verse highlights that the destruction of any community is not arbitrary; rather, it occurs according to a predetermined and clear divine decree. It emphasizes God's absolute knowledge and control over the fate of societies, reminding that consequences are part of a just and deliberate divine plan.

translation: No nation can precede its appointed time, nor can it delay it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the time decreed by Allah for the end or significant change of each community is fixed and cannot be altered; it reflects the divine control over the destiny of peoples and the inevitability of God's predetermined plan.

translation: And they said, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection and mockery faced by Prophet Muhammad from some of his contemporaries who, unable to understand the divine nature of the revelation, dismissed him as insane. It reflects the challenge of conveying a transcendent truth to a society resistant to change and highlights the perseverance required in the face of misunderstanding and opposition.

translation: If only you would bring us the angels, if you should be among the truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges the claimant to bring forth angels as proof of truthfulness, highlighting the demand for irrefutable evidence and emphasizing the impossibility of fulfilling such a challenge to validate false claims.

translation: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, and they do not cause [disorder].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that angels are sent by Allah solely with truthful and purposeful messages, never engaging in falsehood or chaos. It highlights the purity and precision of divine communication through angels, underscoring that whatever they convey is grounded in ultimate truth and serve to maintain order rather than create confusion.

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the preservation of the Qur'an is solely under God's protection. It signifies that despite any attempts to alter, distort, or forget its contents, God guarantees its unaltered existence across time, ensuring the guidance remains pure and accessible to all humanity.

translation: And indeed, We sent before you [O Muhammad] messengers to former peoples.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance through messengers sent to previous communities, illustrating that the message brought by Prophet Muhammad is part of a longstanding tradition of revelation aimed at guiding humanity toward righteousness.

translation: And no messenger comes to them except that they ridicule him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent rejection and mockery faced by messengers and prophets from certain groups of people. It reflects a hardened attitude and unwillingness to sincerely listen to divine guidance, often leading to spiritual blindness and the consequences of dismissing truth out of arrogance or ignorance.

translation: Thus, We instill it into the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse signifies that divine guidance or certain feelings are placed within the hearts of those who commit wrongdoing as a form of trial or consequence, highlighting that their inner disposition is influenced by their actions and choices.

translation: They do not believe in it, while the way of those who passed away before them has already passed away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of disbelievers rejecting the truth despite clear signs and the precedents set by previous nations who also denied divine revelations and faced consequences. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of persistent disbelief and an encouragement to reflect on history to avoid repeating the same mistakes.

translation: And if We had opened to them a gate from the heaven and they continued ascending through it,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitations of human faith and perception; even if a clear and undeniable sign from the heavens were made manifest, many would still refuse to believe, illustrating that true guidance comes from sincere intention and inner openness rather than just external wonders.

translation: They said, "Our eyes have only been dazzled; rather, we are a people affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the reaction of those who deny the truth, attributing their inability to perceive it clearly to external forces like magic or illusions, rather than admitting their own blindness or refusal to accept guidance.

translation: And indeed, We have made in the heaven constellations and have beautified it for the observers.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's intricate design and beautification of the heavens, demonstrating His power and artistry. The constellations serve not only as adornments but also as signs for humanity to observe, ponder upon, and recognize the greatness of the Creator. It invites reflection on the order and elegance of the universe as evidence of divine wisdom and intentionality.

translation: And We have guarded it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an is protected and preserved from any distortion, corruption, or influence of evil forces, ensuring its purity and authenticity as the divine guidance for humanity.

translation: Except one who snatches [some words] by stealing and follows the flashing fireball (shooting star).
interpretation: This verse refers to those who try to eavesdrop on the unseen world in the heavens. It highlights that such attempts are futile because the heavens are guarded by flaming meteors (shooting stars) that intercept and prevent any secret knowledge from being stolen. Symbolically, it demonstrates the protection of divine knowledge from being illicitly accessed by human beings.

translation: And the earth, We have spread it out and cast therein firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein every kind of balanced thing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's power and wisdom in creating a balanced and sustaining environment on earth. By laying out the earth, placing stable mountains, and causing diverse, measured vegetation to grow, it reflects the perfect design intended to support life in a harmonious and balanced manner.

translation: And We made for you therein means of living, and for those for whom you are not providers.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision for all creatures, emphasizing that sustenance is not limited to humans alone but extends to all living beings, regardless of human ability to provide for them. It reminds us of Allah's comprehensive care and sustenance for all creation, fostering trust in His provision and encouraging gratitude.

translation: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine control and precision in the management of all creation. It signifies that everything in existence is under Allah's custody and governance, and nothing occurs without His predetermined measure and wisdom. This reassures believers that all affairs unfold according to Allah's perfect knowledge and plan, reflecting His authority and the meticulous balance in the universe.

translation: And We sent the winds as pollinators, then sent down water from the sky and gave you to drink from it; and you are not its storekeepers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's control over natural phenomena and human dependence on His providence. It illustrates that sustenance, such as water, is granted by God's will through natural processes, yet humans have no ultimate control or ownership over these blessings; they are entrusted provisions from God, reminding us of our reliance on His mercy and power.

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute authority over life and death, underscoring that human existence is entirely dependent on His will. It also highlights that after the end of all creation, Allah alone remains the inheritor of everything, signifying His eternal sovereignty and the transient nature of worldly possessions and beings.

translation: And indeed, We know those among you who went ahead [in faith], and indeed, We know those who are to come later [after them].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's complete knowledge of all individuals, regardless of time. It serves as a reminder that no one can hide their intentions or actions from Allah, whether they came before or will come after, highlighting His omniscience over past, present, and future generations.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the one who will gather them together. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ultimate authority and control over the resurrection and the gathering of all beings for judgment. It reassures believers that God's wisdom and knowledge govern all affairs, and that the final outcome will be managed with perfect justice and insight.

translation: And indeed, We created man from a sounding clay of altered black mud.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble and intricate origin of human creation, reminding us that despite our physical beginnings from simple substances, we are endowed with purpose and potential by the Creator. It serves to humble human pride and highlight the divine power and wisdom in creating life from seemingly insignificant material.

translation: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that jinn are a distinct creation made from a subtle, intense fire, highlighting the diversity of beings created by God and the unique nature of jinn compared to humans, who are created from clay.

translation: And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay of altered black mud."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine origin and humble earthly materials from which human beings are created, emphasizing that despite being formed from mere clay, humans are bestowed with life and purpose by God, highlighting His supreme power and wisdom in creation.

translation: Then when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him.
interpretation: This verse signifies the unique honor and status granted to Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) by Allah. When Allah created him with precise care and imparted His spirit into him, it established Adam’s inherent dignity and the reason why the angels were commanded to prostrate to him, symbolizing respect and recognition of human nobility bestowed by divine spirit.

translation: So all the angels prostrated, all of them together.
