It underscores that what Allah offers in return—spiritual fulfillment, mercy, and eternal rewards—is far superior to any fleeting material advantage, encouraging sincere adherence to divine covenants.

translation: What you have will come to an end, but what Allah has is everlasting. And We will surely reward those who were patient with a reward better than what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly possessions and experiences contrasted with the eternal and everlasting blessings that Allah possesses. It reassures believers that endurance and patience in the face of life's difficulties will be met with a reward from Allah that surpasses any worldly recompense, highlighting the ultimate value of steadfast faith and perseverance.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the value of righteous deeds is not limited by gender; both men and women who sincerely believe and act righteously will be granted a good life, signifying well-being and satisfaction in this world. Moreover, Allah promises to reward such individuals with the best of their deeds, indicating a fair and generous recompense both in this life and the hereafter.

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to consciously seek Allah's protection from Satan before engaging in the recitation of the Qur'an, emphasizing the need to guard oneself against distractions and evil influences to ensure sincere and focused worship.

translation: Indeed, he has no authority over those who have believed and upon their Lord rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the impotence of Satan over true believers who place their trust in Allah. It highlights that faith and reliance on God create a protective barrier that Satan cannot penetrate or influence, reminding believers to maintain their trust in Allah to safeguard themselves from evil.

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as a protector and those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the power and influence of false deities or misled leaders are limited; they can only affect those who follow them or associate partners with God, highlighting the futility of their dominion compared to the true sovereignty of Allah.

translation: And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and Allah knows best what He sends down - they say, "You are but a forgery." But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations made against the Prophet Muhammad regarding the abrogation of certain revelations. It highlights that Allah, in His wisdom and knowledge, reveals guidance progressively, sometimes replacing earlier verses with new ones to suit the needs of the time. The criticism from disbelievers stems from their ignorance of divine wisdom, mistaking the evolution of revelation for forgery. The verse reassures that such changes are by Allah's command and knowledge, not fabrication.

translation: Say, "It [the Qur'an] was revealed by the Spirit, the Holy Spirit, from your Lord in truth, to confirm those who have believed and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a truthful revelation brought by the Holy Spirit, affirming the faith of believers, guiding them on the straight path, and offering glad tidings to those who submit to God. It reassures the believers of the divine origin and reliability of the message, strengthening their conviction and commitment.

translation: And indeed, We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is an Arabic clear language.
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge posed by disbelievers who attribute the Qur'anic revelation to human origins, specifically to a foreign teacher. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an being in clear, eloquent Arabic, contrasting it with the alleged foreign teacher's language. This underscores the uniqueness and divine origin of the Qur'an, as it could not have been taught or inspired by a person unfamiliar with Arabic's depth and nuances.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah, Allah does not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequence of rejecting the clear signs and revelations from Allah. It indicates that guidance is a divine gift granted only to those who accept faith sincerely. When a person persistently denies God's revelations, Allah withdraws guidance, leading them further away from truth and towards punishment as a result of their own disbelief and refusal to accept divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah are the ones who forge falsehood, and it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights that falsehood and fabrications are developed by those who reject the evidence and revelations of God. Their denial of divine signs is not a neutral stance but an active distortion, marking them as the true liars because they oppose the truth knowingly.

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after having believed, except for one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith - but those who open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse conveys that true faith is not merely a superficial acknowledgment but resides deeply in the heart. When someone is forced externally to deny their faith, yet internally remains firm, they are excused. However, those who willingly and openly turn away from belief after having embraced it invite divine anger and severe consequences. This underscores the gravity of sincere, unwavering faith and the peril of deliberate rejection after acceptance.

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse explains that those who choose the fleeting pleasures and concerns of this worldly life over the eternal and spiritual benefits of the Hereafter distance themselves from guidance. Their prioritization of immediate gratification blinds them from spiritual truths, making them unreceptive to divine guidance and ultimately leading to their misguidance.

translation: Those are the ones upon whose hearts, Allah has set a seal and (on) their hearing and their sight. And those are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse signifies that when people consistently reject truth and guidance, Allah seals their hearts and senses to prevent them from recognizing the reality. It reflects a spiritual state where due to persistent negligence or disbelief, individuals become closed off from comprehension and enlightenment, thus remaining heedless.

translation: Indeed, in the Hereafter, they are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who disbelieve or act unjustly, despite whatever success they may have in this worldly life, will ultimately suffer loss in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that true success is determined by one's standing before God after death, not by worldly gains or status.

translation: Then indeed, your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were harmed and then fought and were patient, indeed, your Lord afterward is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah recognizes the sincere sacrifices and struggles of those who leave their homes due to persecution or trials, continue to strive in His cause, and remain patient. Their efforts do not go unnoticed; Allah's forgiveness and mercy await them, highlighting His compassionate nature towards the steadfast believers.

translation: The Day when every soul will come disputing for itself, and every soul will be recompensed for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of the Day of Judgment, where each individual will stand accountable for their own deeds. It highlights personal responsibility and ensures that no one will be treated unjustly; everyone will receive exactly what they deserve based on their actions. This serves as a reminder to remain conscious of one's behavior and decisions, knowing that ultimate accountability rests with Allah, who is perfectly just.

translation: And Allah sets forth an example of a town that was safe and secure, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it disbelieved in the favors of Allah; so He made it taste the garments of hunger and fear because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of ingratitude and disbelief in God's blessings. The town, once prosperous and secure due to God's grace, faces hardship as a direct result of its own corruption and rejection of divine favors. It serves as a reminder that the security and sustenance we enjoy are from God, and neglecting this truth leads to suffering and loss.

translation: And indeed, a Messenger from among themselves came to them, but they denied him; so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that when a community rejects the guidance sent to them through a messenger who is one of their own, they incur divine punishment as a consequence of their injustice and obstinacy. It emphasizes the responsibility to heed sound guidance and warns against the perils of willful denial.

translation: So eat of the provision which Allah has provided for you, [which is] lawful and good, and be grateful for the favor of Allah, if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming what Allah has provided in a manner that is both lawful and wholesome, highlighting that gratitude towards Allah's blessings is an essential aspect of true worship. It reminds believers that worship is not only about rituals but also about recognizing and appreciating the sustenance and blessings granted by Allah, which in turn strengthens their faith and obedience.

translation: He has only forbidden to you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines specific prohibitions in dietary laws, emphasizing the sanctity of what is lawful and the prohibition of what is harmful or associated with polytheism. The allowance made for necessity reflects Allah's mercy and understanding of human circumstances, highlighting that when faced with dire need, one may deviate from the prohibition without blame, provided it is done without desire or excess. It underscores the balance between divine commandments and compassionate flexibility toward human hardship.

translation: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, "This is lawful and this is forbidden," to invent falsehood against Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse warns against the act of declaring something permissible or forbidden without true knowledge or divine sanction. It emphasizes that fabricating laws or misrepresenting divine commandments constitutes lying against Allah, which leads to failure and ruin. The interpretation highlights the importance of sincerity, honesty, and adherence to authentic teachings rather than personal opinions or falsehoods in matters of religious rulings.

translation: A brief enjoyment for them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary and limited nature of worldly pleasures when compared to the eternal consequences of one's actions. It serves as a warning that those who indulge solely in fleeting worldly gains without adhering to moral and spiritual responsibilities will face severe punishment in the hereafter.

translation: And for those who are Jews, We prohibited whatever We related to you before. And We did not wrong them, but they used to wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the prohibitions given to the Jewish people were part of divine legislation revealed previously, and that God has never acted unjustly towards them; rather, any harm that befell them was due to their own injustices and wrong actions.

translation: Then indeed, your Lord, for those who have done wrong in ignorance and then repent after that and amend, indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and readiness to forgive those who falter out of ignorance but sincerely repent and reform their ways. It reassures believers that past mistakes do not condemn them if they turn back to righteousness, highlighting the importance of sincere repentance and personal improvement.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth and not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound devotion and singular faith of Abraham, portraying him as embodying an entire community in his submission to God. It emphasizes his pure monotheism and steadfastness in worshiping Allah alone, serving as a timeless exemplar of sincere faith and rejection of idolatry or associating partners with God.

translation: Being grateful for His blessings. He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of gratitude towards Allah's blessings. It emphasizes that being thankful is not only an appreciation of what one has received but also a key to receiving further guidance from Allah. The 'straight path' (صراط مستقيم) symbolizes the righteous and correct way of living as ordained by Allah, and the verse illustrates that Allah's favor includes His guidance towards this path, which is essential for spiritual success and fulfillment.

translation: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, he is among the righteous in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the individual mentioned not only enjoys blessings and goodness in the worldly life but also merits a place among the righteous in the eternal life, emphasizing the connection between righteous deeds and divine reward both in this world and the hereafter.

translation: Then We inspired you to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and following the pure, unadulterated faith of Abraham, who sincerely devoted himself to the worship of one God without associating partners. It serves as a directive to adhere to the true path of Islam by rejecting polytheism and maintaining the purity of monotheistic belief as exemplified by Abraham.

translation: Indeed, the Sabbath was only appointed for those who differed about it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse implies that the commandment regarding the Sabbath was specifically legislated for the Jewish people because of their disputes about it; it serves as a test of obedience. Ultimately, Allah will judge all disputes and controversies on the Day of Judgment, affirming His ultimate authority and justice over all matters of disagreement among people.

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of approaching others with patience, kindness, and wisdom when calling them to faith or righteousness. It emphasizes that guidance is ultimately in Allah's hands, and that harshness or arrogance are not the means to win hearts or lead people to the truth. The best method is gentle, respectful dialogue that considers the other person's understanding and circumstances.

translation: And if you retaliate, retaliate with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle of balanced justice and the virtue of patience. It permits responding to harm with equivalent measures, ensuring fairness and preventing escalation, but it elevates patience as a superior moral response, highlighting that enduring wrongdoing without retaliation leads to greater spiritual reward and inner peace.

translation: And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah. And do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they plan.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true patience is granted by Allah alone, highlighting the importance of relying on Him during trials. It advises the believer not to be overwhelmed by sorrow or anxiety over the schemes and plots of others, emphasizing trust in Allah's wisdom and justice in dealing with adversities.

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who do good.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that God's support and presence are with those who maintain their consciousness of Him through piety (taqwa) and who actively engage in righteous and benevolent actions (ihsan). It emphasizes that divine companionship is a reward for sincere devotion combined with moral excellence.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Exalted is He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous Night Journey of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), carried out by God's command and power. It signifies God's ability to transcend the ordinary limitations of space and time, demonstrating His supreme dominion and the blessed nature of certain sacred places. The journey serves as a reminder of God's closeness, His awareness of His servant's surroundings, and the purpose of revealing divine signs to strengthen faith.

translation: And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, [saying], "Do not take anyone besides Me as a disposer of affairs."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation given to Moses was meant to guide the Children of Israel toward monotheism and reliance solely on Allah. It warns against associating partners with God or appointing others as lords or protectors besides Him, highlighting the importance of exclusive devotion to Allah in all matters of life and faith.

translation: Descendants of those We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of Prophet Noah as a thankful and devoted servant of Allah, emphasizing the significance of gratitude and steadfast faith in trials. It reminds believers that faithfulness and thankfulness to God are qualities that are revered and rewarded, regardless of the hardships faced.

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach [a great] height.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of human behavior, specifically among the Children of Israel, indicating that despite having divine guidance, they experienced periods of widespread wrongdoing and corruption followed by phases of great dominance or influence. It serves as a reflection on how societies can oscillate between moral decline and power, emphasizing the consequences of persistent disobedience to divine commandments and the eventual rectification or change in their status.

translation: Then when the first of the two promised times came, We sent against you Our servants, those of great military might; they entered the very innermost parts of your homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse conveys that when the initial divine retribution was due, God sent powerful agents to punish a people, penetrating even their most secure places, demonstrating that divine judgment is inevitable and comprehensive, reaching beyond human protection and ensuring that promises of recompense are fulfilled precisely.

translation: Then We returned to you the favor against them and provided you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah's support is manifested not only through material means like wealth and progeny but also through increasing the strength and unity of the community, enabling believers to overcome their adversaries through both divine blessing and collective effort.

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is against yourselves. Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, they will make your faces black and enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and will destroy what they had taken over with [total] destruction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of personal accountability and the inevitable consequences of one's actions. It emphasizes that the good or evil one commits affects oneself primarily, and serves as a reminder that in the Hereafter, the oppressors will face humiliation and defeat, as vividly illustrated by their blackened faces and the desecration they will undergo in the very mosque they once entered with arrogance. The verse warns believers to remain steadfast and to recognize that ultimate justice belongs to Allah, who will right the wrongs and restore dignity to the oppressed.

translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you. But if you return [to sin], then We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the balance between divine mercy and justice. It conveys that while God's mercy is vast and He may forgive and show leniency to sinners who repent, persistent rejection and return to wrongdoing will inevitably lead to His retribution. The verse reminds believers and disbelievers alike that God's patience has limits, and consequences await those who persist in disbelief and rebellion.

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's role as a beacon of moral and spiritual guidance, steering believers toward the most just and upright path in life. It emphasizes that adherence to this guidance, coupled with righteous actions, results in divine promise and substantial reward, underscoring the intrinsic link between faith, righteous conduct, and ultimate success.

translation: And those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of denying the Hereafter, signifying that belief in life after death is essential in Islam. The punishment mentioned serves as a warning that rejecting the reality of the afterlife leads to severe consequences, motivating believers to uphold faith and righteousness.

translation: And man invokes evil upon himself while he is expecting good, and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impulsive nature of humans who often wish for what seems beneficial in the short term without fully considering the long-term consequences, sometimes inviting harm upon themselves while desiring good. It serves as a reminder to exercise patience and wisdom in our hopes and actions, recognizing that our immediate desires may not always lead to our true welfare.

translation: And We have made the night and the day two signs. Then We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the calculation. And everything We have detailed distinctly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the alternation of night and day as signs from God. The visibility of the day allows human beings to carry out their activities and seek their livelihood, while the measurement of time grants awareness of the passage of life and the ability to organize and plan. It signifies the purposeful design in natural phenomena to facilitate human existence, understanding, and accountability in the world.

translation: And every person, We have tied their deeds to their neck, and on the Day of Resurrection, We will present to them a book which they will find spread open.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes that every individual is bound to their actions, which are like a heavy burden carried visibly and unavoidably. On the Day of Judgment, these deeds will be clearly presented and made evident, leaving no room for denial, emphasizing personal accountability for one's actions.

translation: Read your book; sufficient is yourself against you this day as an accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability, indicating that each person will be responsible for their own deeds without any mediator. On the Day of Judgment, one's own actions will be fully known and judged, making external intercession unnecessary.

translation: Whoever is guided, it is for [the benefit of] his own soul; and whoever goes astray, it is against it only. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And We do not punish until We have sent a Messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in matters of faith and actions. Guidance and misguidance are experiences that impact one's own soul; no one can choose or bear the spiritual consequences on behalf of another. Additionally, it underscores divine justice—that punishment is not meted out arbitrarily but follows the sending of a Messenger who delivers God's guidance, giving people the opportunity to understand and choose rightly.

translation: And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word [of punishment] comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that the corruption and defiance of the wealthy and influential people in a community lead to its downfall. Their immoral actions and rejection of guidance become the cause for the entire society's punishment, signifying the responsibility of those in power for the fate of their people.

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah! And sufficient is your Lord, concerning the sins of His servants, as an Acquainted, Aseeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's justice in dealing with human transgressions by demonstrating that entire generations who persisted in sin and disbelief were destroyed as a consequence of their actions. It serves as a warning that divine retribution is inevitable for those who reject guidance, while also emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of the deeds of His servants and judges them accordingly.

translation: Whoever desires the immediate (worldly life), We hasten for him that which We will for whom We intend; then We have appointed for him Hell, wherein he will burn, disgraced and rejected.
interpretation: This verse warns against being solely driven by the desire for immediate worldly gains without consideration of the hereafter, illustrating that such a pursuit leads to eventual disgrace and punishment in Hell, emphasizing the importance of prioritizing eternal success over fleeting worldly pleasures.

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and exerts the effort due to it while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated.
interpretation: This verse highlights that sincere striving and effort made with the intention of attaining the Hereafter, combined with true faith, are highly valued and rewarded by Allah. It emphasizes that genuine faith coupled with purposeful action towards spiritual goals ensures that one's endeavors will not be wasted, as Allah acknowledges and accepts such sincere efforts.

translation: Never; We give both this one and that one from the gift of your Lord. And never is the gift of your Lord restricted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless generosity of God, illustrating that His blessings and provisions are extended to all people without discrimination or limitation. It teaches that divine sustenance and mercy are not confined or withheld; rather, they reach everyone according to His wisdom and decree.

translation: See how We have favored some of them over others; but the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in excellence.
interpretation: This verse highlights that while people may differ in worldly status and blessings, these are temporary and lesser compared to the rewards and rank in the Hereafter. The true and lasting superiority lies in one's standing with Allah in the afterlife, which surpasses any worldly distinction.

translation: Do not set up another god with Allah, lest you be sitting blamed and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse warns against associating partners with Allah, emphasizing that doing so leads to disgrace and abandonment. It underscores the seriousness of shirk (associating others with God) and its consequence of spiritual ruin and social condemnation.

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to do good to parents. If one or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them "uff" nor repel them, but speak to them a noble word.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount importance of monotheism and kindness to one's parents, highlighting that worship must be directed solely to God while maintaining utmost respect and gentleness towards parents, especially in their old age. It instructs believers to avoid any form of disrespect or harshness, underscoring that noble and compassionate speech is integral to fulfilling one's duties both to God and to family, reflecting a comprehensive approach to piety that combines devotion and humane ethics.

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.'
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of showing deep humility, kindness, and compassion towards one's parents, recognizing their significant efforts in nurturing and raising us. It emphasizes seeking God's mercy upon them as a way to honor and repay their love and care, reminding us that our duties toward parents are a profound form of worship and gratitude.

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves. If you are righteous, He is indeed Oft-Forgiving to the repentant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of the innermost thoughts and feelings of every individual, beyond outward appearances. It assures that sincere righteousness and repentance are always met with His forgiveness, encouraging believers to maintain purity of heart and trust in His mercy.

translation: And give the relative his due, as well as the poor and the traveler, and do not squander wastefully.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to fulfill their obligations toward those who are closely related to them, extending generosity also to the needy and travelers who might be vulnerable or transient. It emphasizes measured charity, warning against wastefulness, thereby promoting a balanced approach to giving that preserves resources while supporting social bonds and caring for those in need.

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral condemnation of extravagance and wastefulness, equating those who squander resources with the companions of Satan. It serves as a reminder that such behavior reflects ingratitude and rebellion against the blessings and provisions granted by God, paralleling Satan's own ingratitude towards his Lord.

translation: And if you turn away from them seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, then say to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet to respond to those who reject or oppose with gentleness and kindness when his intent is to seek Allah's mercy. It emphasizes the importance of patience and soft speech in the face of adversity, highlighting that a compassionate approach can foster understanding and maintain dignity even when dealing with opposition.

translation: And do not make your hand tied to your neck, nor stretch it forth completely, so that you become blameworthy and destitute.
interpretation: This verse teaches the balance in generosity and restraint; it warns against being miserly to the extent of withholding support entirely, as well as against being excessively lavish to the point of self-impoverishment. True wisdom lies in moderation, giving what one can without causing harm to oneself, maintaining dignity and responsibility.

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Knower and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that provision and sustenance are ultimately in the control of Allah alone. He increases and decreases it according to His wisdom and knowledge of each individual's needs and circumstances. It reminds believers to have trust in God's wisdom, recognizing that wealth or livelihood is not solely dependent on human effort but is tightly regulated by divine wisdom, which is comprehensive and all-encompassing.

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, killing them is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and warns against the practice of killing children due to fear of destitution or financial hardship. It reassures believers that sustenance and provision are ultimately from Allah, encouraging trust in His mercy and provision rather than resorting to sinful acts out of despair.

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers to not only avoid committing fornication or adultery but also to stay away from anything that leads one to such acts, emphasizing both the moral corruption and the social harm caused by such behavior.

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right. And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in the matter of taking life. Indeed, he has been supported (by the law).
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of human life as ordained by God, allowing its taking only through a just cause, such as legal retribution for murder. It emphasizes fairness and restraint in the application of justice, cautioning against excess or revenge beyond what is warranted. It reflects the divine principle of balance—preserving life while upholding justice—and ensures that any act of taking life is regulated with clear authority and righteous intent, maintaining social order and moral integrity.

translation: And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of safeguarding the rights of orphans and managing their wealth with utmost care and integrity until they are capable of doing so themselves. It underscores the seriousness of fulfilling promises and trustworthy deeds, indicating that everyone will be held accountable for their commitments, particularly concerning vulnerable individuals like orphans.

translation: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is best and most just in the outcome.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and integrity in transactions, instructing believers to be honest and precise in their dealings. It teaches that maintaining justice in everyday actions, such as trade and measurement, is a reflection of righteousness and leads to the best outcomes in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse cautions against speaking or acting without knowledge, emphasizing personal accountability for one's faculties—hearing, seeing, and understanding—implying that individuals will be responsible for what they perceive and comprehend, and should therefore seek truth and certainty before pronouncing judgments or taking actions.

translation: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse teaches humility by reminding us that human beings, despite their pride or arrogance, have limits and cannot match the vastness and grandeur of creation. It cautions against prideful behavior and encourages walking on the earth with modesty and humility, recognizing our place within the created order rather than overestimating our own importance.

translation: All that was evil in the sight of your Lord, detestable.
interpretation: This verse highlights that actions or behaviors considered evil and detestable by God are inherently harmful and rejected. It serves as a reminder that what may seem insignificant or overlooked by people is, in fact, severely disapproved by God, emphasizing the importance of aligning oneself with divine guidance and avoiding acts that incur His displeasure.

translation: That is from the inspiration of your Lord's wisdom. So do not associate any other deity with Allah, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and rejected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the wisdom conveyed to the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting its sacred and infallible nature. It warns against associating partners with Allah, underscoring the severity of shirk (polytheism) as a grave violation that leads to severe consequences in the Hereafter, thereby calling for exclusive devotion and monotheism.

translation: Does your Lord take for Himself sons while He created the angels as females? Indeed, you say a grave statement.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim made by some that God has children, emphasizing the absurdity of assigning offspring to the Divine. It highlights the incorrect anthropomorphic views held by certain people who imagine angels as females and attribute human-like familial relations to God, thereby cautioning against such grave misconceptions about the nature of the Creator.

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every [kind of] example, but most of the people refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an uses a variety of narratives, parables, and examples to convey its messages, intending to guide and remind people. However, despite this diversity in approach, many still choose to turn away and reject faith, illustrating the stubbornness of some hearts and their resistance to accepting divine guidance.

translation: Say, "If there were with Him gods as they say, then they would surely seek a way to the Owner of the Throne."
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, emphasizing that if there were multiple deities as some claim, they would be in constant pursuit of accessing the ultimate authority and source of power, the Owner of the Throne, demonstrating the impossibility of such a scenario and affirming Allah's singular divinity and supremacy.

translation: Glorified and Exalted is He above what they say, [a position of] great elevation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and exalted status of Allah above any false claims or inappropriate attributions made by others. It underscores that Allah's nature and attributes are beyond human misconceptions and misrepresentations, affirming His absolute perfection and majesty.

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse teaches that all of creation, from the vastness of the heavens to the entire earth and everything within them, continuously glorifies and praises God in a manner beyond human comprehension. It highlights the inherent obedience and submission of all things to God's majesty, while acknowledging that human beings cannot perceive or fully grasp the divine way in which everything praises God. This calls believers to recognize the limits of human understanding and to trust in God's perfect wisdom and mercy.

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed veil.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur'an serves as a barrier preventing those who reject the concept of the Hereafter from truly comprehending its guidance and wisdom. Their disbelief causes a spiritual blindness or barrier, which God has made impenetrable, thus protecting the message from being internalized by those who deny fundamental truths about life after death.

translation: And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn back in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual barriers that prevent certain individuals from comprehending the profound message of the Qur'an. Their hearts are veiled, rendering them unable to grasp the truth, and their ears are closed off, symbolizing an active rejection of guidance. When the message emphasizes the oneness of God alone, they react with aversion, turning away due to their entrenched disbelief or denial.

translation: Indeed, We are most knowing of what they listen to when they listen to you, and when the wrongdoers conspire saying, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the secret plots and whispered conversations of the disbelievers who accuse the Prophet ﷺ of being bewitched. It teaches that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge, whether public or private, and that the unjust attempt to undermine the message by attributing false claims. This serves as a reassurance to the Prophet that despite opposition and slander, Allah's knowledge encompasses all, and He will protect His message and servant.

translation: Consider how they set forth for you examples, yet they went astray and cannot find a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to reject or misinterpret the clear guidance and lessons provided to them, leading to their deviation and inability to find the correct path despite the clarity of the examples given.

translation: And they say, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we surely be resurrected as a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and doubt of disbelievers regarding the resurrection after death. They question the possibility of being brought back to life after their bodies have decayed to dust and bones, expressing their disbelief in life after death and accountability. The verse highlights human doubt in the unseen and serves to remind believers that resurrection is a divine power beyond human comprehension, affirming that Allah is capable of recreating life from death.

translation: Say, "Be stones or iron,"
interpretation: This verse challenges those who oppose the message to demonstrate their power or truth even if they were as unyielding as stones or iron, emphasizing the steadfastness of divine truth and the limits of human resistance against it.

translation: Or [the time of resurrection is] an unknown creation within your breasts. They will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "He who created you the first time." Then they will nod their heads toward you and say, "When is that?" Say, "Perhaps it will be soon."
interpretation: This verse highlights human doubt and curiosity about the resurrection and the afterlife, acknowledging that the knowledge of its exact timing is hidden within us but remains uncertain. It emphasizes that the same Creator who fashioned us initially holds the power to bring us back to life, thereby affirming God's absolute control over creation and resurrection. The response "Perhaps it will be soon" serves as a warning and reminder to remain conscious of the Day of Judgment, encouraging readiness and mindfulness of one's deeds.

translation: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you had only stayed a little.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment when all will be summoned to account for their deeds. Despite thinking that their worldly life was brief, people will be confronted with the reality of eternal recompense, highlighting the transient nature of life and the importance of being mindful of one's actions.

translation: And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan sows discord among them. Indeed, Satan is ever, to mankind, a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of speaking with kindness and wisdom to maintain harmony among people, warning that Satan actively instigates conflict by encouraging harsh or harmful speech, thus reminding us to be mindful of our words to prevent division and enmity.

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you as a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge of each individual is complete and beyond human comprehension. It reminds us that Allah's mercy and punishment are dispensed according to His wisdom and will, underscoring His absolute sovereignty. Moreover, it clarifies that the Prophet's role is to convey the message, not to control or enforce judgments over people's fate, highlighting the importance of personal accountability and the divine prerogative in matters of mercy and punishment.

translation: And your Lord is most knowing of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly favored some prophets over others, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge encompasses all beings in the heavens and the earth, highlighting His supreme awareness and wisdom. It also reflects the divine wisdom in differentiating among prophets, granting them varied degrees of honor and specific revelations, such as the Psalms given to Prophet David, illustrating that each prophet had a unique role and status in guiding humanity according to God's plan.

translation: Say, "Call upon those whom you claim [as deities] besides Him; they do not possess the power to remove any harm from you, nor can they change it."
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of invoking deities other than Allah, emphasizing that they have no ability to prevent harm or alter any state of affairs. It highlights God's unique power and the ineffectiveness of false gods, urging believers to recognize and rely solely on Allah's supreme authority and mercy.

translation: Those are the ones who invoke their Lord, seeking means of nearness to Him, who are closest (to Him), hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared.
interpretation: This verse signifies the attitude of sincere believers who, in their worship and supplications, earnestly seek closeness to Allah through every permissible way. They balance hope in His mercy with fear of His punishment, adopting a mindset that motivates them to strive for righteousness while being mindful of accountability. Their awareness of Allah's severe punishment leads them to avoid sin and persist in obedience, recognizing that the path to Allah's pleasure lies in being both hopeful and cautious.

translation: And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That is written in the Book (decree).
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty and inevitability of divine justice, emphasizing that no community escapes accountability for its actions. It underlines the principle that every nation that turns away from righteousness and persists in wrongdoing will face destruction or severe punishment before the final Day of Judgment, as decreed by God in the preserved divine record.

translation: And We did not send down the signs except that the former peoples had denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send down the signs only as a warning.
interpretation: This verse explains that divine signs and miracles are sent primarily as warnings to those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing, illustrating that prior peoples rejected these signs leading to their destruction. The mention of Thamud's she-camel exemplifies how even clear, manifested signs can be denied or mistreated, highlighting human stubbornness and the necessity of warnings to guide towards righteousness.

translation: And [remember] when We told you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people." And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, as well as the cursed tree in the Qur'an, and We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse highlights that all of humanity is within the knowledge and control of God, underscoring His omnipresence and omniscience. The mention of the vision shown to the Prophet as a test indicates that divine revelations can serve as trials to distinguish true believers from others. The reference to the 'cursed tree' symbolizes a forbidden or harmful element that serves as a warning within the Scripture. It suggests that admonitions and warnings from God, rather than deterring the wrongdoers, often lead them to greater rebellion and disobedience, reflecting the stubbornness of those who reject guidance.

translation: And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except for Iblis. He said, "Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the beginning of Iblis's defiance and pride, where he refuses to obey Allah's command due to his arrogance and perceived superiority over Adam, who was created from clay. It serves as a profound lesson about the dangers of arrogance and disobedience to divine commands, emphasizing that status before God is not determined by origin or form, but by obedience and humility.

translation: He said, "Do you see this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely ruin his descendants, except for a few."
interpretation: This verse reflects the jealousy and pride of Iblis (Satan) towards Adam, whom God honored by creating him from clay and giving him a high status. Iblis's vow to corrupt Adam's progeny shows his determination to lead humanity astray and highlights the ongoing spiritual struggle between good and evil. It teaches us about the dangers of envy and arrogance, and the importance of seeking refuge in God from such destructive intentions.

translation: He said, 'Go, and whoever among them follows you – then indeed, Hell will be your recompense, a full recompense.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the warning given by a prophet to a transgressor who challenges him, informing him that following in sinful ways leads to severe consequences, namely Hell. It emphasizes personal responsibility and the clear distinction between guidance and misguidance, underscoring that those who choose to follow error willingly will receive a just and abundant punishment.

translation: And incite against them whatever you can with your voice and with horses and chariots and infantry, and be present in person among them, and share with them in wealth and children, and promise them; indeed, Satan only promises them to delude.
interpretation: This verse highlights the methods used by Satan to sow discord and incite enmity among people through agitation and false promises. It serves as a warning that Satan's tactics involve stirring conflict by exploiting weaknesses—whether through verbal incitement or mobilizing forces like horses and infantry—and by tempting people with worldly possessions and offspring. Ultimately, these promises are deceptive illusions meant to lead people astray from the path of righteousness.

translation: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as a disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Satan has no control or power over the servants of Allah who are His true believers and seekers of guidance. It reassures that God's protection and management over His servants are absolute and sufficient, highlighting the futility of Satan's attempts to mislead those under God's care.

translation: Your Lord is the one who drives the ships through the sea for you, that you may seek of His bounty; indeed, He has been ever Merciful to you.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and provision, illustrating His control over the natural elements like the sea and ships to benefit humanity. It emphasizes that the means through which people seek livelihood and sustenance are directed by God's mercy and wisdom, reminding believers to be grateful and aware of His continual care and blessings.

translation: And when adversity touches you at sea, you cry out to Him alone, but when He brings you safely to land, you turn away; and mankind is ever ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the tendency of human beings to remember and turn to God only in times of distress or calamity, seeking His help fervently. However, once the danger is averted and safety is restored, they forget their dependence on Him and turn away, displaying ingratitude despite the divine mercy they have received.

translation: Do you feel secure that He will not cause the earth to swallow you up or send against you a storm of stones, and then you will find no protector for yourselves?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's ultimate power and control over the forces of nature and the fate of humanity. It warns against complacency and false security, highlighting that if people persist in wrongdoing or disbelief, divine punishment can swiftly and decisively befall them, leaving them with no protector or refuge. The message encourages humility and mindfulness of God's authority and the consequences of one's actions.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send upon you a violent wind, so that it will strike you with ruin for what you disbelieved in? Then you would not find for yourselves against Us an ally.
interpretation: This verse warns that divine punishment can come unexpectedly and with great severity as a consequence of disbelief and wrongdoing. It serves as a reminder that no one should feel safe or complacent in their misdeeds, because God's justice can manifest in powerful ways, leaving no protection or help for those who reject faith.

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam and carried them on land and sea and provided them with good things and preferred them over many of those We have created with a marked preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent dignity and high status bestowed upon human beings by their Creator. It emphasizes that despite the diverse challenges faced in life, humans are granted honor, sustenance, and distinction above many other creatures, reflecting their unique capacity for intellect, moral responsibility, and spiritual potential.

translation: The Day We will call every people with their record [of deeds]. Then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and injustice will not be done to them, [even] as much as a thread [inside the date seed].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every person will be called with their own record of deeds. Receiving the book in the right hand signifies success and salvation, indicating that those individuals will receive their just recompense without any oppression or unfairness, even to the smallest detail.

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequences of negligence or blindness in recognizing the signs and guidance in this worldly life; such neglect leads to a profound and enduring blindness in the Hereafter, resulting in being further misguided and lost from the true path.

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you so that you might fabricate against Us something else; and then they would have taken you as a close friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the constant threat faced by the Prophet from those who wished to divert him from the true revelation sent by God. Their intention was to make him alter the divine message or invent something false. The verse serves as a warning against the influence of those who try to sway believers from upholding the authentic teachings, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in adhering to God's word despite external pressures.

translation: And if We had not established you firmly, you would have almost inclined towards them a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human susceptibility to be influenced by others, particularly when faced with opposition or challenges. It emphasizes the divine support granted to the Prophet to keep him steadfast and unwavering in his mission, safeguarding him from diverting towards the distractions or pressures posed by those who opposed his message.

translation: If We do not grant you a taste of double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] after death, then you will not find for yourself against Us any protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and the severe consequences of persistent wrongdoing. It warns that if a person does not experience intensified trials and punishment both in this life and the hereafter, they will be utterly helpless and without any protector when facing God's ultimate judgment.

translation: Indeed, they were about to drive you out of the land to expel you from it. And they will not remain in your vicinity except for a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent hostility and attempts by adversaries to dislodge the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from his land. Yet, it reassures that their efforts will not succeed in the long term, and their time of dominance or proximity will be brief. It serves as a reminder that divine protection prevails over worldly attempts to harm or displace the righteous.

translation: It is the established way of those We sent before you as Our messengers; and you will never find any alteration in Our way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consistency and unchangeable nature of God's principles in dealing with humanity through His messengers. It emphasizes that the divine laws and methods set by God are constant and cannot be altered or overridden by human will, underscoring the reliability and justice of God's approach throughout history.

translation: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and [also] the Qur'an of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistently performing prayers at prescribed times, particularly highlighting the significance of the dawn prayer. The phrase "the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed" indicates that this prayer holds a special status, as it is observed by angels and serves as a testimony to one's devotion and commitment to God. It encourages believers to maintain their spiritual discipline through regular worship, especially during the quiet and serene hour of dawn, strengthening their connection with God and reaffirming their faith.

translation: And during the night, pray with it an additional (optional) prayer for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station.
interpretation: This verse encourages voluntary night prayers (Tahajjud) as a means of spiritual elevation and closeness to God. It suggests that through sincere devotion and effort in these extra prayers, one may be granted a distinguished status honored by God, reflecting the transformative power of earnest worship beyond obligatory duties.

translation: Say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and to exit a truthful exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."
interpretation: This verse is a supplication emphasizing the importance of sincerity and truthfulness in one’s actions and transitions in life, asking God to guide a person to begin and end endeavors with honesty and integrity, and to provide divine support and strength to uphold righteousness and overcome challenges.

translation: And say, "The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable triumph of truth over falsehood, assuring that falsehood, by its very nature, cannot endure and will ultimately be eliminated, affirming the ultimate victory of divine guidance and righteousness.

translation: And We reveal from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's dual effect based on the listener's spiritual and moral state: for believers, it serves as a source of healing and mercy, bringing solace and guidance, whereas for the wrongdoers, it deepens their ruin as they reject its teachings and persist in their wrongdoing.

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be ungrateful and heedless when blessed with ease and blessings, neglecting to acknowledge or thank the source of these favors. Conversely, in times of hardship or adversity, humans become despondent and lose hope, often turning away from trust and reliance on God. It underscores the inconsistency in human attitude, reminding us to remain humble and grateful in prosperity and resilient and trusting in hardship.

translation: Say, "Each works according to his own manner, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everyone acts according to their own nature, beliefs, and inclinations, and that ultimate guidance comes from God who knows best who is rightly guided. It reminds us that while people may differ in their paths and actions, only God has perfect knowledge of their intentions and who is on the true path.

translation: And they ask you about the soul. Say, "The soul is from the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little."
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitation of human understanding regarding the soul, emphasizing that the soul's nature and essence are part of the divine knowledge known only to God. It reminds us that our grasp of such metaphysical realities is limited, and we must acknowledge God's supreme authority and wisdom in matters beyond human comprehension.

translation: And if We willed, We could take away that which We revealed to you, then you would not find any protector against Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and power of Allah over His revelation. It serves as a reminder that the divine guidance granted to the Prophet is a trust from Allah, which can be withdrawn by His will. Therefore, the verse underlines the importance of recognizing that the sacred message is maintained solely by Allah's permission, and without His support, no one can safeguard or retain it.

translation: Except for mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His bounty upon you has been great.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that any favorable outcome or relief granted is purely due to the mercy and grace of Allah. It emphasizes that human beings are not entitled to such blessings by right; rather, these are manifestations of the immense kindness and generosity of God bestowed upon us despite our shortcomings.

translation: Say, "If mankind and jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce its like, even if they were to help one another."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature and divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that its eloquence, depth, and impact are beyond the capacity of all human and jinn beings combined to replicate. It challenges the skeptics to produce even a single chapter like it, highlighting the Qur'an's uniqueness as a testament to its truth and the power of its message.

translation: And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example, but most of the people refused [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deliberate and comprehensive use of diverse parables and examples in the Qur'an to convey its messages in ways accessible and relatable to all people. However, despite the clarity and variety of signs provided, the majority remain obstinately in denial, choosing to reject faith rather than understand the guidance offered.

translation: And they said, "We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the demand for a tangible, miraculous sign as proof of prophecy, reflecting a common human tendency to require concrete evidence before accepting truth, which often leads to stubborn disbelief despite prior clear signs.

translation: Or you may have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and cause rivers to gush forth in it in streams.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the blessings and bounties that can be bestowed upon a person, depicting an ideal state of prosperity and abundance where one’s efforts or divine favor result in a flourishing and fertile environment. It serves as a metaphor for the rewards of faith, righteousness, and gratefulness, highlighting that true success is marked not just by material wealth but also by the continuous flow of sustenance and well-being that benefits oneself and others.

translation: Or does the sky fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed? Or do you bring Allah and the angels before [us]?
interpretation: This verse challenges the claims made against the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing the implausibility of such exaggerated accusations. It highlights that no one can bring forth Allah and the angels physically as proof, reminding the listener that faith is based on belief, not on witnessing such impossible scenes.

translation: Or you might have a house of gold, or ascend into the sky; yet We will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book that we can read. Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Was I anything except a human messenger?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that miracles or impressive displays alone are not sufficient to establish true belief in a prophet's message. Faith is grounded in clear guidance revealed through scripture. The prophet is reminded that despite any extraordinary signs, his role is solely to convey God's message as a human messenger, not to demand blind faith based on wonders.

translation: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and prejudice of those who reject divine guidance simply because it comes through a human messenger. Their refusal is not due to any fault in the message itself, but because they cannot accept that Allah would choose an ordinary person to convey His revelation. This reflects a broader lesson about humility and openness to truth, regardless of the form in which it arrives.

translation: Say, "If there were angels on the earth walking securely, We would certainly have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness of human beings as recipients of divine revelation. It highlights that if the earth were inhabited by angels — beings of pure obedience who do not require guidance — there would be no need for a messenger. The presence of humans, with their free will and capacity for guidance, necessitates the sending of prophets. Hence, the verse underscores why Allah sent messengers to humanity and not to angels, affirming the special role of prophethood in guiding humans who are tested in their choices.

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge and observation are complete and infallible. When disputes or accusations arise, one can trust Allah's judgment and witness, as He is fully aware of the intentions and actions of all His servants, making His testimony the ultimate and most reliable.

translation: And whoever Allah guides - for him there is no misleader; and whoever He sends astray - for them you will not find any protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides, We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority of Allah in guiding or misguiding individuals, underscoring that no one can protect those whom He allows to go astray. It also highlights the severe consequences in the Hereafter for those who reject guidance: they will be humiliated and punished continuously in Hell, demonstrating the seriousness of turning away from divine guidance.

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and skepticism of disbelievers regarding resurrection. They mock the idea of life after death, doubting Allah's power to reassemble them from mere bones and dust into a new form. It emphasizes human weakness in understanding divine ability and the consequences of rejecting clear signs from God.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the like of them? And He has appointed for them a term, surely there is no doubt about it; but the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah as the Creator of the heavens and the earth, highlighting His capability to recreate them. It underscores the certainty of the appointed time of judgment, affirming that no one can escape this divine decree. The verse also points to the stubbornness of the wrongdoers who reject faith despite clear evidence, illustrating human arrogance in the face of divine truth.

translation: Say, "If you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending it. And ever has man been stingy."
interpretation: This verse highlights human nature's inclination to withhold and be miserly, even in matters of mercy and generosity. It emphasizes that if humans truly had control over the boundless mercy of Allah, they would still be reluctant to share it freely due to fear of loss. It serves as a reminder that Allah's mercy is abundant and bestowed without limitation, contrasting human stinginess with divine generosity.

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think you are bewitched, Moses."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, highlighting how despite the clear miracles granted to Moses as evidence of his prophethood and the truth of his message, Pharaoh chose to dismiss them as mere magic. It reflects the human tendency to reject divine truth when it challenges one's authority or worldview, emphasizing the struggle between belief and disbelief.

translation: He said, "Indeed, I know that what these have been sent down with is only from the Lord of the heavens and the earth, full of knowledge. And indeed, I think that, O Pharaoh, you are doomed to destruction."
interpretation: This verse reflects the acknowledgment by a knowledgeable person that the divine revelation received by the messengers is undoubtedly from the all-knowing Creator of the heavens and the earth. It also conveys a warning to Pharaoh, symbolizing arrogance and injustice, that such defiance against divine truth inevitably leads to ruin. The verse emphasizes the certainty of divine authority and the consequences of rejecting it.

translation: So he intended to cause corruption therein, and We drowned him and those with him all together.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that when injustice and corruption arise, Divine justice intervenes decisively; it serves as a reminder that those who spread evil and disrupt harmony will face ultimate consequences, reaffirming that moral corruption is not tolerated by God.

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land," and when the time of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in multitudes.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise and decree concerning the Children of Israel, indicating that although they are granted the right to live in the land temporarily, there is an appointed time in the Hereafter when all will be gathered for judgment. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of the ultimate meeting with God, emphasizing accountability and the importance of recognizing divine authority and destiny.

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Qur'an is grounded in absolute truth, and that the Prophet's mission is divinely ordained to both bring glad tidings to the believers and warn those who reject guidance. It underscores the balanced role of the Prophet as one who delivers God's clear message impartially, inviting people to recognize and respond to divine guidance.

translation: And a Qur'an which We have separated (clearly) that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period, and We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deliberate and gradual revelation of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its verses were revealed over time to facilitate ease of understanding, reflection, and implementation by the believers, allowing them to internalize the guidance and apply it effectively in their lives.

translation: Say, "Believe in it or do not believe." Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of the Qur'an on those who have deep, prior knowledge. It suggests that true understanding and recognition of divine truth naturally lead to humility and submission before God, as exemplified by the scholars and learned people who, when hearing the Qur'an, are so moved that they prostrate in reverence and acceptance.

translation: And they say, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord is to be accomplished."
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' recognition and affirmation of God's promise, highlighting their unwavering faith in the fulfillment of divine decree even if the fulfillment seems distant or difficult. It emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of God's promises, encouraging patience and steadfastness in the believers.

translation: And they prostrate themselves with their faces to the ground, weeping, and it increases them in humility.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound emotional and spiritual impact of sincere prayer and submission to God. The act of prostration is not merely physical but is accompanied by deep sorrow and humility, reflecting true devotion and recognition of human fragility before the Divine. The more they humble themselves and weep in sincere worship, the stronger their sense of reverence and submission becomes, indicating that genuine faith naturally leads to a heightened state of mindfulness and humility.

translation: Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names." And do not recite loudly in your prayer or quietly but seek between that a way.
interpretation: This verse teaches the believer to recognize the various names and attributes of God, emphasizing that no matter which name is used, the Divine essence remains the same and possesses the most beautiful attributes. It encourages moderation and balance in worship, advising against extreme behavior—neither raising one's voice excessively nor whispering—in prayer, suggesting a middle path in devotion that reflects sincerity, humility, and mindfulness.

translation: And say: Praise be to Allah, Who has not taken a son and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He had a protector out of weakness; and magnify Him with great magnificence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah, rejecting any notions of Him having offspring or partners, thereby affirming His uniqueness and transcendence above all imperfections. It calls upon believers to recognize and proclaim His majesty with profound reverence, reflecting the pure monotheistic belief central to Islam.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not placed therein any crookedness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and purity of the Qur'an, revealed by Allah without any distortion or error, highlighting that Divine revelation is a straight and clear guidance free from any falsehood or contradiction.
