translation: A reminder to warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual purpose of divine revelation: to caution against the consequences of disobedience, highlighting the seriousness of accountability before God, and to motivate the faithful by assuring them that sincere righteous deeds will be rewarded generously, thus encouraging a balanced life of awareness and hope.

translation: Dwelling therein forever.
interpretation: This phrase refers to the eternal nature of the abode prepared for the righteous or the wrongdoers, emphasizing the permanence of their final destination in the afterlife, highlighting the unending consequence of one's deeds.

translation: and warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."
interpretation: This verse addresses the misconception of attributing offspring to Allah, emphasizing His absolute uniqueness and transcendence, and warns against belief in such notions that contradict the concept of God's oneness.

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor do their forefathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.
interpretation: This verse highlights how some people speak authoritatively about matters they lack true knowledge of, perpetuating misinformation across generations. It condemns the arrogance of such baseless assertions, emphasizing that their statements are serious falsehoods that mislead others and distort the truth.

translation: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this message, out of sorrow.
interpretation: This verse conveys the deep emotional distress the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) feels when people reject the message of Islam. It highlights the intense compassion and concern for humanity’s guidance, illustrating that disbelief can cause profound sorrow, yet the Prophet is urged to maintain patience and continue his mission despite the sadness.

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth an adornment for it, to test them as to which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the beauty and blessings of the worldly life are a test from God. The adornments and bounties on earth are not merely for enjoyment but serve as a means to evaluate human conduct. True success lies in how individuals respond to these trials by performing righteous deeds and maintaining upright character, demonstrating their faith and obedience amidst worldly temptations.

translation: And indeed, We will make what is upon it [the earth] a barren ground.
interpretation: This verse signifies the transient nature of the earth and all that is upon it. It serves as a reminder that the world will eventually die, become desolate, and devoid of life and productivity, reinforcing the concept of mortality and the temporary state of worldly existence.

translation: Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs, a wonder?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the story of the companions of the cave, emphasizing that their remarkable experience is not merely a strange or extraordinary incident, but rather a meaningful sign from God, meant to affirm faith and demonstrate His power over life and death.

translation: When the youths sought refuge in the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincere plea of the youths who, facing distress, turn to Allah seeking His mercy and guidance. It teaches us the importance of placing our trust solely in Allah during times of hardship and seeking His assistance to navigate our difficulties wisely.

translation: So We cast [a cover of sleep] over their ears within the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's mercy and protection over the sleepers in the cave by causing them to fall into a deep, uninterrupted sleep, shielding them from the passage of time and worldly harms. It signifies divine intervention that preserves the faithful in a state beyond ordinary human experience, highlighting God's power over life, time, and human affairs.

translation: Then We raised them up to know which of the two parties would best estimate the time they had tarried.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God revived a group after they had been in a state of suspension or dormancy to test the perception and judgment of different factions regarding the duration of their absence, emphasizing the divine control over time and human knowledge.

translation: We relate to you their story in truth. Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound impact of sincere faith and divine guidance on the righteous, emphasizing that true belief in God not only strengthens resolve but also brings about increased spiritual enlightenment and direction.

translation: And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any deity besides Him, for we have certainly spoken an excessive word."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the strengthening of the believers' resolve and faith by God in times of trial or confrontation. It highlights the resolute declaration of monotheism, rejecting false gods, and acknowledging past errors as a step towards sincere faith and devotion to the one true God.

translation: These are our people who have taken other gods besides Him. Had they come to them with a clear authority, then who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound injustice of attributing falsehoods to Allah by worshiping deities other than Him. It underscores that those who invent such lies do so without any legitimate proof or divine authority, and thus commit a grave injustice. The verse invites reflection on the futility and wickedness of idol worship, as it is based on baseless claims, contrasting with the true authority of God.

translation: And when you withdrew from them and that which they worship except Allah, then retreat to the cave; your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of separating oneself from false beliefs and practices to preserve one's faith. By retreating to a place of safety and reliance on Allah, such as the Cave, believers receive divine mercy and are granted ease in their trials. It highlights that spiritual refuge and trust in God's support are essential when facing adversity for one's faith.

translation: And you see the sun when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it sets, passing away from them on the left, while they are in a spacious cavity therein. That is from the signs of Allah. Whomever Allah guides is the rightly guided; and whomever He sends astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the miraculous nature of the cave dwellers' protection by Allah, highlighting how the natural movement of the sun shifted away from their cave, preventing discovery. It signifies Allah's power in guiding whom He wills to the truth and leaving whom He wills to stray, emphasizing that true guidance and protection come solely from Him.

translation: And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, and their dog stretched out its two forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound state of the sleepers who were in a miraculous slumber, seemingly awake but truly asleep. Their turning from side to side signifies the mercy and protection of God, preserving them through their prolonged sleep. The presence of their dog at the entrance symbolizes loyalty and vigilance. The verse conveys that their condition was so remarkable and awe-inspiring that an observer would instinctively fear and flee, emphasizing the divine power that preserved them and the extraordinary nature of their situation.

translation: And thus We raised them up so that they might question one another. A speaker among them asked, "How long have you stayed?" They said, "We have stayed a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you stayed. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city, and let him look to see which food is the purest, and bring you provision from it; and let him be cautious and let no one be aware of you.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine wisdom in the narrative of the Companions of the Cave, emphasizing the subtle ways in which God guides and tests His servants. The act of raising them for mutual questioning signifies awakening from a state of slumber or inactivity, indicating that awareness and reflection are part of God's plan. The instruction to send one to the city to discreetly obtain provision highlights the importance of reliance on God while maintaining prudence and discretion in worldly affairs, underscoring a balance between trust in divine decree and responsible action.

translation: Indeed, if they gain dominance over you, they will stone you or return you to their religion; and you will never succeed, ever.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about the severe consequences of falling under the control of those hostile to your faith. It emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast and vigilant in one's beliefs, highlighting how dominance by enemies can lead to persecution and coercion, ultimately causing loss not only in worldly success but in spiritual guidance as well.

translation: And thus We caused them to stumble so that they would know that the promise of Allah is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour. When they disputed among themselves about their affair, they said, "Construct over them a building." Their Lord knows best about them. Those who prevailed over their affair said, "We will surely take for them a mosque."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that God's promises are certain and that the Day of Judgment will undoubtedly come. The events leading to the construction mentioned symbolize the human tendency to memorialize and sometimes venerate past generations, often without recognizing the deeper lessons. The verse cautions believers to recognize the truth behind worldly events and not to be distracted by disputes or outward displays but to maintain faith in God's promises and the ultimate reality of the Hour.

translation: They will say, "Three, the fourth of them being their dog," and they say, "Five, the sixth of them being their dog," guessing blindly. And they say, "Seven, and the eighth of them is their dog." Say, "My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few." So do not dispute about them except with an obvious argument, nor inquire about them of any among them.
interpretation: This verse addresses the speculative and unfounded debates about the number and nature of the Companions of the Cave, cautioning against conjecture without clear evidence. It teaches that such matters are known only to Allah and a few special people, and thus believers should avoid fruitless disputes and baseless inquiries, focusing instead on faith and trust in God's knowledge.

translation: And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,"
interpretation: This verse advises against absolute certainty and presumptuousness about future actions, reminding us to remain humble and recognize that the realization of our plans depends ultimately on God's will and permission.

translation: Except that Allah wills. And remember your Lord when you forget and say, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this to right conduct.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah's will in all matters, acknowledging that human free will is ultimately subject to His decree. It encourages one to remember Allah, especially in moments of forgetfulness or error, and to seek His guidance towards better understanding and right actions, trusting that His guidance can bring one closer to the best path.

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous preservation of the young believers who sought refuge from persecution. Their extended stay in the cave signifies divine protection and the suspension of time, symbolizing God's power over natural laws and the enduring strength of faith in trials.

translation: Say, "Allah is most knowing of how long they tarried. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How clear of sight and hearing He is! They have no protector besides Him, and He does not share His judgment with anyone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's exclusive and absolute knowledge of all matters, including the unseen and the unknown past and future. It asserts that no one else shares His authority or possesses His perfect perception, thus reaffirming that ultimate power and governance belong solely to Him without any partners or associates.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. None can change His words, and you will never find besides Him a refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unalterable and perfect nature of the divine revelation. It stresses that God's words are eternal and beyond human manipulation, highlighting the uniqueness and authority of the Qur'an as guidance, and that no other source or being can offer a true alternative or protection against His decree.

translation: And be patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornments of the worldly life, nor obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire, and whose affair is ever lost.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of steadfast companionship and patience with those who are devoted to sincere worship of Allah, emphasizing the value of seeking His pleasure over worldly attractions. It warns against being distracted by the fleeting allurements of this life and against following those whose hearts are neglectful of divine remembrance, as such heedlessness leads one astray and results in ruin.

translation: And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills—let him believe; and whoever wills—let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass which scalds faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clear and undeniable nature of divine truth, giving individuals the freedom to choose belief or disbelief. It warns that those who persist in injustice and rejection of truth will face severe consequences, symbolized by a blazing fire with intense torment. The imagery of burning water highlights the severity and inescapability of this punishment, underscoring the seriousness of turning away from guidance and the moral responsibility each person holds in accepting the truth.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds—Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of any who do good in deed.
interpretation: This verse assures the believer that faith coupled with righteous actions guarantees that their good deeds will not be wasted. It emphasizes God's justice and mercy, affirming that every sincere effort for good will be recognized and rewarded, inspiring perseverance and sincerity in moral conduct.

translation: They will have Gardens of Eternity, beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward, and good is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal reward for the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing that their reward is not only abundant and everlasting but also adorned with beauty and comfort beyond worldly comparisons. It highlights the perfect peace, honor, and luxury that await those who are granted Paradise, serving as an encouragement for believers to strive towards righteousness.

translation: And set forth for them the example of two men, We made for one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We surrounded them with date palms, and placed crops between them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the variability of worldly blessings and the profound lessons they carry. It serves as a metaphor for the diverse circumstances individuals face—one blessed with abundance and prosperity. The example calls attention to the importance of gratitude and humility in times of plenty, reminding that material wealth is temporary and dependent on divine favor. It warns against complacency and pride, encouraging reflection on the true source of blessings and the necessity to use them wisely and righteously.

translation: Both gardens yielded their fruit and did not fall short thereof in anything, and We caused to gush forth within them a river.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the complete and abundant blessings granted by God to the righteous, emphasizing that their rewards are perfect and without deficiency. The presence of flowing rivers symbolizes continuous bounty and ease, signifying that divine favors are not only plentiful but also sustaining and unending.

translation: And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while conversing: "I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in followers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of a person who, possessing material wealth and influence, boasts over others. It serves as a reminder that true worth is not measured by worldly possessions or social status, but by humility and righteousness before God.

translation: And he entered his Paradise while he was unjust to himself. He said, "I do not think that this will ever perish."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and self-deception of a person who unjustly claims Paradise as his rightful place, underestimating the power of divine justice and the transient nature of worldly assumptions about eternal bliss.

translation: And I do not think the Hour will be established, and even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a place of return.
interpretation: This verse reflects the speaker's skepticism about the imminence of the Day of Judgment, expressing a belief that it will not occur soon. At the same time, it conveys a confident hope in the mercy and justice of God, indicating that the ultimate return to God will be a better and more favorable state than any worldly matters or concerns, emphasizing trust in divine wisdom and the eternal reward.

translation: His companion said to him, while he was conversing with him, "Have you disbelieved in the One who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you into a man?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the denial of God's power and existence by reminding one of the unmistakable signs of divine creation evident in the human origin, urging recognition and acknowledgment of God's sovereignty over life and creation.

translation: But no, He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the speaker's firm belief in the oneness of Allah and their personal commitment to monotheism, rejecting any form of associating partners with God.

translation: And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, "What Allah has willed; there is no power except with Allah"? If you did, perhaps your inheritance would remain with you, and you would fear on yourself.
interpretation: This verse teaches humility and recognition of Allah's ultimate control over all blessings. Despite possessing wealth and offspring, one should always acknowledge that all favors come from Allah alone, and without His will, these are not guaranteed. This acknowledgment leads to gratitude and mindfulness, protecting from arrogance and loss.

translation: It may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and will send upon it a calamity from the sky, so it becomes a slippery, barren land.
interpretation: This verse expresses a profound trust in God's wisdom and justice. It suggests that material wealth or blessings, like a garden, are transient and can be taken away by divine will. The speaker hopes that God may replace apparent worldly loss with something better, indicating that ultimate good comes from God alone, regardless of worldly appearances.

translation: Or its water becomes deep and it will not be able to seek it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extent of human helplessness in the face of certain divine decrees or natural phenomena. It signifies situations where human efforts to attain or reclaim something become futile, emphasizing reliance on God's will and the limits of human power.

translation: And he enclosed the fruit, then became regretful over what he had spent on it while it was devastated and barren, and he said, "Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of placing trust in worldly investments or associates besides Allah. The person invested all efforts into something that ultimately proved worthless, leading to deep regret and the realization that relying on anything other than Allah is a source of loss and despair.

translation: And he did not have any group to support him besides Allah, and he was never supported.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that ultimate help and support come only from Allah. No matter how much human backing one might seek or obtain, true victory and assistance are under Allah's control alone. It serves as a reminder that reliance on created beings is futile without divine support.

translation: Indeed, the true authority belongs to Allah. He is the best in reward and the best in conclusion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate sovereignty and authority rest solely with Allah, affirming that His dominion is just and perfect. It also assures believers that adhering to Him leads to the best outcome both in this world and the hereafter, highlighting Allah's supreme ability to grant the highest reward and final success.

translation: And present to them the example of the worldly life: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it and becomes dry stubble which the winds scatter. And Allah is ever, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transient and fragile nature of worldly life, likening it to water nourishing plants that eventually wither and scatter as dry stubble by the wind. It serves as a reminder that worldly pleasures and achievements are temporary and will ultimately fade away, whereas Allah's power and authority remain absolute and enduring beyond all temporal matters.

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world; but the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for hope.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly possessions and relationships, highlighting that while wealth and children beautify our earthly existence, it is the lasting righteous deeds that hold true value and promise in the sight of God. It serves as a reminder to prioritize good actions and spiritual accomplishments over fleeting material gains, as these enduring deeds are the source of eternal reward and hope.

translation: And [mention] the Day We will move the mountains and you will see the earth prominent, and We will gather them, and not leave behind from them anyone.
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute power of Allah on the Day of Resurrection when all natural and worldly stabilizers, like mountains, will be removed, and the earth will lay bare, symbolizing the total exposure and thoroughness of the divine judgment where no one can escape being held accountable.

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, [and He will say], "You have come to Us just as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would never make for you an appointment."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable Day of Judgment when all people will stand before Allah, returning to their original state as they were first created. It highlights the falsehood of the disbelievers' claim that there would be no resurrection or accountability, affirming that just as creation was the beginning, so too will be the inevitable appointed time for recompense.

translation: And the Book is placed [open], and you see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does not wrong anyone.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive justice of Allah, where every deed, no matter how minor or significant, is recorded and accounted for. At the time of judgment, the wrongdoers are filled with fear and regret upon seeing their actions laid bare, emphasizing that nothing escapes divine record. The verse reassures that Allah's judgment is perfectly equitable, and no soul will be wronged in the slightest, affirming the accountability and fairness inherent in the divine system.

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.
interpretation: This verse highlights the defiance of Iblis in refusing to obey God's command, marking the origin of enmity between him and humanity. It serves as a warning against taking Iblis and his progeny—representatives of evil and misguidance—as protectors or allies over God. Embracing their influence leads one away from righteousness, and for the unjust to replace divine guidance with allegiance to such enemies is a grievous error and a source of ruin.

translation: I do not bear witness that they created the heavens and the earth, nor that they created themselves, and I was not one to take the misguiders as supporters.
interpretation: This verse conveys the Prophet's declaration that he has no knowledge or claim that the misguided individuals he is addressing were responsible for the creation of the universe or themselves, emphasizing that he neither endorses nor supports those who lead others astray. It underscores the Prophet's role as a messenger who disassociates himself from false claims and misguidance, affirming monotheism and the singular divine origin of creation.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will say, "Call upon My partners whom you claimed," and they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them. And We will put between them a valley of destruction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of invoking false deities or partners alongside God on the Day of Judgment. Those whom people falsely worship will abandon them, demonstrating the absolute oneness of God and the emptiness of shirk (associating partners with God). It serves as a warning against idolatry, emphasizing that reliance should be solely on God.

translation: And the criminals will see the Fire and will think that they are to fall into it, and they will find no way to avoid it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitability of punishment for wrongdoers; when the consequences of their actions become evident, they realize there is no escape from the justice of God, emphasizing accountability and the certainty of divine retribution.

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every [kind of] example; but man has ever been, most of anything, [intricately] argumentative.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in using diverse parables and examples within the Qur'an to address the varied understandings and circumstances of people. Despite these clear and varied illustrations, human nature tends to engage in excessive argumentation, often challenging the truth out of stubbornness or desire for dispute rather than genuine seeking of knowledge.

translation: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and seeking forgiveness from their Lord except that the precedence of the former ways should come upon them or that the punishment should come to them first?
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to resist faith and repentance despite the arrival of clear guidance and the opportunity to seek forgiveness. It implies that people often delay embracing belief and reform until they witness the consequences that befell previous generations due to their rejection, or until they themselves face impending punishment. Thus, it underscores the importance of timely acceptance of truth and the dangers of procrastination in matters of faith.

translation: And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve argue by means of falsehood to invalidate the truth, and they have taken My verses and what they were warned of in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual role of the messengers as bearers of glad tidings for those who obey and warnings for those who deny. It underscores the persistent reaction of disbelievers who, despite clear signs and warnings, engage in arguments rooted in falsehood to reject the truth and mock divine revelations, reflecting their obstinacy and resistance to guidance.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severity of willful rejection of divine guidance. It shows that when one consciously chooses to ignore the signs and reminders from God, it leads to a spiritual state where understanding and receptivity are blocked. This not only highlights human accountability in accepting guidance but also explains that persistent denial results in a hardened heart and closed ears, making true guidance unattainable despite exhortations.

translation: And your Lord is the Most Forgiving, Full of Mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. But for them is an appointment from which they will never find an escape.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's immense mercy and willingness to forgive, emphasizing that despite people's wrongdoings, immediate punishment is withheld to allow room for repentance and reform. It assures that while God's justice is certain and inevitable, His patience precedes the final reckoning, giving humans hope and opportunity for redemption before the unavoidable Day of Judgment.

translation: And those villages We destroyed when they were wrongdoers, and We made for their destruction a determined appointment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle that societies which persist in injustice and wrongdoing will ultimately face consequences ordained by God. It emphasizes divine justice, highlighting that destruction is not arbitrary but is scheduled in accordance with God's wisdom and timing as a response to persistent oppression.

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his servant, "I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period."
interpretation: This verse highlights the determination and perseverance in the pursuit of knowledge and understanding. Moses expresses his resolve not to stop until he reaches a critical point symbolizing a meeting place of profound insight or after an extended journey, indicating that seeking truth requires persistent effort and patience.

translation: So when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, which had made its way into the sea by a road of its own.
interpretation: This verse highlights how forgetfulness can lead to losing something valuable. The fish is a symbol of sustenance or provision, and the story illustrates that being engrossed or careless at critical moments can result in missing out on important blessings or opportunities. It teaches the importance of mindfulness and attentiveness in managing the provisions bestowed upon us.

translation: So when they reached the place between the two mountains, he said to his boy, "Bring us our breakfast; indeed, we have encountered a fatigue from this, our journey."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human experience of fatigue and the need for rest and sustenance after hardship, even during a journey guided by divine purpose. It reflects the natural tendency to seek comfort and refreshment before proceeding with one's tasks, emphasizing the importance of patience and preparation in the pursuit of a higher goal.

translation: He said, "Have you considered when We sheltered you by the rock? And indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea, marvelously."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human susceptibility to forgetfulness, even in moments of divine significance, and underscores the subtle influence of Satan in diverting one's remembrance of God's signs or commands. It serves as a reminder to remain vigilant and conscious of God's guidance, recognizing that lapses in memory or attention are not mere accidents but can be influenced by spiritual forces that seek to lead one astray.

translation: He said, "That is not what we sought." So they both retraced their steps over their tracks.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the reaction of individuals who realize that the outcome of their actions or desires is not as they intended. It reflects the human experience of regret and the effort to reconsider or undo previous deeds when confronted with unintended consequences.

translation: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a knowledge.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine selection and grace bestowed upon a chosen individual, highlighting that true knowledge and mercy originate solely from God. It emphasizes that guidance and enlightenment are not acquired by effort alone but are gifts granted by God's will and favor upon His devoted servant.

translation: Moses said to him, "May I follow you so that you teach me of the knowledge you have been taught?"
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses's humility and eagerness to seek true knowledge by following a learned person, emphasizing the importance of being open to guidance and willing to learn from those who possess deeper understanding.

translation: He said, "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."
interpretation: This verse reveals a moment of human limitation and the acknowledgement of personal weaknesses. It highlights the challenge of enduring hardships or following divine guidance with steadfast patience, emphasizing that some trials require more perseverance than one might initially expect.

translation: And how can you be patient over something about which you have no knowledge?
interpretation: This verse highlights the difficulty of maintaining patience regarding matters that one does not fully understand. It suggests that true patience is tied to knowledge and awareness; when a person lacks understanding of the reality or wisdom behind a situation, enduring its challenges becomes exceedingly hard. Therefore, seeking knowledge and insight is essential to cultivate genuine patience and resilience in the face of life's trials.

translation: He said, "You will find me, God willing, patient and I will not disobey you in any matter."
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound commitment to patience and obedience in the face of trials or commands, emphasizing reliance on God's will (Insha'Allah) as the source of strength to endure difficulties and remain steadfast without rebellion.

translation: So if you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in the guidance being provided. It teaches that one should refrain from unnecessary questioning or skepticism before fully receiving the intended explanation or teaching, indicating that understanding comes gradually and in its proper time.

translation: So they both proceeded until, when they boarded the ship, he made a hole in it. [Moses] said, "Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? Surely, you have done a grave wrongdoing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of righteous conduct and the gravity of harming others unjustly. The act of sabotaging the ship, which would endanger innocent people, is a clear violation of moral and ethical principles. It serves as a reminder that causing harm to others, especially without just cause, is a serious transgression that goes against the integrity one should uphold in all dealings.

translation: Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?
interpretation: This verse highlights the human difficulty in exercising patience, especially in trying circumstances or relationships. It reflects the natural tendency to struggle with endurance and perseverance, reminding us of the challenge patience poses and the importance of acknowledging our limitations in maintaining it.

translation: He said, "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot and do not burden me with hardship in my matter."
interpretation: This verse highlights a plea for mercy and understanding in human fallibility, emphasizing that the divine does not impose burdens beyond one's capability and recognizes genuine human forgetfulness and limitations.

translation: Then they both proceeded until they met a young man, and he killed him. He said, "Have I killed a soul that was pure and innocent without cause? Indeed, you have done a terrible thing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of unjustly taking an innocent life, emphasizing that such an act is profoundly wrong and shocking. It serves as a moral lesson against committing violence without just cause, underscoring the sanctity of innocent human life and the severe consequences of its violation.

translation: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to bear with Me patiently?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to underestimate the challenges presented by divine commands or tests. It serves as a reminder that patience in the path of faith and obedience to God requires strength beyond ordinary endurance, emphasizing the importance of sincere effort and reliance on God's support in overcoming difficulties.

translation: He said, "If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. Indeed, I have already received an excuse from my Lord."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) reliance on divine guidance and the importance of following God's commands even when they may seem difficult or unclear. It teaches that obedience to Allah's instructions, especially in matters beyond human reasoning, is essential and that excuses from Allah are sufficient justification for one's actions.

translation: So they set out until, when they reached the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to entertain them. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he restored it. He said, "If you wished, you could have taken a payment for it."
interpretation: This verse highlights acts of kindness and selflessness. Despite being refused hospitality, the individual chooses to repair the weakened wall instead of seeking recompense. This demonstrates a commitment to helping others without expecting reward, embodying sincere charity and concern for the community's well-being.

translation: He said, "This is the separation between me and you. But I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not patiently endure."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) reveals to his brothers the meaning behind his earlier dreams and the events that transpired, emphasizing that understanding often requires patience and that God provides clarity when the time is right. It teaches that hardships and misunderstandings may precede enlightenment and reconciliation.

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to poor fishermen; so I intended to cause defect in it, and there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force.
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassion for the humble and disadvantaged, indicating that unjust interference or harm towards their livelihood is condemned, especially when there exists an oppressive force exploiting or seizing their possessions unjustly. It teaches the importance of standing against oppression and injustice faced by the vulnerable in society.

translation: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and We feared that he would burden them by transgression and disbelief.
interpretation: This verse indicates God's wisdom and mercy in protecting the believing parents from potential hardship caused by a child who might grow up to oppose their faith. It reflects the principle that faith and guidance are part of divine care, and sometimes, the absence of a child can be a mercy to the righteous, sparing them from trials that could challenge their belief and well-being.

translation: So their Lord intended that He should replace them with better ones: charity and closer kinship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's wisdom and mercy in replacing what is lost or taken away with something better. It highlights the importance of sincere charity (zakah) and maintaining strong family ties as virtues favored by God, suggesting that true blessings come through acts that purify wealth and nurture relationships, thereby drawing one closer to God and to others.

translation: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure for them, and their father was righteous. Your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it by my own accord. That is the interpretation of what you could not bear patiently.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine wisdom and mercy in guiding human affairs beyond apparent hardships. The act of revealing the treasure beneath the wall at the right time signifies that Allah plans for the well-being of these orphans, awaiting their maturity to grant them their rightful inheritance. It also emphasizes that the prophet's actions were directed by divine command, illustrating that certain knowledge or events are beyond human endurance and require patience and trust in God's plan.

translation: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you about him a remembrance."
interpretation: This verse highlights that when people seek knowledge about significant figures like Dhul-Qarnayn, the Prophet Muhammad is instructed to convey the information revealed to him, emphasizing the importance of relying on divine revelation and not on hearsay or speculation.

translation: Indeed, We established him firmly upon the earth and gave him to all things a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special position God granted to certain individuals (often interpreted as Prophet Solomon) by bestowing upon them authority and the ability to utilize and manage resources in the world effectively. It underlines the divine empowerment given to humans to rule and derive benefit from the earth, showcasing God's favor and enabling humans to fulfill their responsibilities through guidance and provisions.

translation: So I followed a way.
interpretation: This verse signifies the decision to pursue a particular path or method in seeking a goal or understanding. It reflects the importance of intentional action and deliberate choice in one's journey, emphasizing that following a chosen way can lead to meaningful outcomes or insights.

translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring, and he found near it a people. We said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish [them] or treat them with kindness."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extent of Dhul-Qarnayn's journey and the power entrusted to him. The phrase 'setting in a murky spring' symbolizes the limits of human perception rather than a literal phenomenon. The people he encounters represent those living in ignorance or hardship. The command to either punish or treat them kindly reflects the balance of justice and mercy in leadership, emphasizing the responsibility to govern wisely, either through discipline or benevolence, as circumstances require.

translation: As for the one who is unjust, We will surely punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of accountability for those who commit injustice. It emphasizes that worldly consequences are just a precursor to the ultimate divine judgment, where the wrongdoer faces a severe punishment from Allah, underscoring the importance of justice and righteousness.

translation: But as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, for him is the best reward, and We will speak to him with ease from Our command.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy and generosity of God towards those who maintain faith and engage in righteous actions; their reward is not only the best in the Hereafter but also includes a gentle and comforting experience in the divine presence, symbolizing both spiritual ease and honor bestowed by God's own decree.

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This verse signifies the initiative and agency of a person who, upon being given guidance or instruction, takes the necessary steps to pursue a path or cause. It emphasizes human responsibility in acting upon the means and opportunities presented, highlighting that while guidance can be given, it is ultimately up to the individual to follow through and seek the path towards their goals or towards righteousness.

translation: Until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising upon a people for whom We had not made any shelter against it.
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment of realization and reflection, illustrating how certain phenomena like the rising sun occur without protection or shield for some beings, symbolizing unmediated exposure to divine decree. It teaches that God's ordained laws and phenomena transpire with perfect wisdom and purpose, even if they seem harsh or unshielded, reminding us that encountering challenges without apparent protection is part of the divine wisdom in the order of creation.

translation: Thus, and indeed We have encompassed (completely) what he has, in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive knowledge and awareness of God over all matters, including the intentions and actions of every individual. It reassures that nothing is hidden from God's knowledge, highlighting His omniscience and complete understanding of all things.

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of human free will and choice. It suggests that after being presented with guidance or opportunities, a person chooses a particular path to follow. This verse emphasizes that individuals bear responsibility for their decisions and the consequences that follow from following certain paths, whether righteous or misguided.

translation: Until, when he reached the middle of the two barriers, he found on the other side a people who scarcely understood any speech.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Prophet Moses, after traveling between two veils or barriers in the sea, encounters a people (the Ethiopians or Midianites) who are linguistically and culturally distinct from him, emphasizing the diversity of humanity and the challenges in communication; it suggests that understanding is not always immediate and that patience and effort are required when engaging with those different from ourselves.

translation: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concern of a people troubled by the destructive acts of Gog and Magog, seeking Dhul-Qarnayn's help to establish a protective barrier. It highlights the notion of communal responsibility and the trust placed in a just and capable leader to safeguard society from harm by instituting measures of protection and order.

translation: He said, "My Lord has enabled me in this (task); so help me with strength, that I may make between you and them a barrier."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on the strength and enablement granted by Allah when undertaking a mission or facing a challenge. It teaches that success is rooted in divine support, and with this support, one can actively work to protect and safeguard their community or values against harm or injustice.

translation: "Bring me sheets of iron." So, when he had leveled [them] between the two mountains, he said, "Blow [with bellows]," until when he had made it [like] fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extraordinary power and wisdom endowed to Prophet Solomon by Allah, enabling him to command the natural elements and forces of the earth, such as controlling the iron and fire, which symbolizes a divine authority and mastery over creation that is beyond human capability. It teaches us about the strength of faith and the divine support granted to those chosen to fulfill God's commands.

translation: So they were not able to manifest it, nor were they able to penetrate it.
interpretation: This verse reflects the impotence of those who attempted to thwart or conceal the truth; despite their efforts, they could neither reveal it fully nor penetrate its profound meaning, signifying that truth remains protected and unreachable by forces of denial or interference.

translation: He said, "This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it [completely] level, and the promise of my Lord is truth."
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of God's actions: His mercy is evident in the blessings and favors bestowed upon people, yet His promises of judgment and recompense are certain and absolute. It serves as a reminder that while God's mercy is vast, His promise of justice will inevitably come to pass, emphasizing accountability and the certainty of divine decree.

translation: And We let some of them that Day surge over others; and We blew the trumpet, and gathered them all together.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of the Day of Resurrection when people will be resurrected and gathered for judgment. The phrase 'let some of them surge over others' depicts the chaotic and tumultuous scene as the dead emerge from their graves, reflecting the overwhelming nature of that critical moment. The blowing of the trumpet signifies the divine command that initiates resurrection and assembly, emphasizing God's absolute authority over life and death.

translation: And We will expose Hell that Day for the disbelievers, to see it exposed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and reality of Hell as a consequence for those who reject faith. It serves as a clear warning by making the punishment visible and undeniable, emphasizing divine justice and the certainty of accountability on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Those whose eyes were blind to My remembrance, and who could not bear to hear it.
interpretation: This verse speaks about people who deliberately avoid or reject the message of God, to the extent that their hearts are closed (their eyes are ‘covered’) and they are unable or unwilling to listen to divine guidance. It reflects a state of spiritual blindness and deafness caused by obstinacy or heedlessness, emphasizing the consequences of turning away from truth and guidance.

translation: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies instead of Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of seeking protection or alliance with others besides God, especially by those who reject faith. It conveys that true loyalty and support are with God alone, and those who turn away from Him and rely on others grant themselves only destruction and punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?"
interpretation: This verse draws attention to the reality that not all efforts are fruitful; those who forsake true guidance and righteousness, despite their endeavors, ultimately suffer loss. It serves as a warning that success is measured not by mere activity, but by adherence to God's commands and sincere faith, emphasizing the importance of aligning one's actions with divine guidance.

translation: Those whose efforts have gone astray in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing well.
interpretation: This verse warns against self-deception in evaluating one's actions. It emphasizes that people may sincerely believe they are doing good, yet their efforts are misguided and ultimately lead to failure, especially when their focus is solely on worldly gains without consideration of the hereafter or divine guidance.

translation: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless, and We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight.
interpretation: This verse teaches that rejecting the signs of God and denying the meeting with Him in the Hereafter undermines the very foundation of faith. Such disbelief renders a person's actions void and without any merit, emphasizing that genuine belief and consciousness of accountability are essential to give value to one's deeds on the Day of Judgment.

translation: That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequence for those who reject faith and mock the divine revelations and messengers. It underscores the gravity of disbelief coupled with the disrespect and scorn towards God's signs and His prophets, leading to the punishment of Hell as a just recompense.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them are the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith combined with righteous actions leads to the ultimate reward: eternal residence in the highest levels of Paradise. It highlights the inseparability of belief and action, indicating that faith is actualized and proven through good deeds, and that such a combination is the basis for divine reward and bliss in the hereafter.

translation: They will abide therein forever; they will not desire from it any transfer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence and contentment of the dwellers of Paradise. It highlights that those admitted to this eternal abode will experience unending bliss and will have no desire to leave or change their state, reflecting the fulfillment and perfect satisfaction granted by Allah to the righteous.

translation: Say, "If the sea were ink for [writing] the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless and infinite nature of God's words, knowledge, and wisdom. It illustrates that no matter how vast or abundant something in creation might be—in this case, the sea as ink to write with—it is still insufficient to encompass the entirety of God's divine speech. This underscores the greatness of God and the limitless extent of His guidance and decrees, encouraging believers to recognize the depth and breadth of divine wisdom beyond human comprehension.

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is but one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that he is not divine but a messenger conveying God's revelation. It stresses the importance of monotheism and sincere worship, encouraging believers to focus on righteous deeds and to avoid any form of idolatry or associating partners with God, as true faith is demonstrated through sincere devotion and ethical conduct in anticipation of meeting the Creator.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Kaf Ha Ya 'Ain Sad.
interpretation: These disjointed letters, known as 'Muqattaʿat,' appear at the beginning of certain chapters of the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is known only to Allah, serving as a divine sign and a reminder of the miraculous and inimitable nature of the Qur'an.

translation: Remember the mercy of your Lord upon His servant Zakariya.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy by recalling how He favored Zakariya, highlighting that divine mercy is a source of support and comfort for the faithful during times of difficulty and longing.

translation: When he called to his Lord a call in secret,
interpretation: This verse highlights the intimate and sincere communication between the Prophet and his Lord, emphasizing that true devotion and supplication often come from the heart in quiet humility, away from public attention, underscoring the importance of sincere faith and personal connection with God.

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy."
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's humble acknowledgment of his old age and physical frailty, coupled with his steadfastness and sincerity in prayer. It teaches us the importance of persistent and sincere supplication to God throughout our lives, regardless of our physical conditions, highlighting that true devotion is measured not by one's strength or youth but by the constancy and purity of one's prayers.

translation: And indeed, I fear the supporters (after me), and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir.
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Abraham's sincere plea to God for a righteous heir, expressing concern about the succession and continuity of his legacy, highlighting the human anxiety about future generations and the desire for a chosen successor who will uphold faith and righteousness after one's passing.

translation: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing (to You).
interpretation: This verse expresses a prayer for the continuation of blessings and favor through successive generations, highlighting the importance of legacy and divine approval. It reflects a desire for the spiritual and moral qualities to be passed down within a blessed lineage, ensuring that the individual is not only physically inherited but also accepted and favored by God.

translation: O Zakariya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be Yahya. We have not assigned this name to anyone before.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine announcement of a unique and blessed birth, emphasizing that the name Yahya (John) is special and unprecedented. It highlights the extraordinary nature of this child, who will be endowed with significant spiritual qualities and a distinguished role among the prophets.

translation: He said, "My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound faith and reliance on Allah's power beyond human limitations. Despite physical impossibilities—such as old age and barrenness—prophets express their trust that Allah's command can override natural laws, signifying that with Allah, all things are possible and encouraging believers to place hope and trust in His divine intervention.

translation: Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me, and indeed, I created you before when you were nothing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and authority over creation. It conveys that creating and sustaining life is effortless for God, highlighting His omnipotence. Additionally, it serves as a reminder that before human existence, there was nothing, and it was through God's will that life came into being, underscoring human dependence on Divine creation and control.

translation: He said, "My Lord, show me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, being sound."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound concept of a divine sign manifesting through a period of silence, emphasizing that sometimes, communication and understanding transcend spoken words. The silence serves as a testament to the truthfulness of the prophet's mission and a means to draw attention and reflection from the people, highlighting that signs from God can come in various forms, including the absence of speech.

translation: Then he came out to his people from the sanctuary and informed them to glorify Allah morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of regular worship and remembrance of Allah at the start and end of the day, emphasizing a balanced spiritual routine that nurtures the soul continuously.

translation: O Yahya (John), take the Scripture with determination; and We gave him judgment while he was a youth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gift of divine wisdom and responsibility bestowed upon Prophet Yahya (John) from a young age, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness and strength in upholding and implementing divine guidance.

translation: And a mercy from Us and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah's mercy is a profound gift granted from His own presence, serving as a source of blessing and spiritual growth. The mention of 'zakat' (which here signifies purification) indicates that this mercy purifies the soul, and it is particularly beneficial to those who are conscious of God (the pious or 'taqwa'), as it strengthens their faith and keeps them on a righteous path.

translation: And be dutiful to your parents and do not be a rebellious tyrant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of kindness and respect towards one's parents, highlighting that obedience and gratitude to them are essential virtues. At the same time, it warns against harshness, arrogance, and disobedience, which can sever familial bonds and lead one away from moral righteousness.

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perpetual honor and divine peace bestowed upon the Prophet Jesus ('Isa), affirming his elevated status at all significant stages of his existence: his birth, death, and resurrection, thereby signifying God's ongoing protection and respect for him.

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
interpretation: This verse highlights Mary's piety and devotion, as she sought seclusion and purity, distancing herself from worldly distractions to focus on her spiritual connection with God. It emphasizes her distinctiveness and the special status she holds among women due to her submission and dedication.

translation: So she took a screen (to shield herself) from them, and We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared before her as a well-proportioned man.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine intervention in delivering the message to Maryam (Mary). The 'screen' symbolizes her modesty and separation from others, emphasizing her purity. The 'Spirit' refers to the angel Gabriel, who came in human form to convey God's message. This signifies that God's communication transcends ordinary human means, bringing guidance directly from the Divine.

translation: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing Allah."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of seeking protection in God's mercy against harm, emphasizing the importance of fearing God as a means of safeguarding oneself from wrongdoing and maintaining righteousness in interpersonal dealings.

translation: He said, "Indeed, I am the messenger of your Lord to give you a sound boy."
interpretation: This verse conveys the divine assurance and hope brought by the messenger's announcement of a righteous child. It signifies God's power to grant blessings and fulfill promises, emphasizing faith in God's ability to bring forth goodness against all odds.

translation: She said, 'How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the miraculous nature of God's power to create life without human intervention, emphasizing the purity and innocence of Mary, highlighting that the birth of Prophet Jesus was a divine miracle beyond human comprehension.

translation: Thus [it is]. And your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. And We will surely make them [i.e., the dead] as a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ability of Allah to cause resurrection or bring life after death is an act of His supreme power and mercy. It serves as a sign to humanity, demonstrating His control over life and death, and as a mercy by granting hope of recompense and justice beyond worldly existence.

translation: So I carried him and withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the act of seeking privacy and protection for the vulnerable. It emphasizes the care and caution taken to preserve someone’s safety away from harm or scrutiny, highlighting the importance of safeguarding innocence and maintaining secrecy when necessary for protection.

translation: Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was completely forgotten."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense physical anguish and emotional despair experienced at the moment of childbirth, highlighting human vulnerability in times of extreme trial. The woman's wish to have been forgotten rather than endure such hardship underscores the profound struggle between suffering and hope, reminding us of the resilience and endurance required to overcome life's most difficult challenges.

translation: He called her from beneath her, "Do not grieve; indeed, your Lord has provided beneath you a stream."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Allah's mercy and provision, reassuring that in moments of despair, Divine support and relief are already arranged, often in ways not immediately visible, highlighting trust in God's planning.

translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's provision and ease granted to the Prophet and believers. It symbolizes how, by a simple action (shaking the palm tree), blessings and sustenance are made readily available, highlighting divine mercy and the natural bounty provided without hardship.

translation: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see any human being, then say, "Indeed, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak today to any man."
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of fulfilling vows made to Allah sincerely and with dedication. It highlights that worship may involve not only acts of abstention like fasting but also a commitment to silence and restraint in social interactions. Such practices serve to purify the soul, strengthen self-discipline, and draw one closer to God by minimizing worldly distractions.

translation: Then her people came to her, carrying him, and they said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of Mary's people upon seeing her with the child Jesus. Their accusation reflects their surprise and suspicion, as they presumed that Mary had committed an act unheard of in their community. The verse underscores the human tendency to judge based on appearances and societal norms, prompting reflection on trust, innocence, and divine intervention beyond human conventions.

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a bad man, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the honorable and righteous lineage of Maryam (Mary), affirming that her parents were respected and chaste individuals. It serves to dispel any misconceptions about her background, highlighting the importance of respecting her purity and status as the mother of Prophet Isa (Jesus).

translation: So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the astonishment and disbelief of the people toward the miraculous nature of the prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) speaking as an infant in the cradle. It highlights how divine revelation can transcend normal human expectations and limitations, emphasizing that God's signs can manifest in ways beyond human understanding.

translation: He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and servitude of the prophet, emphasizing that his authority and knowledge come directly from Allah. It signifies that prophethood is not a position of personal grandeur, but a trust and responsibility granted by God, with the Scripture as guidance to lead people towards truth and righteousness.

translation: And He made me blessed wherever I was, and He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I lived.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine blessing and favor granted to the speaker, indicating that their presence brings goodness and blessings universally. Additionally, it underscores the importance of continual devotion through prayer and charity (zakah) as lifelong obligations, emphasizing that spiritual discipline and generosity are essential components of a blessed and righteous life.

translation: And be kind to my mother, and He did not make me arrogant and miserable.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's emphasis on kindness and humility. It underscores the importance of showing compassion and gratitude toward one's mother while also embodying humility and avoiding arrogance and misery, reflecting a balanced and virtuous character.

translation: And peace be upon the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: This verse expresses a heartfelt invocation of peace upon significant moments of human existence: birth, death, and resurrection. It reflects a deep hope for tranquility and divine mercy at these pivotal stages, emphasizing the belief in life beyond death and the ultimate return to God for judgment.

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary—the statement of truth concerning which they doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the incontrovertible truth of Jesus, son of Mary, affirming his identity despite the doubts and disputes of those who question his reality and nature. It underscores the certainty of divine revelation against human skepticism.

translation: It is not befitting for Allah to take a son. Exalted is He! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, asserting that assigning offspring to Him is inconsistent with His divine nature. It highlights His supreme authority and power, where His command alone is sufficient to bring anything into existence without any intermediate process or progeny.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse calls for sincere worship and devotion to Allah alone, emphasizing the unity of God as the Lord of all. It highlights the importance of following the path prescribed by Him, which is clear and true, guiding believers toward righteousness and away from misguidance.

translation: So the factions differed among themselves. And woe to those who disbelieved from a great Day.
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequences awaiting those who disbelieve, particularly on a day of immense trial and accountability. The discord among opposing groups is highlighted, suggesting that internal divisions weaken their cause, while the ultimate woe pertains to their fate on the Day of Judgment when their deeds will be assessed.

translation: I hear them and I see them on the Day they will come to Us, but the wrongdoers are in clear error today.
interpretation: This verse highlights that on the Day of Judgment, the speaker (representing divine awareness) will witness the wrongdoers as they come forth for judgment. Despite their apparent confidence or denial in this world, their wrongdoing places them in evident misguidance and error, making their eventual accountability unavoidable and their delusion apparent.

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and seriousness of the Day of Judgment, a day when all matters will be irrevocably decided. It serves as a stern warning that many people remain heedless and unprepared, failing to believe despite the clear signs. The verse calls for awareness and reflection, urging people to awaken from their negligence before it is too late.

translation: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and those upon it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ultimate sovereignty over the earth and everything within it. It reminds believers that worldly possessions and life itself are transient, and that all beings will ultimately return to God for judgment and recompense. It serves as a call to humility and recognition of divine authority above all creation.

translation: And remember in the Book Ibrahim (Abraham); indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Abraham, emphasizing his unwavering truthfulness and prophetic mission. It serves as a reminder of his steadfast commitment to monotheism and righteousness, encouraging believers to emulate his sincerity and faithfulness.

translation: When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees nor benefits you in any way?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rational and compassionate approach to guiding others away from idolatry, highlighting the futility of worshipping lifeless objects that cannot respond or provide benefit, and encouraging belief in a living, aware, and responsive God.

translation: O my father, indeed I have received knowledge that has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of embracing new guidance and wisdom, even if it conflicts with longstanding beliefs or traditions. It portrays a sincere invitation to trust in the truth brought by prophetic revelation, promising that such adherence leads to a clear, balanced, and righteous way of life.

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been ever, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and wrongfulness of worshiping Satan, highlighting that Satan is inherently rebellious and disobedient even toward Allah, the Most Merciful. It serves as a warning that following Satan leads away from mercy and guidance.

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will seize you, so that you become a companion of the Satan.
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep concern and sorrow of the speaker, who fears that his father's rejection of faith will lead him to divine punishment and spiritual downfall, becoming allied with forces opposed to God's mercy.

translation: He said, "Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me alone for a while."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound conflict between Ibrahim's unwavering monotheism and the entrenched idolatry of his society. It highlights the resistance and hostility faced by prophets when challenging false beliefs, emphasizing the courage required to stand firm in truth despite threats and social alienation.

translation: He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed, He has always been attentive to me."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates a compassionate and hopeful attitude, emphasizing the importance of praying for others' forgiveness and recognizing that God is always attentive to our pleas. It highlights mercy, the power of intercession, and the personal relationship one can have with the Divine.

translation: And I will withdraw from you and from those you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord, hoping that I will not be unblessed in my supplication to my Lord.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the speaker's conscious decision to dissociate from the polytheistic practices of invoking other than Allah, emphasizing a sincere reliance solely on God in prayer. It underscores the importance of monotheism and the hope that dedicating one's supplication to Allah alone will lead to spiritual well-being and avoid misery.

translation: So when he withdrew from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and each of them We made a prophet.
