interpretation: This verse illustrates the reward and confirmation of faith that comes from turning away from false gods and devotion to Allah alone; it emphasizes that sincere abandonment of idolatry is met with divine blessings, such as the granting of righteous offspring who continue the prophetic mission.

translation: And We granted them of Our mercy, and We made for them a truthful high ground.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon certain individuals, emphasizing that through God's mercy, they are granted not only blessings but also a position of honor and truthfulness. It signifies that true elevation in status comes from sincerity and divine grace, underscoring the importance of mercy and integrity as foundations for genuine esteem and authority.

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Moses. Indeed, he was a sincere devotee and a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Prophet Moses in the Qur'an, highlighting his purity of intention and his status as a true messenger and prophet. It teaches that sincerity and dedication to God's mission are essential qualities for those chosen to convey divine messages to humanity.

translation: And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near, safe and sound.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intimate and direct communication between God and Prophet Moses. It signifies how God chose to manifest His presence in a powerful and protective manner, assuring Moses' safety in the divine encounter. It teaches us about the closeness and favor granted to those chosen by God for special revelations, emphasizing the sanctity and seriousness of prophetic experiences.

translation: And We bestowed upon him from Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: This verse signifies God's grace in providing Moses with the support of his brother Aaron, not only as a companion but as a prophet himself. It emphasizes the importance of mutual support and divinely appointed assistance in fulfilling divine missions.

translation: And mention in the Book Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Isma'il, emphasizing his unwavering truthfulness and steadfastness in fulfilling his commitments, as well as his esteemed status as a messenger and prophet. It serves as a reminder of his dedication to God's mission and the importance of integrity and prophetic guidance in leading a righteous life.

translation: And he used to enjoin upon his family prayer and zakah, and was pleased with his Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of steadfastness in worship and righteousness within one's family. It teaches that true devotion involves not just personal piety but also guiding one's household in fulfilling their religious duties, which leads to being accepted and favored by God.

translation: And mention in the Book Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and honoring Prophet Idris, emphasizing his honesty and prophetic status. It serves as a reminder that truthfulness and piety are virtues that elevate a person to a distinguished rank among prophets, encouraging believers to emulate such qualities.

translation: And We raised it (the Qur'an) to a high station.
interpretation: This verse signifies the exalted status and importance of the Qur'an, indicating that it has been elevated to a supreme and honored position by Allah. It highlights the divine origin and distinguished rank of the revelation, which is meant to guide humanity and serves as a source of wisdom and light.

translation: Those are the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall in prostration and weep.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favor and selection bestowed by Allah on a lineage of chosen prophets, emphasizing their exceptional devotion and submission. Their worship stems from an intimate recognition of Allah's words, causing them to respond with humility and deep spiritual emotion when they hear His verses, illustrating that true faith manifests in a heartfelt, submissive reaction to divine guidance.

translation: Then after them came successors who neglected prayer and followed their desires; so they will surely encounter destruction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual decline that occurs when a community abandons the fundamental act of worship—prayer—and instead pursues fleeting worldly desires. Such neglect leads to loss and inevitable ruin, illustrating the essential link between steadfastness in devotion and maintaining righteousness and success.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. For them, Allah will admit into Paradise, and they will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sincere repentance, belief in God, and righteous actions are the key conditions for forgiveness and entry into Paradise. It implies that past sins can be absolved if one genuinely reforms and commits to a life of faith and good deeds, highlighting God's justice and mercy in rewarding true transformation without any injustice.

translation: Gardens of Eden which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen; indeed, His promise is ever coming to pass.
interpretation: This verse assures the believer that the eternal bliss of Paradise, promised by Allah (the Most Merciful), is not mere empty talk or wishful thinking but a certain reality that will undoubtedly manifest in the Hereafter, affirming Allah's unfailing truthfulness and the certainty of divine reward for the faithful.

translation: They will not hear therein any vain or sinful talk — only greetings of peace. And they will have their provision therein morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse signifies the purity and tranquility of the Hereafter, where believers are free from any corrupt or harmful speech, highlighting a state of peace and spiritual nourishment that is constant and fulfilling.

translation: That is the Paradise which We give as inheritance to some of Our servants who were righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Paradise is a reward specially designated for those among God's servants who lived with righteousness and piety. It highlights the concept that eternal bliss is not granted arbitrarily, but as an inheritance to individuals who cultivate God-consciousness and moral integrity in their lives.

translation: And We do not descend except by the order of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between them, and your Lord is never forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute control and authority of Allah over all matters, affirming that nothing occurs except by His command. It highlights His encompassing knowledge of the past, present, and future, reassuring that Allah is fully aware and never neglects His creation or duties. This teaches us to trust in His wisdom and timing, knowing that all events are part of His divine plan and knowledge.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be patient in His worship. Do you know of any name for Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's lordship over all creation and calls for sincere worship and patience. It challenges any attribution of names or attributes to God other than those revealed, underscoring the uniqueness and transcendence of Allah beyond human conceptions.

translation: And man says, "When I am dead, shall I then be brought forth alive?"
interpretation: This verse expresses the skepticism and doubt that humans often have about life after death. It highlights a natural human tendency to question and deny the resurrection and the hereafter, emphasizing the need for faith and reflection on the reality of life beyond death.

translation: Did man not consider that We created him from a sperm-drop? Yet he is a clear adversary.
interpretation: This verse reminds humans of their humble origins, emphasizing that they were created from something as insignificant as a sperm-drop. It calls attention to the tendency of humans to reject the truth or act arrogantly despite this, highlighting the importance of humility and recognizing the power and wisdom of the Creator in bringing life into existence.

translation: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them [that Day] round Hell upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment when all wrongdoers and evildoers, along with the devils who misled them, will be assembled and brought humbly to Hell. It illustrates the gravity of accountability and the inevitable consequence of persistent wrongdoing, highlighting God's supreme authority in administering justice.

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were worst against the Most Merciful in insolence.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, God will distinguish and remove from every group the individuals who were the most arrogant and defiant against His mercy. It highlights the concept that wrongful behavior, especially that which rejects or disrespects divine compassion, will not be overlooked, and such individuals will face consequences distinct from others in their community.

translation: Then indeed, We are most knowing of those who are best suited for it.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has perfect knowledge of who truly deserves His rewards and blessings, emphasizing that human judgment is limited and that ultimate decisions rest with God, who knows the inner realities and true worth of individuals.

translation: And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is ever, upon your Lord, a matter decreed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the certainty of returning to the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that every soul will eventually face the Day of Judgment, a fixed decree from Allah. This understanding encourages mindfulness of one's actions and accountability, knowing that life is transient and the ultimate outcome is predetermined by God's will.

translation: Then We save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers therein bound in chains.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy of Allah towards the righteous who maintain God-consciousness (taqwa), promising their salvation from worldly trials or the hereafter's consequences. Conversely, it warns that the unjust and oppressive, those who transgress divine limits, will face severe punishment, depicted here as being left helpless and restrained. It reflects the principle of divine justice where protection and rescue are reserved for the mindful and the pious, while the arrogant and oppressive incur retribution.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of the two parties is better in position and better in speech?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and rivalry of disbelievers who, when confronted with the clear signs of God, challenge the believers by questioning whose cause is better or whose speech is more eloquent. It reflects a challenge to the legitimacy of faith, rooted in worldly pride, rather than genuine understanding or submission to truth.

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in possessions and appearances?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that worldly wealth and outward beauty do not guarantee safety or success. Despite having greater material possessions and more splendid appearances, previous generations were destroyed due to their rejection of divine guidance and evil deeds. It warns that reliance on worldly status is futile without adherence to righteousness, and that divine justice prevails regardless of one's external advantages.

translation: Say, "Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him a respite." Until, when they see what they are promised - either the punishment or the Hour - then they will know who is worst in position and weakest in soldiers.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's patience and mercy by allowing those who persist in error time to reconsider and repent. However, it also conveys that when the inevitable consequences—whether punishment or the Day of Judgment—arrive, the true reality will become clear: those who rejected guidance will be revealed as being in the worst position, lacking any form of protection or support.

translation: And Allah increases those who have been guided in guidance. And the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord in reward and better for recourse.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Divine guidance is not static but grows and deepens for those who sincerely follow the right path. Moreover, it highlights the supreme value of righteous deeds that endure beyond this life, signaling that continuous good actions hold greater significance and reward with Allah than fleeting worldly achievements. It encourages steadfastness in goodness and reliance on Allah's infinite mercy and justice.

translation: Have you seen the one who disbelieves in Our verses and says, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and false assurance of those who reject God's signs while vainly hoping to secure worldly prosperity and progeny as a means of protection or permanence. It serves as a reminder that true security and success come from faith and submission to God, not from material possessions or lineage.

translation: Does He who knows the unseen not know? Or has He taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, highlighting that He alone possesses complete awareness of the unseen. It challenges any notion that Allah might have limitations or agreements that restrict His knowledge, affirming His absolute sovereignty and omniscience.

translation: No! We will record what he says and extend to him the punishment extensively.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that nothing uttered by a person goes unnoticed; every word is being recorded and accounted for. It serves as a warning that actions and speech have consequences, and persistent wrongdoing will lead to prolonged punishment. This underscores the principle of divine justice and accountability.

translation: And We inherit what he says and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly matters and the inevitable meeting with God alone after death. Whatever a person says or leaves behind in this world ultimately becomes part of God's knowledge and possession, highlighting that human legacy and deeds return to Allah, and every individual is accountable solely to Him in the Hereafter.

translation: And they took gods besides Allah so that they might be given honor.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to associate partners with Allah in an attempt to gain status or respect, reflecting a misplaced reliance on false deities rather than trusting in the true power and sovereignty of God alone.

translation: No! They will deny their worshipping (the idols), and they will be, against them, opponents.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of rejection and opposition towards those idols which people wrongly worship. It serves as a warning that devotion to false deities is futile and will ultimately be repudiated, leading to hostility and conflict, emphasizing the importance of true monotheistic belief.

translation: Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them to [evil] agitation?
interpretation: This verse highlights how those who reject faith are influenced and provoked by negative forces, symbolized by 'devils,' leading them to heightened hostility and opposition against truth and righteousness.

translation: So do not hasten on their account. We are only accumulating for them punishment.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle of divine justice unfolding according to Allah's wisdom and timing. It cautions against impatience in expecting the consequences for the wrongdoers, emphasizing that Allah's punishment is being prepared with certainty but will occur in due time as decreed. It underscores that human beings should trust the process without rushing or doubting God's plan.

translation: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful, (as) a delegation.
interpretation: This verse portrays a scene from the Day of Judgment where those who were righteous and mindful of God throughout their lives will be brought together before Allah in a special assembly. It emphasizes the honor and closeness the righteous will have in the presence of the Most Merciful, highlighting the reward for those who lived with piety and consciousness of God.

translation: And We drive the criminals to Hell, in thirst.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable consequence of wicked deeds and crimes, illustrating that those who commit sins will be forcibly led to Hell as a just recompense. Their punishment is not only physical but also metaphysical, signifying a state of deprivation and torment, highlighting Allah's just nature and the serious consequences of immoral behavior.

translation: They do not possess intercession except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that intercession on the Day of Judgment is not a matter of privilege or arbitrary authority; rather, it is granted exclusively to those who have established a sincere and binding relationship with Allah through faith, obedience, and righteousness. It highlights the importance of maintaining a covenant with Allah, underscoring that mercy and intercession come through His permission and are accessible only to those who truly adhere to His guidance.

translation: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son."
interpretation: This verse addresses the false claim made by some that Allah, the Most Merciful, has begotten a son. The statement emphasizes the incorrectness and untruth of ascribing offspring to Allah, who is unique, self-sufficient, and free from human attributes such as lineage or progeny. It serves as a repudiation of such beliefs that compromise the pure monotheism central to Islam.

translation: You have certainly come with something extraordinary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the remarkable nature of the message or action being addressed. It acknowledges that what has been presented is unprecedented and challenges existing norms, indicating a significant impact or transformation that demands attention and reflection.

translation: The heavens almost break apart from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse down in devastation.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the overwhelming magnitude and power of the Day of Judgment, signifying that the natural order of the universe will be dramatically upheaved in response to the final reckoning, emphasizing the seriousness and inevitability of divine accountability.

translation: They have attributed to the Most Merciful a son.
interpretation: This verse highlights the false claim made by some that Allah, the Most Merciful, has begotten a son, emphasizing the error of ascribing offspring to the Divine Essence, which transcends human attributes and relationships.

translation: And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and transcendence of Allah, rejecting any association or attribution of offspring to Him, which contradicts His nature as the One and Only, free from human-like attributes or relationships.

translation: Indeed, everyone in the heavens and the earth will come as a servant to the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and mercy of Allah, illustrating that all beings, regardless of their realm or status, are ultimately under His dominion and will return to Him in servitude. It serves to remind us of the comprehensive nature of divine authority and the inevitable submission to God's mercy and judgment.

translation: Indeed, He has counted them and numbered them precisely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge and precise accounting of all things, including actions and people. It conveys that nothing escapes His awareness and that every deed and individual is recorded with exactness, underscoring Divine justice and accountability.

translation: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual accountability of every soul on the Day of Judgment. Regardless of relationships, status, or associations in worldly life, each person will stand alone before Allah to receive the recompense for their deeds. It highlights the personal nature of the final reckoning and the importance of one's own actions and faith.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds – the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: This verse signifies that sincere faith combined with righteous actions elicits a special love and mercy from Allah. It highlights that divine favor is not merely due to belief alone but is manifested through faith reflected in good deeds, resulting in a close and loving relationship with the Most Merciful.

translation: So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings to the righteous and warn a people who are obstinate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine facilitation granted to the Prophet Muhammad in conveying the message of the Qur'an in his own language, making it accessible and clear for his audience. It underscores the purpose of the revelation: to bring glad tidings to the righteous who follow the guidance and to warn those who are stubborn and reject the truth, thereby emphasizing both mercy and accountability in the divine message.

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them? Can you perceive from them anyone or hear a sound from them?
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human existence and the consequences of disregarding divine guidance. It serves as a reminder that entire communities who denied the truth were eradicated, leaving no trace or influence behind; thus, it cautions that ignoring God's warnings leads to obliteration and emphasizes the importance of heeding the messages brought by the prophets.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ta Ha.
interpretation: The opening words invoke Allah's mercy and compassion, setting a tone of divine grace. The letters 'Ta Ha' are among the mysterious disjointed letters (Muqattaʿat) of the Qur'an whose precise meaning is known only to Allah, serving to capture attention and signify the miraculous nature of the revelation.

translation: We have not sent down the Qur'an upon you to cause you distress.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is revealed as a source of guidance, mercy, and ease for believers, rather than hardship or suffering. Its purpose is to lead humanity towards betterment and spiritual well-being, not to burden or oppress them.

translation: Except as a reminder to those who fear (Allah).
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an serves primarily as a reminder and guidance specifically for those who are conscious of Allah and who hold a reverent fear of Him. It implies that such individuals are receptive to its messages and are motivated to seek righteousness and avoid wrongdoing, recognizing the importance of accountability and the consequences of their actions.

translation: A revelation from the One who created the earth and the highest heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine message sent down by the Creator, who has power over all creation, both the earth and the highest heavens, underscoring His supreme authority and the truthfulness of the revelation.

translation: The Most Merciful established Himself above the Throne.
interpretation: This verse signifies Allah's supreme authority and dominion over the entire universe, emphasizing His elevated status and control beyond human comprehension while affirming His mercy as an essential attribute.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all realms—visible and invisible, earthly and celestial. It serves as a reminder that nothing exists outside His control or authority, affirming His power and ownership over all creation, which instills humility and recognition of His ultimate governance.

translation: And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that Allah's knowledge encompasses both our spoken words and the deepest, most concealed thoughts within our hearts. It emphasizes the importance of sincerity and mindfulness in our speech and actions, knowing that nothing remains hidden from Divine awareness.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and oneness of Allah as the sole deity worthy of worship, and highlights that He possesses the most beautiful and perfect names and attributes, which reflect His majesty, mercy, and power. It calls for recognizing and affirming God's singularity and reverence through His exalted characteristics.

translation: Has there reached you the story of Moses?
interpretation: This verse invites the listener to reflect on the significant and well-known narrative of Prophet Moses, emphasizing the importance of understanding the lessons derived from his experiences and the divine guidance associated with him.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a burning torch from it or find at the fire guidance."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Prophet Abraham's initiative and faith in seeking guidance and light from a tangible source of fire. It symbolizes the human effort to attain knowledge and enlightenment through exploration and hope, trusting that seeking truth will lead to illumination and guidance.

translation: So when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses!"
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of divine communication where God directly addresses Moses, indicating the beginning of a profound spiritual encounter and mission. It reflects the importance of readiness and attentiveness to divine guidance when it arrives unexpectedly.

translation: I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine command to Prophet Moses, indicating the sacredness and purity of the place he stands in. Removing sandals symbolizes respect, humility, and the acknowledgment of being in a holy presence. It teaches that approaching God requires reverence and mindfulness, emphasizing that certain places and moments demand sacred behavior.

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to that which is revealed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special selection and appointment of the Prophet for the divine mission, underscoring the importance of attentively receiving and adhering to the guidance from God conveyed through revelation.

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the singularity and exclusivity of Allah's divinity, asserting that He alone deserves worship. It highlights the importance of establishing prayer as a means to remember and maintain a conscious connection with Allah, reinforcing the relationship between the Creator and the believer.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming—I almost conceal it—that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and imminence of the Day of Judgment, highlighting that while its exact time is hidden, its purpose is clear: each individual will be held accountable and rewarded or punished fairly according to their actions and efforts in life.

translation: So let not those who do not believe in it and follow their own desires divert you from it, lest you perish.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believer to remain steadfast in the truth of divine revelation, emphasizing that the disbelief and seductive allure of personal desires by others should not cause one to abandon the message. Turning away due to such influences leads to ruin; therefore, commitment to faith must override societal pressures and internal temptations.

translation: And that is not [by] your right hand, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse addresses Moses, indicating that the power or miraculous ability he has demonstrated does not originate from his own strength or physical might, but from the divine will and command of God. It serves as a reminder that true power and miraculous signs come from God, not from human agency.

translation: He said, "It is my staff; I lean on it, and I strike with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it."
interpretation: This verse reflects the importance of simple tools and support in daily life, symbolizing reliance and utility. It suggests that what may seem ordinary or humble can have multiple significant purposes, emphasizing resourcefulness and faith in God-given means.

translation: He said, "Throw it, O Moses."
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of trial where Moses is commanded to cast down his staff to demonstrate a divine sign, emphasizing the importance of trust in God's guidance and the manifestation of miracles to affirm God's authority.

translation: So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent moving swiftly.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformation granted by Allah to Prophet Moses' staff as a miraculous sign, emphasizing God's power to alter the natural order and affirm Moses' prophethood to his people.

translation: He said, "Take it and do not fear; We will return it to its former condition."
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's assurance and power over the state of things, indicating that even after a transformation or overwhelming event, He can restore it to its original state. It serves as a reminder of God's control over life's changes and His ability to alleviate fear by promising restoration and continuity.

translation: وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ يَدُكَ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ ۖ آيَةً أُخْرَىٰ
interpretation: This verse illustrates the miraculous signs granted to Prophet Moses, where his hand becomes shining white as a sign of divine support without causing harm. It signifies the power of Allah to manifest clear, extraordinary signs to affirm His messengers’ truth and to inspire belief among the people.

translation: That We may show you some of Our greater signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's intent to reveal to the Prophet, and through him to humanity, profound and significant signs of His power and wisdom. These 'greater signs' are meant to strengthen faith by presenting clear evidence of God's existence, authority, and the truth of His message, encouraging reflection and submission to Him.

translation: Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed beyond bounds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and oppression of Pharaoh, emphasizing that his disobedience and tyranny have reached an extreme level. It serves as a call to confront injustice and corruption boldly, recognizing when a leader has gone beyond rightful limits and must be challenged.

translation: My Lord, expand for me my chest.
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication for inner peace, clarity, and confidence. It signifies the desire for a heart that is broad and free from anxiety, enabling one to face challenges with calmness and understanding.

translation: And make my task easy for me.
interpretation: This verse expresses a heartfelt plea to God for facilitation and ease in accomplishing one's duties or endeavors. It reflects the understanding that human efforts are limited without divine assistance, highlighting reliance on God's mercy and support to overcome challenges and achieve success.

translation: And untie the knot from my tongue.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication asking God to remove the impediment in speech, enabling the speaker to express themselves clearly and confidently. It reflects a plea for divine assistance to overcome hesitation or difficulty in communication, highlighting the importance of clarity and eloquence in conveying one's thoughts and messages effectively.

translation: That they may understand My speech.
interpretation: This phrase highlights the importance of deep comprehension of divine guidance, emphasizing that true understanding of God's words is essential for believers to internalize and live by His message.

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family.
interpretation: This verse reflects the importance of having a trusted and close companion to assist in leadership and responsibilities, emphasizing the value of shared trust, loyalty, and support within one's own family or close circle for effective governance and decision-making.

translation: Harun is my brother.
interpretation: This statement emphasizes the close familial relationship and support between Prophet Musa (Moses) and his brother Harun (Aaron), highlighting the importance of cooperation and mutual assistance in carrying out their divine mission.

translation: Strengthen my back with it.
interpretation: This phrase is a prayer for support and reinforcement, asking God to provide strength and firmness in one's resolve or efforts, often implying a need for perseverance in the face of hardship.

translation: And associate him in my matter.
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea to Allah, expressing a desire to share the burden or responsibility of a particular matter with another person, often implying reliance or partnership. In a broader spiritual sense, it signifies the human tendency to involve others in decisions or affairs that are ultimately between oneself and God, highlighting the importance of seeking divine guidance alone rather than attributing partners to Allah in matters of control and destiny.

translation: That we may extol You abundantly.
interpretation: This phrase expresses the intention to glorify and praise Allah extensively, highlighting the believer's desire to recognize and honor the divine attributes and greatness of God through continuous and earnest worship.

translation: And We remind you often.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuous effort of God to remind and guide humanity through repeated messages, highlighting the importance of constant remembrance and reflection upon divine guidance to maintain faith and righteousness.

translation: Indeed, you were, concerning Us, among those well-informed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had clear insight and understanding granted by Allah about the divine matters and the truth of the message. It highlights the Prophet's special awareness and awareness of God's plans and decrees, distinguishing him with a higher level of spiritual knowledge.

translation: He said, 'Your request has been granted, O Moses.'
interpretation: This verse conveys the assurance given to Prophet Moses that what he asked for — typically understood as meeting with God on Mount Sinai or receiving divine wisdom — will be fulfilled, emphasizing God's responsiveness to the sincere requests of His prophets.

translation: And We had certainly given you, [O Muhammad], another favor.
interpretation: This verse signifies the continuous blessings and support granted by Allah to Prophet Muhammad, highlighting divine favor as a source of strength and encouragement in the face of trials and difficulties.

translation: When We inspired to your mother what was inspired,
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine communication bestowed upon the mother of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), signifying the special guidance and revelation given to her. It underscores the sacred process through which the Prophet's life and mission were initiated by divine command, emphasizing the important role of revelation in the commencement of prophethood.

translation: Then cast him into the river and cast him into the sea; the sea will throw him upon the shore, where an enemy and a friend will find him. And I have cast upon you love from Me that you may be cared for under My watchful eye.
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound wisdom and divine plan in the protection and destiny of the individual, illustrating that even when seemingly cast into hardship or abandonment, God's loving care ensures preservation and ultimately guides towards benefit. The 'love from Me' symbolizes divine mercy and guidance that watches over and nurtures, turning adversity into opportunity under the protective gaze of God.

translation: [Remember] when your sister walked and said, "Shall I direct you to one who will be responsible for him?" So We restored you to your mother so that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We saved you from the consequence of that grief and We tested you with trials. And you stayed for years among the people of Midian, then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse reflects the compassionate care of God in the life of Moses, highlighting how divine intervention guides and supports individuals through trials and tribulations. It shows that even when one faces serious mistakes or challenges, such as Moses killing a soul, God's mercy and testing serve a purpose in shaping character and preparing a person for their destined mission. The verse teaches that patience, endurance through trials, and trust in God's plan are essential, as ultimate success and fulfillment come at the appointed time by God's wisdom.

translation: And I have created you for Myself.
interpretation: This verse expresses the intimate and special purpose behind the creation of an individual, highlighting that the ultimate aim of existence is closeness and devotion to God alone, emphasizing the exclusivity of this divine relationship.

translation: Go, both you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse encourages perseverance and steadfastness in conveying the message of God, emphasizing that both the messenger and his brother must be diligent and consistent in calling people to faith and remembrance of God, without becoming lazy or neglectful.

translation: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse commands the messengers to confront Pharaoh, highlighting his excessive arrogance and defiance against God's guidance. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of pride and unjust tyranny when one exceeds the limits set by righteousness.

translation: So speak to him with gentle speech, perhaps he may remember or fear (Allah).
interpretation: This verse instructs us to approach others with kindness and gentleness in our speech, especially when advising or reminding them about important matters. The gentle tone increases the likelihood that the person will be receptive, reflect upon the message, and develop a consciousness of Allah, leading to positive change or repentance.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we fear that he might harm us or become tyrannical."
interpretation: This verse reflects the sincere concern and fear of the sons of Prophet Jacob (Ya'qub) regarding their brother Joseph (Yusuf). They were apprehensive that Joseph might either act unjustly towards them or overpower them through tyranny. This illustrates human nature's vigilance against potential injustice even among close relations, and underscores the importance of expressing one's fears and seeking God's help and protection in such matters.

translation: He said, "Do not be afraid; indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see."
interpretation: This verse highlights the assurance and support offered by a divine or authoritative presence, emphasizing that one should not succumb to fear because they are not alone; the One who hears and sees all is with them, providing protection and confidence in facing challenges.

translation: So they came to him while saying, "Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord. So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and peace will be upon whoever follows the guidance."
interpretation: This verse highlights the mission of divine messengers who advocate for mercy and deliver a message of guidance. It emphasizes the importance of obeying God's commands, refraining from unjust punishment, and following the path of righteousness. The greeting of peace to those who follow guidance reflects the spiritual reward and tranquility granted to believers who adhere to divine direction.

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon those who deny and turn away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes a divine warning that those who reject the truth and deliberately avoid or reject guidance will face the consequences of their actions, highlighting the cause-and-effect relationship between denial and punishment in the hereafter.

translation: He said, "Then who is your Lord, O Moses?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the questioning of Moses about the true nature and identity of his Lord, prompting a deeper reflection on the source of divine authority and power. It invites believers to contemplate the ultimate source of guidance and sovereignty, distinguishing the true Lord from any false deities or idols.

translation: He said, "Our Lord is the One who gave everything its creation and then guided it."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and guidance of all creation, highlighting that not only does God create every being with its unique form and nature, but He also provides the guidance necessary for it to fulfill its purpose. It reflects the continuous relationship between the Creator and creation, where creation is not left aimless but is led towards its intended path by God's wisdom and knowledge.

translation: So what is the matter with the former generations?
interpretation: This verse prompts reflection on the fate of previous communities who were sent divine guidance but ultimately rejected it, leading to their downfall. It serves as a warning that dismissing the message or acting unjustly can result in consequences, urging the listeners to learn from history and adhere to the path of righteousness.

translation: He said, 'Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute knowledge and perfect memory of Allah. It teaches that all knowledge is preserved eternally in the Divine record, and unlike humans, Allah does not make mistakes or forget. Thus, believers can trust in the accuracy and reliability of divine knowledge and decrees.

translation: He who made the earth a cradle for you and made paths for you therein, and sent down water from the sky, with which We brought forth pairs of diverse plants.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's merciful provision and the signs of His creative power in the natural world. It reminds us that the earth is prepared as a nurturing and livable place, with pathways to facilitate travel and communication, and that the rain sent from the heavens sustains life by producing diverse plants in pairs, demonstrating the balance and order established by Allah. This serves as a reminder of human dependence on divine sustenance and the blessings embedded in the environment.

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock, for in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse advises moderation and care in utilizing the blessings provided by Allah, such as livestock. It encourages people to use resources responsibly, not overindulging or causing harm, recognizing that such prudence and gratitude are signs of true wisdom and insight into divine guidance.

translation: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth once again.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cycle of human life and death, underscoring that the earth is both the place of our origin and our ultimate return after death. Furthermore, it highlights the resurrection wherein humans will be brought forth again from the earth for judgment, affirming the reality of life after death and accountability in the hereafter.

translation: And indeed, We showed him all Our signs, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality of human free will and the consequences of stubborn denial. It shows that even when clear and numerous signs from God are presented, some individuals may still choose to reject them out of arrogance or obstinacy, thereby distancing themselves from guidance and truth.

translation: He said, "Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the suspicion and resistance faced by Prophet Moses from the people who doubted his mission and attributed his message and miracles to sorcery, highlighting the initial rejection by those who preferred the status quo over divine guidance.

translation: Then We will bring to you a magic like it, so appoint a meeting between us and you that we may meet, not violating the appointment, and neither you nor we will be late.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a challenge posed to Prophet Muhammad by disbelievers demanding a miraculous demonstration as proof of the divine origin of the Qur'an. The request for a meeting at a specified time underscores their desire to test and compare, but it also emphasizes a failure to recognize that the Qur'an's truth and miraculous nature are beyond magical imitation, highlighting the contrast between human tricks and divine revelation.

translation: Your appointment is on the Day of Display, and when the people will be gathered in the forenoon.
interpretation: This verse refers to the inevitable Day of Judgment, described here as a ‘Day of Display’ when all people will be assembled openly and unmistakably. It highlights the certainty and fixed timing of this event, serving as a reminder of accountability and the comprehensive gathering of humanity for final reckoning.

translation: Then Pharaoh turned away, gathered his forces, and then came forth.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Pharaoh's reaction to opposition, highlighting his arrogance and determination to confront and suppress those who challenge his authority. It symbolizes how tyrannical leaders often consolidate power to resist truth and maintain their dominion.

translation: Moses said to them, "Woe to you! Do not fabricate lies against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment; and he who fabricates lies will surely fail.
interpretation: This verse warns against attributing falsehoods to Allah, emphasizing that such deceit leads to Divine punishment and ultimate failure. It highlights the seriousness of lying about God's words or commandments, underscoring the principle of truthfulness and the consequences of misguiding others through false claims.

translation: But they disputed their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to engage in secretive disputes when confronted with matters of great importance or crisis. It reflects how people may retreat into private counsel, motivated by fear, uncertainty, or strategy, rather than open consultation, which can lead to division and weaken collective resolve.

translation: They said, "Indeed, these two are magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and change your best way."
interpretation: This verse highlights the suspicion and hostility that the people directed towards the messengers when they perceived their message as a threat to their established way of life. It reflects how the introduction of divine guidance can be met with accusations and rejection from those who fear losing their social or cultural dominance.

translation: So collect your plan and come forward in ranks; and he who overcomes today will be successful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of confrontation where the adversaries are urged to unite their efforts and face each other directly. The outcome hinges on those who strive with unwavering determination and righteousness, signaling that true success belongs to those who prevail through sincere effort and God's support.

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw first or we will be the first to throw."
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge posed by Pharaoh's sorcerers to Prophet Moses, expressing their readiness to confront his signs by demonstrating their own magic first, highlighting the tension between divine miracles and human deception.

translation: He said, "Throw them down!" So when they had thrown them down, behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him by their magic as if they were moving.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how the magicians' illusions, empowered by their deceptive sorcery, can create a bewildering appearance of motion and life in inanimate objects. It emphasizes that what may seem magical or supernatural can often be a trick or deception, warning believers against being misled by such lies and encouraging reliance on true divine power rather than illusions.

translation: So Musa felt a fear in himself.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human aspect of Prophet Musa (Moses), showing that despite being a chosen messenger of God, he experienced moments of doubt and apprehension. It teaches that even those entrusted with great responsibilities may face fear, but this feeling does not diminish their faith or mission.

translation: We said, "Do not fear; indeed, you are the supreme."
interpretation: This verse conveys reassurance and empowerment, affirming that the individual addressed possesses a status of honor and elevation, encouraging them to overcome fear by recognizing their inherent worth and higher rank bestowed by God.

translation: And cast what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have forged. Indeed, they have made a plot like that of a magician, but the magician will never succeed wherever he comes.
interpretation: This verse assures that truth and divine support will prevail over deception and falsehood. The 'casting of what is in your right hand' symbolizes reliance on sincere faith and divine power, which will inevitably expose and nullify the tricks and schemes of those who oppose the truth, likened here to the futile efforts of a magician who cannot achieve real success.

translation: Then the magicians prostrated themselves, saying, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a profound moment of recognition and submission where the magicians, initially opposed to Moses due to their reliance on magic, acknowledge the truth of his prophethood and the supremacy of God's power. Their prostration and declaration of faith signal a transformation from disbelief to belief, highlighting that when confronted with undeniable divine truth, even those entrenched in falsehood may embrace faith and submit sincerely to God.

translation: He said, "Did you believe him before I gave you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is severer in punishment and more enduring."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the firmness and authority of the speaker in dealing with those who promote falsehood and lead others astray through harmful knowledge, such as magic. It emphasizes the consequences of aligning oneself with misleading influences and the need for decisive actions to deter such harmful practices in society.

translation: They said, "We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and over He who created us; so judge between us, [if you should] judge." Indeed, you are only [able to] judge this worldly life.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle that truthful and clear evidence, as well as the natural disposition ingrained by the Creator, should take precedence over personal preferences or biases. It reminds that earthly judgments are limited to this worldly life and do not encompass the ultimate, divine justice that will be established beyond this world.

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us to do of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincere belief and repentance of those who were forced into wrongdoing against their will. It emphasizes that true faith includes seeking Allah's forgiveness for any wrongs committed, even under compulsion, and recognizing that Allah's mercy and permanence surpass worldly struggles and trials.

translation: Indeed, he who comes to his Lord as a criminal – for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe and eternal punishment awaiting those who stand before God burdened by their sinful actions without repentance. It emphasizes the absoluteness of divine justice, where such individuals are condemned to remain in Hell eternally, highlighting the gravity of approaching God as a wrongdoer unrepentant.

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds—those will have the highest degrees (in status).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true acceptance by God is rooted in both faith and righteous actions; achieving the highest ranks in the hereafter is contingent upon a sincere belief coupled with consistent good deeds, illustrating the inseparable link between inner faith and outward practice in attaining spiritual elevation.

translation: Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is the reward for those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal reward awaiting the righteous who purify their souls and lead virtuous lives. The imagery of gardens with flowing rivers symbolizes peace, abundance, and eternal bliss in the afterlife, reinforcing the principle that spiritual cleanliness and moral integrity lead to divine favor and everlasting happiness.

translation: And indeed We inspired Moses, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued."
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's guidance to Moses to lead the Israelites through the sea by a secure path, assuring them not to fear nor be apprehensive. It reflects divine protection and the importance of trusting God's plan even in seemingly perilous situations, emphasizing reliance on divine support in times of trial.

translation: But Pharaoh followed them with his soldiers, and the sea covered them, overwhelming them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine rescue of the believers and the destruction of the oppressors, emphasizing that no human power can stand against the will of God. It serves as a reminder that injustice and tyranny will ultimately be overcome, and that faith in God's guidance leads to deliverance.

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the corrupt leadership of Pharaoh, emphasizing his deliberate misguidance of his people. It serves as a warning against following leaders who deviate from the truth and lead others away from guidance and righteousness.

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We promised you the right side of Mount Sinai, and sent down upon you manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's favor and mercy towards the Children of Israel, reminding them of His salvation from their enemies and the divine provisions He granted. It serves as a reminder of the covenant and blessings bestowed upon them, encouraging gratitude and obedience to God's commands.

translation: Eat of the good things which We have provided for you, and do not transgress therein, lest My wrath descend upon you; and he upon whom My wrath descends is truly ruined.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and moderation in enjoying the blessings that God has granted. It teaches that while consuming what is lawful and good from God's provisions is encouraged, one must not exceed bounds or act arrogantly and unjustly, as such transgression invites divine displeasure and leads to spiritual downfall.

translation: And indeed, I am Forgiving to those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds, and then are guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's encompassing mercy and readiness to forgive those who sincerely turn back to Him. It highlights the importance of repentance combined with faith and righteous actions, culminating in guidance—a continuous process where one remains steadfast on the path of truth after returning from error.

translation: And what has hastened you from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of concern and questioning directed at Moses, highlighting the urgency and unexpectedness of his departure from his people. It emphasizes the importance of timely action and the consequences that arise when one leaves their community prematurely, perhaps indicating the gravity of the mission Moses undertook and the emotional or practical impact of his departure.

translation: He said, "They are upon my wealth, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You may be pleased."
interpretation: This verse reflects the speaker's acknowledgment that others have authority over their possessions or estate, yet the speaker turns to God swiftly, seeking divine approval and contentment despite earthly losses, highlighting reliance on God's satisfaction above worldly matters.

translation: He said, "Indeed, we found your people to be misguided after you, and indeed, the Samiri led them astray."
interpretation: This verse highlights how, after the departure of a guiding prophet, the community fell into error and misguidance, with the Samiri as a key figure who diverted them from the right path. It illustrates the vulnerability of people to deviation without steadfast leadership and the influence of individuals who promote falsehood.

translation: Then Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make a good promise to you? Did the covenant seem to you to be too difficult, or did you wish that the wrath of your Lord would descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the frustration and sorrow of Prophet Moses when his people failed to uphold their commitment to God. It illustrates how human beings can become negligent or impatient despite receiving promises of mercy and help from God. The verse serves as a reminder of the seriousness of breaking one's covenant with God and the consequences of provoking divine wrath through disobedience.

translation: They said, "We did not betray your trust regarding the calf, but we were burdened with the ornaments of the people, so we threw them down, and thus did the Samaritan toss them."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the attempt of the people to shift blame for their wrongdoing onto an external agent—'the Samaritan'—in order to absolve themselves of responsibility. It reflects a common tendency among humans to deny accountability for their errors by attributing fault to others, highlighting the importance of personal responsibility and repentance before God.

translation: So he made for them a calf, having a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses," but he forgot.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to forsake true guidance and fabricate idols when faced with uncertainty or impatience. It highlights how even those who have witnessed divine signs can succumb to forgetfulness and idol worship, emphasizing the importance of steadfast faith and remembrance of God's commandments.

translation: Do they not see that there is no word that will benefit them or harm them after it reaches Him, nor do they possess any power?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and finality of God's decree. Once a matter has come before Him, no human word or action can alter its outcome or influence His decision. It serves as a reminder of human powerlessness in the face of divine will and that ultimate control and knowledge belong solely to God.

translation: And indeed, Harun had said to them before, "O my people, you are only being tested through him. And indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of Harun (Aaron) as a guiding figure who warns his people against being led astray by a person causing mischief. It emphasizes the importance of discernment during trials, obeying true guidance, and recognizing the mercy of God as the ultimate source of guidance and salvation.

translation: They said, "We will not depart from it, ever, until Moses returns to us."
interpretation: This verse shows the persistence and determination of the people to remain steadfast in their worship and devotion to the place or the matter at hand until the promised leader, Moses, returns to guide them. It emphasizes the importance of patience and unwavering faith during times of waiting and uncertainty.

translation: He said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of a leader to act decisively when witnessing error or corruption among their people. It calls attention to the necessity of confronting wrongdoing and not remaining passive in the face of misguidance, especially when one holds a position of authority and influence.

translation: Will you not follow? Have I perhaps commanded you unjustly?
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's appeal to his people, emphasizing that his guidance is just and rightful. It calls attention to the importance of following guidance that is rooted in fairness and divine instruction, reminding us not to reject the truth out of stubbornness or misunderstanding.

translation: He said, "O son of Umm, do not take my beard or my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You have split the Children of Israel, and did not observe my word.'"
interpretation: This verse highlights the care taken by the Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) in his dealings, particularly in communication. It reflects the importance of words and actions that do not cause division among people, especially among the Children of Israel. The verse teaches us to be mindful of how our behavior and speech can affect social unity and warns against causing unnecessary discord through rash actions or harsh words.

translation: He said, "Then what is your matter, O Samiri?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Prophet Moses questions Samiri about his actions. The inquiry emphasizes personal accountability and the importance of staying true to God's commands, as Samiri's act led to misguidance for the people. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of deviating from divine guidance and the necessity of sincere obedience.

translation: He said, "I have seen what they have not seen, so I seized a handful from the trace of the Messenger and threw it. Thus my soul suggested to me."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of self-deception and regret, highlighting how personal desires can lead one to reject truth or meaningful spiritual experiences. The speaker acknowledges acting on a misguided impulse prompted by his own nafs (inner self), emphasizing the internal struggle between following divine guidance and succumbing to selfish inclinations.

translation: He said, "Then go, for you have in life the power to say 'No touch' (a barrier). And indeed, you have an appointment you will not fail to keep. And look at your god to whom you have been devoted, Îlâ (Idol) — We will burn it and then scatter it into the sea utterly."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the assertion of God's ultimate power over false deities and obstacles that people may place between themselves and the Divine. The expression "you have in life the power to say 'No touch'" indicates the control over worldly life and affairs but also emphasizes that the ultimate appointment (death and judgment) cannot be avoided. The resolve to destroy the false god shows the futility of worshipping anything besides the One True God, emphasizing that idols are powerless and perishable compared to the divine authority and the inevitable outcome decreed by God.

translation: Indeed, your God is Allah, there is no deity except Him. He encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive oneness of Allah as the sole deity worthy of worship, highlighting His unique status above all gods. It also declares His omniscience, indicating that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing, extending to every aspect of creation, leaving nothing beyond His awareness. This serves to remind believers of Allah's supreme authority and complete understanding of all affairs.

translation: Thus We relate to you, [O Muhammad], some of the news of what has passed before. And We have given you from Us a message.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a recipient of divine revelation, through which previous histories and lessons are conveyed to guide humanity. It underscores the continuity of God's message through time and the special status of the Prophet as the one entrusted with conveying God's final reminder to mankind.

translation: Whoever turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability that every individual will face on the Day of Judgment for ignoring or rejecting the message of guidance. Turning away from the divine admonition does not simply erase responsibility; rather, it results in carrying a heavy burden, symbolizing the consequences of neglecting or rejecting God's commands.

translation: They will abide therein forever, and evil indeed is that for which they are burdened on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment for those who reject faith and commit wrongdoing, highlighting that the burden they carry on the Day of Judgment is exceedingly grievous and inescapable.

translation: The Day when the trumpet will be blown, and We will gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse vividly describes the moment of the Resurrection when the horn (the trumpet) will be blown, signaling the commencement of the Day of Judgment. The gathering of the wrongdoers is emphasized, portraying their disgrace and the severity of their imminent accountability. The term 'blue-eyed' metaphorically conveys their distress and embarrassment, highlighting the stark contrast between the fate of the guilty and the righteous on that Day.

translation: They whisper among themselves, "If you remained [here], it would only be ten [of you]."
interpretation: This verse reflects the secretive and plotting nature of some individuals who doubt the endurance or resilience of others in a situation, implying that only a small number would persist. It highlights human tendencies toward distrust and the lack of faith in collective strength, reminding believers to maintain steadfastness and unity despite the doubts and conspiracies of others.

translation: Indeed, We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them say, "You will not remain except a day."
interpretation: This verse highlights that God is fully aware of the words and doubts of disbelievers, even when their strongest claim is that the Prophet's stay or punishment will be only brief; it emphasizes God's comprehensive knowledge of both spoken challenges and the hidden intentions behind them, underscoring that their skepticism does not escape divine awareness and that God's plans transcend their limited understanding.

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast."
interpretation: This verse signifies the impermanence of seemingly unmovable and permanent creations like mountains, illustrating the absolute power of God to obliterate even the mightiest of natural formations. It serves as a reminder of God's authority over all creation and the ultimate transformation that will occur on the Day of Judgment, where worldly structures and symbols of strength will be completely dismantled.

translation: So He leaves it as a plain, white land.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformation of a once fertile and cultivated land into a barren and desolate plain, symbolizing the consequences of neglect or divine punishment, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly life and blessings.

translation: Therein you will see no crookedness nor any deformity.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and purity of Paradise, indicating that everything within it is flawless and harmonious, free from any form of imperfection or distortion, symbolizing the ultimate state of peace and beauty granted to the righteous.

translation: On that Day, they will follow the Caller without any deviation, and the voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment when all humankind will follow the divine summons without hesitation or error. The imagery of voices subdued to whispers signifies the overwhelming awe and deep humility before God's majesty, reflecting the profound recognition of His authority and mercy at that moment.

translation: On that Day, no intercession will avail except for those for whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose word He approves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, intercession will have no power except by the permission of Allah, the Most Merciful. It highlights that ultimate authority rests with God alone, and only those whom He allows can intercede, underscoring His absolute control over mercy and justice in the hereafter.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they do not encompass it in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing knowledge of God, affirming that He is fully aware of everything—past, present, and future—beyond human comprehension. It serves as a reminder of human limitations in understanding the divine wisdom and unseen realities, encouraging humility and trust in God's omniscience.

translation: And the faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer. And he who has carried injustice will surely fail.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the humbling of all beings before the eternal and self-sustaining God, emphasizing His supreme authority and power. It also serves as a warning that those who commit injustice and bear its burden will ultimately face failure and loss, reinforcing the principle that oppression cannot prevail in the sight of divine justice.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith accompanied by righteous actions brings a profound sense of security and trust in God's justice. Such a person need not fear any form of wrongdoing or loss because divine justice ensures that their good deeds are recognized and rewarded, and no unfairness will befall them in the ultimate reckoning.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and diverted therein [from the warnings] that perhaps they might fear [Allah] or it would cause them to remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deliberate choice of Arabic as the language of the Qur'an to ensure clarity and understanding. It also indicates that warnings and reminders are purposefully included in the text to awaken Taqwa (God-consciousness) in people or to serve as a reminder that stirs reflection and spiritual awakening.

translation: So exalted is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth; and do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of patience and reverence in receiving divine revelation. It emphasizes that knowledge, especially sacred knowledge, unfolds according to God's wisdom and timing, and rushing through understanding can lead to misconceptions. The supplication for increased knowledge highlights the believer's humble dependence on God for guidance and deeper insight.

translation: And indeed, We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him firm resolve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human propensity to forget divine guidance despite earlier commitments, emphasizing the importance of perseverance and strength of will in adhering to God's commands. It teaches that forgetting or slipping is part of human nature, but true steadfastness lies in sincere effort to remain resolute and return to the path after lapses.

translation: And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except for Iblis; he refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obedience of the angels to God's command and the defiance of Iblis due to his arrogance and pride. It underscores the importance of humility before God's will and serves as a warning against arrogance, which leads to disobedience and loss of God's grace.

translation: And We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife; so let him not expel you from Paradise so you would suffer.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of Satan as an adversary to human beings, emphasizing the importance of vigilance against his temptations to preserve one's state of blessing and avoid the hardship that comes from being removed from a state of grace and nearness to God.

translation: Indeed, you will not hunger therein nor will you be unclothed.
interpretation: This verse promises a state of complete provision and security, indicating that in the hereafter or in the favored abode, the believer will be free from basic needs and vulnerabilities such as hunger and exposure, symbolizing ultimate comfort, dignity, and divine care.

translation: And therein you shall neither suffer thirst nor scorching heat.
interpretation: This verse describes the blessings of Paradise, emphasizing a state of perfect comfort and relief where inhabitants will not experience any form of physical suffering such as thirst or extreme heat, symbolizing the ultimate pleasure and ease granted by Allah to the believers.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him, saying, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not deteriorate?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive nature of Satan, who tempts Adam by promising him eternal life and an everlasting kingdom, highlighting the danger of succumbing to alluring but false promises that divert one from obedience to God.

translation: So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to sew together leaves from Paradise to cover themselves. But Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when Adam and his wife became aware of their nakedness after eating the forbidden fruit, symbolizing the loss of their initial innocence. Their attempt to cover themselves reflects human awareness of sin and shame. Adam's disobedience and subsequent error signify the beginning of human accountability and the need for guidance and repentance, highlighting that falling into error is part of the human condition, but it also opens the path to seeking forgiveness and spiritual growth.

translation: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy and grace of Allah in selecting an individual, forgiving their past mistakes, and providing them with guidance. It emphasizes that divine selection is accompanied by compassion and the opportunity for transformative guidance, signifying that no one is beyond the reach of Allah's forgiveness and the potential to be rightly guided.

translation: He said, "Descend, all of you, from it. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when humanity is sent to Earth, emphasizing that while they may become adversaries to each other, guidance from God remains available to direct them. Following divine guidance safeguards a person from misguidance and hardship, signifying the essential role of God's guidance in navigating the challenges and potential enmities of worldly life.

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will raise him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual consequences of neglecting God's guidance and remembrance. Turning away from divine wisdom leads to a life filled with hardship and inner emptiness, and ultimately spiritual blindness on the Day of Judgment, symbolizing a loss of insight and understanding in the hereafter.

translation: He said, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound regret and sorrow of a person who has been denied the blessings they once had due to their own misdeeds or disobedience. It illustrates the consequences of one’s actions and the justice of God, who withholds favor as a response to persistent wrongdoing or neglecting His commandments.

translation: Thus Our verses came to you, but you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of neglecting and forgetting the signs and guidance of God.
