It emphasizes the importance of maintaining dignity and peace by avoiding needless contention with foolishness, focusing instead on one's own righteous conduct.

translation: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance is ultimately granted by Allah alone and is not subject to human desire or preference. Even if one loves someone and wishes for their guidance, it is only Allah's will and knowledge that determine who is rightly guided. This underscores the concept of divine wisdom and sovereignty in guiding human hearts to the truth.

translation: And they said, "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be driven out from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance and fear of certain people towards accepting divine guidance, fearing loss of their worldly possessions and status. Yet, it reminds them of the blessings and security that God has already provided, emphasizing that true guidance is accompanied by provision and safety, even if they fail to recognize it. The verse admonishes the ignorance of those who prefer to cling to their material attachments at the cost of forsaking the path of righteousness.

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed that was excessive in its living; those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except a little, and We (were) the inheritors thereof.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of a community's moral and spiritual corruption leading to their destruction. It serves as a warning that indulging excessively and neglecting righteousness results in loss that endures beyond the immediate destruction, and ultimately, Allah inherits and controls all things after such events.

translation: And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine punishment or destruction is not arbitrary but is a consequence of persistent wrongdoing and injustice. Allah ensures that before any community faces destruction, they are given clear guidance through messengers who convey His signs, providing an opportunity to amend their ways. Thus, the verse underscores Allah's justice and mercy, highlighting that destruction occurs only after people have chosen to persist in their wrongful conduct despite receiving guidance.

translation: And whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment. And what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then use reason?
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the possessions and pleasures we experience in this life are temporary and ultimately insignificant compared to the eternal rewards and blessings that Allah has prepared. It encourages us to reflect and prioritize the hereafter over fleeting worldly gains, urging the intellect to recognize the superiority of spiritual and everlasting success.

translation: Is then one who has promised Us a good promise [of reward] and will meet it, like one to whom We have given enjoyment of worldly life, and then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those presented [for punishment]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the true believers who sincerely strive for the promised reward from Allah and will ultimately attain it, and those who are merely given worldly pleasures but fail to prepare for the Hereafter, culminating in their regret and punishment on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, 'Where are My partners, those whom you used to claim?'.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that those false deities or entities that people wrongly worshipped alongside Allah will be absent and unable to intercede or assist, emphasizing the oneness of Allah and the error of polytheism.

translation: Those upon whom the word will come true said, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray; indeed, we led them astray just as we were astray. We declare our disassociation from them; indeed, they did not worship us."
interpretation: This verse reflects the accountability of devils who admit their role in misleading certain people, but also clarify that those misguided individuals did not truly worship the devils themselves. It underscores that misguidance is a mutual consequence between devils and humans' choices, and ultimately the responsibility rests on human free will and worship directed appropriately to God alone.

translation: And it was said, "Call upon your 'partners' (gods) whom you claimed," but they called upon them, and they did not respond to them. And they saw the punishment. If only they had been guided!
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of invoking false gods or partners alongside Allah. It illustrates that these so-called deities neither hear prayers nor provide any help, emphasizing the importance of pure monotheism and the guidance that comes from recognizing Allah alone as the true deity. It also serves as a warning that ignoring this reality leads to inevitable punishment due to misguidance.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will call them and say, "What was the response you gave to the messengers?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of every individual on the Day of Judgment regarding their response to the divine messages conveyed by the prophets. It signifies that people cannot deny or escape the question of how they listened, understood, and acted upon the guidance brought by the messengers, underscoring the importance of sincere obedience and acknowledgment of the truth revealed through them.

translation: So on that Day, the news will be concealed from them, and they will not ask any questions.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severity of the Day of Judgment, highlighting that people will be so overwhelmed and spiritually blinded that they will be unable or unwilling to inquire or seek explanations about their fate, emphasizing the finality and seriousness of that day.

translation: As for the one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, it is possible that he will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of sincere repentance combined with faith and virtuous actions. It reassures that no matter one's past, turning back to God sincerely, affirming belief, and engaging in good deeds can lead to true success in both this life and the hereafter.

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; there is no choice for them. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah in creation and choice, affirming that human beings have no real say in matters of divine selection or destiny. It highlights that Allah's will is supreme and perfect, and that any form of association or partnership with Him is baseless and exalted beyond human understanding or imitation.

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of the innermost feelings and thoughts of individuals, including what they hide in their hearts and what they outwardly express. It serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from God, and therefore, one should be sincere and conscious of His awareness in all actions and intentions.

translation: And He is Allah, there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs all praise in the first and the last. And His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah, emphasizing that He alone deserves all praise and possesses ultimate authority over all creation. It reminds us that all human affairs culminate in His judgment, and ultimately, every soul will return to Him for accountability, underscoring the transient nature of worldly life and the permanence of divine authority.

translation: Say, "Have you considered if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique power and authority of Allah as the sole source of light and guidance, highlighting the futility of worshiping any deity other than Him. It invites reflection on the natural world as evidence of Allah's exclusive ability to control and alter the conditions of existence, prompting recognition of His singular divinity.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"
interpretation: This verse calls attention to the dependency of human beings on Allah for the cycle of day and night, highlighting that no other deity or power can replace His role. It urges reflection on the divine provision of light and darkness as signs of Allah's sovereignty and asks humans to recognize and appreciate this divine control rather than turning to false gods.

translation: And out of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek from His bounty, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy manifested in the alternation of night and day, providing humans with periods of rest and activity. The design encourages balance in life—night for rest and rejuvenation, day for labor and seeking sustenance—thus establishing a framework for appreciating divine blessings through gratitude.

translation: And [mention] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah (shirk). On the Day of Judgment, those false deities or partners that people claimed will be powerless and absent, unable to assist or defend. It underscores the absolute oneness of Allah and serves as a reminder that reliance should be placed solely on Him, as all fabricated deities have no real existence or authority.

translation: And We raised up a witness from every nation. Then We said, "Bring your proof," and they knew that the truth belonged to Allah, while what they used to invent deserted them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle that among every community, God has appointed a witness or a messenger to bear testimony to the truth. When called upon to produce evidence for their claims, the truth becomes unmistakably clear and is recognized as belonging solely to Allah. Meanwhile, the falsehoods and fabrications previously propagated by people fall away, revealing the inherent clarity and inevitability of divine truth.

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he behaved arrogantly toward them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men. When his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of arrogance and pride stemming from worldly wealth. Qarun's abundant riches led him to become prideful and oppressive despite being part of the community of Prophet Moses. The key lesson is that possessing great wealth should not lead one to arrogance or disregard for others, as such pride is disliked by God. True contentment comes from humility and gratitude rather than boastfulness.

translation: And seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and do not forget your share of the world; and do good as Allah has done good to you; and do not seek corruption in the land; indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the balance between striving for success in the Hereafter while responsibly managing one's worldly life. It teaches that one should use the blessings given by Allah not only to prepare for the eternal life after death but also to enjoy and improve their worldly existence without excess or wrongdoing. Furthermore, it instructs kindness and goodness towards others modeled on the benevolence of Allah, urging believers to avoid causing harm or corruption in society because such behavior is detested by God. Essentially, it calls for ethical stewardship of both the temporal and eternal aspects of life.

translation: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed generations before him who were mightier in strength and more in number? And the criminals are not asked about their sins.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and ignorance of those who boast about their power or knowledge, forgetting that Allah's punishment has previously befallen people who were stronger and more numerous. It serves as a reminder that worldly might does not guarantee protection from divine accountability, and that those who commit sins will inevitably be held responsible.

translation: Then he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, "Oh, that we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is the possessor of great fortune."
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of those who admire and covet worldly wealth and status, symbolized by Qarun's display of riches. It highlights how people's desire for material gains can lead them to envy and prioritize temporal success over spiritual values, overlooking the moral and ethical responsibilities that come with wealth.

translation: And those who have been given knowledge say, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds; and none will be granted it except the patient."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true knowledge recognizes the ultimate value of Allah's reward over worldly gains. It teaches that sincere faith combined with righteous actions leads to the best reward, which is only attainable by those who exercise patience and perseverance through trials.

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, and he had no group to help him other than Allah, nor was he of the victorious.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of arrogance and defiance against divine commandments, highlighting that without the support of God, any worldly alliances or strength are futile and lead to ultimate defeat and destruction.

translation: And those who wished to [have] his place yesterday said, "Indeed, Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it]. If not that Allah had conferred favor upon us, He would have caused us to be swallowed up [by the earth] or a severe punishment. Indeed, it is not for the disbelievers to succeed."
interpretation: This verse reflects the shifting attitudes of people when their circumstances change, highlighting the reality that provision and success are ultimately determined by Allah's will and decree. It cautions against envy and reliance on worldly status, reminding that divine favor protects believers and that true success is reserved for those who have faith.

translation: That [Garden of Paradise]—We will assign it to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true success in the Hereafter is bestowed upon those who live humbly and avoid arrogance or causing harm and corruption in the world, underscoring that godliness and fear of God lead to eternal rewards and ultimate triumph.

translation: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it; and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except for what he used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and mercy, assuring that good deeds are rewarded manifold, while evil deeds are only punished to the extent of their commission, underscoring God's fairness in judgment and encouraging believers to strive for good while warning against wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to the Resurrection. Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance and who is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that the One who revealed the Qur'an is fully capable of resurrecting humanity for final accountability. It emphasizes that ultimate knowledge of who is rightly guided and who is evidently misguided rests with God alone, underscoring the necessity of trusting His judgment and the truth of the message delivered through the Qur'an.

translation: And you did not expect that the Book would be conveyed to you except as a mercy from your Lord. So be not an advocate for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad was an act of divine mercy intended to guide humanity. It warns against siding with those who reject this guidance, urging steadfastness in faith and caution against supporting disbelief.

translation: And do not let them avert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And call to your Lord, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in conveying God's revelations without being swayed by opposition or distractions. It encourages sincere devotion to calling others towards monotheism and warns against associating partners with God, affirming the purity and exclusivity of worship due to Him alone.

translation: And do not invoke with Allah any other deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah, asserting that no other deity is to be worshiped alongside Him. It reminds us that all creation is transient and will ultimately perish, but Allah's existence is eternal. The verse underscores that ultimate authority and judgement belong solely to Allah, and all beings will return to Him for accountability, highlighting the importance of sincere monotheism and preparing for the hereafter.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: This opening declares the beginning of the Qur'an with the invocation of Allah's name, emphasizing His mercy and compassion. The letters 'Alif, Lam, Meem' are among the mysterious 'disjointed letters' whose precise meaning is known only to Allah, serving as a reminder of the divine origin and miraculous nature of the Qur'an.

translation: Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried?
interpretation: This verse highlights that professing faith is not the end of a believer's journey; rather, true faith is proven through trials and challenges. Believers will inevitably face tests to strengthen, purify, and affirm their conviction, ensuring their faith is genuine and resilient.

translation: And indeed We tried those before them, so Allah may know those who are truthful and He may know the liars.
interpretation: This verse signifies that trials and tests are a divinely ordained means to distinguish between sincerity and falsehood in faith. Difficulties serve as a way for God to reveal the true character and steadfastness of individuals, separating the genuine believers from those who merely claim belief without sincere commitment.

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? Evil is the judgment they make.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who commit sins should not be deluded into believing that they can evade divine justice or outpace God's reckoning. Their assumption is a grave error, reflecting arrogance and misunderstanding of God's ultimate authority and wisdom in judgment.

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah—indeed, the appointed time of Allah will surely come. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of meeting Allah, reassuring the believer that no matter how distant or uncertain the appointment seems, it is unquestionably decreed by Allah. It serves as a reminder that patience and steadfastness in faith are essential, as the promise of Allah's encounter is guaranteed and His knowledge encompasses all things, which instills hope and accountability in the believer.

translation: And whoever strives, only strives for [the benefit of] himself. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle that every individual's efforts and struggles are ultimately for their own benefit; one does not harm others through their striving, but works for their own spiritual and moral growth. Moreover, it asserts that Allah is independent and self-sufficient, not needing humanity's efforts or worship, highlighting that our striving is for our own sake, not to add anything to Allah's perfection.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and justice of Allah in forgiving the sins of those who sincerely believe and engage in righteous actions. It highlights that faith combined with good deeds leads to the cleansing of past errors and to a reward that surpasses their efforts, affirming the transformative power of sincere belief and continuous virtuous conduct.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount importance of honoring and treating one's parents with kindness and respect. However, it establishes a clear boundary: if they urge one to engage in idolatry or associating partners with God—actions contrary to divine guidance—obedience to them should be set aside. Ultimately, accountability before God is supreme, and human relationships cannot justify disobedience to divine commands.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the connection between faith and righteous actions, affirming that true belief is manifested through good deeds, and assures the believers that their efforts will be rewarded by being included among the righteous in the hereafter.

translation: Among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. And if there comes to him a victory from your Lord, he will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity of some who claim faith outwardly but lack true conviction. When faced with hardship for Allah's cause, they attribute the difficulty to divine punishment instead of seeing it as a test, revealing their weak faith. However, when victory comes, they quickly join the believers to claim association. This verse teaches us that genuine faith is tested through perseverance during trials, and that only Allah truly knows the sincerity within people's hearts.

translation: So that Allah may make evident those who believe and that He may make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse highlights that trials and events are means through which Allah reveals the true nature of individuals' faith, distinguishing genuine believers from those who only outwardly profess belief but inwardly harbor hypocrisy.

translation: And those who disbelieve said to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins." But they will not bear anything of their sins; indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of disbelievers proposing their path to the believers under the false pretense of sharing their burdens. It emphasizes that misguidance and disbelief cannot alleviate the consequences of one's own sins, and those who suggest otherwise are deceitful and dishonest in their claims.

translation: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens along with their own burdens; and they will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense accountability on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that individuals will not only bear the consequences of their own sins and falsehoods but also carry the burden of additional wrongdoings, possibly including those they encouraged or propagated. It serves as a stern warning against fabricating lies and misguiding others, as such actions increase one's responsibility before God.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years; then the flood took them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the patience and perseverance of the Prophet Noah in guiding his people towards righteousness over many centuries, despite their persistent rejection and wrongdoing. It also warns of the inevitable consequences of persistent injustice and disbelief, exemplified by the flood that befell them.

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship and made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy of Allah in saving Prophet Noah and the believers with him from the great flood, demonstrating His power over creation. The event is presented not just as a historical incident but as a lasting sign for all peoples, reminding them of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of heeding divine guidance.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him; that is best for you, if you should know."
interpretation: This verse highlights Prophet Abraham's call to his people to worship the One true God and to be conscious of Him. It emphasizes that true benefit and safety lie in monotheistic belief and God-consciousness (taqwa). The phrase "if you should know" invites reflection, implying that this guidance is not arbitrary but comes from wisdom and knowledge, encouraging people to recognize what is truly best for them beyond their customary practices.

translation: You worship besides Allah mere idols and invent falsehood; indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess provision for you. So seek provision from Allah and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, emphasizing that idols or deities besides Him have no power to provide sustenance or benefit. It calls attention to the importance of recognizing Allah as the sole provider and sustainer, urging believers to place their trust and reliance on Him alone. The verse also reminds us that all gratitude and worship should be directed to Allah, as ultimately, everyone will return to Him for judgment and accountability.

translation: And if you deny, then other peoples before you have denied; and the Messenger's duty is only to convey [the message] clearly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that rejection or denial of the message is not a new phenomenon; previous communities have also rejected their prophets. It serves to reassure the Messenger that his responsibility is solely to deliver the message transparently and clearly, regardless of whether it is accepted or rejected. The ultimate accountability lies with those who choose to reject guidance, while the messenger remains a faithful conveyor of the divine truth.

translation: Have they not considered how Allah begins creation and then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and ability to create life initially and then resurrect it after death. It serves as a reminder that resurrection is not beyond divine capability, reinforcing the belief in life after death and the accountability that comes with it.

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the origin and progression of creation as evidence of Allah's power and wisdom. By observing the natural world and its beginnings, we recognize the deliberate and precise unfolding of existence, which assures us of the reality of resurrection and the final re-creation that Allah will bring about. It emphasizes that Allah's ability to create initially implies His ability to resurrect and recreate, pointing to His absolute dominion over all things.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills. And to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and authority over all matters of punishment and mercy. It reminds us that Allah's decisions are based on His perfect wisdom and justice, and that ultimately, all people will return to Him to be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: And you are not able to cause failure [to Allah's plan] in the earth or in the heaven, and you will have no protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute inability of any being—no matter how powerful—to thwart the divine will of Allah either on earth or in the heavens. It underscores the futility of relying on anyone other than Allah, affirming that ultimate protection and assistance belong solely to Him.

translation: And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in the meeting with Him—those, they have despaired of My mercy; and those will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that rejecting Allah's clear signs and denying the reality of meeting Him leads to losing hope in His mercy. Such despair signifies a hardened heart turning away from guidance, thereby deserving severe consequences. It serves as a solemn reminder of the grave spiritual peril in rejecting divine truth and the importance of maintaining faith with hope in Allah's mercy.

translation: But the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him." However, Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the steadfastness and faithfulness of a prophet in the face of extreme opposition and threat from his own people. It emphasizes Allah's power to protect His servants and deliver them from harm, reinforcing the idea that true belief is accompanied by trust in God's protection and justice, even in the most dire circumstances.

translation: And he said, "You have only taken idols besides Allah to show affection between yourselves in the worldly life, but on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others and curse them. Your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and destructive consequences of idol worship, emphasizing that those idols serve only to create superficial bonds among people in this life. However, on the Day of Judgment, these false ties collapse, leading to mutual rejection and enmity among idolaters themselves. It underscores that reliance on anything other than Allah leads ultimately to ruin and that such attachments offer no real salvation or support in the hereafter.

translation: So Lot believed in him. He said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse highlights Prophet Lot's firm faith and trust in God's plan, demonstrating his resolve to leave behind a corrupt society and seek refuge and guidance from God alone, acknowledging God's omnipotence and wisdom as the foundation of his decision.

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob and placed prophecy and the Scripture among his descendants. And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is among the righteous in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's blessings upon the prophet Abraham and his progeny by granting them distinguished status through prophethood and divine revelation. It signifies that righteous lineage is honored not only by worldly rewards but more importantly by spiritual elevation and ultimate success in the Hereafter.

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave immorality of the people to whom Prophet Lot was sent. Their actions were so egregious and unprecedented that even the entire world before them had not engaged in such behavior. It serves as a strong condemnation of their conduct and a warning about the consequences of persistent sin and disobedience to divine guidance.

translation: Do you approach men with desire instead of women? Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the condemnation of approaching men with sexual desire, which was considered a deviation from the natural order established by God. The response of the people, challenging the prophet to bring God's punishment if he is truthful, reflects the rejection and defiance of truth by those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: He said, "My Lord, help me against the corrupt people."
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine assistance in facing adversity, emphasizing reliance on God's support to overcome wrongdoing and maintain justice amidst corruption.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city, for its people have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice in addressing the corruption and wrongdoing within a community. It serves as a reminder that persistent injustice and oppression among people lead to consequences decreed by God, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and moral conduct in society.

translation: He said, "Indeed, there is Lot in it." They said, "We are most knowing of who is with him. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is to be of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine protection and mercy towards Prophet Lot and his righteous family, while also signifying that not everyone close to the prophet shares the same faith or is saved; specifically, his wife is excluded due to her disbelief or opposition. It emphasizes that salvation is granted based on faith and trust in God’s guidance, rather than mere familial relations.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt helpless, and said, "This is a trying day." They said, "Do not fear or grieve; indeed, We will save you and your family except your wife; she is of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the compassion and warning given to Prophet Lot regarding the impending punishment for his people due to their immorality. Despite his distress, the messengers assure him of Allah's protection for him and his family, highlighting that divine mercy extends to the righteous even in times of great calamity, but those who choose to persist in wrongdoing, like Lot's wife, will face consequences.

translation: Indeed, We sent down upon the people of this city a punishment from the heaven because they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of persistent wrongdoing and rebellion against divine commands; it serves as a warning that continual immoral actions can lead to severe punishment decreed by God, emphasizing His justice and the importance of adhering to righteousness.

translation: And indeed, We have left therein a clear sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has placed unmistakable signs within His creation and revelation, which serve as evidence of His existence and power, meant to be understood and appreciated by those who use their intellect and reflect deeply.

translation: And to Madian [We sent] their brother Shu`ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And expect the Last Day, and do not cause corruption in the land."
interpretation: This verse highlights the message delivered by the Prophet Shu'ayb to his people of Midian, emphasizing the importance of monotheism, belief in the Hereafter, and moral responsibility. His call against causing corruption in the land teaches that true faith must translate into ethical behavior, preserving social justice and harmony rather than spreading injustice and disorder.

translation: But they denied it, so a seizure took them, and they woke up in their home prostrating.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of rejecting divine truth: those who deny God's signs are overtaken by sudden calamity or punishment, symbolized by the seizure and their humbled state in their own homes, emphasizing the inevitable accountability and the power of divine retribution.

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and there have certainly come to you clear indications from their dwellings. And Satan had made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the way, while they were trying to be guided.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how despite clear signs and guidance being evident, the people of 'Aad and Thamud allowed themselves to be misled by Satan, who made their wrongful actions seem attractive. This highlights the danger of self-deception and the importance of sincerely adhering to truth, as external signs alone do not ensure guidance if one's heart is swayed by falsehood and arrogance.

translation: And Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman; indeed, Moses brought them clear proofs, but they were arrogant on the earth, and they were not the first among those who did wrong.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent arrogance and denial of clear guidance by powerful figures despite receiving unequivocal signs from Moses. It underscores that such prideful rejection is a recurrent human failing, not unique to them, and warns against the consequences of haughtiness and rejecting divine truth.

translation: But each one We seized for his sin; among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the blast, and among them were those whom the earth swallowed up, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that every people who deviated and committed sins were punished accordingly, but these punishments were not unjust impositions from Allah; rather, they were the inevitable consequences of their own wrongdoing and transgressions. It highlights the principle that divine justice is fair and that individuals bear responsibility for their actions, and that their suffering stems from their own choices, not from injustice by Allah.

translation: The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and fragility of relying on false deities or protectors instead of Allah. Just as the spider's web is delicate and easily destroyed, so too is the protection sought from anyone other than Allah weak and unreliable. It serves as a reminder of the importance of placing trust solely in Allah, the true and ultimate protector.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows what they call upon besides Him, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the false deities or entities that people may invoke or worship apart from Him. Despite their devotion or invocation of these other objects or beings, Allah's knowledge surpasses all, affirming His ultimate authority, power, and wisdom. It also serves as a reminder that reliance on anything other than Allah is misplaced, as He alone possesses the capacity to respond and govern with justice and wisdom.

translation: And these examples We present to the people, but only those who have knowledge understand them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the parables and lessons in the Qur'an are presented for all to hear, but true comprehension and deep insight are granted only to those endowed with knowledge and understanding. It highlights the importance of learning and reflection in grasping the wisdom contained within divine revelation.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens and the earth was a purposeful and truthful act of Allah, serving as a profound sign for those who have faith. It calls the believers to recognize the deliberate design and wisdom behind existence, reinforcing their conviction and trust in Allah's power and plan.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of prayer and the recitation of the divine revelation. It teaches that sincere worship and remembrance of Allah serve as a means to protect and guide believers away from immoral and evil behaviors, reinforcing spiritual discipline and consciousness of God's awareness in all actions.

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them. And say, "We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respectful and gentle dialogue when discussing religious matters with the People of the Scripture, advocating for an approach based on kindness and wisdom rather than harshness or hostility. It acknowledges the common ground shared in faith — the belief in the same God and the legitimacy of divine revelation — urging unity and mutual respect while cautioning against engaging with those who are unjust or hostile in such debates.

translation: And thus We have sent down to you the Book; and those to whom We have given the Book believe in it, and among these are those who believe in it; but none deny Our signs except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin of the Quran and the sincere belief it inspires among the People of the Book, emphasizing that true faith involves accepting the guidance bestowed through revelation. The refusal to acknowledge God's signs is characteristic solely of those who reject faith outright, underscoring a clear demarcation between believers and disbelievers based on their response to divine revelation.

translation: And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. In that case, the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an by highlighting that Prophet Muhammad neither read from previously revealed scriptures nor wrote it down himself. The implication is that the Qur'an's profound content and eloquence could not have originated from human sources, and if it had, skeptics would have found inconsistencies or reasons to doubt its authenticity. Thus, it underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, affirming its truth and the impossibility of its fabrication by the Prophet.

translation: But it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge; and none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the truths and signs of God are deeply ingrained and manifest clearly in the hearts of those who possess true knowledge and understanding. It points to the idea that rejecting God's signs is not born out of ignorance but stems from injustice and wrongdoing within a person. Thus, faith and comprehension are intertwined, and denial is an act of oppression against oneself and divine wisdom.

translation: And they say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, the signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the roles of Allah and the Prophet. While people demand extraordinary signs or miracles as proof, the verse clarifies that such signs are ultimately controlled by Allah alone. The Prophet's role is to warn and convey the message clearly, not to produce signs on his own. This serves to emphasize reliance on faith and trust in Allah's wisdom rather than demanding physical proof from prophets.

translation: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran, being a clear and divine revelation recited to humanity, is sufficient as guidance and mercy. It implies that the message within the Book should be enough to guide believers and soften hearts, warning against seeking additional signs or arguments beyond what has already been provided through the Quran, highlighting its completeness and significance as a source of mercy and remembrance for those who have faith.

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah - those are the losers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge and testimony are ultimate and complete, transcending human judgment. It highlights the consequences of embracing falsehood and rejecting the truth of Allah, declaring that such denial leads to true loss and failure, not only in this life but in the hereafter.

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. But if it were not for a predetermined term, the punishment would surely come to them. Then it will come to them suddenly while they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine punishment is not arbitrary or immediate but occurs according to a fixed, predetermined time known only to God. The impatience of disbelievers requesting swift punishment does not alter God's plan. The suddenness of the punishment serves as a reminder that human beings must remain conscious of their deeds and the accountability that awaits them, rather than expecting immediate retribution.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment, but indeed Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and inescapable nature of divine punishment for those who reject faith. It highlights that God's judgment will come at its appointed time, and no one should be misled into thinking it will be delayed or avoided. The imagery of Hell encompassing the disbelievers underscores the certainty of consequence for their persistent denial and wrongdoing.

translation: On the Day when the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and it will be said, 'Taste what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the comprehensive and inescapable nature of divine punishment for those who have committed wrongdoing. The imagery of punishment engulfing from above and beneath signifies that no place will be safe from the consequences of one's actions, emphasizing the certainty and severity of accountability in the hereafter. It serves as a stern warning to take earthly deeds seriously, as their repercussions will be fully experienced.

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and generosity of God's creation as more than sufficient to provide for all. It serves as a reminder that despite the abundance and opportunities available in the world, true fulfillment and success come from dedicating worship and obedience solely to God, highlighting the importance of sincere monotheism.

translation: Every soul will taste death; then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitability of death for all beings, emphasizing that life is transient and that ultimately, everyone will return to God for judgment. It serves as a call to live righteously, mindful of our ultimate accountability and the eternal life that follows this temporary worldly existence.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely assign to them Paradise rooms beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and generosity of God's reward for believers who combine faith with righteous actions. It signifies that true faith is reflected in consistent good deeds, and such individuals will be honored with eternal bliss in Paradise, illustrating the inseparability of belief and action in achieving divine reward.

translation: Those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience combined with reliance on Allah. It teaches that steadfastness in the face of difficulties, while entrusting one's affairs to God, is a sign of true faith and leads to inner strength and eventual success.

translation: And how many a creature carries not its own provision. Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of Allah's absolute control and mercy in providing sustenance to all living beings, irrespective of their efforts or ability to carry out their provision. It teaches reliance on Allah's wisdom and care, and encourages trust in His knowledge and hearing of our needs, emphasizing that provision is ultimately from Him alone, not dependent solely on our means or endeavors.

translation: And if you were to ask them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency in the beliefs of some people who acknowledge Allah as the Creator when questioned, yet fail to truly submit to Him or recognize His sovereignty in their lives. It points to a disconnect between intellectual acknowledgment and genuine faith or action, emphasizing that mere verbal affirmation without sincere belief and obedience leads to misguidance.

translation: Allah extends provision to whom He wills among His servants and restricts it for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights that sustenance and provision are ultimately under the control and wisdom of Allah alone. It reminds us that wealth and livelihood are not solely dependent on human effort, but on divine decree, reflecting Allah's comprehensive knowledge and wisdom in distributing resources in a way that serves a greater purpose beyond our understanding.

translation: And if you ask them, "Who sends down water from the sky and revives the earth after its death?" they will surely say, "Allah." Say, "All praise is due to Allah." But most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental acknowledgment of God's power over nature, specifically His control over life-giving rain and the revival of barren land. Despite this clear evidence of divine authority, many people fail to reflect deeply or appreciate the wisdom behind these signs, showing a lack of true understanding or contemplation.

translation: And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter is the real life, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the temporary pleasures and distractions of this worldly life are insignificant compared to the eternal and true life of the Hereafter. It serves as a warning that those who are engrossed in the fleeting enjoyments may fail to recognize the importance of preparing for the everlasting life to come.

translation: Then when they boarded the ship, they supplicated Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivered them to the land, behold, they associated others with Him (began to commit shirk).
interpretation: This verse highlights human nature's tendency to turn to God sincerely in moments of distress or need but to lapse into forgetfulness and associating partners with Him when their situation improves. It serves as a reminder that true faith requires consistent sincerity and devotion, not conditional worship based solely on hardship.

translation: So that they disbelieve in what We have given them and may enjoy themselves; but they will know (the consequence).
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine wisdom behind allowing people to indulge in worldly pleasures and reject guidance temporarily. It serves as a warning that such enjoyment without regard for truth and righteousness is transient, and ultimately, they will come to realize the reality and consequence of their disbelief and actions.

translation: Have they not seen that We made the Sacred House a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away all around them? Then in falsehood do they believe and deny the favor of Allah?
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and security established by Allah around the Sacred House (the Kaaba), emphasizing that despite this divine protection, people continue to be attacked and harmed elsewhere. It draws attention to the irony of their faith: they trust in unfounded beliefs yet reject the clear blessings and protection granted by Allah. The interpretation underscores the contrast between misguided faith and the rejection of divine grace, urging reflection on true belief and gratitude.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of falsely attributing lies to Allah or rejecting the clear truth after it has been presented. Such actions represent extreme injustice and arrogance, as they deny the divine guidance meant for humanity's benefit. The verse warns that such rejection leads to a just consequence: eternal punishment in Hell for those who persist in disbelief and deceit.

translation: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sincere effort and struggle in the cause of Allah are met with divine guidance. When a person dedicates themselves earnestly to the path of righteousness and seeking Allah's pleasure, Allah facilitates their journey by illuminating the right path and supporting them internally and externally. Moreover, Allah's presence and support accompany those who perform good deeds genuinely, reinforcing the principle that perseverance in striving for goodness leads to spiritual success and divine companionship.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These opening words emphasize that the Quran is revealed by Allah, who is characterized by mercy and compassion. The letters 'Alif, Lam, Meem' are among the mysterious Arabic letters that appear at the beginning of some chapters in the Quran, serving as a divine sign that invites reflection on the miraculous nature of the Quran's language and message.

translation: The Romans have been defeated.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges a moment of apparent defeat for the Romans, highlighting the ebb and flow of worldly events. It serves as a reminder that apparent setbacks are part of a larger divine plan, and that ultimate success and restoration may follow adversity.

translation: They will be at the lowest point of the earth, and after their defeat, they will surely be victorious.
interpretation: This verse conveys the cycle of triumph and defeat that nations or groups experience over time; even though a people may be humbled or defeated temporarily, there is a divine promise and natural course through which they will regain strength and overcome their adversaries in the future.

translation: In a few years; to Allah belongs the command before and after. And on that Day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and ultimate control of Allah over all matters across time, reminding believers that His authority is eternal and encompasses everything. It serves to comfort the faithful by assuring them that despite any trials or uncertainties they face in the present or future, their trust in Allah's plan will lead to joy and triumph on the Day of Judgment.

translation: By the help of Allah; He helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all victory comes solely by the help of Allah, who grants support to whomever He chooses according to His wisdom and mercy. It reminds believers that success is not merely a result of human effort but is ultimately dependent on divine assistance, reflecting Allah's power and compassion.

translation: Allah's promise — Allah will not fail in His promise; but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty and trustworthiness of Allah's promises. It reassures believers that whatever Allah has promised will inevitably come to pass, reflecting His perfect knowledge and power. The statement also reflects on human ignorance, as many people fail to recognize or understand this divine certainty, leading to doubt or mistrust in God's decrees.

translation: They know the apparent things of the worldly life, but they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to be preoccupied with worldly matters, focusing only on what is visible and immediate, while neglecting the eternal and unseen realities of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to maintain awareness of the ultimate purpose of life and the consequences beyond this transient existence.

translation: Have they not considered themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for an appointed term. And indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the purpose of creation and human existence. It emphasizes that the universe and life have been created deliberately and with truth, pointing towards an ultimate accountability. The recognition of an appointed time and the reality of meeting the Lord underscores the importance of faith and preparation for the hereafter, reminding that denial of this meeting leads to disbelief and misguidance.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were mightier than them in strength and they left the earth more inhabited than it is now. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah would never wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the fates of past nations who were physically stronger and more prosperous yet faced destruction due to their rejection of divine guidance and injustice. It highlights that any ruin or punishment they endured was not due to God's injustice but was a consequence of their own oppressive actions and refusal to heed the messengers. The lesson stresses the importance of humility, accountability, and heeding divine warnings to avoid repeating the mistakes of those who came before us.

translation: Then the outcome of those who did evil was that they denied the signs of Allah and mocked them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of wrongdoing, where those who commit evil not only reject the divine signs but also ridicule them, indicating a spiritual blindness that leads to their downfall and serves as a warning against arrogance and disbelief.

translation: Allah begins creation; then He repeats it; then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power as the Creator and Sustainer of life. It reminds us that life and death are under His control, and after He initiates creation, He has the authority to recreate or resurrect. Ultimately, all beings will return to Him for judgment, highlighting the inevitability of accountability and the transient nature of worldly existence.

translation: And the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound despair that will overwhelm wrongdoers when the Hour (the Day of Judgment) arrives, signifying a moment of ultimate accountability where their misdeeds are exposed and no escape or remedy is possible.

translation: And they had no intercessors with their partners, and they were disbelievers in their partners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) will find that their supposed partners cannot intercede for them on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the futility of relying on other than Allah and indicates that actual belief requires recognizing Allah's sole authority and rejecting all forms of polytheism.

translation: And the Day the Hour will be established, that Day they will become separated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and severity of the Day of Judgment, when all people will be divided according to their deeds and ultimate destiny, emphasizing the reality of accountability and the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, delighted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who combine faith with righteous actions. It indicates that true belief is not just a matter of inner conviction but is proven through good deeds. The 'garden' symbolizes paradise, a place of eternal happiness and peace. The word 'delighted' suggests not just physical comfort but a profound spiritual joy and satisfaction. Thus, the verse serves as an encouragement for believers to maintain their faith and engage in righteous behavior, promising them a blissful recompense.

translation: As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice for those who reject God's revelations and deny the existence of life after death. It underlines the accountability and consequences awaiting those who persist in disbelief and falsehood, affirming that their punishment is certain and imminent in the Hereafter.

translation: So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistently remembering and glorifying Allah throughout the different times of the day, signifying that worship and mindfulness of God should be a continuous practice, transcending specific moments and encompassing the rhythms of daily life.

translation: And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the evening and when you rise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the continuous and all-encompassing nature of praise due to God. It highlights that God's praise is not confined to any place or time but extends throughout the entire universe—both the heavens and the earth—as well as during all times of the day, signifying His eternal and unchanging sovereignty and the obligation on believers to remember and praise Him constantly.

translation: He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death. Likewise, you will be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power over life and death, illustrating His control over natural processes as a sign of the resurrection to come. Just as life emerges from non-life and vice versa, and barren earth is revived after death, so too will human beings be resurrected after death, affirming the certainty of the Hereafter.

translation: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are humans who spread far and wide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and origin of human beings, reminding us that despite our vast numbers and worldly achievements, we all come from the same humble beginning—dust. It serves to foster humility and unity among people, emphasizing that all humans share a common origin and are part of a divine plan.

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the creation of human companionship. It emphasizes that the relationships between spouses are not merely social constructs but are signs of God's design to provide comfort, emotional support, and harmony. The affection and mercy between partners are manifestations of divine mercy, encouraging believers to contemplate the profound purpose behind human bonds and to recognize God's presence in the intimacy and mutual care that spouses share.

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your tongues and colors. Indeed in that are signs for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity and variety in creation — in the vastness of the universe as well as in humanity’s differences in language and appearance — as clear evidence of the existence and power of the Creator. Such diversity is not random but purposeful, encouraging reflection on the wisdom and unity behind this multiplicity, which serves as guidance for all people to recognize the oneness of God and the interconnectedness of His creation.

translation: And of His signs is your sleep by night and day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural, daily experiences of human beings—sleep and striving for sustenance—as clear signs of God's power and mercy. It calls on those who reflect and listen attentively to recognize that these routine aspects of life are manifestations of divine wisdom and blessings, encouraging gratefulness and awareness of God's ongoing care and provision.

translation: And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, inspiring both fear and hope, and sends down water from the sky, by which He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and mercy of God, seen through natural phenomena like lightning and rain. It invites reflection on how these events evoke emotional responses—fear of His might and hope in His benevolence—and demonstrate His ability to bring life to barren land. The deeper lesson is that such signs should inspire thoughtful contemplation about God's existence, control over nature, and the reality of resurrection.

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a call from the earth, you will come forth.
interpretation: This verse indicates God's absolute power and control over the entire universe, emphasizing that the heavens and the earth exist and function solely by His command. The latter part refers to the Day of Resurrection, when God will call forth all creatures from the earth for judgment. It serves as a reminder of the inevitability of accountability and the reality of life after death, urging believers to heed God's call and prepare for that day.

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every being in the universe, whether in the heavens or on the earth, is under the dominion and authority of Allah. It signifies that all creations, whether angels, humans, or jinn, are in a state of submission and obedience to Allah's will, reflecting His absolute sovereignty and the inherent order within creation.

translation: And He it is who begins creation and then repeats it, and it is easier for Him; and to Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and the earth; and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme power and wisdom in creating and restoring life effortlessly, highlighting His unmatched status and authority above all creation both in the heavens and on earth.

translation: We have set forth a parable for you from among yourselves: Do you have partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear one another? Thus do We explain the signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the injustice and illogical nature of associating partners with Allah in the provision and sustenance He grants us. It invites us to reflect on the absurdity of fearing or revering others as we fear or revere ourselves regarding provision, highlighting that such belief is baseless. The verse encourages understanding through reason that all sustenance ultimately belongs to Allah alone, and therefore, attributing partners to Him contradicts the fundamental truth of divine sovereignty and provision.

translation: But those who have wronged followed their desires without knowledge. So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray? And they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of forsaking divine guidance in favor of following one's own desires without knowledge. It emphasizes that such misguided choices remove the possibility of genuine guidance from Allah, leading to a state of being led astray with no support or helpers to assist in returning to the straight path.

translation: So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah (natural disposition) of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse urges the believer to steadfastly adhere to the pure and natural religion established by Allah, reflecting the innate disposition with which all humans are created. It emphasizes that divine creation and inherent inclination towards truth are unalterable, highlighting that true guidance is found in maintaining this original, uncorrupted faith despite widespread ignorance or deviation.

translation: Turning to Him in repentance and fear Him, and establish prayer, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance and consciousness of God, urging believers to maintain regular prayer as a means to strengthen their connection with the Divine, and to avoid associating partners with God, which undermines the essence of pure monotheism.

translation: Among the people are those who divide their religion into sects, each faction rejoicing in what they have.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to split into groups based on their own interpretations and beliefs, often leading to division, with each group feeling content or even proud of their own distinct identity, which can hinder unity and mutual understanding.

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He bestows upon him a mercy from Himself, a portion of them associate others with their Lord,
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the human tendency towards inconsistency in faith: in times of distress, people sincerely call upon God seeking help, yet upon relief, some return to associating partners with Him, showing ingratitude and neglecting true monotheism.

translation: So that they disbelieve in what We have given them; enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject or turn away from the divine guidance and blessings bestowed upon them. It warns that their temporary enjoyment or indulgence is futile because they will ultimately face the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that true knowledge and justice rest with God, and denial of His gifts leads to inevitable accountability.

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority who speaks to them by Our command?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no messenger or divine authority has been sent to justify or advocate for the false beliefs or practices of polytheism. Rather, any legitimate authority sent by God speaks only by His command, upholding monotheism and truth, and not the fabrications or associations made by people in their worship.

translation: And when We give people a taste of mercy, they rejoice therein; but if an evil befalls them because of what their own hands have sent before [them], then indeed, they despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be grateful and hopeful when experiencing blessings and mercy from God, yet quick to lose hope and fall into despair when faced with trials or consequences of their own actions. It serves as a reminder that gratitude and patience should be maintained consistently, regardless of circumstances, and that negative outcomes often stem from one's own deeds, emphasizing the importance of self-accountability and sustained trust in divine wisdom.

translation: Do they not see that Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the divine wisdom behind sustenance and provision; it teaches that wealth and livelihood are ultimately controlled by Allah's will, emphasizing reliance on Him rather than solely on human effort, and serves as a sign to strengthen the faith of believers by reminding them that sustenance is a manifestation of God's power and mercy.

translation: So give the relative his due, and the poor, and the traveler; that is best for those who seek the Face of Allah, and those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling our responsibilities towards our close relatives, the needy, and travelers, highlighting that true success lies in seeking God's pleasure through acts of generosity and kindness. It teaches that righteousness is demonstrated not merely through belief, but through tangible care for others, especially those in vulnerable situations.

translation: And whatever you give for usury to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah; but whatever you give in charity, desiring the pleasure of Allah - those are the multipliers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that wealth acquired through usury, which is gained by exploiting others, holds no real value or increase in the sight of Allah. In contrast, wealth given sincerely in charity for Allah's pleasure is spiritually multiplied and truly rewarded. It emphasizes the superiority of sincere charity over unjust gains and encourages believers to seek divine reward through generosity rather than through unjust enrichment.

translation: Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, and then gives you life again. Is there any among your partners who can do any of that? Glory be to Him and Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and unparalleled power of Allah in the entire cycle of human existence—from creation to provision, death, and resurrection. It illustrates His unique authority over life and death, underscoring that none of the so-called partners or idols can claim even a fraction of this capability. The verse serves as a reminder that associating partners with Allah is baseless and unjustified, affirming His singular sovereignty over all aspects of life and death.

translation: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste some of what they have done, so perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of human actions impacting the natural world and society, emphasizing that the corruption and damage we see are results of our own deeds. It serves as a warning that experiencing the negative outcomes of one's actions may provoke reflection and repentance, encouraging a return to ethical and righteous conduct.

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before [us]. Most of them were polytheists."
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the history of past nations who engaged in disbelief and idolatry, reminding us that their end was ruinous. It serves as a warning that turning away from monotheism and moral guidance leads to destruction, emphasizing the importance of learning from previous generations' mistakes to avoid similar consequences.

translation: So set your face toward the religion, upright, before there comes the Day from Allah which cannot be turned away. On that day, they will break apart.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and sincerity in following the true religion, urging believers to dedicate themselves wholeheartedly to a righteous path before the inevitable Day of Judgment arrives, a day from which there is no escape. It serves as a solemn reminder that worldly distractions should not divert one from preparing spiritually for accountability, as the consequences then will be profound and irreversible.

translation: Whoever disbelieves, upon him is [the consequence of] his disbelief; and whoever does righteous deeds - for themselves they prepare [a good provision].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. Disbelief leads to its inherent consequences, while performing righteous deeds benefits the doer by preparing a positive outcome or reward in the hereafter. It highlights the principle that each person is accountable for their faith and actions, and that good deeds serve as an investment for one's own well-being and success beyond this life.
