interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reality that the clear signs and revelations from Allah have already been presented to the individual, yet they chose denial out of pride and arrogance. It highlights that disbelief is not born out of ignorance but is a deliberate rejection fueled by arrogance, leading one away from faith despite the evident truth.

translation: And [on] the Day of Resurrection, you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences awaiting those who falsely attribute lies to Allah, emphasizing that their deceit leads to spiritual darkness symbolized by blackened faces. It underscores the ultimate accountability on the Day of Judgment and indicates that Hell is the rightful abode for the prideful and those who reject truth out of arrogance.

translation: And Allah saves those who fear Him by their salvation; no harm shall touch them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine protection granted to those who have Taqwa (God-consciousness or piety). Their trust and fear of Allah act as a shield, safeguarding them from harm and sorrow. It conveys the assurance that sincere faith and mindfulness of God lead to true security and peace, both in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that Allah is the origin and maker of everything in existence, highlighting His absolute authority and control over the universe. It establishes the understanding that nothing occurs without His will, and He manages all affairs meticulously, underscoring the importance of placing trust in Him alone as the ultimate guardian and sustainer.

translation: He has the keys of the heavens and the earth. Those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah—they are the losers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah alone possesses ultimate authority and control over all creation, symbolized by the keys to the heavens and the earth, and that rejecting His signs and revelations leads to true loss—both in this worldly life and in the hereafter.

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the folly of idol worship by highlighting the irrationality in venerating anything or anyone besides Allah, urging people to recognize the oneness and supremacy of God and to abandon ignorance in matters of worship.

translation: And indeed, it has been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you were to associate others with Allah, your deeds would certainly become null and you would certainly be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the foundational principle of Islamic monotheism, warning that associating partners with Allah (shirk) nullifies all deeds regardless of their apparent goodness, leading to spiritual ruin and loss in the Hereafter. It underscores that sincerity in worship and exclusive devotion to Allah are essential for the acceptance of one's actions.

translation: But Allah, so worship Him and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse calls for exclusive devotion to Allah alone, emphasizing the importance of sincere worship and gratitude. It reminds us that recognizing Allah's sovereignty and favor necessitates that we express our thankfulness through dedicated worship and obedience, reflecting a heart that acknowledges His blessings and is committed to Him alone.

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and incomprehensible power of Allah, indicating that human beings have failed to truly grasp or appreciate His greatness. It serves as a reminder of Allah's ultimate authority over all creation, especially on the Day of Resurrection when everything will be under His control, and underscores the futility of associating partners with Him, as He is transcendent and beyond all likeness.

translation: And the trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse signifies the resurrection moment when all creation will be struck down by the divine command, indicating the absolute power of Allah to determine life and death. The second blowing of the trumpet awakens all beings to stand and witness the unfolding of the hereafter, emphasizing the certainty and immediacy of resurrection and judgment.

translation: And the earth shone with the light of its Lord, and the Book was placed, and the prophets and the witnesses were brought, and judgment was passed among them in truth, and they were not wronged.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate establishment of divine justice and truth at the end of times, when the fullness of God's guidance illuminates the world; all matters are settled fairly with the presence of prophets and witnesses, ensuring that no soul suffers injustice.

translation: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it did; and He is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of God in rewarding or punishing every individual according to their deeds. It assures that no action, good or bad, escapes His knowledge, and everyone will receive their due recompense fairly on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And those who disbelieve will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse reflects on the inevitability and justice of divine punishment for those who rejected the message of God despite receiving clear warnings through His messengers. It underscores that disbelief and deliberate rejection lead to a predetermined consequence, illustrating God's fulfillment of His word and the certainty of accountability on the Day of Judgment.

translation: It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein; and wretched is the residence of the arrogant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe punishment awaiting those who exhibit arrogance and pride at the expense of humility and submission to God. It serves as a warning that arrogance leads to eternal disgrace and condemnation, emphasizing the importance of humility as a virtue to attain God's mercy.

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say, 'Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute serenity and honor granted to the righteous at the gates of Paradise, emphasizing that their constant consciousness and fear of God throughout their lives have purified them, and thus they are welcomed with peace and assured eternal residence in the hereafter.

translation: And they said, 'Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the earth, that we may dwell in Paradise wherever we wish.' And excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound gratitude and satisfaction of the believers who recognize the fulfillment of Allah's promise to them. It signifies that faithfulness and steadfastness in righteous deeds lead to divine reward, granting them not only success in this worldly life but also eternal bliss in Paradise. Their inheritance of the earth symbolizes spiritual and moral victory, affirming that true success is achieved by those who trust in Allah and act accordingly.

translation: And you see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praises of their Lord. And judgment is passed between them with truth, and it is said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the majesty and justice of Allah's dominion, emphasizing that not only are the angels in constant worship and glorification of Him, but also that all decisions and judgments in the divine realm are executed with absolute truth and fairness. The proclamation of praise to the Lord of the worlds underscores the universality of His sovereignty and the perfect order maintained in creation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: This verse consists of the basmala, an invocation seeking the mercy and grace of Allah before beginning, and the mysterious letters 'Ḥā Mīm', which serve as a unique marker for the chapter and remind the reader of the divine origin of the Quran, prompting reflection on the miraculous nature of the revelation beyond human capacity.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran is a divine revelation bestowed by Allah, who is both All-Powerful and All-Knowing. It asserts the authority and authenticity of the scripture, highlighting that its origin is from the Almighty who possesses complete knowledge and control over all matters.

translation: Forgiving of sin, acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, owner of abundance. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the balance in Allah's nature between His mercy and His justice. He readily forgives and accepts those who sincerely repent, highlighting His compassion and readiness to pardon. At the same time, He is stern in punishment for those who persist in wrongdoing, underscoring the accountability humans have for their actions. Ultimately, since there is no deity but Him, all people inevitably return to Him for judgment, reminding believers to live conscientiously and seek forgiveness.

translation: Only those who disbelieve dispute concerning the signs of Allah, so do not be deceived by their movements throughout the land.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that those who deny God's revelations will persist in their opposition and may appear influential or active across various regions. However, such outward activity should not mislead believers into thinking that the disbelievers' cause is strong or will prevail, as true guidance and success lie with those who uphold faith in God's signs.

translation: The people of Noah denied before them, and the confederates after them. Every nation intended to seize their messenger to punish him. They argued falsely and disputed to refute the truth, but they were seized, so how [terrible] was My punishment!
interpretation: This verse illustrates a recurrent theme in the history of mankind: that those who reject and oppose divine messengers do so with arrogance and false arguments, striving to suppress the truth. Despite their efforts, divine justice inevitably prevails, and their punishment becomes a lesson and warning to others. It emphasizes the certainty that rejecting guidance and harming messengers leads to inevitable and severe consequences from God.

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has come to pass against those who disbelieved that they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of divine justice upon those who reject faith, indicating that the consequences of disbelief are clearly established and unalterable, resulting in their fate as dwellers of Hellfire.

translation: Those who carry the Throne and those around it exalt the praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for the believers: "Our Lord, Your mercy encompasses all things, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and save them from the punishment of Hell."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound mercy and knowledge of Allah, whose encompassing mercy invites believers to seek forgiveness earnestly. The glorification and faith of the angels who carry the throne demonstrate the perfection of divine praise and trust, serving as a model for believers to repent sincerely and follow God's path, thereby attaining His mercy and protection from punishment.

translation: Our Lord, admit them to Gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication seeking Allah's mercy and His fulfillment of the promise of Paradise to the believers and their righteous family members. It reflects the comprehensive nature of divine rewards extending beyond individual deeds to encompass the righteousness within a person's close relations, emphasizing the mercy and justice of Allah as both Almighty and Wise.

translation: And He will shield them from the evil of that Day, and will bestow His mercy upon them. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy of Allah as the ultimate protection against the severe hardships of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that being guarded from the consequences of misdeeds and receiving divine mercy is the highest success one can achieve, surpassing all worldly gains.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve are calling out for the hatred of Allah to be greater than your own hatred of yourselves, when you were called to faith but you disbelieved.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intensity of the enmity of disbelievers towards Allah, which surpasses even their own self-hatred. It emphasizes that rejecting faith not only distances one from divine guidance but is also accompanied by a profound internal conflict and self-destructive stance, as their denial of truth is more vehement than any personal grievance they hold.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and to live twice, and we have confessed our sins. So is there any way out?"
interpretation: This verse conveys the depth of human experience through the metaphor of 'dying and living twice,' symbolizing significant hardships and moments of realization. It reflects the acknowledgment of one's sins and the sincere seeking of God's mercy and guidance. The plea 'is there any way out?' illustrates the yearning for forgiveness and a hopeful path to redemption despite past transgressions.

translation: That is because when Allah alone is invoked, you disbelieve, but if associates are invoked with Him, you believe. So the judgment is for Allah, the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency in the attitude of those who reject monotheism when Allah alone is addressed, yet accept faith when others are associated with Him. It serves as a reminder that ultimate judgment belongs solely to Allah, who is exalted and all-powerful, emphasizing the futility of associating partners with Him and underscoring the importance of sincere monotheistic worship.

translation: He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down to you provision from the sky. But only those who turn to Him in sincere repentance take heed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the merciful nature of God, illustrating how He manifests His power and sustenance in the world as signs for humanity. However, the true benefit of these signs is realized only by those who sincerely repent and turn back to God with humility and earnestness, highlighting the importance of heartfelt submission in understanding and appreciating divine guidance.

translation: So invoke Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and purity of devotion towards Allah in one's worship and religious practice. It instructs believers to call upon Allah with wholehearted faith and commitment, regardless of opposition or dislike from those who reject the message. True devotion requires patience and steadfastness even in the face of hostility or rejection by others.

translation: The One exalted in degrees, Owner of the Throne, who sends the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's supreme authority and power, highlighting that He alone determines the bestowal of His spirit, symbolizing divine revelation or inspiration, upon chosen servants. It underscores the purpose of this selection: to deliver warnings and guidance concerning the inevitable Day of Judgment, thus reminding believers of accountability and the ultimate meeting with God.

translation: The Day they will emerge, not a thing concerning them will be hidden from Allah. To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah on the Day of Judgment, highlighting that every individual will be fully exposed and accountable before Him, and that ultimate authority belongs solely to Allah, who is singular and all-powerful.

translation: Today, every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There will be no injustice this Day. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment. Every individual will be held accountable precisely for their deeds, without any oppression or unfairness. It assures that reward or punishment will be meted out based on one's own actions, reflecting the swiftness and certainty of divine judgment.

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the hearts will reach the throats, choking, and the wrongdoers will have no close friend, nor any intercessor who is obeyed.
interpretation: This verse conveys the intense anguish and helplessness on the Day of Judgment, when fear and remorse will choke the hearts of the wrongdoers. It emphasizes that no familiar friend or intercessor will be able to assist them, highlighting the absolute accountability and isolation faced by those who committed injustice.

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the hearts conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, highlighting that nothing escapes His awareness—not only the outward actions and glances that may betray deceit but also the innermost hidden intentions and feelings within the hearts. It reminds us that sincerity and purity in inner thoughts are known to Allah, urging believers to maintain integrity both outwardly and inwardly.

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those whom they invoke besides Him do not judge anything. Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate judgment belongs solely to Allah, who administers justice with absolute truth and fairness. In contrast, the idols or false deities worshiped by people possess no power to judge or influence outcomes. The attributes of Allah being 'Hearing' and 'Seeing' signify His complete awareness of all matters, reinforcing that His judgment is based on full knowledge and perfect justice.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were mightier than them in power and in the traces they left on the earth. But Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the consequences faced by previous nations who were powerful and prominent in the world but were ultimately destroyed due to their sins and disobedience to God. It teaches that worldly strength and achievements do not protect one from divine judgment, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and obedience to God's commandments.

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved; so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse explains that the destruction or punishment of certain peoples occurred because, despite being presented with clear evidence and guidance through their messengers, they chose disbelief and rejection. It emphasizes the consequence of stubborn denial in the face of truth and highlights Allah's might and justice in holding accountable those who persist in rejecting divine guidance.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Moses was sent by God equipped with unmistakable miracles and clear evidence to establish his legitimacy and to guide the Children of Israel. It signifies the divine support given to prophets, confirming that their mission is backed by evident authority and signs to invite people towards faith and righteous guidance.

translation: To Pharaoh and Haman and Qarun, they said, "You are a magician and a liar."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection and hostility faced by the messengers or believers from the powerful figures of their time. It reflects a common reaction to divine truth when it challenges established authority and arrogance—labeling truthful words as magic and lies to discredit and oppose them.

translation: But when the truth from Us came to them, they said, "Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive." And the plot of the disbelievers is not but in error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extremity of the hostility faced by the early believers from their opponents. It reflects the malicious intent to not only physically destroy the believers but also to dismantle their social fabric by targeting their families. The verse underscores the futility and misguided nature of such schemes, as the true outcome of the disbelievers' plots is inevitable misguidance and failure.

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or cause corruption in the land."
interpretation: Pharaoh's statement reflects his fear of losing power and control over his people if Moses succeeds in guiding them towards a new faith and disrupting the established order. This verse illustrates the resistance to divine truth and reform often faced by prophets, where the ruling powers perceive the call to monotheism as a threat to their authority.

translation: And Moses said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and faith in the Hereafter. Moses seeks protection from arrogance, which blinds individuals to the reality and accountability of the Day of Judgment. The verse teaches that true faith requires both recognition of one's limitations before God and acceptance of the eventual reckoning, reminding believers to maintain sincerity and humility in their worship and dealings.

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said, 'Will you kill a man because he says, "My Lord is Allah," while he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? If he is lying, then upon him is his falsehood; but if he is truthful, you will be harmed by some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the courage of a true believer who, despite being surrounded by oppression and disbelief, openly professes the oneness of God, emphasizing the importance of faith and truth over fear of worldly consequences. It highlights the principle that falsehood carries its own burden and that divine guidance cannot reach those who persist in arrogance and deceit, reminding believers to stand firm in their convictions even in hostile environments.

translation: O my people, you have the kingdom today, being prominent on the earth, but who will protect us from the punishment of Allah if it comes to us? Pharaoh said, "I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the way of right conduct."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and delusion of Pharaoh, who, despite his apparent power and control over the land, dismisses the reality and warnings of divine punishment. He falsely claims that his perception is the only truth and that his guidance is the sole path to justice, reflecting how leaders can blind themselves and their people to the truth by relying solely on their authority and limited understanding.

translation: And the one who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you the like of the Day of the Confederates.
interpretation: This verse reflects a believer's deep concern for his people, fearing that they may face a severe trial or punishment similar to the Day of the Confederates (the Battle of the Trench). It serves as a warning against disobedience and rejection of guidance, emphasizing the importance of heeding divine messages to avoid disastrous consequences.

translation: The example of the behavior of the people of Noah, and 'Aad, and Thamud, and those who came after them: Allah does not want to do injustice to His servants.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that the persistent corruption and transgression of past nations, despite repeated warnings, serve as a warning to humanity, and emphasizes that any punishment from God is just and not unjust; it underscores God's fairness and mercy, showing that misguidance and destruction come as a result of people's own choices, not divine oppression.

translation: O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling (Judgment Day).
interpretation: This verse reflects the prophet's deep concern for his community, warning them of the inevitable accountability before God. It emphasizes the seriousness of the Day of Judgment and serves as a reminder that neglecting divine guidance will lead to regret and punishment.

translation: The Day you turn your backs fleeing, there will be no protector from Allah for you. And whoever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of abandoning faith or truth at a critical moment; when one turns away from guidance and seeks to escape accountability, divine protection is withdrawn. It highlights that ultimate guidance and protection come solely from Allah, and if He allows someone to go astray, no one else can guide that person back to the right path.

translation: And indeed, Joseph came to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought to you. Until, when he died, you said, 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.' Thus Allah causes the one who is extravagant in doubt to stray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some individuals to persist in doubt and denial even when clear evidence has been presented to them. The example of Joseph illustrates that despite explicit signs and guidance, people rejected the message. The concluding part teaches that excessive doubt and suspicion lead one away from the straight path, as Allah allows those who indulge in such doubt to become misguided. It serves as a warning against skepticism that obstructs acceptance of truth and divine guidance.

translation: Those who dispute regarding the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—they bear an immense hatred in the sight of Allah and among the believers. Likewise, Allah seals the heart of every arrogant, tyrannical person.
interpretation: This verse highlights the peril of arrogantly challenging divine guidance without valid knowledge or authority. Such behavior breeds hatred both in the eyes of God and the faithful, and results in the hardening of the heart, making one resistant to truth and guidance due to pride and tyranny.

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build me a tower that I might reach the ways—
interpretation: This verse reflects Pharaoh's arrogance and his determination to attain power and reach lofty heights by his own means, disregarding divine authority. It symbolizes human pride and the desire to challenge God's dominion, illustrating the folly of relying solely on material might to achieve ends that are beyond human capacity.

translation: He said, "The knowledge of the heavens; then I will look towards the God of Moses, for indeed, I think him to be a liar." Thus it was made appealing to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the way. And the plot of Pharaoh is only in ruin.
interpretation: This verse reflects the obstinate attitude of Pharaoh who, despite witnessing clear signs and being invited to the truth, chooses to reject and accuse the messenger, Moses, of falsehood. It highlights the spiritual blindness caused by arrogance and the allure of evil actions, which make one deviate from the right path. Ultimately, such rejection and plotting against God's command lead only to self-destruction and failure.

translation: And the one who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct."
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsibility of a true believer to lead others towards guidance and righteousness by example, emphasizing the importance of inviting others to the path of truth with wisdom and sincerity.

translation: O my people, indeed this worldly life is but amusement and diversion, but the Hereafter is the home of permanence.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the temporary pleasures and distractions of this life should not be our ultimate focus, as true and everlasting life lies in the Hereafter. It calls for prioritizing actions and intentions towards what is eternal rather than being consumed by the fleeting nature of worldly enjoyment.

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except by the like thereof; and whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and be given provision therein without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the just nature of Divine recompense, affirming that evil actions are repaid in kind, while righteousness—irrespective of gender and grounded in faith—is rewarded abundantly with entry into Paradise and unmeasured blessings, highlighting God's perfect justice and mercy.

translation: And O my people, what is [the matter] with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Ibrahim's lament over his people's rejection of his guidance. He is bewildered that while he invites them to the path of righteousness and salvation, they instead threaten him with punishment and fire. It highlights the conflict between truth and falsehood, and the pain a sincere messenger feels when his earnest call to guidance is met with hostility.

translation: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that about which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental conflict between truth and falsehood, emphasizing the responsibility to uphold monotheism and avoid attributing to God what one does not know. It underscores the steadfastness in inviting others to sincere worship of the One true God, who is all-powerful and forgiving, despite the pressure or accusations to deviate from that path.

translation: Indeed, what you call me to has no authority either in this world or in the Hereafter, and to Allah is our return, and indeed, the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that false and baseless claims or invitations that contradict divine guidance hold no power or validity in either this life or the afterlife. It underscores the certainty of returning to Allah for judgment, reminding that those who exceed bounds and persist in wrongdoing will inevitably face punishment in the Hereafter, highlighting the ultimate justice of God.

translation: So you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of placing trust in Allah after delivering a message or advice. It reassures that ultimately, Allah is fully aware of our actions and situations, and thus, one should rely on Him with confidence and patience, knowing that He supervises and will judge fairly.

translation: May Allah protect him from the evil of what they plotted; and the family of Pharaoh was afflicted with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah safeguards the righteous from the harm planned by their enemies, illustrating that despite the scheming of oppressors like Pharaoh and his people, divine justice ultimately prevails and they suffer the consequences of their own evil deeds.

translation: They will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening, and on the Day when the Hour is established, the family of Pharaoh will be admitted to the severest punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severity and inevitability of divine justice, emphasizing that those who held oppressive power, like the family of Pharaoh, will face continuous exposure to punishment both in this life and even more so in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of tyranny and disbelief, and the certainty of accountability on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And when they dispute in the Fire, the weak will say to the arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers; then will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and futile hopes of the weak who had followed the arrogant evildoers in their misguidance, expecting some mercy or shared fate. It illustrates the consequence of blindly following those who are arrogant in disbelief, revealing that each individual bears responsibility for their deeds and cannot escape punishment by association.

translation: Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, all within it will perish." Indeed, Allah has decreed the matter concerning His servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the arrogant who dismiss the value and permanence of everything in the world, claiming all within it will perish. It affirms that Allah has ultimate authority and wisdom in judging the affairs of His creation, reminding believers of divine justice and control beyond human arrogance.

translation: And those who are in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, 'Call upon your Lord to lighten for us the punishment for a day.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense suffering of those condemned to Hellfire, highlighting their desperate plea for relief even if only temporarily. It underscores the severity of the punishment in the Hereafter and the power of Allah alone to grant respite, emphasizing human dependency on His mercy and the consequences of one's deeds in this life.

translation: They said, "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They said, "Yes." They said, "Then invoke [for us]." But the invocation of the disbelievers is only in error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection and obstinance of disbelievers despite being presented with clear signs and proofs by their messengers. Their response is not genuine seeking but a challenge, and the verse emphasizes that their prayers or calls not rooted in faith remain in misguidance.

translation: Indeed, We support Our messengers and those who have believed during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's steadfast support and protection for His messengers and the believers not only in this worldly life but also on the Day of Judgment, assuring them victory and vindication against their adversaries.

translation: The Day when the wrongdoers will not be able to excuse themselves; for them is a curse, and for them is a dreadful home.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice on the Day of Judgment, where those who transgress and oppress will find no excuse to evade their punishment. It serves as a stern warning that the consequences of injustice are severe and inescapable, highlighting the importance of righteousness and accountability.

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the guidance and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture.
interpretation: This verse signifies that divine guidance was granted through Prophet Moses, and the responsibility and privilege of preserving and practicing this guidance were entrusted to the Children of Israel through the inheritance of the Scripture. It emphasizes the continuity of God's guidance to humanity via prophets and transmitted through sacred texts to specific communities.

translation: [It is] guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an serves as a source of clear guidance and a profound reminder specifically for those who possess deep intellect and comprehension. It highlights that true understanding and reflection enable one to benefit fully from the teachings and wisdom contained in the Qur'an.

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse teaches perseverance in the face of challenges, assuring that Allah's promises are certain and true. It encourages seeking forgiveness for one's mistakes and maintaining a continuous remembrance and glorification of Allah throughout different times of the day, reflecting a balanced approach of patience, repentance, and devotion.

translation: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of Allah without any authority having come to them—they will have a painful punishment. In their hearts is only pride, and they will never attain to it. So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse warns against arguing about the signs of Allah without knowledge or rightful authority, highlighting that such arrogance stems from pride, which blinds one to the truth and leads to divine punishment. It advises seeking protection and guidance from Allah, who perceives all, to guard against this arrogance and to approach His signs with humility and sincerity.

translation: Indeed, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the grandeur and complexity involved in the creation of the vast heavens and earth far surpasses that of human beings. It serves to humble mankind, encouraging reflection on God's immense power and wisdom. Yet, despite this clear sign, many people remain unaware or unappreciative of the magnitude of God's creative power, highlighting a spiritual blindness or neglect in recognizing and submitting to the Creator.

translation: And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark difference between guidance and misguidance, faith and disbelief, and good and evil. It highlights that true understanding and vision come with belief and righteous action, and those who choose wrongdoing remain separated from this light. The reminder is to reflect deeply and remember that people's inner states and deeds fundamentally distinguish them before God.

translation: The Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt about it, but most people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the Day of Judgment, despite the skepticism or denial of many people. It serves as a reminder to remain conscious of the ultimate reality and to prepare for the consequences of one's actions, as ignoring this truth leads to spiritual loss.

translation: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell humbled.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God invites sincere supplication and promises a response, emphasizing the power and mercy of God in answering prayers. It warns that arrogance and pride in worship — refusing to humble oneself before God — leads to disgrace and eternal punishment. Thus, humility and earnest seeking of God's help are essential attitudes in faith.

translation: Allah is the One who made the night for you to rest therein and the day to see clearly. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the creation of night and day, emphasizing how Allah’s provision facilitates human life by allowing rest and activity in turn. It serves as a reminder that despite Allah's continual favors and blessings, many people fail to recognize and express gratitude for them. The verse calls for an acknowledgment of these blessings and encourages thankful behavior toward the Creator.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him. So how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the sole Creator of everything that exists. It highlights the futility of worshipping others besides Him and questions the reason for being misguided or led astray when the evidence of His existence and authority is clear and undeniable.

translation: Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequences for those who reject the clear signs and revelations from Allah. It implies that their denial leads to misguidance and alienation from the truth, preventing them from recognizing and benefiting from divine guidance.

translation: Allah is the One who made the earth a resting place for you, and the sky a structure, and formed you and perfected your forms; and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in creating and sustaining the universe, emphasizing His role not only as the creator of physical structures but also as the perfecter of human forms and the provider of sustenance. It reminds believers of Allah's comprehensive care and authority over all existence, encouraging gratitude and recognition of His blessings.

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so invoke Him, being sincere to Him in religion. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and eternal nature of Allah, urging believers to call upon Him with sincere devotion and pure intention, acknowledging that true worship and allegiance belong solely to Him alone.

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah when clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse conveys a firm declaration of the Prophet Muhammad's commitment to monotheism and obedience to Allah alone. It underscores that despite the practices of others who associate partners with God, the Prophet is guided by undeniable evidence from Allah, which commands exclusive worship of Him. This highlights the principle that true guidance requires abandoning false deities and submitting fully to the one true Lord of all existence.

translation: He it is who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you forth as a child, that you may reach your maturity; then that you may become old men. And some of you die before that, so that you reach an appointed term; and perhaps you will understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stages of human creation and development, emphasizing the deliberate and gradual process by which God forms human life from an insignificant origin to full maturity. It also reminds us of the inevitability of death occurring at an appointed time, underscoring the transient nature of life and encouraging reflection on God's wise design and the purpose behind our existence.

translation: He it is Who gives life and causes death; and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of God over life and death, illustrating that His command is so potent that mere utterance brings things into existence or causes them to cease. It underlines God's sovereignty and the effortless nature of His will, reminding believers of His unmatched capability to control all aspects of existence.

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the verses of Allah, how they are turned away?
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of those who argue against the signs and revelations of Allah. Their disputes are not based on sincere seeking of truth but on ego, obstinance, or ulterior motives, leading them to be misguided and diverted from understanding the true message. It serves as a warning that hostile argumentation against divine guidance results in confusion and misguidance rather than enlightenment.

translation: Those who denied the Scripture and that by which We sent Our messengers - they will know.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject the truth of the revealed Scripture and dismiss the messages brought by the prophets will ultimately face the consequences of their denial, as the reality of divine truth will become evident to them beyond doubt, often through punishment or the unfolding of events that confirm the validity of the revelation.

translation: When the shackles are placed around their necks and the chains; they are dragged along.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe punishment for those who reject faith and commit great wrongs, symbolized by the shackles and chains. It signifies the state of being burdened and restrained due to their actions, highlighting the consequences of turning away from righteousness and the divine guidance.

translation: In the boiling water; then into the fire they will be thrown.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe and escalating punishment awaiting those who disbelieve or commit grievous sins, emphasizing the intense and unbearable nature of the torment as a consequence of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: Then it was said to them, 'Where are the things which you used to associate as partners [with Allah]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of idol worship on the Day of Judgment, when no intercession or help will come from false deities. It highlights the ultimate accountability and the realization of the truth that the idols possess no power or existence independent of Allah.

translation: "Other than Allah" — they said, "They have gone astray from us; no, we did not invoke anything before. Thus does Allah lead the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection and denial by disbelievers of the messengers and their message. Their claim that they had not worshipped anything before underscores their obstinacy, and Allah's decree to let the disbelievers remain in misguidance is a reflection of divine justice, where persistent denial leads to spiritual blindness and deviation from the truth.

translation: That is because you were rejoicing in the land without right and because you were living in enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of indulging in wrongful pleasures and unjust enjoyment in life. It serves as a reminder that excessive joy derived from unjust actions or without rightful cause leads to adverse outcomes, emphasizing the importance of aligning one's happiness with righteousness and truth.

translation: Enter through the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein; what an evil abode is that for the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences awaiting those who are arrogant and reject humility before God. It serves as a stern warning that pride and arrogance lead to eternal punishment, illustrating the spiritual downfall that results from such attitudes.

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you some of what We threaten them with or take you in death, to Us is their return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's promise, affirming that divine justice and recompense are certain. It reassures that, regardless of whether one witnesses the consequences faced by the wrongdoers or departs from this world beforehand, everyone ultimately returns to Allah for judgment and recompense.

translation: And indeed, We sent messengers before you; among them are those whose stories We have related to you, and among them are those whose stories We have not related to you. And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it is concluded with truth, and the falsifiers are losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine authority given to every prophet, indicating that their miracles and signs occur solely through Allah's permission. It teaches that the fulfillment of Allah's decree is inevitable and just, ultimately resulting in the downfall of falsehood and those who oppose the truth.

translation: Allah is the One who made for you the livestock that you may ride on some of them and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision and mercy in creating livestock as a means of transportation and sustenance for humans, emphasizing His role as the sole provider who facilitates human needs and comforts.

translation: And for you therein are benefits, and that you may fulfill a need in your breasts, and upon it and upon the ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and bounties Allah has provided through the sea, emphasizing not only the material benefits such as sustenance and transportation but also its role in fulfilling human needs and desires. It signifies trust in Allah's provision and the reliance on the sea for travel and livelihood.

translation: And He shows you His signs; so which of the signs of Allah will you deny?
interpretation: This verse challenges mankind to recognize and accept the clear signs and evidences of God's existence, power, and wisdom present in the universe and in their lives. It emphasizes the futility of denying these manifestations of divine truth, urging reflection and acknowledgment of God's authority and presence.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and mightier in strength and in the traces they left on the earth, yet what they used to earn did not benefit them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to examine the fate of previous nations who were powerful and prosperous yet were ultimately destroyed due to their disobedience and arrogance. It illustrates that worldly power and wealth cannot save one from the consequences of wrongdoing and invites reflection on the transient nature of worldly success.

translation: But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they already possessed of knowledge, and the punishment they used to mock overtook them.
interpretation: This verse highlights human nature's tendency to cling to their preconceived notions and knowledge despite clear evidence presented by divine messengers. It emphasizes that arrogance and denial lead to the consequences they mock or disregard, illustrating the inevitability of facing the results of one's disbelief and ridicule.

translation: So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in that which we were associating with Him."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the reaction of people who, when faced with the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing, profess faith in Allah alone. It highlights how fear of punishment can lead to a superficial acknowledgment of monotheism, revealing that true belief should be sincere and not merely a response to hardship or adversity.

translation: But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This is the way of Allah which has passed before among His servants. And the disbelievers thereupon lost all hope.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that mere belief is insufficient if it does not translate into sincerity and righteous action; when faced with the reality of divine punishment, those whose faith was superficial are powerless to protect themselves. It also emphasizes the consistency of Allah's laws in dealing with evil, serving as a warning that rejecting God's truth leads to inevitable ruin.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: These opening words emphasize that the guidance of the Qur'an comes from Allah, the Most Merciful, highlighting both His compassion and authority. The letters 'Ḥā Mīm' are among the mysterious disjointed letters whose exact significance is known only to Allah; they serve to draw attention, inspire reflection, and remind us of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an.

translation: A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation bestowed by Allah, who is characterized by His boundless mercy towards all creation. It highlights the compassionate nature of God as the source of guidance and mercy for humanity.

translation: A Book whose verses have been made clear, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a clear and elucidated scripture, revealed in the Arabic language, specifically addressed to people who have the capacity and willingness to understand and comprehend its guidance. It highlights the importance of clarity in the divine message and the readiness of the intended audience to grasp and implement its teachings.

translation: A bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet as one who delivers both glad news and warnings, yet most people choose to ignore these messages, demonstrating a spiritual deafness and unwillingness to engage with divine guidance.

translation: And they say, "Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a partition. So work; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the attitude of those who reject the message of the Prophet despite clear signs. Their hearts are veiled, making them incapable of accepting guidance; their ears reject the truth, and there is a barrier preventing understanding. Their defiance is manifested in a challenge to the Prophet, asserting their own agency while simultaneously closing themselves off from the truth.

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God, so be steadfast to Him and ask His forgiveness." And woe to the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting that he is a mortal like others, chosen to convey the divine message. It calls for the recognition of the oneness of God as the fundamental truth and urges people to adhere sincerely to this belief, seek forgiveness from God, and advises warning against associating partners with Him, which leads to ruin.

translation: Those who do not give zakat while they deny the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the connection between faith and social responsibility; rejecting the obligation of zakat—an essential act of worship and community support—is indicative of a broader denial of the afterlife and accountability, thereby reflecting a fundamental lack of true belief.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward without end.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers who engage in good and righteous actions are promised a continuous and ungrudged reward from Allah, highlighting the eternal and generous nature of divine recompense for sincere faith and good conduct.

translation: Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the notion of God's sole and sovereign power in creating the universe rapidly and perfectly. It highlights the absurdity of associating partners with the Creator, emphasizing that the One who fashioned the earth so purposefully is the Lord governing all existence, and hence deserves exclusive worship and acknowledgment.

translation: And He placed within the earth firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four days uniformly for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's meticulous and purposeful creation of the earth, highlighting how the mountains serve as stabilizers, the blessings imbue the land with fertility, and the precise allotment of sustenance ensures that all creatures are provided for fairly. It reflects the wisdom and balance inherent in the natural world as established by the Creator.

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute power and sovereignty of God in the creation of the universe. The skies and the earth are depicted as initially formless or in a state of smoke, emphasizing the primordial condition before creation. God's command for the heavens and the earth to come into existence, and their willing submission, symbolizes the harmony and obedience of creation to the divine will. It highlights that everything in existence is by God's command and that nature's order is a manifestation of God's authority and purposeful design.

translation: So He completed them as seven heavens in two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's precise and powerful creation of the universe, where the seven heavens are formed in perfect order within a measured timeframe. The "command" given to each heaven signifies divine regulation and purposeful design, while the adornment with lamps symbolizes both decoration and protection against harm. It emphasizes Allah's supreme power and knowledge in orchestrating creation with wisdom and control.

translation: But if they turn away, then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud."
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning about the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It reminds the audience of the fate of previous nations, 'Aad and Thamud, who were destroyed by a powerful punishment because of their persistent disobedience and denial of God's messages. The speaker is cautioning that similar consequences may befall those who ignore the warnings and persist in disbelief.

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, [saying], "You shall not worship except Allah," they said, "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels; indeed, we are, concerning that which you have been sent with, disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject divine guidance despite clear signs. It emphasizes that people often set conditions or excuses to deny the truth, such as demanding angelic proof, thereby demonstrating their deliberate disbelief and unwillingness to accept God's messengers and message.

translation: As for 'Aad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right and said, "Who is more powerful than us?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them? Yet they were denying Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of the 'Aad people who challenged the natural order and the authority of Allah by boasting about their strength. It serves as a reminder that human power is insignificant compared to the power of the Creator, and rejecting divine signs stems from ignorance and leads to ruin.

translation: So We sent upon them a furious wind during days of misfortune to make them taste the humiliation of punishment in the worldly life; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more humiliating, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that worldly punishment and humiliation serve as a temporary consequence for wrongdoing, but the ultimate disgrace and suffering lie in the Hereafter for those who persist in injustice and reject guidance. It emphasizes the transient nature of worldly punishment compared to the eternal consequences of the Hereafter, highlighting the seriousness of remaining heedless and unrepentant.

translation: As for Thamud, We guided them; but they preferred blindness over guidance, so a thunderbolt of a humbling punishment seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of willful rejection of divine guidance. Despite being guided, the people of Thamud chose ignorance and disobedience, leading to their destruction. It underscores the importance of accepting guidance to avoid downfall caused by one's own choices.

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse signifies that salvation and deliverance are granted to those who maintain faith and uphold consciousness of Allah's presence, manifesting through righteousness and God-conscious behavior; it highlights the inseparable link between belief, piety, and divine protection.

translation: And [mention] the Day when Allah will gather the enemies to the Fire; then they will be assembled.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitable accountability on the Day of Judgment, where those who opposed Allah and rejected His guidance will be brought together and collectively punished in Hell. It signifies the certainty of divine recompense and serves as a warning to turn away from disbelief and hostility towards God's commands.

translation: Until, when they come to it, their hearing, their eyes, and their skins will bear witness against them for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, every part of a person's being—not just their words or actions—will testify to their deeds. It highlights the comprehensive nature of accountability, showing that nothing is hidden from God's knowledge and that all senses, which were once instruments of sin or virtue, become witnesses to the truth of one's life.

translation: And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "Allah has caused us to speak - He who created everything and first created you, and to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound accountability on the Day of Judgment, where even one's own skin will bear witness against their deeds. It emphasizes God's omnipotence as the creator who enables all existence and communication, signifying that nothing escapes His knowledge or justice. The skin's testimony symbolizes the inescapability of truth and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions before God.

translation: And you did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins bear witness against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that nothing about a person's actions is hidden from Allah, not even what is sensed by the ears, eyes, or skin; human attempts to hide their deeds are futile because Allah's knowledge encompasses all. It serves as a reminder that one cannot escape divine accountability and that Allah is fully aware of all actions, both apparent and concealed.

translation: And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord - that He would not send against you any messenger. So you became among the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangerous consequence of complacency and arrogance in one's belief about God's mercy and accountability. It warns that underestimating God's justice and neglecting the message brought by His messengers leads to ultimate loss, emphasizing the importance of sincere belief and obedience to God.

translation: So if they endure patiently, then the Fire will be their refuge; and if they seek to apologize, they are not of those who seek to make amends.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the consequences for those who persist in wrongdoing despite being given an opportunity to repent. The term 'if they endure patiently' refers to continuing in sin without remorse, leading to the eternal punishment of Hellfire. Conversely, 'if they seek to apologize' indicates a sincere effort to repent and amend one's ways, but in this context, those people are not genuine in their attempts; they neither genuinely repent nor correct their behavior, implying a state of obstinacy and disregard for accountability.

translation: And We appointed for them companions who made pleasing to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word proved true against the former peoples from among the jinn and mankind: indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights how individuals are often influenced by companions who lead them into falsehood and distraction, making corrupt deeds appear attractive. The consequences of following such companions have historically led entire communities, both among jinn and humans, to destruction and regret, underscoring the importance of choosing righteous company to avoid loss in this life and the hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an and talk about it so that you may overcome."
interpretation: The verse highlights the attempts of disbelievers to undermine the Qur'an's message by advising others to ignore it and to argue frivolously against it, hoping thereby to prevail. This reflects their opposition and desperation to prevent guidance from reaching people, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness and critical listening to the divine message despite such challenges.

translation: We will surely cause those who disbelieve to taste a severe punishment, and We will recompense them for the worst of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and severity of divine justice for those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing; it serves as a warning that their evil deeds will be met with a just and harsh recompense from God.

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire. For them therein is the home of eternity, as a reward for their denial of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate consequence for those who oppose and reject the signs of Allah: eternal punishment in the Fire. It serves as a reminder that denial of divine guidance leads to a permanent state of ruin, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging and adhering to the truth revealed by Allah.

translation: And those who disbelieved said, "Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind so that we may put them under our feet and be among the lowest."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the disbelievers' request to be shown those who misled them, with the intention of exerting dominance over them as an expression of their denial and defiance. It reflects the misguided desire to reverse perceived injustice through oppression rather than seeking forgiveness or understanding, highlighting their stubbornness and the futility of their demand in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah" and then remained steadfast - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers who sincerely declare their faith in Allah and maintain their commitment with steadfastness. It emphasizes that such sincerity and perseverance attract divine protection and comfort, symbolized by the angels' descent, removing fear and sorrow. Ultimately, it promises the believers the reward of Paradise, encouraging patience and unwavering faith in the face of difficulties.

translation: We are your protectors in this worldly life and in the Hereafter; and for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of divine guardianship and favor both in this life and the Hereafter, assuring believers of God's generosity and their fulfillment of desires and supplications, highlighting the comprehensive nature of His mercy and support.

translation: (They) descended from the Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This phrase highlights that the divine revelation or mercy comes from Allah, who is characterized by His immense forgiveness and boundless mercy, emphasizing His compassionate nature towards creation.

translation: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the most excellent speech is that of one who calls others to the awareness and worship of Allah, couples this invitation with righteous deeds, and sincerely identifies themselves as a submitter to God's will. It teaches that true guidance combines both words and actions rooted in faith and submission to Allah.

translation: And not equal are the good and the evil. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle that responding to harm with kindness has the power to transform hostility into friendship. It emphasizes that goodness and evil are fundamentally different in value and effect, and by choosing to respond to negativity with excellence and grace, one can overcome enmity and foster reconciliation.

translation: And none will meet it except those who are patient, and none will meet it except the possessor of great good fortune.
interpretation: This verse highlights that enduring trials with patience is essential to attain the ultimate reward and success in the hereafter. True victory and divine meeting require steadfastness and perseverance, which are marks of those truly blessed and fortunate in the sight of Allah.

translation: And if an evil suggestion from Satan tries to tempt you, seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that when one is confronted with whispers or temptations from Satan, the appropriate response is to seek protection through supplication and reliance upon Allah, recognizing His perfect awareness and ability to guard against one’s spiritual vulnerabilities.

translation: And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if you truly worship Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between the Creator and His creation. Though the sun and moon are magnificent signs of God's power and precision, they themselves are not objects of worship. True devotion and submission should be directed only to Allah, the One who created these celestial bodies, reminding believers to avoid idolatry and to recognize the singular divinity behind all aspects of the universe.

translation: But if they are arrogant, then those near your Lord exalt Him by night and day, and they never become weary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between human arrogance and the continuous, tireless glorification of God by the angels or the close attendants of the Divine. It implies that true devotion and worship are characterized by humility and perseverance without fatigue, unlike the obstinate denial of the disbelievers. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their worship regardless of opposition, as those who are near to God maintain their praise ceaselessly.

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells. Indeed, He who gives it life is the one who gives life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and mercy of God through the analogy of the earth's response to rain: barren and lifeless it appears, yet with the divine blessing of water, it revives and flourishes. This signifies God's ability to resurrect the dead, emphasizing His absolute control over life and death; just as He rejuvenates the earth, He resurrects human beings, affirming the certainty of resurrection and reinforcing faith in His omnipotence.

translation: Indeed, those who deviate from Our signs are not hidden from Us. So is one who is cast into the Fire better or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and awareness of human actions, indicating that no deviation from His guidance can be concealed from Him. It contrasts the fate of those who reject divine signs with those who believe and are rewarded with security on the Day of Judgment, reminding humanity to be mindful of their deeds because Allah observes and will hold them accountable.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them — and indeed, it is a mighty Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strength and undeniable truth of the Qur'an as a Book of profound authority and power. Despite its clear message, some people reject it out of stubbornness or arrogance, failing to recognize its divine origin and guidance.

translation: Falsehood cannot approach Him from before Him or from behind Him; He sends down the Revelation from wisdom and praised be He.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute protection and purity of Allah's speech and revelation from any falsehood or alteration. It signifies that divine guidance is safeguarded from corruption, reflecting the perfect wisdom and praiseworthy nature of Allah. Thus, the message delivered through the Qur'an is preserved in its authenticity and purity, ensuring that believers receive unadulterated truth.

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness and Owner of painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the messages and experiences of the Prophet Muhammad are not unique but follow the pattern of previous messengers; it reassures that the divine guidance is consistent and that while God's mercy and forgiveness are vast, His justice and punishment for wrongdoing are also severe and certain.

translation: And if We had made it a Quran in a foreign language, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail?" Is it a foreign language and an Arab [messenger]? Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and healing." And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse addresses the objections of disbelievers regarding the Quran's language and clarity. It highlights that regardless of whether the Quran was revealed in Arabic or another language, those rejecting faith would find fault. The verse emphasizes that the Quran serves as guidance and healing for believers, while disbelief results in spiritual deafness and blindness. Ultimately, it affirms that the rejection is due to the hearts' condition, not the language or style of the revelation.

translation: And indeed We gave Moses the Scripture, and they differed therein. And if not a word had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed they are, concerning it, in grave doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to dispute and differ even over divinely revealed guidance. Although Moses was given clear guidance from God, the people still contested it. The 'word that preceded from your Lord' signifies God's will to delay final judgment, allowing room for human free will and trial. It emphasizes that divine decree ultimately governs all disputes, and human skepticism and doubt persist, underscoring the need for submission to God's wisdom and decrees.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and justice in the sight of God. Each individual is accountable for their own actions; doing good benefits the soul itself, while wrongdoing harms it. Moreover, it affirms that God is absolutely just and does not wrong His servants, ensuring that every person's fate is fair and deserved based on their deeds.

translation: To Him will return the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes forth from its sheath, nor does a female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. And [on] the Day He will call them, "Where are My partners?" They will say, "We announce to You that there is none of us who bears witness."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all knowledge of fate, especially the knowledge of the exact timing of the Last Hour, is solely with Allah. Every natural process, from the growth of fruits to the birth of living beings, occurs by His will and knowledge alone. On the Day of Judgment, all false gods and partners will be called upon but will deny having any power or knowledge, highlighting the futility of associating partners with Allah and reinforcing His absolute sovereignty and oneness.

translation: And what they used to invoke before has deserted them, and they, [themselves], have lost hope of escape.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when those who falsely invoked other deities or idols realize their futility and abandonment in times of distress, highlighting the ultimate helplessness and despair that arise when relying on false objects of worship rather than turning sincerely to God.

translation: A person does not tire of supplicating for good, but when harm touches him, he becomes hopeless and despairing.
