It serves as a warning that turning away from this duty may lead to Allah's choosing others who fulfill this obligation, implying a loss of privilege and blessings for those who persist in stinginess.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the success and victories granted to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are by the grace and decree of Allah. It signifies a moment of decisive triumph that opens the path for the message of Islam to spread clearly and effectively, reassuring the believers of divine support in their cause.

translation: So that Allah may forgive you what has preceded of your sin and what will follow, and complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and forgiveness extended to the believer, emphasizing that God's pardon is not limited by time or the magnitude of sins. It reassures that through Allah's grace, one's past and future shortcomings can be forgiven, favor can be perfected, and one can be guided away from error towards a path of righteousness and spiritual fulfillment.

translation: And Allah will grant you a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse assures the believers that divine support will come with overwhelming strength and honor, emphasizing that true victory is granted by Allah alone, reinforcing reliance on Him during times of struggle and adversity.

translation: He it is Who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers so that they would increase in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true tranquility and peace in the hearts come from divine support, which strengthens believers by deepening their faith. It reminds us that all power and control, including the guardianship of the heavens and the earth, belong to Allah alone, who possesses perfect knowledge and wisdom. Thus, the believer's confidence and growth in faith stem from the assurance that Allah's support encompasses all realms and matters.

translation: To admit the believing men and believing women into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, and to remove from them their misdeeds - and that is ever, in the sight of Allah, the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate success for believers: eternal life in paradise where their past wrongdoings are forgiven. It signifies the mercy and justice of God, rewarding steadfast faith and righteousness with everlasting happiness and spiritual purification.

translation: And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, those who have evil thoughts about Allah. Upon them is a misfortune of evil; and Allah's wrath is upon them, and He has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences awaiting those who conceal disbelief and hypocrisy, harboring wrongful assumptions about God. It serves as a warning about the internal corruption that arises from insincerity and associating partners with Allah, highlighting the divine justice that will manifest in their ultimate punishment.

translation: To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over all forces and powers in the universe, both celestial and terrestrial. It reminds us that all strength, authority, and governance belong to Him alone, highlighting His might and perfect wisdom in managing creation and unfolding events according to His divine decree.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness to the truth, one who delivers glad news of God's mercy and reward to believers, and a warner about the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. It underlines the responsibility entrusted to him to convey God's message clearly and completely to guide humanity.

translation: So that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, support Him, honor Him, and glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith in God and His Messenger, coupled with active support and reverence. It underscores that true belief is demonstrated not only through acknowledgment but also by defending, respecting, and consistently praising God throughout all times of the day.

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself; and whoever fulfills what he has promised Allah - He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sacredness and seriousness of pledging allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad as an act that is ultimately an allegiance to Allah Himself. It highlights that such a pledge is under the direct authority and power of Allah ('the hand of Allah over their hands'), indicating divine oversight and responsibility. Breaking such a commitment harms only the person who breaks it, while fulfilling it brings immense reward from Allah, underscoring the moral and spiritual imperative to honor one's promises in faith and community.

translation: The Bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, "Our wealth and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, "Who could protect you from Allah if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you?" Rather, Allah is ever, concerning what you do, Aware.
interpretation: This verse conveys that merely uttering words of repentance or seeking forgiveness without sincere intention is futile, especially when one’s distractions from spiritual duties stem from preoccupations like wealth and family. It emphasizes that ultimate control over harm and benefit lies solely with Allah, who is fully aware of all actions and their inner realities, underscoring the importance of genuine faith and awareness of divine sovereignty.

translation: But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and it was made pleasing in your hearts, and you conceived an evil conception and were a people ruined.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who doubted the return of the Prophet Muhammad and the believers to their homes, reflecting a profound mistrust and ill-will towards them. It highlights the distorted assumptions held by such individuals, influenced by malice and ignorance, leading to their ultimate ruin. The verse teaches that misguided disbelief and hostile scheming against the truth result in spiritual and communal devastation.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the critical importance of faith in Allah and His Messenger as a foundation of belief. The consequence for rejecting this faith is a severe punishment, symbolized by the blazing fire, underscoring Allah's justice and the seriousness of disbelief. It serves as a warning to recognize and accept divine guidance to attain salvation.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over all creation, highlighting that His authority and control encompass everything in the heavens and the earth. It serves as a reminder that His mercy and forgiveness are vast, yet His justice is also real, as He disciplines whom He wills according to His wisdom. This balance reflects the profound nature of divine governance, encouraging believers to seek His mercy while being mindful of His justice.

translation: Those who lag behind will say when you set out to take the spoils, "Let us follow you." They want to alter the word of Allah. Say, "You will not follow us. Thus did Allah say before." They will say, "Nay, but you envy us." But they understood not except a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity and hypocrisy of those who feign eagerness to join the believers only to gain worldly benefits, seeking to distort divine commandments for their interest. The denial and excuses they offer reveal a lack of true understanding and a disposition marred by jealousy and superficiality.

translation: Say to those who remained behind among the Bedouins, "You will be called to a people of great military strength; you will either fight them or submit to them." But if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward. But if you turn away, as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse admonishes those who stayed behind from the battle, warning them that they will face a formidable enemy and must choose between fighting bravely or submitting. It underscores the importance of obedience and commitment to the cause, promising divine reward for steadfastness and warning of severe punishment for cowardice and betrayal, reflecting the principle that one's faith and actions have direct consequences.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the ill; and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; but whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy by acknowledging the limitations imposed by certain physical conditions, thereby relieving those with disabilities from religious burdens that they cannot bear. It also highlights the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger as the path to eternal bliss, while warning of severe punishment for those who consciously reject faith, underscoring personal accountability and divine mercy balanced with justice.

translation: Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah’s pleasure with the sincere commitment and faith of the believers manifests as inner peace and tangible success. It emphasizes that genuine faith and unity, rooted in heartfelt conviction, are honored by divine support and lead to forthcoming triumphs.

translation: And many war gains they take. And Allah is Powerful and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while people may accumulate considerable material gains or spoils, it is Allah alone who possesses ultimate power and wisdom, guiding and determining the outcomes beyond human control.

translation: Allah has promised you many spoils to be taken, so He hastened to you this victory and restrained the hands of people from you; that it may be a sign for the believers and guide you on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that Allah's support in granting them swift victories and tangible gains serves not only as a reward but also as a reassurance of His favor; it strengthens faith and directs believers towards steadfastness and righteousness by manifesting divine intervention in their affairs.

translation: And others you were not able to encompass; Allah has encompassed them. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that human beings have limitations in their understanding and knowledge, and there are matters beyond their capacity to grasp. Allah, however, has complete knowledge and control over all things, including those beyond human comprehension, highlighting His omnipotence and the necessity of trusting in His wisdom.

translation: And if those who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs in retreat; then they would not find a protector or a helper.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inherent weakness and lack of true solidarity among the disbelievers who oppose the believers; despite their opposition, when faced with actual conflict, they would flee and be abandoned, demonstrating that true strength and support come from faith and reliance on God rather than mere numbers or alliances.

translation: It is the way of Allah that has passed before (i.e., established practice), and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unchangeable nature of Allah's laws and decrees. It serves as a reminder that the divine principles governing creation and human affairs are steadfast and will not be altered by human desires or actions. Therefore, believers should accept the outcomes appointed by Allah with patience and trust in His wisdom, knowing that His way is consistent and just.

translation: And He it is Who held back their hands from you and your hands from them within the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. And Allah is Observant of what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's protective intervention during conflict, emphasizing that He restrains the harm both parties could inflict, ensuring a period of peace after a victory. It reflects the divine wisdom in controlling the unfolding of events, reminding believers that their actions are always under Allah's watchful care, and that victories and truces are manifestations of His will, not merely human effort.

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and the sacrificial animals from reaching their place of sacrifice. If it had not been for believing men and believing women who you did not know, so that you might not trample them and suffer from them without knowledge, Allah would have admitted whoever He wills into His mercy. If they had removed, We would have punished those who disbelieve among them with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and mercy in protecting the community of believers during times of conflict or hostility. The presence of believing men and women among adversaries acted as a safeguard, preventing harm to the Prophet's people through inadvertent violence. It underscores that Allah's mercy and protection manifest through subtle means that may not be immediately apparent, and in the absence of such protective barriers, divine punishment would have descended upon the disbelievers. Thus, it serves as a reminder of God's overarching control, mercy, and justice, as well as the importance of caution and awareness in dealing with enmity.

translation: When those who disbelieved had in their hearts vehement pride — the pride of the Age of Ignorance — Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and imposed upon them the word of righteousness; and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the arrogance and prejudice of the disbelievers stemmed from the ignorance and pride of pre-Islamic times. Allah responded by granting tranquility and peace to His Messenger and the believers, strengthening them with faith and righteousness. This indicates that true strength and honor come from adherence to piety and consciousness of God, rather than from pride and ignorance. It underscores that Allah's knowledge encompasses all affairs, affirming that His support and wisdom guide the believers through trials.

translation: Indeed, Allah has confirmed the truth of His Messenger's vision: you will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram in safety, with your heads shaved and hair shortened, not fearing anything. He knew what you did not know and granted a near victory.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine affirmation of the Prophet Muhammad's dream about entering the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) peacefully, symbolizing Allah's assurance of protection and success despite apparent obstacles. It underlines that Allah's knowledge encompasses things beyond human understanding and that He orchestrates victories according to His wisdom and timing, instilling confidence and trust in His plans among believers.

translation: He it is Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and Allah is sufficient as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of the Prophet Muhammad as the bearer of guidance and the true religion, destined to establish the supremacy of Islamic monotheism and truth over all other beliefs; it underscores that Allah alone is the ever-sufficient witness to the fulfillment of this promise, affirming the certainty and justice inherent in His plan.

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those who are with him are severe against disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot, then strengthens it, and it becomes thick and stands firm on its stalk, delighting the sowers so that it may enrage the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinctive characteristics of the believers who follow the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: they embody a balance of strength and mercy—as fierce against injustice and oppression but compassionate among themselves. Their devotion and humility before Allah manifest in physical signs of worship, reflecting sincerity and dedication. The comparison to a thriving plant illustrates their spiritual growth and firmness, inspiring fellow believers and provoking disbelievers. Ultimately, the verse reassures that sincere faith combined with righteous actions leads to divine forgiveness and immense reward, emphasizing the transformative and rewarding nature of true adherence to the faith.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O you who have believed, do not put forward yourselves before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches the believers to show humility and restraint by not presuming to act on their own judgment ahead of divine guidance and prophetic instruction. It emphasizes the importance of obedience and reverence toward God's commands and the messenger's teachings, reminding believers that God is all-hearing and all-knowing, fully aware of their intentions and actions.

translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to show utmost respect and humility towards the Prophet Muhammad by lowering their voices in his presence and not addressing him as loudly as they would others. The underlying meaning is that elevating one's voice before the Prophet reflects a lack of reverence and can nullify one's good deeds, as respect for the Prophet is integral to demonstrating true faith and devotion.

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah - they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound respect and reverence one should have when in the presence of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It signifies that true piety is marked by humility and self-restraint, especially in sacred contexts. Allah tests the sincerity of believers through such acts of modesty and restraint, and those who embody this humility are assured of His forgiveness and abundant reward, reflecting the deep connection between external behavior and inner spiritual state.

translation: Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private rooms, most of them do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impropriety and lack of understanding of those who call the Prophet Muhammad from behind private chambers instead of directly and respectfully. It admonishes such behavior as indicative of a failure to grasp proper etiquette and consideration, emphasizing the importance of respectful and thoughtful communication.

translation: And if they had been patient until the messenger came to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of trials and delay, particularly in matters of faith and guidance. It suggests that enduring with patience until the Prophet could come and deliver the message personally would have brought greater benefit and success. It underscores the virtue of restraint and trust in Allah's timing, highlighting that rushing or losing patience may lead to missed opportunities for forgiveness and mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, if a disobedient person comes to you with information, verify it, lest you harm people unknowingly and afterward regret what you have done.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of verifying information before acting upon it, especially when it comes from unreliable or sinful individuals, to prevent unjust harm to others and the resulting remorse. It emphasizes caution, responsibility, and the pursuit of truth within the community.

translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would surely be in error; but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has beautified it in your hearts and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance, and disobedience. Those are the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the essential wisdom behind why the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not comply with every desire or opinion of the people; it serves to safeguard the community from falling into misguidance and error. It underscores that true guidance and righteousness come from aligning oneself with the faith that Allah has made beloved and appealing in the hearts of the believers, fostering an aversion to disbelief, sin, and rebellion. Those who embody this internalization of faith and rejection of wrongdoing are the ones who are truly on the straight path.

translation: A bounty from Allah and a mercy; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the blessings and favors received are not merely by chance or personal effort, but are manifestations of Allah's generous grace and mercy. It reminds us that God's wisdom and knowledge encompass all things, and His grace is part of a deliberate divine plan to guide and support His creation.

translation: And if two groups of believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. Then, if it returns, reconcile between them with justice and be equitable. Indeed, Allah loves those who are just.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining unity and justice among believers. When conflict arises, reconciliation is the first course of action. However, if one party transgresses unjustly, it becomes necessary to confront and restrain the oppressor to uphold divine law. Once justice is restored, fairness and equitable treatment must prevail, reflecting Allah's love for those who are just.

translation: The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your brothers and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of unity and brotherhood among believers, urging them to resolve conflicts and disputes peacefully. The call to 'fear Allah' serves as a reminder that maintaining harmony is not just a social duty but a spiritual obligation that leads to divine mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them. Nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse teaches the essential value of humility and respect among believers, emphasizing that no one should mock or belittle others because superiority is known only to God and can change; the verse warns against the harms of arrogance, insults, and offensive labeling, calling such behavior a grievous misconduct that betrays the spirit of faith, and reminding that persistence in such sins without repentance makes one truly unjust.

translation: O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of guarding one's inner thoughts and social behavior by discouraging unfounded suspicions and negative assumptions about others, as these often lead to sin. It forbids invading others' privacy through spying and harshly prohibits backbiting, equating it to the abhorrent act of consuming a deceased brother's flesh, which emphasizes the spiritual and social harm caused by such behavior. The verse underscores the need to cultivate respect, compassion, and mindfulness of God, reminding believers that God is forgiving and merciful, always ready to accept repentance for those who amend their ways.

translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inherent equality of all human beings by highlighting their common origin from a male and a female, and it teaches that diversity in peoples and tribes is a means for mutual recognition and understanding, not for causing division or superiority. True honor and nobility in the eyes of God are determined by righteousness and piety, not by lineage, race, or social status, reminding us to value virtue above worldly distinctions.

translation: The Bedouins said, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the difference between mere verbal submission and true faith that resides in the heart. It emphasizes that proclaiming belief is not sufficient; genuine faith must be internalized and reflected in sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger. The verse reassures that sincere obedience results in unblemished reward, highlighting Allah's forgiveness and mercy toward those striving earnestly.

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, then they do not doubt but strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is not merely a declaration of belief, but it is characterized by unwavering certainty and active dedication. The genuine believers are those who not only affirm their faith in Allah and His Messenger without any hesitation or doubt but also demonstrate their commitment by exerting themselves both financially and personally in the path of God. This sincerity and perseverance mark them as the truthful and authentic believers.

translation: Say, "Do you know Allah by your religion?" And Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim to understand or define Allah based purely on their limited religious perspectives. It emphasizes that human knowledge is insufficient to fully comprehend the essence and attributes of Allah, as He alone has complete knowledge of the unseen realms and everything within existence. Therefore, true understanding of Allah requires humility and recognition of His infinite knowledge beyond human constructs.

translation: They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved so you would be alike. Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided envy some people have toward the believers, desiring that they abandon their faith to be like them. However, true guidance and faith are blessings from Allah alone, and no one can grant or withhold them except Him. The verse underscores the importance of recognizing that faith is a divine favor, not a human achievement or something to be resented by others.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge encompasses all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth, including the unseen realities beyond human perception. It reminds believers that nothing escapes His awareness, and He observes all actions, making humans accountable for their deeds even when others cannot see them.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an,
interpretation: This verse underscores the significance of the Qur'an as a majestic and sacred revelation. The isolated letter 'Qaf' draws attention, symbolizing the profound nature of the message to follow, emphasizing that the Qur'an is a glorious reminder from Allah deserving respect and reflection.

translation: Rather, they were astonished that a warner had come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers said, "This is an amazing thing."
interpretation: The verse highlights the incredulity and denial of the disbelievers when a messenger arises from among their own people. It reflects their surprise and rejection not just of the message, but of the fact that someone familiar to them, a part of their community, brings such warnings. This disbelief stems from their arrogance and unwillingness to accept guidance from a source so close to their own society.

translation: When we have died and become dust, is it then a return (to life) that is distant?
interpretation: This verse challenges the skepticism regarding resurrection after death. It invites reflection on the power of God to bring the dead back to life, emphasizing that despite our physical dissolution into dust, resurrection is neither impossible nor far-fetched. The verse encourages belief in the life hereafter and reminds us that God's creative power extends beyond our physical end.

translation: Indeed, We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a binding record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete and precise knowledge of everything that occurs on earth, including the disappearance or loss of individuals or resources. It reassures that nothing escapes His awareness and that a protected and comprehensive record (the preserved Tablet or divine record) is maintained by Him, underscoring His attribute of perfect knowledge and control over all affairs.

translation: But they denied the truth when it came to them, and they are in a state of confused doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject divine truth despite clear evidence, illustrating that such denial often arises from inner turmoil and confusion. It emphasizes that when guidance reaches the hearts of those who reject it, their minds become unsettled, leading to hesitation and uncertainty in accepting what is right.

translation: Do they not look at the sky above them—how We have built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the perfection and order of the natural world, emphasizing that the sky is a meticulously crafted and harmonious creation without flaws or splits. It points to the existence of a purposeful, powerful Creator whose design is evident in the stability and beauty of the heavens, urging people to recognize and appreciate this divine artistry as a sign of God's sovereignty and wisdom.

translation: And the earth - We have spread it out and cast therein firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein every pleasing kind,
interpretation: This verse illustrates the mercy and power of God in creating and sustaining the earth as a suitable abode for life. By spreading out the earth and stabilizing it with mountains, God ensures its balance and stability. Furthermore, by growing various beautiful pairs of plants, God provides sustenance and aesthetic pleasure for His creatures, highlighting the intricate design and generosity in creation.

translation: A clear admonition and reminder for every devoted servant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the guidance and reminders contained within are meant for those who humbly turn to God with sincerity and devotion. It highlights the importance of being receptive and obedient to divine instruction as the path to spiritual growth and closeness to God.

translation: And We sent down from the sky blessed water, and caused to grow thereby gardens and grain for harvest.
interpretation: This verse expresses how divine mercy manifests through the provision of life-sustaining rainfall, which nurtures the earth to produce vegetation and crops, emphasizing Allah's power and benevolence in sustaining all creation.

translation: And the towering palm trees having fruit arranged in layers,
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's creation of palm trees standing tall and strong, bearing neatly arranged clusters of fruit, symbolizing order and sustenance. It signifies the divine provision and the harmony present in nature, reminding us of God's power to create and maintain life in its various forms.

translation: A provision for the servants, and by it We revived a dead town. Thus is the emergence.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that sustenance, often understood as both physical provision and spiritual blessings, is granted by God to His servants. It parallels the revival of a barren town with the revival brought about by God's provision and mercy. The term 'thus is the emergence' emphasizes that just as God can restore life to what was dead or dormant, He similarly brings forth sustenance and blessings to reinvigorate both individuals and communities.

translation: The peoples before them—those of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud—also denied (the messengers).
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of human rejection of divine guidance, emphasizing that previous communities, despite witnessing clear signs and receiving messengers, chose disbelief. It serves as a warning that disbelief leads to consequences and stresses the importance of heeding the messages brought by prophets.

translation: And [mention] 'Aad and Pharaoh and the brothers of Lot.
interpretation: This verse references three significant groups or figures who were warned by the prophets but persisted in their arrogance and wrongdoing. Their stories serve as warnings about the consequences of rejecting God's guidance and persisting in injustice and disbelief.

translation: And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba`; all the messengers were denied, and there was a just punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the recurring pattern in history where communities like the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba` rejected the messages brought by the prophets sent to them. Their denial of the truth led to inevitable divine retribution. It serves as a warning that rejecting clear guidance and the messengers of God brings about consequences, emphasizing the importance of heeding the warnings and instructions conveyed through the prophets.

translation: Are We tired from the first creation? No, but they are in confusion about a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God's power to create is not limited or exhausted by the original creation; instead, it challenges the skeptics who doubt the resurrection, highlighting that their confusion and disbelief pertain to the concept of a new creation (resurrection), which is fully within God's ability.

translation: And We have certainly created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's intimate knowledge and presence with every individual, highlighting that nothing is hidden from Him—not even the innermost doubts and thoughts of a person's soul. It assures believers that God's closeness surpasses even the closest physical connections, reminding them of His constant watchfulness and understanding, which should inspire mindfulness and reliance on Him.

translation: When the two receivers receive [the soul] from the right and from the left sitting [in wait],
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment of death, describing angels positioned on the right and left side who come to take the soul. Their presence signifies the transition from life to the afterlife, highlighting the certainty and inevitability of death, as well as the spiritual reality that accompanies it.

translation: Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer prepared (to record it).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the constant presence of divine watchers who precisely record every word and deed of an individual. It serves as a reminder that nothing escapes the knowledge of God, encouraging mindfulness, sincerity, and accountability in speech and actions.

translation: And the agony of death came with the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable and undeniable reality of death. Despite any attempts to evade or deny it, death arrives as a certain truth that no one can escape. It serves as a reminder of human mortality and the ultimate transition from worldly life to the hereafter, emphasizing the importance of being prepared for that reality.

translation: And the trumpet will be blown; that is the Day of Announcement.
interpretation: This verse signifies the momentous event when a trumpet blast will signal the commencement of the Day of Judgment, marking the transition from worldly life to the ultimate reality of resurrection and divine reckoning.

translation: And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of accountability in the hereafter, where each person is accompanied by an angel who guides their soul and another who bears witness to their deeds, underscoring that no one's actions will go unnoticed or unrecorded.

translation: Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this, so We removed from you your cover, and your sight is sharp this day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the awakening from ignorance or heedlessness through divine intervention. The 'cover' symbolizes previous barriers preventing clear understanding or awareness, and its removal leads to heightened perception and insight. It underscores the idea that true comprehension and clarity come by the grace of God, moving from a state of blindness to clear vision, both literally and metaphorically.

translation: And his companion said, "This is what I have, prepared."
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of preparedness and sharing one's resources or knowledge. It suggests that one should offer what they have available, even if it seems limited, as it reflects sincerity and readiness to contribute or assist others.

translation: They will be thrown into Hell, every obstinate disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable consequence for those who persist in disbelief and stubborn defiance against God's guidance. It highlights the firmness of God's justice, where those who continuously reject faith and oppose divine commandments without repentance are destined to face severe punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: Preventer of good, transgressor, doubter.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who obstructs goodness and righteousness, not only by withholding benefit from others but also by exceeding bounds in wrongdoing. Being 'doubter' indicates a mindset steeped in suspicion and skepticism, which leads one to reject truth and guidance. Collectively, these traits portray an individual whose negative disposition harms both themselves and their community by opposing the path of moral and spiritual guidance.

translation: He who has set up another god alongside Allah; then they will be thrown into severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave sin of associating partners with Allah (shirk), emphasizing that those who attribute divinity besides Him will face severe consequences in the hereafter, reminding believers of the importance of pure monotheism.

translation: He said, "My Lord, do not disgrace me on the Day they are [all] resurrected."
interpretation: This verse reveals a supplication where the speaker seeks protection from disgrace or humiliation in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the awareness of accountability before God and the desire to maintain dignity on the Day of Judgment.

translation: He said, 'Do not argue with me over the matter, and I have already brought you clear warning.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of heeding prophetic warnings and refraining from fruitless disputes when clear guidance has been presented; it serves as a reminder that rejecting truthful admonitions leads to accountability and consequences.

translation: My word does not change with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute consistency and justice of God. It affirms that God's decrees and promises remain firm and unaltered, reflecting His truthfulness and reliability. Furthermore, it declares that God does not wrong His servants in any way, underscoring His perfect justice and mercy towards human beings.

translation: The Day We say to Hell, 'Have you been filled?' and it will say, 'Is there any more?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the insatiable nature of Hell in response to the deeds of those who are punished therein. It symbolizes the endless capacity of divine punishment for those who persist in wrongdoing, emphasizing the seriousness of accountability and the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter.

translation: And Paradise is brought near to the righteous, not far away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that for those who are God-conscious and pious, Paradise is not a distant or unattainable reward; rather, it is made close and accessible as a direct consequence of their righteousness and fear of God.

translation: This is what you have been promised for every devoted, ever-watchful one.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward and certainty awaiting those who are consistently repentant and remain vigilant in their faith and duties. It emphasizes that the promised blessings are designated for those who turn to God sincerely and maintain steadfast awareness of their responsibilities and surroundings.

translation: Whoever fears the Most Merciful unseen and comes with a repentant heart,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity and devotion of a believer who maintains reverence for Allah even without seeing Him, demonstrating true faith. It highlights the importance of an internal, heartfelt turning towards Allah with humility and repentance, indicating that genuine spirituality is based on inner conviction and submission rather than merely external observance.

translation: Enter it in peace; this is the Day of Eternity.
interpretation: This verse signifies the eternal peace and security granted to the believers in Paradise, emphasizing that their reward is everlasting and free from any fear or suffering, marking the final abode where they will remain forever.

translation: For them, whatever they wish for therein, and with Us is more.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the blessings and rewards granted to the righteous in Paradise are abundant and satisfying to their desires, yet God's generosity surpasses even that, offering continuous and inexhaustible bounties beyond human comprehension.

translation: And how many generations We destroyed before them, who were mightier than them in power, and they roamed through the cities. Is there any place of escape?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that despite the strength and dominance of past peoples, they were ultimately destroyed because of their wrongdoing and rejection of truth. It teaches that human power and might are temporary, and no one can escape the consequences of their deeds in the face of divine justice.

translation: Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is present [in mind].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true understanding and acceptance of guidance come not merely through external observation but through the presence of a sincere and attentive heart. It indicates that God’s signs and messages serve as reminders, but their impact depends on the spiritual receptivity and mindfulness of the individual.

translation: And indeed, We created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and perfection of Allah's creative act. It shows that the creation of the vast universe happened in an orderly, measured period, reflecting divine wisdom and control. The mention that no fatigue touched Allah underscores His transcendence and perfection, indicating that unlike human beings who tire, God's power is absolute and effortless.

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.
interpretation: This verse teaches the virtue of patience in the face of opposition and criticism, emphasizing steadfastness in one's commitment to divine truth. It also highlights the importance of regular remembrance and glorification of God, particularly during the transitions of day—before dawn and at sunset—symbolizing continuous devotion throughout life's cycles.

translation: And glorify Him during a part of the night and at the ends of the prostrations.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in worship and remembrance of Allah during the quiet, contemplative hours of the night, as well as immediately after performing the physical act of prostration in prayer. It highlights the importance of consistent, heartfelt devotion both in solitude and within the structured rituals of prayer, emphasizing a deep connection and reverence toward the Creator beyond obligatory worship.

translation: And listen on the Day the Caller calls from a near place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immediacy and certainty of the Day of Judgment, when the divine call will be made close at hand, making all excuses impossible and compelling all to respond and witness the unfolding of ultimate accountability.

translation: On the Day when they will hear the blast with the truth; that will be the Day of Emergence (Resurrection).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitable moment of resurrection when all beings will hear the decisive and truthful blast signaling the awakening from death. It reminds us that the Day of Judgment is certain, marked by absolute reality and clarity, leaving no room for denial or doubt.

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over life and death, reminding us that He is the ultimate source of both, and that every soul will return to Him, highlighting the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: On the Day the earth will split open for them, hastening forth. That is a gathering easy for Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and ease with which Allah will gather all people on the Day of Judgment. The splitting of the earth symbolizes the complete and undeniable resurrection, where no one can escape being brought forth for judgment. It serves as a reminder of Allah's power over creation and the certainty of the final accountability.

translation: Indeed, We are most knowing of what they say, and you are not over them a tyrant. So remind with the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that God is fully aware of the false accusations and doubts uttered by disbelievers, and that the Prophet is not responsible for forcing belief upon anyone. The emphasis is placed on the duty to deliver the message through the Qur'an, targeting those who are conscious of God and heedful of His warnings. It serves as a reminder that guidance is ultimately linked to one's own receptiveness and fear of divine accountability, and that the Prophet's role is to remind, not to compel.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By those [winds] scattering [dust] far and wide,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah through the natural phenomena He has created. The scattering winds symbolize the divine control over the elements and the unfolding of events in the universe, indicating that nothing happens without Allah's will and purpose.

translation: By those [angels] who carry [the Throne] and those who bear burdens,
interpretation: This verse swears by the angels who carry the divine Throne and those who bear heavy duties in the unseen realm, emphasizing the solemnity and truthfulness of what follows. It serves as an oath to affirm the seriousness of the message, highlighting the power and majesty of God's creation and authority.

translation: Then [when] the female camels are running swiftly,
interpretation: This verse uses the imagery of swift camels to symbolize powerful and unstoppable forces or events unfolding by the command of Allah. It reflects on the natural phenomena under divine control, illustrating the might and precision of God's will in orchestrating the universe's affairs.

translation: By those [angels] who distribute [each] matter,
interpretation: This verse swears by the angels who measure and assign affairs according to divine wisdom, emphasizing the precise and purposeful nature of God's creation and the unfolding of events in the universe.

translation: What you are promised is surely true.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and truthfulness of the promises made by Allah, particularly regarding the hereafter and the consequences of one's deeds. It serves as a reminder that the warnings and rewards described in the Qur'an are not mere tales or empty threats, but definitive realities that will come to pass, urging believers to heed the guidance and prepare accordingly.

translation: Indeed, the religion will surely prevail.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true faith of Islam is certain to endure and overcome all opposition. It signifies the inevitable dominance of divine guidance and righteousness over falsehood and disbelief, assuring believers that despite challenges, the religion's truth and principles will ultimately prevail.

translation: And the sky having [constellations] woven [in harmony],
interpretation: This verse signifies that the sky is created with precise order and interconnectedness, much like a woven fabric. It reflects the meticulous design and harmony in the universe, showing the power and wisdom of the Creator in establishing a balanced and purposeful cosmos.

translation: Indeed, you are in differing speech.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality of disagreement and conflict among people in their words and opinions. It serves as a reminder that human beings naturally have diverse perspectives, which can lead to disputes. The verse calls for awareness of this tendency and encourages seeking harmony, understanding, and guidance to overcome divisions rooted in differing expressions and viewpoints.

translation: He is diverted away from it by those who distort (the truth).
interpretation: This verse highlights that falsehood and misguidance can cause people to stray from the true guidance of the Qur'an, emphasizing the importance of adhering to authentic knowledge and being cautious of those who spread misconceptions.

translation: The liars are killed.
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the severe consequences of deceit and falsehood, highlighting that those who habitually lie and fabricate falsehoods face ultimate punishment, symbolizing the eradication of dishonesty to uphold truth and justice.

translation: Those who, amidst distractions, are heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of individuals who are engrossed in their worldly affairs and distractions to the extent that they become oblivious to their spiritual and moral duties. It serves as a reminder to remain vigilant and conscious of the transient nature of life and to prioritize remembrance of God and accountability over being lost in heedlessness.

translation: They ask, "When is the Day of Judgment?"
interpretation: This verse highlights human curiosity and concern about the inevitable Day of Judgment, emphasizing that people are eager to know when they will be held accountable for their deeds; it serves as a reminder to remain conscious of the transient nature of life and the importance of preparing for the hereafter.

translation: On the Day when they will be tested over the Fire,
interpretation: This verse highlights the trial and torment faced by the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, illustrating that their punishment will be a severe test designed to manifest their true state, emphasizing the reality and gravity of the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Taste your trial; this is what you used to hasten.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who demanded or hastened the punishment due to their disbelief or transgressions. It implies that they will soon experience the consequences they were eager for, emphasizing the certainty and inevitability of divine retribution for their actions.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who are God-conscious and live with mindfulness of their duties toward Allah will be rewarded with eternal bliss in Paradise, symbolized by lush gardens and flowing springs, representing tranquility, abundance, and pure joy.

translation: [They are] receiving what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward and recognition given to the righteous for their prior goodness. It emphasizes that those who have consistently performed good deeds and lived righteously are bestowed with blessings from their Lord. Their past conduct merits the grace they now receive, underscoring the principle that sincere, continuous righteousness leads to divine reward.

translation: They used to sleep but little during the night.
interpretation: This verse highlights the devotion and sincerity of the believers who prioritized worship and remembrance of Allah over worldly comforts, showing their commitment and spiritual vigilance by sacrificing sleep to engage in prayer and reflection.

translation: And in the pre-dawn hours, they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the practice of devout believers who dedicate the quiet, peaceful time just before dawn to sincerely ask Allah for forgiveness. It underscores the importance of humility, repentance, and the spiritual significance of the pre-dawn hours as a time when prayers are especially accepted and when one can reconnect deeply with God.

translation: And there is a right [due] for the petitioner and the deprived out of their wealth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral responsibility of sharing one's wealth with those in need. It underlines the importance of charity and social justice in Islam, reminding believers that wealth is not solely for personal benefit but carries an obligation to support and uplift the less fortunate members of society.

translation: And on the earth are signs for the certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the natural world around us contains clear evidence of God's existence, power, and wisdom. Those who are certain in their faith perceive these signs as manifestations of divine creation and as proofs that strengthen their conviction in the oneness and greatness of Allah.

translation: And in yourselves; then will you not see?
interpretation: This verse invites deep self-reflection, urging individuals to contemplate the signs and wisdom embedded within their own selves as evidence of God's existence and design. It emphasizes that understanding and faith can arise from recognizing the intricacies and conscious faculties inherent in human beings.

translation: And in the heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the sustenance and provisions granted to us originate from the heavens, symbolizing Allah's power and control over all provisions. It serves as a reminder that not only our immediate needs but also the promises of the Hereafter are within Allah’s authority, encouraging trust in divine wisdom and provision.

translation: By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth, just as you speak.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and truthfulness of the message being conveyed, affirming that what is proclaimed by the Prophet is as real and undeniable as the speech of those who reject it, underscoring the divine authority behind the revelation.

translation: Has there reached you the story of the honored guests of Abraham?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the profound hospitality and respect Abraham showed to his guests, who were heavenly messengers. Their visit signifies God's communication through chosen messengers and highlights the virtues of kindness, faith, and divine guidance.

translation: When they entered upon him, they said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, a people unaware."
interpretation: The verse illustrates a moment of encounter where a greeting of peace is exchanged; however, the response acknowledges that the people addressed are unaware or ignorant of the divine message or true guidance. This highlights the contrast between genuine peace, which arises from understanding and faith, and mere outward greetings that lack such depth.

translation: He hurried to his family and brought a fat calf.
interpretation: This verse illustrates eagerness and generosity in sharing blessings with one's family, emphasizing the importance of promptly bringing good provisions and showing care and hospitality to loved ones.

translation: So he brought it near to them and said, "Will you not eat?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the act of offering and sharing, highlighting the importance of generosity and hospitality. It suggests that bringing food close to others and inviting them to partake is an expression of kindness and an encouragement to foster fellowship and unity among people.

translation: So he felt apprehension from them. They said, "Do not be afraid," and gave him good tidings of a knowledgeable boy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when a prophet, feeling apprehensive about a divine message or event, is reassured by angelic messengers who bring glad tidings of a significant and wise child. It underscores the theme of divine reassurance and the importance of trust in God's plan despite initial fears or uncertainties.

translation: Then his wife came forward holding a baby, and struck his face, saying, "A barren old woman!"
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of despair and insult, where the wife, upon witnessing the announcement of a forthcoming child, reacts out of skepticism and bitterness by mocking the possibility of childbirth due to her past experiences or social perceptions. It reflects human emotions of doubt and frustration in the face of unexpected news, highlighting the challenge of embracing faith or hope when confronted with prior disappointments.

translation: They said, "Thus said your Lord; indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the words conveyed to the Prophet are direct from Allah, who possesses ultimate wisdom and complete knowledge, affirming the reliability and divine authority of the message delivered.

translation: So what is your matter, O you messengers?
interpretation: This verse expresses a moment of questioning directed towards the messengers, prompting reflection on their purpose or situation. It serves to highlight the gravity of their mission and the challenges they face, inviting consideration of their trials and the nature of their message.

translation: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals."
interpretation: This verse highlights the acknowledgment of a prophet or messenger about the moral state of the people he was sent to. It reflects that the community had deviated from righteousness and were engaged in wrongdoing, which underscores the challenges faced by messengers in guiding a sinful society towards justice and virtue.

translation: We will cast upon them stones of clay.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a divine punishment wherein God sends stones made from clay upon the transgressors as a means of chastisement, signifying the power of God to enforce justice and the consequences of disobedience to His commands.

translation: (That) is decreed with your Lord for the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse indicates that a certain fate or punishment is firmly established by God for those who exceed limits and persist in wrongdoing. It emphasizes divine justice, affirming that excessive wrongdoers cannot escape the consequences ordained by God.

translation: So We brought forth from it those who believed.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and protection for the faithful by saving them from trials or punishment that befall a particular people or place, emphasizing that belief and righteousness are ultimately rewarded by divine deliverance.

translation: So we found within it only a house of Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that despite searching or investigating, the only dwelling or presence found was of those who submit to God's will, highlighting the exclusivity and purity of faith in that particular context.

translation: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that within the subject being referenced, there is a clear sign or evidence intended to guide and remind those who are conscious of and heedful toward the consequences of their actions, encouraging them to remain mindful of accountability and to strive for righteousness to avoid severe punishment.

translation: And [mention] when We sent Moses to Pharaoh with clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah sent Moses to Pharaoh equipped with clear signs and undeniable authority, emphasizing that the message and mission given to the prophets are supported by divine power and evidence to call people towards truth and justice, even in the face of oppression and disbelief.

translation: Then he turned away, being of those who disbelieve, and said, "[This is] a magician or a madman."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection and denial faced by the Prophet when he presented the truth. It highlights how people often dismiss divine messages by labeling the messengers as sorcerers or insane, reflecting their unwillingness to accept the spiritual reality and their attachment to false beliefs.

translation: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, and he was blameworthy.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine justice executed upon a tyrant and his forces who oppressed others. It signifies that those who commit wrongdoing will ultimately face consequences by God's will, emphasizing the inevitability of accountability and the triumph of righteousness over injustice.

translation: And [mention] 'Aad, when We sent upon them the barren wind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of 'Aad, who were destroyed due to their arrogance and rejection of the prophets. The 'barren wind' is a severe and punishing wind, symbolizing divine punishment that leaves no benefit or sustenance, emphasizing that God's retribution is absolute and eradicates the oppressors who refuse to heed guidance.

translation: He leaves nothing unburned when He has passed over it but makes it like scorched stubble.
interpretation: This verse highlights the totality and thoroughness of divine retribution. It signifies that when God's punishment or judgment descends upon something, nothing remains intact or unaffected; everything is reduced to a state of ruin or desolation, emphasizing the absolute power and justice of God in eradicating wrongdoing.

translation: And [remember] the people of Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time."
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly enjoyment and serves as a warning against heedlessness. It reminds us that the people of Thamud were given comfort and respite but chose to indulge and persist in their wrongdoing, ultimately leading to their destruction. The verse teaches that temporary pleasures should not distract from moral responsibility and awareness of divine accountability.

translation: So they disregarded the command of their Lord, and the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of willful neglect and rebellion against divine guidance. It serves as a warning that heedlessness toward God's commands can lead to sudden and severe punishment, even when one perceives it coming, underscoring the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: So they were unable to stand [firmly] and they were not helped.
interpretation: This verse reflects the ultimate weakness and defeat of those who opposed the truth; despite their efforts, they failed to maintain their position or gain victory, illustrating the destined triumph of justice and divine will over oppression and falsehood.

translation: And the people of Noah before; indeed, they were a disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rebellious nature of the people who lived during the time of Prophet Noah, emphasizing their persistent refusal to obey divine guidance and their moral corruption, which ultimately led to their downfall.

translation: And We have built the heaven with might, and indeed, We are [its] expander.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's powerful and deliberate creation of the universe, highlighting His control and ongoing authority over it. The phrase 'We are its expander' can be seen as a reference to the continuous expansion of the heavens, symbolizing Allah's dynamic and limitless power that sustains and extends all creation beyond initial limits.

translation: And the earth – We have spread it out, and excellent is the preparer (of space).
interpretation: This verse highlights God's deliberate act of preparing and shaping the earth to serve as a sustainable environment for life. It underscores the perfection and care in the creation, allowing humans and other creatures to live comfortably, cultivate, and find refuge. The verse invites reflection on God's wisdom and power in making the earth a suitable home.

translation: And of everything We have created pairs, that you may remember (the grace of Allah).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in creating all things in pairs, which reflects the balance and harmony in the universe. It serves as a reminder for people to recognize the signs of Allah's creation and to be mindful of His blessings, encouraging reflection and gratitude.

translation: So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse calls upon individuals to urgently turn away from sin and seek refuge in Allah alone, emphasizing that sincere repentance and reliance on God are the true means of salvation. The Prophet is informing us that his role is to deliver God's clear warning, and it is up to each person to heed it by abandoning wrongful ways and escaping to the safety and mercy of Allah.

translation: And do not associate with Allah any other deity. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the core Islamic belief in monotheism, urging believers to worship Allah alone without associating any partners or idols with Him. It also highlights the role of the Prophet as a clear and sincere warner who delivers God's message to guide people away from polytheism and towards the truth.

translation: Thus, no messenger who came before them but they said, "He is a sorcerer or madman."
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern throughout history: whenever a new messenger or prophet comes with a divine message, the people often reject him by accusing him of sorcery or insanity. It illustrates the human tendency to resist change and the truth out of fear, ignorance, or stubbornness, and it reassures believers that such opposition is a common experience in the path of delivering God's guidance.

translation: Indeed, they advised one another with it, but they are a rebellious people.
interpretation: This verse indicates that despite discussing or advising each other about the truth or guidance, certain people persist in rebellion and disobedience. It highlights the hardness of some hearts and the persistence in wrongdoing despite warnings and reminders.

translation: So turn away from them; indeed, you are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) to disengage from those who reject his message and persist in their disbelief or opposition. It reassures him that he bears no responsibility for their rejection, emphasizing that his duty is to convey the message faithfully, but guiding or acceptance lies beyond his control.

translation: And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reminding people about divine guidance and moral teachings, as such reminders serve to awaken the consciousness of believers, strengthen their faith, and encourage them to remain steadfast in their commitment to righteousness.

translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental purpose of human and jinn creation, which is to recognize and submit to the worship of the One true God. It emphasizes that all of existence is ultimately meant to serve a higher spiritual purpose beyond worldly pursuits, directing believers to align their lives according to divine guidance.

translation: I do not ask them for any provision, nor do I ask them to feed me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's reliance solely on God rather than seeking material support from people, emphasizing his role as a spiritual guide rather than one driven by worldly gain.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of Power, the Most Strong.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the ultimate source of sustenance and provision. His strength is unmatched and enduring, meaning that all needs are fulfilled through His will and power, highlighting the reliance that believers should have on Him for their livelihood and support.

translation: Surely, for those who have wronged, there are sins similar to the sins of their companions; so they should not hasten [the punishment].
interpretation: This verse implies that the consequences or punishments for those who commit injustice will correspond to the wrongs they have committed, mirroring the severity of previous wrongdoers. It warns against impatience regarding divine justice, emphasizing that God's judgment unfolds in due time, ensuring equitable recompense for every individual according to their deeds.

translation: So woe to those who disbelieve from the Day they are promised.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing the severe consequences awaiting them on the Day of Judgment, a time of inevitable reckoning and divine justice.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the Mount (Tur),
interpretation: This verse begins by invoking the name of Allah, emphasizing His mercy and grace. The oath by the Mount (Mount Sinai) serves to highlight the significance and solemnity of the message that follows, reminding the listener of the profound revelations connected to sacred places and urging attention to the divine truth delivered through the Prophet.

translation: And a written book.
interpretation: This phrase signifies that the knowledge, decrees, or revelations mentioned are preserved in a clear, well-ordered, and enduring form—emphasizing the divine wisdom and the reliability of what is recorded, as a guidance for humanity.

translation: On a spread-out sheet.
interpretation: This phrase alludes to the idea of an open and clear record or document, symbolizing transparency and the clear communication of knowledge or divine revelation. It emphasizes the importance of clarity and accessibility in conveying wisdom or commandments.

translation: And the frequently visited House (the heavens).
interpretation: This phrase refers to the 'Bayt al-Ma'mur,' a celestial house often interpreted as a counterpart to the Kaaba in the heavens, which angels continually visit in worship. It symbolizes a divine realm of constant, unceasing worship and serves as a reminder of the unseen spiritual realities beyond our world, emphasizing the importance of devotion and the eternal nature of worship in the hereafter.

translation: And the elevated ceiling,
interpretation: This phrase highlights the grandeur and magnificence of the creation surrounding us, inviting reflection on the vastness and order of the universe, which points to the greatness and creative power of the Creator.

translation: And the burning sea,
interpretation: This phrase refers to the intense heat and turmoil of the sea, which can be understood as a metaphor for the overwhelming forces of nature or trials one may face. The depiction of the sea as 'burning' emphasizes the power and severity of these challenges, reminding believers of the might of Allah's creation and the need for reliance on Him in times of difficulty.

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely occur.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of God's punishment for wrongdoing, serving as a warning to heed His commands and avoid transgression.

translation: He has no defender.
interpretation: This phrase suggests that the person in question stands alone without anyone to support or protect him, highlighting his vulnerability and isolation in the face of adversity or judgment.

translation: The Day when the heaven will sway with circular motion.
interpretation: This verse depicts the intense and overwhelming nature of the Day of Judgment, highlighting the profound cosmic upheaval that will occur, signifying a total transformation and the end of the current order, thereby invoking a sense of awe and seriousness about the ultimate accountability before God.

translation: And causes the mountains to move on their paths,
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's immense power in commanding even the seemingly immovable mountains to move according to His will, symbolizing His control over all creation and His ability to orchestrate the universe with precision.

translation: So woe on that Day to the deniers (those who reject the truth).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences awaiting those who deny the truth on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the gravity of rejecting divine guidance and the inevitable accountability that follows.

translation: Those who are engaged in vain play.
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals who occupy themselves with frivolous or worthless pursuits, neglecting matters of true importance and seriousness. It serves as a warning against wasting one's time and energy on futile activities that distract from the path of righteousness and meaningful purpose.

translation: The Day they will be summoned to the Fire of Hell with a [single] call.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable moment of accountability on the Day of Judgment when all individuals will be called to face the consequences of their deeds, emphasizing the certainty and severity of divine justice.

translation: This is the Fire which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning by affirming the reality of the punishment that the unbelievers used to reject. It underscores the consequence of denying divine truth and serves as a reminder that the reality of the hereafter’s torment is undeniable and will be witnessed by those who rejected it.

translation: Do I speak openly, or are you not seeing?
interpretation: This verse challenges the listener to reflect on their awareness and understanding. It highlights the speaker's clarity and openness in communication, implying that any misunderstanding or blindness to the message is due to the listener's lack of insight or perception rather than ambiguity in the message itself.

translation: So be patient or be impatient; indeed, it is all the same for you. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and accountability, indicating that regardless of one's reactions—patience or impatience—the consequences of one's actions are inescapable. It serves as a reminder that ultimate recompense is based solely on one's deeds, encouraging self-awareness and responsibility in conduct rather than mere emotional responses.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be amidst gardens and bliss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward awaiting the righteous (those who are conscious of God and live by His guidance). It emphasizes that their steadfastness in faith and good conduct will lead them to eternal pleasure and comfort in paradise, symbolized by gardens and the enjoyment of all that is good and pure.
