interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's intimate nearness and complete awareness of human beings, surpassing even their own self-perception and awareness. It serves as a reminder that God's presence is constant and encompassing, even if humans are unaware or fail to recognize it, highlighting the importance of consciousness of divine proximity and accountability.

translation: So why, if you are not to be repaid, do you not act righteously?
interpretation: This verse challenges the attitude of people who do not repay kindness or debt. It calls for self-reflection and urges individuals to uphold their obligations and be just, especially when they are not under compulsion to do so, highlighting the importance of integrity and moral responsibility.

translation: You will return it, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who make false claims or accusations by asserting that if they are honest and truthful, they should be able to restore or return what they have taken or allege. It underscores the importance of truthfulness and integrity, inviting people to demonstrate their sincerity through actions rather than just words.

translation: But as for one who is brought near (to Allah),
interpretation: This verse signifies the special status of those whom Allah has chosen to be close to Him, indicating that they are honored by divine grace and elevated above others in spiritual proximity.

translation: And a fragrance and a delight from the Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the pure and blissful rewards that await the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing not only their eternal happiness but also the sensory pleasures and tranquility granted by God as a manifestation of His mercy and favor.

translation: But as for one who is from the companions of the right,
interpretation: This phrase refers to those who are deemed righteous and favored by God, destined for happiness and reward in the afterlife. Being among the 'companions of the right' signifies a person who has lived a life of faith and righteous deeds, earning God's mercy and a place in Paradise.

translation: So peace be upon you from the companions of the right.
interpretation: This verse conveys a greeting of peace and a sign of honor given to those who are among the 'companions of the right,' a term used to describe the righteous and those favored by Allah on the Day of Judgment. It signifies their blessed status and the serenity that accompanies their reward in the hereafter.

translation: But as for he who is of the deniers, the misguided,
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of those who reject the truth and persist in misguidance, emphasizing the spiritual consequences of turning away from guidance and embracing falsehood.

translation: So it rained upon them with a shower of molten sulfur.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine punishment that befell a people who defied God's commands, emphasizing the severity of consequences for persistent disobedience and serving as a reminder of God's justice and power to enforce His will.

translation: And a Blaze of Hellfire.
interpretation: This phrase serves as a stern warning about the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance and engaging in sinful behavior. The 'Blaze of Hellfire' symbolizes intense punishment and suffering in the Hereafter for those who turn away from righteousness and persist in disbelief or misconduct.

translation: Indeed, this is the truth of certainty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the undeniable and absolute reality of the message being conveyed, affirming that the knowledge and guidance presented are beyond doubt and must be accepted with complete conviction.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse commands the believer to continually glorify and exalt Allah, recognizing His supreme greatness and majesty. It emphasizes the importance of remembrance and praise as a means to connect with and honor the Lord who is exalted above all.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all creation inherently praises and glorifies Allah, reflecting the perfection and harmony in the universe that stems from His power and wisdom. It reminds us that every element in existence, whether visible or unseen, is in a state of submission and recognition of Allah's authority and wisdom, encouraging humankind to acknowledge and emulate this recognition through sincere worship and obedience.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and power over all creation, highlighting that He alone controls life and death, illustrating His ultimate authority and capability to govern every aspect of existence without limitation.

translation: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Hidden; and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of God's existence and knowledge. It means that God encompasses all aspects of time and reality—He existed before anything came into being (the First), and He will remain after all ends (the Last). He is Manifest in what is evident to us and Hidden beyond our perception. Moreover, His knowledge penetrates every matter, no matter how concealed or apparent, signifying His absolute and all-encompassing awareness of everything in the universe.

translation: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then He established Himself on the Throne. He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends in it; and He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is All-Seer of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and knowledge, portraying Him as the creator who is intimately involved with His creation. His establishing upon the Throne signifies His authority and control over all existence. The verse also highlights that nothing escapes His knowledge—what goes into or comes out of the earth, and what falls from or rises into the skies. Moreover, Allah's presence is not confined to any place; He is always near to His creation, aware of their actions, reminding believers of His encompassing awareness and need to remain conscious of Him in all circumstances.

translation: His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ultimate authority of Allah over the entire universe. It serves as a reminder that all events, decisions, and matters eventually come back under His control, highlighting the transient nature of worldly affairs and the certainty of divine judgment and wisdom.

translation: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse signifies Allah's supreme control over time and natural phenomena, illustrating His capacity to intertwine night and day seamlessly. It also highlights His omniscience, emphasizing that nothing hidden within the depths of human hearts escapes His knowledge.

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger and spend out of that in which He has made you successors. For those who have believed among you and spent, there will be a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith coupled with responsible stewardship and generosity. It highlights that believers are not only to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, but also to actively use the resources entrusted to them by Allah in a charitable and positive manner. The promise of a great reward serves as encouragement for believers to fulfill their duties of spending in the way of Allah, demonstrating that true belief is manifested through sincere and selfless actions.

translation: And why do you not believe in Allah, while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has taken your covenant if you should be believers?
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsibility and accountability of the believers who have been invited by the Messenger to have faith in Allah. It reminds them that their covenant with Allah is a serious commitment that must be upheld, emphasizing the importance of sincere belief and adherence to the teachings brought by the Messenger as a means to fulfill their covenant with Allah.

translation: He it is Who sends down clear verses upon His servant, so that He may bring you out from darkness into light. And indeed, Allah is kind and merciful toward you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of clear signs and guidance through the Prophet is a means by which Allah leads humanity from misguidance, ignorance, and hardship (symbolized by darkness) into understanding, righteousness, and ease (symbolized by light). It highlights Allah's compassion and mercy as the motivation behind sending guidance to facilitate spiritual and moral transformation.

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah, while to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest [of Makkah] and fought [in the cause of Allah] and those who did so afterward. Allah has promised the best [reward] to both. And Allah, with what you do, is acquainted.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend in the cause of Allah, emphasizing that Allah is the ultimate owner of all that exists. It draws a distinction between those who made sacrifices and strove before the key victory (the conquest of Makkah) and those who did so after, highlighting that the early supporters hold a higher rank due to their readiness amid greater trial. Nevertheless, Allah promises good reward to all who strive sincerely. The verse calls for generosity and steadfastness, reminding that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions.

translation: Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him and have a noble reward?
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to give in charity and support righteous causes, assuring them that any act of generosity made for the sake of Allah will be greatly rewarded and multiplied, emphasizing the immense mercy and justice of Allah in recompensing good deeds.

translation: The Day when you will see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right hands, [saying], "Good tidings for you today: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally." That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound reward and honor granted to true believers on the Day of Judgment, symbolized by the light that leads and accompanies them — a manifestation of their righteousness and divine favor. This light represents guidance, purity, and salvation, leading them to eternal bliss in Paradise, signified by gardens beneath which rivers flow. It conveys that their faith and good deeds in this life have secured them an everlasting, exalted state, marking the ultimate success and fulfillment of human purpose.

translation: The Day the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." Then a wall will be erected between them with a door, its interior containing mercy, and on the outside of it is torment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate division between the sincere believers and the hypocrites on the Day of Judgment. The hypocrites, who pretended to believe but lacked true faith, will seek the light and mercy of the believers but will be denied access. The wall with a door symbolizes a clear boundary set by divine justice, separating those granted mercy from those facing punishment. It emphasizes that faith must be genuine; reliance on others' faith or superficial belief will not suffice when reality unfolds in the Hereafter.

translation: They will call to them, "Did we not hold firmly with you?" They will say, "Indeed, but you tried to tempt yourselves and awaited, and you doubted, and false hopes deluded you until there came the command of Allah. And the deception of Allah deceived you."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of wavering in faith and relying on false hopes or delaying righteous action. It conveys that hesitation, doubt, and self-delusion can lead believers away from steadfastness, ultimately resulting in their downfall when divine judgment arrives, reminding us that true reliance must be on Allah rather than illusions or procrastination.

translation: So today, no ransom will be accepted from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your patron, and what an evil destination!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the finality of accountability on the Day of Judgment, where no worldly wealth or ransom can avert divine justice. Those who rejected faith will find their only recourse is the Fire, highlighting the consequences of disbelief and the importance of sincere faith and righteous conduct before that inevitable moment.

translation: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth, and that they would not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long time passed over them, so their hearts hardened? And many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers to cultivate a deep and genuine reverence for the remembrance of Allah and divine truth, emphasizing the necessity of heartfelt humility. It warns against the spiritual stagnation and hardness of heart that befell previous communities who, over time, neglected the guidance they were given, leading to moral waywardness. The verse calls for constant spiritual renewal and attentiveness to divine guidance to prevent such deterioration.

translation: Know that Allah causes the earth to come to life after its death. Indeed, We have made clear to you the signs so that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power to revive the earth after it has been barren or lifeless, symbolizing His ability to bring life from death and reminding us of the resurrection. The signs Allah presents are meant to help us reflect and comprehend the reality of His existence and the hereafter, encouraging us to develop awareness and faith.

translation: Indeed, the men who believe and the women who believe and give charity and lend Allah a goodly loan - it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of faith combined with righteous actions such as charity and financial support for the sake of Allah. It shows that Allah rewards sincere believers who spend their wealth in His way abundantly, promising not only the multiplication of their good deeds but also an honorable and lasting reward. It encourages believers to trust in Allah's generosity and to contribute selflessly, assuring them of divine compensation beyond worldly return.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the truthful ones and the witnesses with their Lord. They will have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those will be companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between true believers, who affirm faith in Allah and His messengers and are thus called truthful and honored witnesses before God, receiving both reward and enlightenment, and disbelievers who reject divine signs and face severe consequences, emphasizing the link between faith, spiritual honor, and ultimate destiny.

translation: Know that the life of this world is but play, amusement, decoration, boasting among you, and rivalry in wealth and children. It is like the rain whose growth pleases the tillers; then it withers and you see it yellowed; then it becomes dry debris. And in the Hereafter is a severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the worldly life is transient and deceptive, filled with distractions and superficial pursuits that captivate people temporarily but ultimately lead to nothing enduring. It compares worldly life to vegetation that flourishes briefly but inevitably fades and perishes. The verse warns believers not to be deluded by temporary pleasures and rivalries, urging them to focus on the eternal Hereafter, where true success lies in Allah's forgiveness and pleasure, contrasting the fleeting nature of this world with the permanence of the next.

translation: Race towards the forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah which He bestows upon whom He wills; and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to strive eagerly and urgently to attain Allah's forgiveness and entry into Paradise, emphasizing that this reward is immense and boundless, reflecting the greatness of God's mercy. It reminds that such blessings are granted by Allah's grace and favor, not merely by human effort, and underscores the importance of faith in Allah and His messengers as the path to receiving divine reward.

translation: No disaster strikes upon the earth or within yourselves except that it is in a decree before We bring it into existence. Indeed, that is upon Allah easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all events, including hardships and calamities, are part of Allah's predetermined plan and knowledge. It teaches us that nothing occurs by chance or without divine wisdom, and this knowledge should bring comfort and trust in Allah's control over all aspects of life.

translation: So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult excessively over what He has given you. And Allah does not like every self-deluded and boastful person.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to maintain a balanced attitude toward life's ups and downs: not to be saddened by losses or failures nor become arrogant and overly proud of their successes or blessings. It warns against pride and arrogance, highlighting that such feelings are disliked by Allah, thus encouraging humility and contentment regardless of one's circumstances.

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess. And whoever turns away - then indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of those who not only hoard their wealth but also encourage others to be miserly, revealing a character focused on restriction and lack of generosity. It cautions believers to avoid following such attitudes and emphasizes that true wealth and praise belong to Allah alone, who is beyond need and fully self-sufficient. Thus, one should trust in Allah's sufficiency and generosity rather than cling to worldly possessions out of fear or selfishness.

translation: Indeed, We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs and revealed with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people, and so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine wisdom in sending messengers with clear evidence and revealed guidance, alongside establishing justice as a fundamental principle for society. The mention of iron symbolizes both strength in conflict and practical benefits, reflecting how God provides means for support and testing. Ultimately, this verse emphasizes that God's power is manifest and that faithfulness and support for the divine cause are known to Him beyond human perception.

translation: And certainly We sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their descendants prophethood and the Scripture; yet among them is he who is guided, and many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's deliberate continuation of divine guidance through chosen prophets and revealed scriptures within certain lineages, emphasizing that despite this privilege, individuals possess free will to accept guidance or rebel, illustrating the diverse responses of humanity to divine messages.

translation: Then We sent after them Our messengers and followed [them] with Jesus, the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. But monasticism, which they innovated, We did not prescribe for them as a duty. They did not observe it with due observance. So We gave those among them who believed their reward, but many of them were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's guidance through successive messengers and the gift of the Gospel to Jesus (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that the qualities of compassion and mercy were instilled in his followers, yet certain practices, like monasticism, were human innovations not mandated by God. The verse serves as a reminder that true obedience lies in sincere adherence to God's commands, not in mere outward rituals or innovations, and that while believers are rewarded, many stray from the right path due to disobedience.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will grant you a double portion of His mercy and provide for you a light by which you may walk and forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith combined with reverence for Allah (God) and trust in His Messenger. When believers fulfill these conditions, Allah responds generously by bestowing abundant mercy, spiritual illumination to guide their actions, and forgiveness for their shortcomings. The promise underscores the comprehensive nature of divine grace, encompassing compassion, guidance, and pardon, which together nurture a believer's growth and righteousness.

translation: So that the People of the Scripture may not boast that they have power over anything of the bounty of Allah. Indeed, all bounty is in the Hand of Allah; He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings and favors come solely from Allah, and no group, including the People of the Scripture, should claim superiority or control over divine grace. It serves to remind humanity that divine favor is not tied to lineage, status, or prior revelations but is granted by Allah according to His wisdom and will.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of the one who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah. And Allah hears your dialogue; indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's attentive awareness to the grievances and disputes of His servants, emphasizing that no complaint or conflict, even those most personal and private, escapes His knowledge. It reassures believers that Allah not only hears their words but also perceives the underlying feelings and realities, highlighting His just and compassionate nature in addressing human affairs.

translation: Those among you who declare their wives as their mothers—while their mothers are only those who gave birth to them—and who say an objectionable and false statement, indeed, Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse addresses a pre-Islamic custom where a man would declare his wife as his mother to sever marital relations, which is a false and harmful practice. The verse emphasizes the true biological bond between mother and child and condemns this wrongful speech as objectionable and deceitful, while highlighting Allah's attribute of forgiveness towards sincere repentance.

translation: And those who declare their wives to be like their mothers and then [wish to] go back on what they said - then [there must be] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished with. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the severe oath known as 'Zihar,' where a man equates his wife to a close female relative, thereby forbidding marital relations. It prescribes the expiation of freeing a slave before they can resume intimacy, emphasizing accountability and the importance of rectifying wrongful speech. The verse serves as a moral deterrent against impulsive declarations that harm relationships, underlining God's awareness of all actions and intentions.

translation: But if anyone is ill or on a journey, the same number (of days) [should be made up] from other days. And those who are unable to fast should feed sixty poor persons. That is so you may complete the period and that you may exalt Allah for His guidance to you, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and flexibility within Islamic law concerning fasting during Ramadan. It recognizes that some may be genuinely unable to fast due to illness or travel and thus provides an alternative way to fulfill their obligation by making up missed days later. For those utterly unable to fast at all, compensatory charity serves both as a means of social support and spiritual responsibility. The verse underscores the balance between obedience to divine commands and compassion for human circumstances, encouraging believers to appreciate God's guidance and maintain faithfulness.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger have been struck down as those before them were struck down. And We have revealed clear verses; and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that hostility toward Allah and His Messenger leads to defeat and humiliation, as experienced by previous peoples who rejected divine guidance. It underscores the inevitability of consequences for rejecting the truth and defying God's commands, affirming that clear signs have been provided, yet disbelief results only in disgrace and suffering.

translation: The Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, but they have forgotten it; and Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of the Day of Resurrection when all individuals will be brought forth to account for their deeds. Although humans often forget or overlook the tally of their actions, Allah has meticulously recorded everything and serves as the ultimate Witness. It reminds us that nothing escapes Divine knowledge, emphasizing the importance of living with awareness of accountability before God.

translation: Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? No secret conversation of three is there, but He is their fourth, nor of five, but He is their sixth, nor less than that or more except that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did, on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive knowledge and presence. It highlights that no matter how secret or small a gathering, Allah is always aware and present with them. This serves to remind believers that their actions and intentions are never hidden from Allah, encouraging sincerity and mindfulness. The verse also underlines that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will fully disclose every deed, affirming His justice and omniscience.

translation: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel but then return to that which they were forbidden, secretly conferring in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting that Allah has not greeted you with, and say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Hell is sufficient for them; they will enter it, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who deliberately conceal their sinful intentions and rebellious behavior, disobeying divine commands while pretending to show respect. Their internal arrogance and disregard for divine punishment reveal the severity of their moral failure, resulting in their destined punishment in Hell. The verse warns against duplicity and treachery in faith, emphasizing that true devotion must be sincere and consistent, not disguised by false appearances or hypocrisy.

translation: O you who have believed, when you converse privately, do not converse with sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, but converse with righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse teaches that believers should be mindful of the content and purpose of their private conversations, ensuring they avoid discussions that involve sinful acts, conflict, or disrespect towards the Messenger. Instead, their dialogues should be rooted in goodness, righteousness, and consciousness of God, reflecting a higher moral and spiritual standard. The emphasis on fearing Allah signifies accountability before Him, reminding believers that all gatherings and actions are ultimately known to God and will be judged accordingly.

translation: Secret counsel is only from Satan, to make those who have believed grieve, but he will not harm them except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse teaches that scheming and plotting in secret can stem from Satan's influence, intending to cause grief among believers. However, such harm cannot actually affect them without Allah's will, highlighting the ultimate protection and control of Allah over all events. Therefore, true believers are encouraged to place their trust fully in Allah's power and wisdom, knowing that He safeguards them against any harm.

translation: O you who have believed, when you are told, "Make room" in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when you are told, "Arise," then arise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility, respect, and discipline in social and communal settings among believers. It teaches that obedience to such commands, even in everyday situations, is rewarded by Allah through elevation in status and knowledge. The verse highlights that spiritual and intellectual growth is linked to one's faith and willingness to maintain order and respect in gatherings, and that Allah's knowledge encompasses all actions, encouraging sincere and mindful conduct.

translation: O you who have believed, when you converse privately with the Messenger, present before your conversation a charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [the means], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches believers to show respect and sincerity when approaching the Prophet Muhammad with private matters by offering a form of charity beforehand. This act serves to purify their intentions, emphasizing the importance of humility and the spiritual value associated with giving. It also reflects the principle that sincere communication with the Messenger, or by extension with divine guidance, should be accompanied by an inner purification and generosity. If one cannot afford to give charity, the verse reassures that God's mercy and forgiveness encompass such limitations, highlighting the balance between striving for good deeds and reliance on divine compassion.

translation: Do you fear that you will hasten the giving of alms before your private consultations? So when you do not, and Allah has pardoned you, then establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hesitation some believers have in offering charity immediately during their private consultations, highlighting God's awareness of their actions and intentions. It emphasizes that while timely charity is commendable, what matters more is sincere repentance, establishing regular prayers, fulfilling obligatory almsgiving, and obedience to Allah and His Messenger, reminding believers that God comprehensively knows their deeds and motives.

translation: Have you not considered those who took as allies a people upon whom is the wrath of Allah? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to falsehood while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly and consequences of aligning oneself with those who bear Allah's wrath, indicating a betrayal of one's own community and values. It warns against forming insincere and hypocritical alliances that are not grounded in truth or mutual trust, as such relationships lead to estrangement and divine disapproval.

translation: Indeed, Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, they were evil in what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and severity of divine retribution awaiting those who persist in wrongful and evil actions. It serves as a warning that the consequences of their misconduct are not only justified but have been decreed by Allah, highlighting the moral responsibility individuals bear for their deeds.

translation: They took their oaths as a cover and (thus) hindered (people) from the way of Allah. For them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grievous sin of using oaths insincerely as a means to deceive and obstruct others from following the path of Allah. It warns against hypocrisy and emphasizes that such deliberate misguidance and betrayal will lead to severe consequences, reflecting the seriousness of hindering truth and righteousness.

translation: Neither their wealth nor their children will benefit them against Allah in any way. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that worldly wealth and progeny cannot shield a person from Allah's judgment. True protection and salvation depend solely on one's deeds and God's mercy, not on material possessions or social status. It serves as a warning about relying on such things for security in the Hereafter.

translation: On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him just as they swear to you, thinking that they are upon something [true]. Indeed, they are the liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delusion of those who rely on their oaths and false assurances to escape accountability. On the Day of Judgment, their attempts to defend themselves with these oaths will be futile, as Allah will bring forth the reality of their falsehood, revealing their claims as lies and exposing their misguided confidence.

translation: Then Satan made them forget the remembrance of Allah; those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan - they will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Satan's influence leads individuals to forget the remembrance of God, detaching them from divine guidance and moral compass. Being part of Satan's party signifies allegiance to misguidance and evil, resulting ultimately in loss and failure both in this life and the hereafter.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger - those are among the most disgraced.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who show enmity towards Allah and His Messenger place themselves in a position of deep dishonor and humiliation, both in this life and the hereafter, as a consequence of their hostility and rejection of divine guidance.

translation: Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the definitive decree from Allah that He and His messengers will ultimately triumph over falsehood and opposition. It underscores the certainty of divine victory and reassures believers that despite challenges, the truth upheld by Allah's messengers will prevail due to Allah's supreme power and authority.

translation: You will not find any people who believe in Allah and the Last Day that they would befriend those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, sons, brothers, or relatives. Such are the ones whose hearts Allah has inscribed with faith and strengthened with a spirit from Him. He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the Party of Allah. Indeed, the Party of Allah— they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers prioritize their faith and allegiance to Allah and His Messenger over all other relationships, even the closest family ties. Their loyalty is defined by their commitment to uphold the principles of Islam and reject opposition to divine guidance. The inward transformation—faith inscribed in their hearts and strengthened by divine support—enables them to endure challenges and remain steadfast. Their ultimate reward is eternal bliss in Paradise, signifying that spiritual allegiance and righteousness transcend earthly bonds and result in true success.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; and He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal glorification of Allah by all creation, highlighting that every being, whether in the heavens or on earth, acknowledges His greatness. It underscores Allah's attributes of might and wisdom, reminding us that His power is absolute and His decisions are guided by perfect wisdom, encouraging believers to submit to His will with trust and reverence.

translation: He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but Allah came upon them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their own houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So, take a lesson, O people of insight.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how reliance on worldly means of protection, such as fortresses or power, cannot ultimately safeguard against the divine decree. It emphasizes that Allah's will is paramount and can subvert human expectations, instilling fear and overcoming even seemingly impregnable defenses. The destruction of their own homes symbolizes the self-inflicted consequences of opposing divine guidance. The verse calls on believers to reflect deeply on these events to understand the futility of arrogance and the importance of submitting to God's will.

translation: And if Allah had not decreed exile upon them, He would have punished them in this world; and for them is the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse reveals that divine punishment can manifest in various forms and timelines; while immediate worldly retribution may be withheld, the ultimate consequences in the Hereafter remain certain. It highlights Allah's wisdom in appointing exile as a form of trial and consequence, balancing justice with mercy, reminding believers of the seriousness of disobedience and the inescapable accountability in the life to come.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah – then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the serious consequences of defying the commandments of Allah and His Messenger. It serves as a warning that resistance against divine guidance leads to severe punishment, emphasizing the importance of obedience and submission to the commands of God to attain peace and avoid divine wrath.

translation: Whatever palm branches you cut off or leave standing on their roots, it is by the permission of Allah, and so that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all events, including the cutting or leaving of palm branches, occur by Allah's will and decree. It highlights that Allah's permission underlies all actions, even those that seem mundane or natural to us. Furthermore, it serves as a reminder that those who act in defiance of divine guidance and rebel against righteousness will ultimately face humiliation and disgrace as part of Allah's plan.

translation: And whatever Allah bestowed on His Messenger from them, you did not spur for it any horses or camels, but Allah grants power to His messengers over whom He wills. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the spoils and blessings granted to the Prophet Muhammad were not a result of the efforts or material means of the believers but by the divine will and power of Allah. It highlights that victory and gain come from Allah's decree and authority, not merely through human striving or military strength.

translation: Whatever Allah has bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the towns is for Allah, the Messenger, the kindred, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, so that it will not (merely) circulate among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of equitable distribution of wealth that Allah grants to His Messenger, emphasizing that it should be shared among specific vulnerable and deserving groups to prevent wealth concentration among the rich. It also establishes the authority of the Prophet in matters of giving and forbidding, obligating the believers to obey him, while instilling fear of Allah's strict punishment to ensure adherence. Fundamentally, the verse advocates social justice and obedience within the Muslim community to maintain harmony and prevent inequality.

translation: [It is] for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, seeking the favor of Allah and His approval, and aiding Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the noble sacrifice of the poor emigrants who left their homes and possessions for the sake of Allah. It emphasizes the sincerity and commitment of those who endure hardship seeking divine favor and aiding the cause of Allah and His Messenger. Their truthfulness lies not just in their words but in their steadfast actions and intentions, showing that true faith manifests through sincere sacrifice and support for righteousness.

translation: And those who have settled in the home and in faith before them love those who emigrated to them, and they find no need in their hearts for what they have been given, and they prefer others over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul — it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of true believers who, despite having limited means, selflessly prefer others to themselves without feeling envy or scarcity. It emphasizes the virtue of generosity and hospitality among the faithful and defines success as being free from the selfishness and stinginess of the soul.

translation: And those who came after them say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound prayer for unity, forgiveness, and the removal of bitterness among believers. It emphasizes the importance of compassion and brotherhood within the faith community, asking God to cleanse hearts from hatred and to unite all believers across generations in mutual love and mercy.

translation: Do you not see those who hypocritically say to their disbelieving brethren among the People of the Book, "If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you?" And if they are fought, they will surely aid you. And Allah bears witness that they are surely liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicity of the hypocrites who deceive both the believers and the disbelievers. They make outward promises of loyalty and support to the disbelievers but have no intention to fulfill them. Their false claims are exposed by Allah's testimony, indicating that hypocrisy involves deceit and betrayal in matters of faith and allegiance.

translation: If they are driven out, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought against, they will not aid them; and if they are helped, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the unreliable nature of certain allies who, in moments of adversity, fail to support or remain loyal. It serves as a lesson on the importance of discernment in alliances, emphasizing that some may abandon or betray when support or loyalty is most needed.

translation: Indeed, you (O Prophet) are more feared in their hearts than Allah; that is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided fear and awe that some people harbor toward the Prophet, which surpasses their fear of Allah. It indicates a spiritual blindness or lack of true understanding, as their hearts are veiled from recognizing the truth and fearing the rightful authority, Allah. The verse points to the importance of proper understanding and wisdom in matters of faith, urging believers to direct their reverence appropriately.

translation: They do not fight you all together except within fortified towns or from behind walls. Their strength is severe among themselves. You would think they are all together, but their hearts are diverse. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of a people who engage in conflict only under certain conditions, often relying on fortifications or defensive positions, which suggests a lack of unified courage or strategy. Their apparent unity is deceptive; in reality, they are divided in their intentions and resolve. The verse serves as a reminder that outward appearances of strength may conceal inner disunity and irrationality, emphasizing the importance of discernment when assessing adversaries or situations.

translation: Like those before them. They tasted the evil consequences of their conduct, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the consequences faced by previous peoples who rejected guidance and committed wrongdoing are a warning for those who follow. It emphasizes that turning away from divine guidance leads inevitably to suffering and painful punishment, underscoring the importance of learning from history and adhering to righteousness.

translation: The example of Satan is when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive nature of Satan, who entices humans to disbelief by pretending to support them, but abandons them at their moment of need, revealing his true fear of Allah and highlighting the individual's vulnerability when they follow such misguided advice.

translation: So the outcome of both of them was that they will abide eternally in the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that persistent injustice and wrongdoing lead to severe consequences in the Hereafter. It serves as a warning that the ultimate fate of those who oppress and act unjustly is eternal punishment, underscoring the seriousness of moral responsibility and accountability before God.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow — and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to be conscious of their actions and their consequences in the hereafter. It urges an ongoing self-assessment to ensure that one's deeds are aligned with righteousness, reinforcing that Allah is aware of all actions and intentions. The admonition to "fear Allah" serves as a reminder of accountability and encourages mindfulness, prompting individuals to prepare earnestly for the Day of Judgment by living a life of piety and good conduct.

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequences of neglecting the remembrance and consciousness of Allah. When a person forgets their Creator, they thereby lose their own true self-awareness and moral compass, leading to inner confusion and moral corruption. It serves as a warning that abandonment of God's guidance results in a loss of identity and righteousness, ultimately causing one to deviate from the path of truth and become rebellious against divine commands.

translation: The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the ones who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound difference between those who earn Paradise and those destined for Hellfire, highlighting that true success and ultimate victory lie in being among the people of Paradise, who have lived righteously and earned Allah's mercy.

translation: If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the immense weight, majesty, and seriousness of the Qur'an's message, emphasizing that even the most solid and immovable of creations, like a mountain, would be overwhelmed and humbled by the profound reality of God's words. It serves as a metaphor to inspire humans to recognize the depth of divine guidance and to approach the Qur'an with reverence and reflection, prompting a heartfelt submission and sincere contemplation of its teachings.

translation: He is Allah, there is no deity except Him, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and singularity of Allah as the sole deity, affirming His exclusive right to be worshipped. It highlights His all-encompassing knowledge, both of the unseen realities beyond human perception and the visible world that we witness. Furthermore, it attributes to Him mercy and compassion, underscoring that His governance and interaction with creation are rooted in kindness and care.

translation: He is Allah, besides Whom there is no deity; the Sovereign, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Protector, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and unparalleled nature of Allah, highlighting His perfect attributes that distinguish Him from all creation. It asserts His absolute sovereignty and transcendence, denying any partners or associates, thus reminding believers to recognize and worship only Him with purity and sincerity.

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth glorifies Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's unique and encompassing power in creation, emphasizing that He alone has the ability to create and shape all existence with perfect wisdom and might. The mention of His beautiful names signifies that His attributes are numerous and noble, forming the basis for understanding and relating to the Divine. The universal glorification by all beings in the heavens and earth reflects the inherent acknowledgment of His sovereignty and perfection, reminding believers of the constant presence and majesty of God in every aspect of life.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, showing them affection while they have disbelieved in the truth which has come to you, expelling the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord, if you have gone forth for jihad in My cause and seeking My pleasure. You show them affection, but I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against forming close bonds with those who are hostile to Islam and have opposed the Prophet, especially when such alliances contradict their faith and struggle in the path of Allah. It emphasizes the inner conflict between outward show of friendship and hidden disbelief or opposition. True loyalty lies with Allah and those who uphold His guidance, and to abandon that for alliances with enemies leads one away from the right path.

translation: If they get hold of you, they will be your enemies and will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns believers about the severity of hostility from certain adversaries who, if given power over the believers, will act with enmity and harm both physically and verbally. It underscores the intensity of their opposition, grounded not merely in superficial disagreement but in a desire for the believers to abandon their faith altogether. The verse serves to alert the believers to the seriousness of such opposition and to remain steadfast despite these challenges.

translation: Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will judge between you. And Allah is All-Seer of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, worldly relationships and ties of kinship will hold no advantage or protection; individual deeds and accountability will be the true measure. It serves as a reminder that reliance should be placed on righteous actions and conscious awareness of Allah, rather than on family connections or social status.

translation: You had an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever, until you believe in Allah alone." Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have no power to benefit you from Allah at all. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the firm stance of Ibrahim (Abraham) and his followers in dissociating themselves from idolatry and polytheism, highlighting the principle of monotheism as a foundational belief. It shows the moral courage required to break from falsehood even at the cost of enmity, while also illustrating compassion in Ibrahim's continued prayers for his father's guidance, acknowledging human limitations and ultimate reliance on God's wisdom and judgment.

translation: Our Lord, do not make us [objects of] trial for the disbelievers and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a sincere supplication seeking protection from becoming a source of temptation or cause for misguidance to disbelievers, alongside asking for forgiveness, recognizing that Allah alone possesses the power and wisdom to guide, punish, or forgive as He wills.

translation: Indeed, for you in them is a good example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the exemplary character and conduct of the Prophet and the righteous predecessors, serving as models for those who place their hope in God and the hereafter. It also reminds that turning away from these exemplars does not diminish God's self-sufficiency or worthiness of praise, highlighting that guidance depends on sincere seeking by the believer.

translation: Perhaps Allah will establish between you and those whom you have enmity a bond of affection. And Allah is All-Powerful. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that enmity and hostility between people are not necessarily permanent and that Allah Almighty has the power to transform relationships marked by hostility into ones of love and harmony. It highlights the divine ability to bring about reconciliation and peace, encouraging believers to hold hope for forgiveness and the healing of divisions, knowing that Allah's mercy and power can overcome enmity.

translation: Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion nor expel you from your homes to be righteous toward them and act justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and good treatment towards those who do not oppose Muslims with hostility or aggression. It instructs believers to discern and separate between enemies and peaceful individuals, promoting fairness and kindness even towards those who are not part of their community as long as they show no animosity. The verse highlights that true justice transcends enmity and is beloved by Allah.

translation: Indeed, Allah only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and support others in your expulsion that you may befriend them. And whoever befriends them - then those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the prohibition of forming alliances or friendly relations applies specifically to those who have shown hostility by fighting believers due to their faith, driving them out of their homes, and aiding in their displacement. It underscores the principle that loyalty should not be extended to those who actively oppress or harm the community, as doing so would be an act of injustice and betrayal.

translation: O you who have believed, when believing women immigrate to you, test them. Allah is most knowing of their faith. And if you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful [husbands] for them. And give the disbelievers what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you give them their due compensation. And do not hold onto the disbelievers in marriage, asking for return while you yourselves have contracted obligations. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of ensuring the sincerity and faith of women who migrate to join the Muslim community, underscoring Allah's knowledge of their true belief. Once established as believers, they are to be protected and not returned to disbelieving husbands, signifying the safeguarding of their faith and dignity. The verse also stipulates fairness in financial dealings during such transitions and prohibits clinging to marital ties with disbelievers for worldly gain, which reflects Allah's just and wise governance in maintaining the integrity and harmony of the Muslim community.

translation: And if any of your wives are inclined toward disbelief, and you have made a marital agreement with them, then there is no sin upon you if you divorce them after being harmed. And give them their due compensation according to what they have spent. And fear Allah, in Whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where a believer's spouse turns towards disbelief during marriage. It guides believers that if such a situation occurs, they are permitted to end the marriage without fault, provided they compensate their spouse fairly for what they have spent. The instruction emphasizes maintaining justice and piety, urging believers to fear Allah who is the basis of their faith even amidst personal hardship.

translation: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor will they steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a false statement they have fabricated between their hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines a covenant of faith and moral commitment between the believing women and the Prophet, emphasizing sincere dedication to monotheism and ethical conduct. It underscores that true faith manifests in both belief and actions, including refraining from major sins and injustices. The Prophet's role includes accepting such sincere pledges and seeking God's forgiveness for the believers, reflecting divine mercy and readiness to pardon sincere repentance.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take a people whom Allah has become angry with as allies, for they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse cautions the believers against forming close alliances or seeking support from groups upon whom Allah's wrath has descended, as their rejection of faith and the Hereafter reflects a deep spiritual loss. Trusting in or aligning with such people can lead believers away from the path of righteousness, undermining their faith and spiritual well-being.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah; and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every creation in the heavens and the earth continuously glorifies and exalts Allah, reflecting His sovereignty and perfection. It underlines that Allah's might and wisdom govern all existence, and thus all creation is engaged in acknowledging His greatness in their own manner.

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers to align their speech with their actions, emphasizing the importance of honesty and integrity. It warns against hypocrisy, where one professes faith or intentions but fails to enact them, highlighting that true belief is reflected not only in words but also in deeds.

translation: It is greatly disliked by Allah that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and integrity in one's speech and actions. It warns against the hypocrisy of making promises or declarations that one does not intend to fulfill, highlighting that such behavior is displeasing to Allah and undermines trust and moral responsibility in society.

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they were a [single] structure joined firmly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity, discipline, and cohesiveness among those who strive in the path of God. Just as a solid building is composed of tightly interlocked bricks, the believers are called to maintain solidarity and mutual support, which strengthens their collective strength and effectiveness in achieving just causes.

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you hurt me while you certainly know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?" But when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of persistent rejection and opposition to divine guidance. It emphasizes that when a community knowingly resists a messenger sent to them, their hearts become hardened and further astray by divine decree, indicating that deliberate and continuous rebellion against truth leads to spiritual loss and misguidance.

translation: And when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, 'O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the message of Prophet Jesus (Isa) as a true messenger who affirmed previous scriptures and foretold the coming of another prophet named Ahmad (commonly understood to be Prophet Muhammad). It underscores the repeated pattern where clear signs and truthful messages from God are often met with rejection and disbelief by some people, illustrating their stubbornness and resistance to accepting divine guidance even when it is manifest.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of falsely attributing lies to Allah, especially when one is aware of the truth and is called to submit sincerely to Islam. Such misconduct not only transgresses divine boundaries but also indicates a conscious rejection of guidance. Consequently, those who engage in this injustice are deprived of Allah’s guidance, emphasizing that turning to falsehood in the face of clear invitation leads to spiritual misguidance and loss.

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of the efforts of those who oppose divine truth; despite their attempts to suppress or negate it verbally or otherwise, the light of Allah—representing guidance, truth, and divine wisdom—will inevitably prevail and cannot be extinguished. It reassures believers that divine truth is unstoppable and protected by God's will, regardless of the opposition it faces.

translation: He it is Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to establish the truth and guidance that transcends all other beliefs. It signifies that despite the resistance or rejection by those who associate partners with God, the message of Islam will ultimately prevail due to its divine origin and inherent truth.

translation: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: This verse invites the believers to consider a spiritual investment or commitment that offers ultimate salvation and protection from severe consequences in the Hereafter, emphasizing the merit of actions grounded in faith and righteousness over worldly gains.

translation: You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of true faith expressed not only through belief but also through active struggle and sacrifice in the path of God. It highlights that committing one's resources and life for a worthy divine cause leads to a higher spiritual reward and greater benefit than mere passive belief.

translation: He forgives your sins and admits you into gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of Eternity; that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vast mercy of God, promising forgiveness of sins and a reward of eternal paradise to the believers. It highlights that true success and ultimate happiness lie not in worldly gains but in God's forgiveness and eternal bliss in the hereafter.

translation: And [another] that you love - victory from Allah and an imminent conquest; and give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse assures the believers that what they long for, whether it is victory, relief, or the fulfillment of their noble aspirations, will be granted by Allah's help and an imminent victory. It emphasizes the certainty and nearness of divine support, encouraging the believers to remain steadfast and hopeful, as their patience and faith will be rewarded with triumph and glad tidings.

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, just as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who will be my supporters for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed, while a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to actively uphold and defend the cause of Allah with the same devotion and commitment shown by the disciples of Jesus. It emphasizes that true faith involves taking a clear and steadfast stand for righteousness and supporting the divine mission, which ultimately leads to the triumph of the believers over their adversaries through divine assistance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah—the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal and comprehensive nature of worship and glorification of Allah. It teaches that all created beings, whether in the heavens or on the earth, are engaged in the praise of their Creator, acknowledging His absolute sovereignty, holiness, power, and wisdom. This reflects the intrinsic order and submission embedded in the cosmos, reminding believers of Allah's unique and exalted attributes and encouraging them to align themselves with this universal act of worship.

translation: He it is Who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they had been before in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and guidance of God in sending a messenger from among the unlettered who would not only recite divine revelations but also purify their hearts and impart knowledge. It highlights the transformative nature of the prophet's mission, bringing those who were in evident error into enlightenment and understanding through scripture and wisdom.

translation: And others from them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there are some who have not yet come to the same understanding or status as those mentioned before, indicating a future inclusion or consequence. It highlights God's ultimate authority and wisdom in managing the affairs of people and the unfolding of events according to His divine plan.

translation: That is the grace of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's grace and blessings are bestowed according to His wisdom and will, underscoring that human efforts are secondary to divine favor. It reminds believers to recognize that all good and success come solely by Allah's generous will, reflecting His immense power and mercy.

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like that of a donkey carrying books. Evil is the example of the people who deny the verses of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and disgrace of possessing knowledge or responsibility without proper understanding, action, or respect for it. It emphasizes that simply having sacred knowledge or scripture without living by its teachings is as fruitless as a donkey carrying books it cannot comprehend. Furthermore, it warns that rejecting divine signs and guidance leads to a state where one remains lost and misled, as Allah does not guide those who knowingly persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Say, "O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah besides the people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim a special closeness or favor with God to demonstrate the sincerity of their claim by wishing for death. It highlights that true allegiance to God is not just verbal but requires readiness to face the ultimate test—death. The verse implies that true faith involves acceptance of life's trials and the hereafter, rather than vain claims of exclusivity or superiority.

translation: And they will never wish for the wrong they did to have been done to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that those who commit injustice will not desire others to experience the same harm they inflicted, highlighting the intrinsic recognition of wrongdoing. It emphasizes that Allah's knowledge encompasses all acts of injustice, assuring that no wrongdoing escapes His awareness or judgment.

translation: Say, "The death from which you flee will surely meet you; then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitability of death and the futility of attempting to escape it. Death is not merely an end but a transition where every soul returns to God, the All-Knowing. It serves as a warning that our worldly actions are accountable and will be known in the afterlife, urging us to live conscientiously and prepare for the ultimate meeting with our Creator.

translation: O you who have believed, when [the call] is made for the prayer on Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing communal worship and remembrance of Allah over worldly affairs, especially during the Friday prayer. It instructs believers to abandon their economic activities promptly when the call to Friday prayer is announced, highlighting that spiritual obligations and collective devotion hold greater benefits than temporary material gains.

translation: So when you have completed the prayer, disperse in the land and seek of the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to balance their spiritual duties with worldly endeavors. After fulfilling the prescribed act of prayer, they are urged to actively engage in seeking sustenance and blessings through permissible means, while continually remembering and being mindful of God. Success is linked not only to worship but also to striving in the world with consciousness of Allah.

translation: And when they see a transaction or a diversion, they rush to it and leave you standing. Say, "What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to be distracted by worldly affairs and engagements, often neglecting spiritual responsibilities. It advises believers to recognize that what God offers—spiritual fulfillment and divine provision—is far superior to material pursuits and entertainment, encouraging trust in God's sustenance over worldly gains.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity of the hypocrites who outwardly profess belief yet conceal disbelief and ill intent. Their words are mere lip service, aimed at deceiving others, but Allah alone knows the truth of their hearts. It serves as a reminder that true faith is not just verbal acknowledgment but genuine conviction known only to Allah, who is the ultimate judge of sincerity.

translation: They made their oaths a barrier and thus obstructed from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of making one's oaths a means to block themselves and others from following the path of Allah. It admonishes those who manipulate their promises to justify disobedience or to hinder righteous actions, emphasizing that such behavior is profoundly wrong and leads to spiritual ruin.

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved; so a seal was set upon their hearts, and they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual consequence of insincerity in faith — when individuals initially accept belief but later reject it, their hearts become spiritually sealed, meaning they are closed off to guidance and insight. This sealing is a metaphor for the loss of perception and understanding caused by persistent disbelief, indicating that true comprehension and acceptance of divine truth require consistent faith and sincerity.

translation: And when you see them, their forms please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech as if they were pieces of wood propped up. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes certain disbelievers whose outward appearance is striking and alluring, thereby capturing attention and causing the listener to be drawn in when they speak. However, their words lack true substance and vitality, likened to lifeless, propped-up wooden logs. Their hypersensitivity to criticism or warnings, perceiving every admonition as a threat, reveals their insecurity and misguided mentality. The verse warns believers to be cautious and not to be deceived by superficial charm, as these individuals are spiritual enemies and sources of misguidance. The invocation of Allah's destruction upon them emphasizes their serious opposition to the truth and a strong admonition against following or emulating them.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside and you see them evading while they are arrogant.
